`README.md`:

```md
# HackiOS — XNU kernel

**HackiOS** boots Apple's open-source **XNU kernel** (`xnu-8796.121.2`, the kernel of iOS 16.5) on Android phone
hardware and runs the **unmodified iOS 16.5 user space** on top of it: launchd → backboardd → SpringBoard →
apps. Our own EFI loader, our own replacements for Apple's closed drivers, a UEFI port, and a Linux Wi-Fi driver
on a compatibility layer make that possible.

It runs in two places:

- **POCO X5 Pro 5G (redwood, Snapdragon 778G)** — nothing is flashed: the UEFI is started with `fastboot boot`,
  the whole system lives in RAM, and after a reboot the phone is back in Android;
- **QEMU** (`virt`, aarch64) — the same thing on any Linux computer, no phone needed.

This repository is half of the project:

| Repository | What |
|---|---|
| **hackios-xnu-kernel** (this one) | XNU patches, the EFI loader, the UEFI port, Wi-Fi, QEMU scripts, `xl`, prebuilt kernel/loader/UEFI, `common/` scripts |
| [hackios-xnu-userland](https://github.com/oosexgang/hackios-xnu-userland) | our init, injected libraries, launchd jobs, the APFS image builder, the scripts that take iOS out of Apple's IPSW, Metal/Mesa work |

> **No Apple files are in either repository.** `ios165/fetch.sh` downloads the iOS 16.5 IPSW from Apple's own CDN
> to *your* machine and extracts what is needed there. HackiOS is an independent research project by OOSEX GANG and
> is not affiliated with, authorised or endorsed by Apple Inc. iOS, iPhone and Apple are trademarks of Apple Inc.

<p>
<img src="docs/lockscreen.jpg" width="190" alt="Lock screen">
<img src="docs/homescreen.jpg" width="190" alt="Home screen">
<img src="docs/control-center.jpg" width="190" alt="Control Center">
<img src="docs/settings.jpg" width="190" alt="Settings">
</p>

Photographed on the phone, the Adreno GPU drawing (`gpu=1`). More in [Screenshots](#screenshots).

## What works

| Works | Does not work (yet) |
|---|---|
| Lock screen, swipe to unlock, home screen with all icons (two pages), stock iOS 16 wallpapers | Cellular, Bluetooth |
| System gestures: swipe up (home, app switcher), edge swipe (back), Control Center | Charging under our kernel (the phone only discharges) |
| Apps: Settings, Clock, Calendar, Photos, Notes, Safari and more; widgets (Weather, Calendar) on the phone | Metal for apps (in progress: 293 of 456 system shaders already run on the Adreno, see `docs/air.md` in hackios-xnu-userland) |
| Phone touchscreen (Goodix GT9916), multitouch, wake on touch; real power and volume keys | App Store content and Apple ID sign-in (no Secure Enclave; FairPlay daemon exits) |
| Up to 8 CPU cores (`cpus=8`), big core at 2.4 GHz, ~20 s to the lock screen | Video and Live Photo recording |
| Adreno 642L GPU through Mesa/freedreno (`gpu=1`, OpenGL ES for CoreAnimation) | |
| Wi-Fi (WCN6750, ath11k): join from Settings, Safari over Wi-Fi, 55–90 Mbit/s | |
| Sound (speakers, main microphone), camera in Camera.app (front/rear, preview, focus, HEIC photos) | |
| Data that iOS writes survives a reboot (`var_store=1 ufs_write=1`); iOS root volume on the phone's flash | |
| Sileo + Procursus (dpkg, apt), tweaks, SSH | |

It is a research bench, not a ROM: a session lasts a given number of seconds, then the kernel returns to the
loader and hands over its log.

## Quick start: QEMU, no kernel build

`prebuilt/` holds the kernel, loader and our programs built from these repositories, so all you need is the system
image, which is made on your machine from Apple's IPSW.

Needs: Linux x86-64, ~12 GB free disk, 4 GB free RAM. Packages (Arch):

```sh
sudo pacman -S --needed git python 7zip lz4 gcc qemu-system-aarch64 qemu-ui-gtk edk2-aarch64
```

(Debian/Ubuntu: `git python3 7zip liblz4-dev gcc qemu-system-arm qemu-efi-aarch64`; 7-Zip must be 23 or newer — it
reads APFS.)

```sh
git clone https://github.com/oosexgang/hackios-xnu-kernel.git hackios
cd hackios
common/setup.sh               # brings hackios-xnu-userland into the same tree, checks the host
ios165/fetch.sh               # downloads 7.4 GB from Apple's CDN and extracts what is needed (5-15 min)
common/build.sh qemu-virt     # builds the APFS images (and the kernel, if the toolchain is there)
common/run.sh qemu-virt       # a 20-minute session in a QEMU window
```

The lock screen appears after 2–3 minutes.

- **Mouse with the left button held = finger.** Unlock / leave an app: swipe up from the very bottom edge; back:
  swipe from the left edge.
- Keys: `H` home, `L` lock/power, `↑`/`↓` volume, `F11` (hold) five fingers.
- From a script: `qemu/touch.py swipe 0.5 0.985 0.5 0.3 250`, `qemu/touch.py tap 0.615 0.71`,
  `qemu/touch.py key home`; screenshot: `qemu/screendump.sh shot.png`.
- Right after SpringBoard appears the system is still registering apps: give it 30–40 s.
- Debian/Ubuntu UEFI firmware: `QEMU_EFI=/usr/share/AAVMF/AAVMF_CODE.fd QEMU_VARS=/usr/share/AAVMF/AAVMF_VARS.fd`.

## On the phone (POCO X5 Pro 5G)

You need a **POCO X5 Pro 5G (redwood)** with an unlocked bootloader, `adb` and `fastboot`, and the images from the
section above. Nothing is written to the phone's storage.

**The phone's own firmware** is not in the repository and cannot be: it is the vendor's and is taken from the very
phone it will run on, from its Android:

```sh
adb pull /vendor/firmware/a660_{gmu.bin,sqe.fw,zap.mdt,zap.b00,zap.b01,zap.b02} fw-gpu/      # GPU (gpu=1)
adb pull /vendor/firmware_mnt/image/wpss.{mdt,b02,b03,b04,b05,b06,b07} fw-wifi/              # Wi-Fi (wifi=1)
adb pull /vendor/firmware_mnt/image/adsp.{mdt,b02,...,b36} fw-audio/                         # sound (adsp=1)
adb pull /vendor/firmware/aw8697_haptic.bin fw-haptic/                                       # haptics
```

(Put the `fw-*` directories next to the workspace. Wi-Fi also needs `fw-wifi/mac` — the radio's address on one
line — and `fw-wifi/network` — network name and password. `userland/build.sh` prints which firmware went in.)

```sh
common/build.sh redwood GL=1          # images + out/redwood-boot.img
common/run.sh redwood 900             # loader into RAM, system image into RAM, a 15-minute session
```

or step by step with `xl`:

```sh
./xl enter            # Android -> fastboot -> our loader in RAM (fastboot boot); it brings up its own USB link
./xl ramdisk          # upload the system image into the phone's RAM (2.5 GB, ~80 s), once per loader session
XL_SECS=900 XL_CMDLINE="touchscreen=1 cpufreq=1 bootcpu=7 cpus=8 gpu=1 wifi=1 adsp=1" ./xl run
./xl screenshot shot.png
./xl reboot           # back to Android
```

`./xl` with no arguments lists every command (logs, screen and sound recording, camera frames, stop, state...).

## Prebuilt boot image

Every release has `hackios-redwood-boot.img` attached: the redwood UEFI with our loader inside, ready for
`fastboot boot`. It contains no Apple files; the system image is still made on your machine (above).

## Building from source

`common/build.sh <device>` runs every step that this machine can run and uses `prebuilt/` for the rest.

- **Kernel** — needs [theos](https://theos.dev/docs/installation-linux) in `~/theos` (cctools and
  `iPhoneOS16.5.sdk`) and `clang lld python perl`. Details: [xnu/README.md](xnu/README.md).
  ```sh
  xnu/apply.sh && xnu-deps/setup.sh && ./xnu-build.sh -j8 -k
  ```
- **Loader** — `xnuloader/build.sh` (clang + lld-link, an EFI application without EDK2).
- **Images** — `REST=1 userland/build.sh` (variables documented at the top of that file).
- **UEFI** — [uefi/README.md](uefi/README.md) (Project Silicium port); not needed to run, `prebuilt/uefi` has it.
- After rebuilding: `tools/update-prebuilt.sh` refreshes `prebuilt/`.

## Porting to another device

```sh
common/new-device.sh <codename> path/to/device.dtb   # profile + loader platform from the phone's device tree
```

Then follow [docs/PORTING.md](docs/PORTING.md): the UEFI port, the loader's platform description, the kernel's
drivers, the firmware. Device profiles live in `common/devices/` (`redwood.conf`, `qemu-virt.conf`, `_template.conf`).

## How it works

```
fastboot boot ──► UEFI (Mu-Silicium) ──► xnuloader (EFI application)
                                           │  stays resident: USB link (fastboot protocol),
                                           │  watchdog, receives the kernel's log
                                           ▼
            XNU (BCM2837 config as the base + our platform)
              ├─ GICv3, timer, video console, return to the loader
              ├─ APFS (images in RAM, iOS volume on flash), ramfs (/private/var, /tmp)
              ├─ minicrypto instead of corecrypto, AMFI and Sandbox stand-ins (MAC policies)
              ├─ driver replacements: IOSurface, IOMobileFramebuffer, AppleKeyStore, network stack
              ├─ input: /dev/redwood-touch ◄─ Goodix GT9916 (phone) / virtio-input (QEMU)
              ├─ GPU: Adreno 642L, Wi-Fi: WCN6750 (ath11k via LinuxKPI), sound: ADSP / virtio-sound
              ▼
   iOS 16.5 launchd → logd, notifyd, cfprefsd, runningboardd, backboardd, SpringBoard, apps
              ├─ our libraries are injected into backboardd, SpringBoard and mediaserverd
              │  (virtual HID services, a few ObjC method swaps — in memory only)
              └─ mediaserverd gets our CoreAudio output device (RedwoodAudio.driver)
```

The iOS programs, frameworks and dyld shared cache are not changed by a single byte: what they miss is done by the
kernel (driver replacements) or by a library the kernel injects with `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES` (`kern.exec_inject`).

## Layout

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `common/` | `setup.sh` (workspace), `build.sh` / `run.sh` (per device), `new-device.sh`, `devices/*.conf`, `ugit` |
| `xl` | drives the phone over USB: loader, kernel runs, logs, screenshots, screen and sound recording |
| `xnuloader/` | the loader: `loader.c` (UEFI application), `mkpayload.py` (kernel + images + arguments container) |
| `xnu/` | our XNU changes: patch, new files, `apply.sh` / `export.sh` |
| `xnu-deps/` | everything for building XNU on Linux: `setup.sh`, tool wrappers, stubs |
| `xnu-build.sh`, `xnu-env.sh` | kernel build |
| `uefi/`, `mkxnuimg.py` | the UEFI port and packing the boot image for `fastboot boot` |
| `wifi/lx/` | the layer on which Linux's Wi-Fi driver builds for our kernel |
| `qemu/` | QEMU runs, touch input, screenshots, stack symbolication |
| `tools/` | recording (`recording.py`, `sound.py`), UFS/flash tools, `mk-ath11k.sh`, `new-workspace.sh`, host tests |
| `prebuilt/` | built kernel, loader and UEFI pieces (`NOTICES.md` for the third-party code in the kernel) |
| `docs/` | screenshots, [checks.md](docs/checks.md), [PORTING.md](docs/PORTING.md) |

## Debugging

- Session log: QEMU's stdout or `logs/HHMMSS-run.log` from the phone.
- `RC_JOBS=rc.jobs.tour REST=1 userland/build.sh` — an image that unlocks and opens every app of the first page.
- `userabort:` in the log is the stack of a process that called `abort()`; `usertrap:` (with `systrace=1`) — crashes.
- Live stacks (QEMU): `qemu/touch.py stacks NAME`, then `qemu/symstack.py LOG NAME`
  (needs [`ipsw`](https://github.com/blacktop/ipsw)).
- How a check can lie to you: [docs/checks.md](docs/checks.md).

`common/build.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# Build everything a device needs, in order, skipping what cannot be built on this machine.
#
# usage: common/build.sh <device> [userland/build.sh variables...]
#   common/build.sh qemu-virt
#   common/build.sh redwood GL=1
#
#   1. kernel   xnu/apply.sh, xnu-deps/setup.sh, xnu-build.sh   -- only with theos + iPhoneOS16.5.sdk,
#                                                                  otherwise prebuilt/ is used
#   2. loader   xnuloader/build.sh                              -- only with clang + lld-link
#   3. images   userland/build.sh (REST=1 and the profile's USERLAND_VARS)
#                                                               -- needs ios165/fetch.sh to have run
#   4. boot     mkxnuimg.py -> out/<device>-boot.img             -- phones: the UEFI image for `fastboot boot`
#
#   SKIP="kernel loader images boot"   leave steps out
. "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/lib.sh"
load_device "$1"; shift
skip() { [[ " $SKIP " == *" $1 "* ]]; }
mkdir -p out

if ! skip kernel; then
	if [ -d "${THEOS:-$HOME/theos}/sdks/iPhoneOS16.5.sdk" ] && command -v clang >/dev/null; then
		[ -d xnu-src ] || xnu/apply.sh
		[ -x xnu-deps/host/bin/ld64 ] || xnu-deps/setup.sh
		# Wi-Fi radio driver (phones with a WCN6750): fetched and built once
		[ "$WIFI_ATH11K" = 1 ] && [ ! -f xnu-deps/build/ath11k/out/ath11k.o ] && { tools/mk-ath11k.sh && tools/mk-wlfw.sh; }
		# the export check fails after the kernel is linked, on purpose (xnu/README.md): judge by the file
		touch out/.kernel-start
		./xnu-build.sh -j"$(nproc)" -k > out/kernel-build.log 2>&1 || true
		K=xnu-src/xnu-8796.121.2/BUILD/obj/DEVELOPMENT_ARM64_BCM2837/mach.development.bcm2837
		[ -f $K ] && { [ $K -nt out/.kernel-start ] || ! grep -q "error:" out/kernel-build.log; } &&
			echo "build: kernel $(stat -c %s $K) bytes" || die "kernel build failed, see out/kernel-build.log"
	else
		echo "build: no theos/iPhoneOS16.5.sdk: using prebuilt/mach.development.bcm2837"
	fi
fi

if ! skip loader; then
	if command -v clang >/dev/null && command -v lld-link >/dev/null; then
		xnuloader/build.sh && echo "build: loader xnuloader/loader.efi"
	else
		echo "build: no clang/lld-link: using prebuilt/loader.efi"
	fi
fi

if ! skip images; then
	have_userland
	[ -d ios165/rootfs ] || die "no iOS files yet: run ios165/fetch.sh first (it downloads them from Apple to this machine)"
	env REST=1 $USERLAND_VARS "$@" userland/build.sh
fi

if ! skip boot && [ "$KIND" = phone ]; then
	# the UEFI with the loader inside, the way `xl enter` makes it: the loader then brings up its USB link
	L=xnuloader/loader.efi; [ -f $L ] || L=prebuilt/loader.efi
	python3 xnuloader/mkpayload.py -o out/usb-payload.bin loader.efi=$L --usb > /dev/null
	FD_BASE=$FD_BASE FD_SIZE=$FD_SIZE PAYLOAD_BASE=$PAYLOAD_BASE UEFI_FD=$UEFI_FD DTB=$DTB UEFI_TARGET=$UEFI_TARGET \
		python3 mkxnuimg.py -p out/usb-payload.bin -o out/$DEVICE-boot.img
	echo "build: out/$DEVICE-boot.img -- boot it with: fastboot boot out/$DEVICE-boot.img (or common/run.sh $DEVICE)"
fi

```

`common/devices/_template.conf`:

```conf
# Device profile: sourced by common/build.sh and common/run.sh. Copy with common/new-device.sh.
# Everything here is plain shell variables; see docs/PORTING.md for where each value comes from.

NAME="Vendor Model (codename)"
KIND=phone                      # phone | qemu
SOC="Qualcomm SMxxxx"

# --- boot chain (phones) ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The phone boots a Mu-Silicium UEFI (Project Silicium) with `fastboot boot`; the UEFI starts our loader.
UEFI_TARGET=codename            # Mu-Silicium device name: build_uefi.py -d $UEFI_TARGET
UEFI_FD=                        # a built SILICIUM_UEFI.fd; empty: Mu-Silicium/Build/<target>Pkg/... or prebuilt/uefi
DTB=                            # the phone's own device tree (from its vendor_boot); empty: prebuilt/uefi/redwood.dtb
FD_BASE=0x9FD00000              # where the boot shim puts the UEFI image (the UEFI port's memory map)
FD_SIZE=0x200000
PAYLOAD_BASE=0xF0000000         # where the kernel + images container goes (free RAM in the memory map)

# --- kernel and loader -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# xnuloader/loader.c picks its `struct platform` by what the firmware reports (see docs/PORTING.md):
# a new SoC needs one there (common/new-device.sh writes a starting point next to this file).
FB_BASE=0x00000000              # framebuffer base the UEFI reports (GOP) -- identifies the device
WIFI_ATH11K=0                   # 1: build the ath11k Wi-Fi driver into the kernel (WCN6750 radios)

# --- what the run needs ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
BOOTARGS="touchscreen=1 cpus=8"
DEFAULT_SECS=900
USERLAND_VARS=""                # extra variables for userland/build.sh, e.g. "GL=1"
# The phone's own firmware, taken from its Android (never in the repository): see docs/PORTING.md.
FIRMWARE=""

```

`common/devices/qemu-virt.conf`:

```conf
# QEMU's `virt` machine (aarch64) on any Linux computer -- no phone needed.
NAME="QEMU virt (aarch64)"
KIND=qemu
SOC="emulated Cortex-A72"

FB_BASE=                        # ramfb; xnuloader falls back to platform_qemu_virt
WIFI_ATH11K=0

SMP=4                           # QEMU's CPUs
BOOTARGS="cpus=4"               # how many of them the kernel takes

`common/devices/redwood.conf`:

```conf
# POCO X5 Pro 5G -- the device HackiOS was brought up on.
NAME="POCO X5 Pro 5G (redwood)"
KIND=phone
SOC="Qualcomm Snapdragon 778G (SM7325)"

UEFI_TARGET=redwood
UEFI_FD=
DTB=
FD_BASE=0x9FD00000
FD_SIZE=0x200000
PAYLOAD_BASE=0xF0000000

FB_BASE=0xE1000000              # 1080 x 2400; xnuloader picks platform_redwood by it
WIFI_ATH11K=1                   # WCN6750

# bootcpu=7: run on the big core; cpufreq=1: top speed; add gpu=1 (with GL=1 images), wifi=1, adsp=1
BOOTARGS="touchscreen=1 cpufreq=1 bootcpu=7 cpus=8"
DEFAULT_SECS=900
USERLAND_VARS=""
# taken from the phone's Android with adb (see README.md, "On the phone")
FIRMWARE="fw-gpu fw-wifi fw-audio fw-haptic"

`common/lib.sh`:

```sh
# Shared by common/*.sh: find the workspace and load a device profile.
#   . "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/lib.sh"; load_device "$1"
ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")")/.." && pwd)
cd "$ROOT" || exit 1

die() { echo "${0##*/}: $*" >&2; exit 1; }

# load_device <name>: common/devices/<name>.conf sets the variables documented in _template.conf
load_device() {
	local name=${1:-${DEVICE:-}}
	[ -n "$name" ] || die "which device? $(ls common/devices | sed -n 's/\.conf$//p' | grep -v '^_' | tr '\n' ' ')"
	local conf=common/devices/$name.conf
	[ -f "$conf" ] || die "no profile $conf (common/new-device.sh $name makes one)"
	# shellcheck disable=SC1090
	. "$conf"
	DEVICE=$name
	export DEVICE KIND
	echo "${0##*/}: device $DEVICE -- $NAME ($KIND)"
}

have_userland() {
	[ -d .userland.git ] || [ -f userland/build.sh ] || die "the userland is not here: run common/setup.sh"
}

```

`common/new-device.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# Start a port of HackiOS to another device: a profile and a loader platform description to fill in.
#
# usage: common/new-device.sh <codename> [path/to/device.dtb]
#
# Writes common/devices/<codename>.conf (from _template.conf) and common/devices/<codename>.platform.c,
# a `struct platform` for xnuloader/loader.c. Given the phone's device tree (from its vendor_boot, or
# `adb pull /sys/firmware/fdt`), it fills in what can be read from it: the GIC addresses, the number of
# CPU cores and how MPIDR numbers them, and which cores are the small ones. What it cannot read is left
# as TODO; docs/PORTING.md walks through all of it.
. "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/lib.sh"
CODE=$1; DTB=$2
[ -n "$CODE" ] || die "usage: common/new-device.sh <codename> [device.dtb]"
[[ "$CODE" =~ ^[a-z0-9_-]+$ ]] || die "codename: lower-case letters, digits, - and _ only"
CONF=common/devices/$CODE.conf PLATC=common/devices/$CODE.platform.c
[ -e "$CONF" ] && die "$CONF exists already"

sed -e "s/^NAME=.*/NAME=\"TODO vendor model ($CODE)\"/" -e "s/^UEFI_TARGET=.*/UEFI_TARGET=$CODE/" \
	common/devices/_template.conf > "$CONF"
[ -n "$DTB" ] && sed -i "s|^DTB=.*|DTB=$(readlink -f "$DTB")|" "$CONF"

GIC_DIST=TODO GIC_REDIST=TODO CORES=8 SHIFT=8 SMALL=0x0
if [ -n "$DTB" ]; then
	command -v dtc >/dev/null || die "dtc is needed to read $DTB (package dtc)"
	# GIC (compatible "arm,gic-v3": reg = <dist size redist size>, one or two cells each), the cores
	# (cpu@N), how MPIDR numbers them (Qualcomm: reg 0x100, 0x200... -- the second affinity field) and
	# which are small (the cluster with the lowest capacity-dmips-mhz)
	read -r GIC_DIST GIC_REDIST CORES SHIFT SMALL < <(python3 - "$DTB" <<'PY'
import re, subprocess, sys
dts = subprocess.run(['dtc', '-I', 'dtb', '-O', 'dts', sys.argv[1]], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
gic = ['TODO', 'TODO']
m = re.search(r'compatible = "arm,gic-v3";(.*?)\};', dts, re.S)
if m:
    cells = [int(x, 16) for x in re.search(r'reg = <([^>]*)>', m.group(1)).group(1).split()]
    if len(cells) == 4: gic = [hex(cells[0]), hex(cells[2])]
    elif len(cells) >= 8: gic = [hex((cells[0] << 32) | cells[1]), hex((cells[4] << 32) | cells[5])]
cpus = []
for m in re.finditer(r'\n\t*cpu@([0-9a-f]+) \{(.*?)\n\t*\};', dts, re.S):
    cap = re.search(r'capacity-dmips-mhz = <(0x[0-9a-f]+)>', m.group(2))
    cpus.append((int(m.group(1), 16), int(cap.group(1), 16) if cap else 0))
shift = 8 if any(r >= 0x100 for r, _ in cpus) else 0
caps = [c for _, c in cpus if c]
small = 0
for r, c in cpus:
    # the little cluster: the lowest capacity, when the cores are not all alike
    if caps and c == min(caps) and min(caps) < max(caps): small |= 1 << (r >> shift)
print(gic[0], gic[1], len(cpus) or 8, shift, hex(small))
PY
)
	echo "new-device: from $DTB: GIC $GIC_DIST / $GIC_REDIST, $CORES cores, MPIDR shift $SHIFT, small cores $SMALL"
fi

cat > "$PLATC" <<EOF
/*
 * $CODE: paste into xnuloader/loader.c next to platform_redwood and add &platform_$CODE to platforms[].
 * Every value is explained in docs/PORTING.md ("The loader").
 */
static const struct platform platform_$CODE = {
	.name = "$CODE",
	.io_base = 0x00400000, .io_size = 0x3FC00000,   /* TODO: one window over the SoC's peripherals, non-zero base */
	.gic_dist = $GIC_DIST, .gic_redist = $GIC_REDIST,
	.uart = 0,                                      /* phones: no PL011 */
	.log_other_cpu = 1,
	.cores = $CORES, .core_shift = $SHIFT,
	.small_cores = $SMALL,                          /* TODO: a bit per "small" core (capacity-dmips-mhz in the DT) */
	.fb_base = 0x0,                                 /* TODO: the framebuffer base the UEFI prints ("display ... at") */
};
EOF
echo "new-device: wrote $CONF and $PLATC"
echo "new-device: next -- docs/PORTING.md, then: common/build.sh $CODE && common/run.sh $CODE"

```

`common/run.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# Boot HackiOS on a device whose images are built (common/build.sh <device>).
#
# usage: common/run.sh <device> [seconds]
#   common/run.sh qemu-virt          QEMU window, 20 minutes (mouse = finger, H = home, L = lock)
#   common/run.sh redwood 900        the phone over USB: loader in RAM, system image in RAM, 15 minutes
#
# Nothing is flashed: on a phone everything lives in RAM and `./xl reboot` (or a power-key reset)
# brings back Android. The session's log is printed (QEMU) or saved in logs/ (phones).
. "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/lib.sh"
load_device "$1"
SECS=${2:-$DEFAULT_SECS}
mkdir -p logs
[ -f userland/root.apfs ] && [ -f userland/system.apfs ] || die "no images: run common/build.sh $DEVICE first"

case "$KIND" in
qemu)
	QEMU_SMP=${QEMU_SMP:-$SMP} CMDLINE="${CMDLINE:-$BOOTARGS}" qemu/run-ios.sh "$SECS" -display "${DISPLAY_KIND:-gtk}" |
		tee logs/qemu-$(date +%H%M%S).log
	;;
phone)
	command -v fastboot >/dev/null || die "fastboot is not installed"
	./xl enter || die "could not get the phone into the loader (USB? unlocked bootloader?)"
	./xl ramdisk userland/system.apfs
	XL_SECS=$SECS XL_CMDLINE="${XL_CMDLINE:-$BOOTARGS}" ./xl run
	echo "run: './xl screenshot shot.png' for the screen, './xl reboot' to go back to Android"
	;;
*) die "unknown KIND=$KIND in common/devices/$DEVICE.conf" ;;
esac

```

`common/setup.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# One-time setup of a HackiOS workspace.
#
# HackiOS lives in two repositories that are built as one tree:
#
#   hackios-xnu-kernel     (this one)  the XNU kernel patches, the EFI loader, the UEFI port, Wi-Fi,
#                                      QEMU scripts, xl and these common scripts
#   hackios-xnu-userland               our init, injected libraries, launchd jobs, the image builder,
#                                      the scripts that take iOS out of Apple's IPSW, Metal/Mesa work
#
# Their scripts refer to each other by path (userland/build.sh uses the kernel's cross toolchain in
# xnu-deps/, the kernel's APFS code is tested with tools/apfs/...). So the userland repository is
# checked out into the SAME directory as this one, as a second git repository whose git dir is
# .userland.git. Every path is then exactly where every script expects it; each repository still
# commits and pushes on its own (use common/ugit for the userland one: `common/ugit status`).
#
# usage: common/setup.sh            clone hackios-xnu-userland into this tree (or update it) and
#                                   check the host for the tools the build needs
#   USERLAND_URL=...   where to clone from (default: github.com/oosexgang/hackios-xnu-userland)
#   USERLAND_REF=...   branch or tag (default: main)
set -e
cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/.."
ROOT=$PWD
URL=${USERLAND_URL:-https://github.com/oosexgang/hackios-xnu-userland.git}
REF=${USERLAND_REF:-main}
UG=(git --git-dir="$ROOT/.userland.git" --work-tree="$ROOT")

if [ ! -d .userland.git ]; then
	echo "setup: cloning $URL ($REF) into this tree"
	tmp=$(mktemp -d)
	git clone --no-checkout --branch "$REF" "$URL" "$tmp/u"
	mv "$tmp/u/.git" .userland.git
	rm -rf "$tmp"
	"${UG[@]}" config core.bare false
	"${UG[@]}" config core.worktree "$ROOT"
	# the kernel's .gitignore is read here too and outranks info/exclude: untracked files are the
	# kernel repository's business; add a new userland file by name (common/ugit add PATH)
	"${UG[@]}" config status.showUntrackedFiles no
	cp common/userland.exclude .userland.git/info/exclude
	# README.md, .gitignore and LICENSE at the top are the kernel repository's: the userland ones stay in git
	# only (skip-worktree), every other file is written out
	"${UG[@]}" read-tree -m HEAD
	for f in README.md .gitignore LICENSE; do
		"${UG[@]}" ls-files --error-unmatch "$f" > /dev/null 2>&1 && "${UG[@]}" update-index --skip-worktree "$f"
	done
	"${UG[@]}" ls-files -z | grep -zvxE 'README\.md|\.gitignore|LICENSE' | xargs -0 "${UG[@]}" checkout --
else
	echo "setup: hackios-xnu-userland already here, updating"
	cp common/userland.exclude .userland.git/info/exclude
	"${UG[@]}" pull --ff-only || echo "setup: could not fast-forward the userland checkout (local changes?)"
fi
"${UG[@]}" log -1 --format='setup: hackios-xnu-userland at %h (%cs) %s'
git log -1 --format='setup: hackios-xnu-kernel   at %h (%cs) %s'

# host check: what is missing only matters for the step that needs it
need() { # need <command> <what for>
	command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0
	printf '  %-22s missing -- needed %s\n' "$1" "$2"; MISSING=1
}
echo "setup: checking the host"
MISSING=0
need python3 "everywhere"
need git "everywhere"
need curl "to fetch iOS, XNU and dependencies"
need 7z "by ios165/fetch.sh (7-Zip 23+, reads APFS)"
need gcc "by ios165/fetch.sh (builds the LZBITMAP decoder)"
need qemu-system-aarch64 "to run in QEMU (DEVICE=qemu-virt)"
need fastboot "to boot a phone"
need adb "to take a phone's own firmware off it"
need clang "to build the kernel and the loader (not needed with prebuilt/)"
need lld-link "to build the loader (not needed with prebuilt/)"
[ -d "${THEOS:-$HOME/theos}/sdks/iPhoneOS16.5.sdk" ] ||
	echo "  theos + iPhoneOS16.5.sdk missing -- needed only to rebuild the kernel and our programs (prebuilt/ has them)"
[ $MISSING = 0 ] && echo "  all there"
cat <<EOF

Next:
  ios165/fetch.sh                   # once: takes iOS 16.5 out of Apple's IPSW onto this machine (7.4 GB download)
  common/build.sh qemu-virt         # images (+ kernel and loader when the toolchain is there)
  common/run.sh qemu-virt           # iOS in a QEMU window
See README.md; porting to another device: docs/PORTING.md and common/new-device.sh.
EOF

```

`common/ugit`:

#!/bin/bash
# git for the hackios-xnu-userland repository that shares this working tree (see common/setup.sh):
#   common/ugit status | common/ugit add userland/src/init.c | common/ugit commit | common/ugit push
ROOT=$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/..
[ -d "$ROOT/.userland.git" ] || { echo "ugit: no userland checkout here; run common/setup.sh first" >&2; exit 1; }
exec git --git-dir="$ROOT/.userland.git" --work-tree="$ROOT" "$@"

`docs/PORTING.md`:

```md
# Porting HackiOS to another device

HackiOS was brought up on the POCO X5 Pro 5G (Snapdragon 778G). A Qualcomm phone with an unlockable bootloader
is the realistic next target: the boot chain (Mu-Silicium UEFI started with `fastboot boot`) and most of the kernel's
platform code carry over. Start with:

```sh
common/new-device.sh <codename> path/to/device.dtb
```

It writes `common/devices/<codename>.conf` (the profile `common/build.sh` and `common/run.sh` read) and
`common/devices/<codename>.platform.c` (the loader's description of the SoC), filling in what the device tree says.
Get the device tree from the phone's `vendor_boot` image, or from a running Android: `adb pull /sys/firmware/fdt`.

## 1. The UEFI

The phone needs a UEFI that our loader can run under. Port [Mu-Silicium](https://github.com/Project-Silicium/Mu-Silicium)
the way `uefi/` ports redwood (it follows `lisa`, the same SoC package):

- `Platforms/<Vendor>/<codename>Pkg`: memory map and driver list (copy the closest device of the same SoC);
- `Binaries/<codename>`: the UEFI drivers of the phone's own firmware, extracted with
  [UEFIReader](https://github.com/WOA-Project/UEFIReader) from its `xbl.img`;
- apply our two changes from `uefi/mu-silicium.patch`: the boot shim copies the "XNUP" container after the UEFI
  image to `PAYLOAD_BASE`, and `BootManagerLib` starts the XNU loader from it instead of the menu.

Put the addresses in the profile: `FD_BASE`, `FD_SIZE` (where the shim puts the UEFI image) and `PAYLOAD_BASE`
(free RAM for the kernel and images). The prebuilt `BootShim.bin` is built for redwood's addresses: build the
shim from your Mu-Silicium tree (`mkxnuimg.py` does it when `Mu-Silicium/` is there).

## 2. The loader

`xnuloader/loader.c` describes each device with a `struct platform` and picks it by the framebuffer base the UEFI
reports. Paste `common/devices/<codename>.platform.c` next to `platform_redwood` and add it to `platforms[]`:

| Field | Where it comes from |
|---|---|
| `io_base`, `io_size` | one window that covers the SoC's peripherals; it must not start at 0 (XNU then skips clock setup) |
| `gic_dist`, `gic_redist` | the `arm,gic-v3` node's `reg` (filled in by `new-device.sh`) |
| `cores`, `core_shift` | the `cpu@` nodes; Qualcomm numbers cores in MPIDR's second affinity field (shift 8) |
| `small_cores` | a bit per core of the little cluster (lowest `capacity-dmips-mhz`) |
| `psci_hvc` | 1 if the firmware's PSCI is called with HVC (QEMU), 0 for SMC (phones) |
| `fb_base` | the framebuffer address; the loader prints it at start (`display W x H at ...`) |

Rebuild with `xnuloader/build.sh`; QEMU must still pick `qemu-virt` (no match = ramfb).

## 3. The kernel

What is generic: GICv3, the timer, PSCI SMP, the display (the UEFI's framebuffer), APFS and ramfs, the driver
replacements, the return-to-loader path. What is redwood-specific and needs looking at:

- **touch**: `bsd/dev/redwood_goodix.c` (Goodix GT9916 over bit-banged SPI) — another panel needs its own driver
  feeding `/dev/redwood-touch` (`bsd/dev/redwood_input.c`);
- **buttons, CPU frequency, watchdog**: GPIO/PMIC numbers and the EPSS block in `redwood_input.c`,
  `redwood_cpufreq.c`, `osfmk/arm64/loader_return.c`;
- **GPU / Wi-Fi / sound**: `redwood_adreno.c` (Adreno 642L), `redwood_wifi.c` (WCN6750 + ath11k), `redwood_audio.c`
  — the same Qualcomm subsystems (SMEM, SMP2P, GLINK, QRTR, QMI) are reused, the addresses and firmware differ.

Start with no extras: the system boots to the lock screen with only the framebuffer, touch and the CPU.

## 4. Firmware

Vendor firmware never goes into the repository; it comes from the phone's own Android (`FIRMWARE` in the profile
lists what to pull, see README "On the phone"). Without `fw-gpu/` the kernel does not start the GPU and says so only
deep in the log (`adreno: THE GPU IS NOT STARTED`); `userland/build.sh` prints which firmware went into the image.

## 5. Run

```sh
common/build.sh <codename>
common/run.sh <codename>
```

The first useful milestone is the loader's own screen and log over USB (`./xl log`), the next one is the kernel's
verbose boot text (`-v`), then SpringBoard. Read [checks.md](checks.md) before trusting a "it is not in the log".

```

`docs/checks.md`:

```md
# How our own checks lie

Eleven ways a check lies, and one habit against them. Each one cost us a run or a wrong line in the
README during the work on this port. They are written down because eleven of the twelve look the same:
**missing information reads as a missing problem.**

- **A skip that is not counted.** A `continue` that adds nothing to the total turns "not checked" into
  "checked and matched". Ten AIR declarations were listed as matching after being compared on one case of
  four (the other three were skipped on an endless wait); `if idx >= len(flat): continue` silently dropped
  short rows; a `read()` into a fixed buffer lost the tail of a file. The total still added up --
  68 + 3 + 7 = 78 -- because the deferred ones were counted as matches. What catches it is not the total but
  **a total in which every exception has its own column with a name and a number**. The extreme case of the
  same trouble is a check over an empty set: a loop of zero iterations prints "0 of 47" and looks exactly
  like an honest zero. It happened once -- the list of kernels lived in a directory that was cleaned between
  sessions -- and only the shell saying "no such file" separately saved us. A denominator lies as quietly as
  a summand.
- **A silenced command.** `patch -s --dry-run` returned 0 and said nothing, and the silence was read as
  "applies exactly"; without `-s` it said `succeeded at 410 (offset 2 lines)`.
- **Inference from absence.** "Not in the log" and "did not happen" are different things: the loader's log
  drops its middle (the sign is a size at the limit and the exact line `the log between the first 256 KB and
  the last 1 MB was dropped`, not the words `was dropped`, which the button driver also prints). A `grep`'s
  field of view reads the same way: six matches of `bin/sh` were `/var/jb/bin/sh`, and "`xl ramdisk` has no
  guard" missed a guard twenty lines higher. And a silent instrument first has to be shown that it **can**
  speak: a watchdog that "never fired" proves something only together with the number of times it ran (ours
  came out 26 of 26 with zero drift); a measurement that printed zero lines once turned out to be a `grep`
  for a pattern `printf` never printed -- a measurement that cannot fire looks exactly like an event that did
  not happen. That zero was caught not by doubting the instrument but by **contradicting what was already
  measured**: three modules translate thanks to pointer binding, so there could not be a zero there. When
  there is no control, consistency with earlier numbers plays its part -- and it works only if the earlier
  results were written down as numbers, not words.
- **A pair without a control.** "Before and after" without "before and before" answers the wrong question:
  10,835 differing pixels looked like the effect of a patch until two runs of the same build gave 13,738.
- **Your own tree instead of the subject.** Compare with someone else's tree only from a clean unpack: our
  copy of Mesa is patched (202,487 bytes against 202,144), and the difference would have been found "on their
  side".
- **A stale instrument in one column.** In the corpus table the "translates" column was counted with the
  frontend from 10:57 and the "compiles with ir3" column with a binary from 09:16: `ir3_compiler` is not part
  of the default target and an ordinary rebuild did not touch it. The result was "315 translate, 313 through
  ir3", and it made a plausible story -- "ir3 cannot do two of something" -- until it turned out the refusal
  message was text removed from the frontend an hour earlier. In fact it was 315/315. Two figures of one table
  measured by different generations of the instrument produce not an error but a **finding that does not
  exist**. The cure is a refusal, not a warning: `corpus.py` no longer runs if `ir3_compiler` is older than any
  frontend source.
- **A true complaint about the wrong thing.** A debugging instrument can report a truth that has nothing to do
  with the problem, and so hide the real cause. When three AIR modules crashed in `nir_repair_ssa`,
  `nir_validate_shader` reported four errors about block indices -- and **exactly the same ones** on a module
  that translates perfectly. That is the state of an unstructured impl before `lower_goto_ifs`, and harmless;
  taking the complaint for the answer, we would have fixed indexing and got nowhere. The real cause (values
  created in the entry point's impl and used in a callback) was found by printing, not by the validator. The
  rule: **take any diagnostic instrument's reading on a known-good input first** -- without it, its output
  cannot be told from an answer.
- **An instrument replaced during the measurement.** `check.sh` was running while `air2nir` was rebuilt under
  it. The run exited 0 -- and had checked a binary that no longer existed by the end. Unlike a stale
  instrument, this one is valid before and after and not the same in the middle; the green is
  indistinguishable from a real one. Same cure as everything else: measure on a tree nobody touches while the
  measurement runs.
- **A claim nobody could refute.** The AIR frontend refused to translate calls to functions defined in the
  module itself, and a comment gave the reason: system shaders do not need it, Apple's inliner flattens
  everything. Not true -- six entry points do it, five of them compute kernels. It survived not because nobody
  looked but because **there was nothing to check it with**: until `air_run` could dispatch compute kernels,
  nobody could run those five. A false claim covered by a missing capability outlives all the others: no
  control, sum or code reading catches it -- only the arrival of the instrument that was missing.
- **A correction nobody re-checks.** Accuracy is more often lost not in the first claim but in the one that
  fixes it: a correction comes with a feeling of diligence and so is not read with the same eyes. Here, after
  dropping "a threshold of two textures", the author put in its place "among forty there are surely some that
  read two" -- a guess, in the same paragraph that apologised for reasoning instead of a number, while the
  numbers were already in a log he had taught to print them. There were eight with two textures and two with
  three, and **all ten were dispatched before the fix too**, so there was no threshold at all. Check a
  corrected claim the way you checked the original, against the same data.
- **An instrument whose error has a direction.** `grep` for a global's name in LLVM bitcode finds **zero**
  almost always: bitcode is packed by bits, and the name matches only when it happens to land on byte
  boundaries. So any corpus count made with such a grep can **only undercount** -- and its zero is
  indistinguishable from an honest one. That is how "two modules declare a `constexpr sampler`" got into the
  notes where there were ten. Knowing the direction helps twice: a zero from an undercounting instrument means
  nothing, and a **non-zero** answer is a lower bound, which is already a fact. Before counting with
  something, ask which way it errs.
- **Write it for whoever will check it.** The cheapest of all: rephrase the claim for the person who will
  re-check it. A control costs a run, a rephrasing costs nothing, and it catches the same things: "checked on
  `main`" fell apart into "one file of two checked" the minute the file had to be handed to another session.
  The habit is not free, though: it needs someone **to** hand it to. Alone you have to imagine the checker,
  and that works worst exactly when you are sure you are right -- so this is more about how the work is
  organised than about self-discipline.

```

`mkxnuimg.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Pack the redwood UEFI (with the hook that starts the XNU loader) and an optional payload
into an Android boot image for `fastboot boot`.

  kernel = gzip(BootShim + UEFI FD + ["XNUP" container]) + DTB

The boot shim copies the FD to its base and the payload to PAYLOAD_BASE.

The UEFI pieces are taken from a Mu-Silicium tree built here (Mu-Silicium/, see uefi/README.md)
or, when there is none, from prebuilt/uefi/.

usage: mkxnuimg.py [-p payload.bin] [-o out.img]

Another device (common/devices/<name>.conf, read by common/build.sh) sets these in the environment:
  UEFI_TARGET   Mu-Silicium device name (default redwood)    UEFI_FD, DTB   files to use instead
  FD_BASE, FD_SIZE, PAYLOAD_BASE                              addresses from its UEFI port's memory map
"""
import argparse, gzip, os, subprocess, sys

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
MU = os.path.join(HERE, 'Mu-Silicium')
PREBUILT = os.path.join(HERE, 'prebuilt', 'uefi')
def env_int(name, default):
    v = os.environ.get(name, '')
    return int(v, 0) if v else default
TARGET = os.environ.get('UEFI_TARGET') or 'redwood'
FD_BASE, FD_SIZE = env_int('FD_BASE', 0x9FD00000), env_int('FD_SIZE', 0x200000)
PAYLOAD_BASE, PAYLOAD_MAX = env_int('PAYLOAD_BASE', 0xF0000000), 0x04000000

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument('-p', '--payload')
ap.add_argument('-o', '--output', default=os.path.join(HERE, 'xnu-redwood.img'))
ap.add_argument('--mode', default='RELEASE')
args = ap.parse_args()

fd_path = os.environ.get('UEFI_FD') or os.path.join(MU, f'Build/{TARGET}Pkg/{args.mode}_CLANGPDB/FV/SILICIUM_UEFI.fd')
if os.path.isfile(fd_path) and os.path.isdir(os.path.join(MU, 'BootShim')):
    shim_dir = os.path.join(MU, 'BootShim')
    for f in ('BootShim.elf', 'BootShim.bin'):
        try: os.unlink(os.path.join(shim_dir, f))
        except FileNotFoundError: pass
    subprocess.check_call(['make', 'REQUIRES_KERNEL_HEADER=1', f'FD_BASE={FD_BASE:#x}', f'FD_SIZE={FD_SIZE:#x}',
                           f'CFLAGS=--target=aarch64-linux-gnu -DPAYLOAD_BASE={PAYLOAD_BASE:#x}'],
                          cwd=shim_dir, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    parts = {'shim': os.path.join(shim_dir, 'BootShim.bin'), 'fd': fd_path,
             'dtb': os.path.join(MU, f'Resources/DTBs/{TARGET}.dtb'), 'ramdisk': os.path.join(MU, 'Resources/ramdisk'),
             'mkbootimg': os.path.join(MU, 'Resources/Scripts/mkbootimg.py')}
else:
    parts = {'shim': os.path.join(PREBUILT, 'BootShim.bin'), 'fd': os.path.join(PREBUILT, 'SILICIUM_UEFI.fd'),
             'dtb': os.path.join(PREBUILT, 'redwood.dtb'), 'ramdisk': os.path.join(PREBUILT, 'ramdisk'),
             'mkbootimg': os.path.join(PREBUILT, 'mkbootimg.py')}
    if os.environ.get('UEFI_FD'): parts['fd'] = os.environ['UEFI_FD']
shim = open(parts['shim'], 'rb').read()
fd = open(parts['fd'], 'rb').read()
assert len(fd) == FD_SIZE, hex(len(fd))

blob = shim + fd
if args.payload:
    data = open(args.payload, 'rb').read()
    # the payload file is a complete "XNUP" container (see xnuloader/mkpayload.py)
    assert data[:4] == b'XNUP' and len(data) <= PAYLOAD_MAX - 0x1000, 'bad or oversized payload'
    blob += data
    blob += b'\0' * (-len(blob) % 16)
    print(f'payload: {len(data)} bytes, bytesum={sum(data) & 0xffffffff:08x}')

if os.environ.get('DTB'): parts['dtb'] = os.environ['DTB']
dtb = open(parts['dtb'], 'rb').read()
kernel = args.output + '.kernel~'
open(kernel, 'wb').write(gzip.compress(blob, 6) + dtb)
try:
    subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, parts['mkbootimg'], '--kernel', kernel, '--ramdisk', parts['ramdisk'],
                           '--header_version', '1', '-o', args.output])
finally:
    os.unlink(kernel)
print(f'{args.output}: {os.path.getsize(args.output)} bytes (shim {len(shim)}, uncompressed {len(blob)})')

```

`prebuilt/uefi/mkbootimg.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
#
# Copyright 2015, The Android Open Source Project
#
# Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
# you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
# You may obtain a copy of the License at
#
#     http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
#
# Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software
# distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS,
# WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
# See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
# limitations under the License.

"""Creates the boot image."""

from argparse import (ArgumentParser, ArgumentTypeError,
                      FileType, RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
from hashlib import sha1
from os import fstat
from struct import pack

import array
import collections
import os
import re
import subprocess
import tempfile

# Constant and structure definition is in
# system/tools/mkbootimg/include/bootimg/bootimg.h
BOOT_MAGIC = 'ANDROID!'
BOOT_MAGIC_SIZE = 8
BOOT_NAME_SIZE = 16
BOOT_ARGS_SIZE = 512
BOOT_EXTRA_ARGS_SIZE = 1024
BOOT_IMAGE_HEADER_V1_SIZE = 1648
BOOT_IMAGE_HEADER_V2_SIZE = 1660
BOOT_IMAGE_HEADER_V3_SIZE = 1580
BOOT_IMAGE_HEADER_V3_PAGESIZE = 4096
BOOT_IMAGE_HEADER_V4_SIZE = 1584
BOOT_IMAGE_V4_SIGNATURE_SIZE = 4096

VENDOR_BOOT_MAGIC = 'VNDRBOOT'
VENDOR_BOOT_MAGIC_SIZE = 8
VENDOR_BOOT_NAME_SIZE = BOOT_NAME_SIZE
VENDOR_BOOT_ARGS_SIZE = 2048
VENDOR_BOOT_IMAGE_HEADER_V3_SIZE = 2112
VENDOR_BOOT_IMAGE_HEADER_V4_SIZE = 2128

VENDOR_RAMDISK_TYPE_NONE = 0
VENDOR_RAMDISK_TYPE_PLATFORM = 1
VENDOR_RAMDISK_TYPE_RECOVERY = 2
VENDOR_RAMDISK_TYPE_DLKM = 3
VENDOR_RAMDISK_NAME_SIZE = 32
VENDOR_RAMDISK_TABLE_ENTRY_BOARD_ID_SIZE = 16
VENDOR_RAMDISK_TABLE_ENTRY_V4_SIZE = 108

# Names with special meaning, mustn't be specified in --ramdisk_name.
VENDOR_RAMDISK_NAME_BLOCKLIST = {b'default'}

PARSER_ARGUMENT_VENDOR_RAMDISK_FRAGMENT = '--vendor_ramdisk_fragment'


def filesize(f):
    if f is None:
        return 0
    try:
        return fstat(f.fileno()).st_size
    except OSError:
        return 0


def update_sha(sha, f):
    if f:
        sha.update(f.read())
        f.seek(0)
        sha.update(pack('I', filesize(f)))
    else:
        sha.update(pack('I', 0))


def pad_file(f, padding):
    pad = (padding - (f.tell() & (padding - 1))) & (padding - 1)
    f.write(pack(str(pad) + 'x'))


def get_number_of_pages(image_size, page_size):
    """calculates the number of pages required for the image"""
    return (image_size + page_size - 1) // page_size


def get_recovery_dtbo_offset(args):
    """calculates the offset of recovery_dtbo image in the boot image"""
    num_header_pages = 1 # header occupies a page
    num_kernel_pages = get_number_of_pages(filesize(args.kernel), args.pagesize)
    num_ramdisk_pages = get_number_of_pages(filesize(args.ramdisk),
                                            args.pagesize)
    num_second_pages = get_number_of_pages(filesize(args.second), args.pagesize)
    dtbo_offset = args.pagesize * (num_header_pages + num_kernel_pages +
                                   num_ramdisk_pages + num_second_pages)
    return dtbo_offset


def write_header_v3_and_above(args):
    if args.header_version > 3:
        boot_header_size = BOOT_IMAGE_HEADER_V4_SIZE
    else:
        boot_header_size = BOOT_IMAGE_HEADER_V3_SIZE

    args.output.write(pack(f'{BOOT_MAGIC_SIZE}s', BOOT_MAGIC.encode()))
    # kernel size in bytes
    args.output.write(pack('I', filesize(args.kernel)))
    # ramdisk size in bytes
    args.output.write(pack('I', filesize(args.ramdisk)))
    # os version and patch level
    args.output.write(pack('I', (args.os_version << 11) | args.os_patch_level))
    args.output.write(pack('I', boot_header_size))
    # reserved
    args.output.write(pack('4I', 0, 0, 0, 0))
    # version of boot image header
    args.output.write(pack('I', args.header_version))
    args.output.write(pack(f'{BOOT_ARGS_SIZE + BOOT_EXTRA_ARGS_SIZE}s',
                           args.cmdline))
    if args.header_version >= 4:
        # The signature used to verify boot image v4.
        args.output.write(pack('I', BOOT_IMAGE_V4_SIGNATURE_SIZE))
    pad_file(args.output, BOOT_IMAGE_HEADER_V3_PAGESIZE)


def write_vendor_boot_header(args):
    if filesize(args.dtb) == 0:
        raise ValueError('DTB image must not be empty.')

    if args.header_version > 3:
        vendor_ramdisk_size = args.vendor_ramdisk_total_size
        vendor_boot_header_size = VENDOR_BOOT_IMAGE_HEADER_V4_SIZE
    else:
        vendor_ramdisk_size = filesize(args.vendor_ramdisk)
        vendor_boot_header_size = VENDOR_BOOT_IMAGE_HEADER_V3_SIZE

    args.vendor_boot.write(pack(f'{VENDOR_BOOT_MAGIC_SIZE}s',
                                VENDOR_BOOT_MAGIC.encode()))
    # version of boot image header
    args.vendor_boot.write(pack('I', args.header_version))
    # flash page size
    args.vendor_boot.write(pack('I', args.pagesize))
    # kernel physical load address
    args.vendor_boot.write(pack('I', args.base + args.kernel_offset))
    # ramdisk physical load address
    args.vendor_boot.write(pack('I', args.base + args.ramdisk_offset))
    # ramdisk size in bytes
    args.vendor_boot.write(pack('I', vendor_ramdisk_size))
    args.vendor_boot.write(pack(f'{VENDOR_BOOT_ARGS_SIZE}s',
                                args.vendor_cmdline))
    # kernel tags physical load address
    args.vendor_boot.write(pack('I', args.base + args.tags_offset))
    # asciiz product name
    args.vendor_boot.write(pack(f'{VENDOR_BOOT_NAME_SIZE}s', args.board))

    # header size in bytes
    args.vendor_boot.write(pack('I', vendor_boot_header_size))

    # dtb size in bytes
    args.vendor_boot.write(pack('I', filesize(args.dtb)))
    # dtb physical load address
    args.vendor_boot.write(pack('Q', args.base + args.dtb_offset))

    if args.header_version > 3:
        vendor_ramdisk_table_size = (args.vendor_ramdisk_table_entry_num *
                                     VENDOR_RAMDISK_TABLE_ENTRY_V4_SIZE)
        # vendor ramdisk table size in bytes
        args.vendor_boot.write(pack('I', vendor_ramdisk_table_size))
        # number of vendor ramdisk table entries
        args.vendor_boot.write(pack('I', args.vendor_ramdisk_table_entry_num))
        # vendor ramdisk table entry size in bytes
        args.vendor_boot.write(pack('I', VENDOR_RAMDISK_TABLE_ENTRY_V4_SIZE))
        # bootconfig section size in bytes
        args.vendor_boot.write(pack('I', filesize(args.vendor_bootconfig)))
    pad_file(args.vendor_boot, args.pagesize)


def write_header(args):
    if args.header_version > 4:
        raise ValueError(
            f'Boot header version {args.header_version} not supported')
    if args.header_version in {3, 4}:
        return write_header_v3_and_above(args)

    ramdisk_load_address = ((args.base + args.ramdisk_offset)
                            if filesize(args.ramdisk) > 0 else 0)
    second_load_address = ((args.base + args.second_offset)
                           if filesize(args.second) > 0 else 0)

    args.output.write(pack(f'{BOOT_MAGIC_SIZE}s', BOOT_MAGIC.encode()))
    # kernel size in bytes
    args.output.write(pack('I', filesize(args.kernel)))
    # kernel physical load address
    args.output.write(pack('I', args.base + args.kernel_offset))
    # ramdisk size in bytes
    args.output.write(pack('I', filesize(args.ramdisk)))
    # ramdisk physical load address
    args.output.write(pack('I', ramdisk_load_address))
    # second bootloader size in bytes
    args.output.write(pack('I', filesize(args.second)))
    # second bootloader physical load address
    args.output.write(pack('I', second_load_address))
    # kernel tags physical load address
    args.output.write(pack('I', args.base + args.tags_offset))
    # flash page size
    args.output.write(pack('I', args.pagesize))
    # version of boot image header
    args.output.write(pack('I', args.header_version))
    # os version and patch level
    args.output.write(pack('I', (args.os_version << 11) | args.os_patch_level))
    # asciiz product name
    args.output.write(pack(f'{BOOT_NAME_SIZE}s', args.board))
    args.output.write(pack(f'{BOOT_ARGS_SIZE}s', args.cmdline))

    sha = sha1()
    update_sha(sha, args.kernel)
    update_sha(sha, args.ramdisk)
    update_sha(sha, args.second)

    if args.header_version > 0:
        update_sha(sha, args.recovery_dtbo)
    if args.header_version > 1:
        update_sha(sha, args.dtb)

    img_id = pack('32s', sha.digest())

    args.output.write(img_id)
    args.output.write(pack(f'{BOOT_EXTRA_ARGS_SIZE}s', args.extra_cmdline))

    if args.header_version > 0:
        if args.recovery_dtbo:
            # recovery dtbo size in bytes
            args.output.write(pack('I', filesize(args.recovery_dtbo)))
            # recovert dtbo offset in the boot image
            args.output.write(pack('Q', get_recovery_dtbo_offset(args)))
        else:
            # Set to zero if no recovery dtbo
            args.output.write(pack('I', 0))
            args.output.write(pack('Q', 0))

    # Populate boot image header size for header versions 1 and 2.
    if args.header_version == 1:
        args.output.write(pack('I', BOOT_IMAGE_HEADER_V1_SIZE))
    elif args.header_version == 2:
        args.output.write(pack('I', BOOT_IMAGE_HEADER_V2_SIZE))

    if args.header_version > 1:
        if filesize(args.dtb) == 0:
            raise ValueError('DTB image must not be empty.')

        # dtb size in bytes
        args.output.write(pack('I', filesize(args.dtb)))
        # dtb physical load address
        args.output.write(pack('Q', args.base + args.dtb_offset))

    pad_file(args.output, args.pagesize)
    return img_id


class AsciizBytes:
    """Parses a string and encodes it as an asciiz bytes object.

    >>> AsciizBytes(bufsize=4)('foo')
    b'foo\\x00'
    >>> AsciizBytes(bufsize=4)('foob')
    Traceback (most recent call last):
        ...
    argparse.ArgumentTypeError: Encoded asciiz length exceeded: max 4, got 5
    """

    def __init__(self, bufsize):
        self.bufsize = bufsize

    def __call__(self, arg):
        arg_bytes = arg.encode() + b'\x00'
        if len(arg_bytes) > self.bufsize:
            raise ArgumentTypeError(
                'Encoded asciiz length exceeded: '
                f'max {self.bufsize}, got {len(arg_bytes)}')
        return arg_bytes


class VendorRamdiskTableBuilder:
    """Vendor ramdisk table builder.

    Attributes:
        entries: A list of VendorRamdiskTableEntry namedtuple.
        ramdisk_total_size: Total size in bytes of all ramdisks in the table.
    """

    VendorRamdiskTableEntry = collections.namedtuple(  # pylint: disable=invalid-name
        'VendorRamdiskTableEntry',
        ['ramdisk_path', 'ramdisk_size', 'ramdisk_offset', 'ramdisk_type',
         'ramdisk_name', 'board_id'])

    def __init__(self):
        self.entries = []
        self.ramdisk_total_size = 0
        self.ramdisk_names = set()

    def add_entry(self, ramdisk_path, ramdisk_type, ramdisk_name, board_id):
        # Strip any trailing null for simple comparison.
        stripped_ramdisk_name = ramdisk_name.rstrip(b'\x00')
        if stripped_ramdisk_name in VENDOR_RAMDISK_NAME_BLOCKLIST:
            raise ValueError(
                f'Banned vendor ramdisk name: {stripped_ramdisk_name}')
        if stripped_ramdisk_name in self.ramdisk_names:
            raise ValueError(
                f'Duplicated vendor ramdisk name: {stripped_ramdisk_name}')
        self.ramdisk_names.add(stripped_ramdisk_name)

        if board_id is None:
            board_id = array.array(
                'I', [0] * VENDOR_RAMDISK_TABLE_ENTRY_BOARD_ID_SIZE)
        else:
            board_id = array.array('I', board_id)
        if len(board_id) != VENDOR_RAMDISK_TABLE_ENTRY_BOARD_ID_SIZE:
            raise ValueError('board_id size must be '
                             f'{VENDOR_RAMDISK_TABLE_ENTRY_BOARD_ID_SIZE}')

        with open(ramdisk_path, 'rb') as f:
            ramdisk_size = filesize(f)
        self.entries.append(self.VendorRamdiskTableEntry(
            ramdisk_path, ramdisk_size, self.ramdisk_total_size, ramdisk_type,
            ramdisk_name, board_id))
        self.ramdisk_total_size += ramdisk_size

    def write_ramdisks_padded(self, fout, alignment):
        for entry in self.entries:
            with open(entry.ramdisk_path, 'rb') as f:
                fout.write(f.read())
        pad_file(fout, alignment)

    def write_entries_padded(self, fout, alignment):
        for entry in self.entries:
            fout.write(pack('I', entry.ramdisk_size))
            fout.write(pack('I', entry.ramdisk_offset))
            fout.write(pack('I', entry.ramdisk_type))
            fout.write(pack(f'{VENDOR_RAMDISK_NAME_SIZE}s',
                            entry.ramdisk_name))
            fout.write(entry.board_id)
        pad_file(fout, alignment)


def write_padded_file(f_out, f_in, padding):
    if f_in is None:
        return
    f_out.write(f_in.read())
    pad_file(f_out, padding)


def parse_int(x):
    return int(x, 0)


def parse_os_version(x):
    match = re.search(r'^(\d{1,3})(?:\.(\d{1,3})(?:\.(\d{1,3}))?)?', x)
    if match:
        a = int(match.group(1))
        b = c = 0
        if match.lastindex >= 2:
            b = int(match.group(2))
        if match.lastindex == 3:
            c = int(match.group(3))
        # 7 bits allocated for each field
        assert a < 128
        assert b < 128
        assert c < 128
        return (a << 14) | (b << 7) | c
    return 0


def parse_os_patch_level(x):
    match = re.search(r'^(\d{4})-(\d{2})(?:-(\d{2}))?', x)
    if match:
        y = int(match.group(1)) - 2000
        m = int(match.group(2))
        # 7 bits allocated for the year, 4 bits for the month
        assert 0 <= y < 128
        assert 0 < m <= 12
        return (y << 4) | m
    return 0


def parse_vendor_ramdisk_type(x):
    type_dict = {
        'none': VENDOR_RAMDISK_TYPE_NONE,
        'platform': VENDOR_RAMDISK_TYPE_PLATFORM,
        'recovery': VENDOR_RAMDISK_TYPE_RECOVERY,
        'dlkm': VENDOR_RAMDISK_TYPE_DLKM,
    }
    if x.lower() in type_dict:
        return type_dict[x.lower()]
    return parse_int(x)


def get_vendor_boot_v4_usage():
    return """vendor boot version 4 arguments:
  --ramdisk_type {none,platform,recovery,dlkm}
                        specify the type of the ramdisk
  --ramdisk_name NAME
                        specify the name of the ramdisk
  --board_id{0..15} NUMBER
                        specify the value of the board_id vector, defaults to 0
  --vendor_ramdisk_fragment VENDOR_RAMDISK_FILE
                        path to the vendor ramdisk file

  These options can be specified multiple times, where each vendor ramdisk
  option group ends with a --vendor_ramdisk_fragment option.
  Each option group appends an additional ramdisk to the vendor boot image.
"""


def parse_vendor_ramdisk_args(args, args_list):
    """Parses vendor ramdisk specific arguments.

    Args:
        args: An argparse.Namespace object. Parsed results are stored into this
            object.
        args_list: A list of argument strings to be parsed.

    Returns:
        A list argument strings that are not parsed by this method.
    """
    parser = ArgumentParser(add_help=False)
    parser.add_argument('--ramdisk_type', type=parse_vendor_ramdisk_type,
                        default=VENDOR_RAMDISK_TYPE_NONE)
    parser.add_argument('--ramdisk_name',
                        type=AsciizBytes(bufsize=VENDOR_RAMDISK_NAME_SIZE),
                        required=True)
    for i in range(VENDOR_RAMDISK_TABLE_ENTRY_BOARD_ID_SIZE):
        parser.add_argument(f'--board_id{i}', type=parse_int, default=0)
    parser.add_argument(PARSER_ARGUMENT_VENDOR_RAMDISK_FRAGMENT, required=True)

    unknown_args = []

    vendor_ramdisk_table_builder = VendorRamdiskTableBuilder()
    if args.vendor_ramdisk is not None:
        vendor_ramdisk_table_builder.add_entry(
            args.vendor_ramdisk.name, VENDOR_RAMDISK_TYPE_PLATFORM, b'', None)

    while PARSER_ARGUMENT_VENDOR_RAMDISK_FRAGMENT in args_list:
        idx = args_list.index(PARSER_ARGUMENT_VENDOR_RAMDISK_FRAGMENT) + 2
        vendor_ramdisk_args = args_list[:idx]
        args_list = args_list[idx:]

        ramdisk_args, extra_args = parser.parse_known_args(vendor_ramdisk_args)
        ramdisk_args_dict = vars(ramdisk_args)
        unknown_args.extend(extra_args)

        ramdisk_path = ramdisk_args.vendor_ramdisk_fragment
        ramdisk_type = ramdisk_args.ramdisk_type
        ramdisk_name = ramdisk_args.ramdisk_name
        board_id = [ramdisk_args_dict[f'board_id{i}']
                    for i in range(VENDOR_RAMDISK_TABLE_ENTRY_BOARD_ID_SIZE)]
        vendor_ramdisk_table_builder.add_entry(ramdisk_path, ramdisk_type,
                                               ramdisk_name, board_id)

    if len(args_list) > 0:
        unknown_args.extend(args_list)

    args.vendor_ramdisk_total_size = (vendor_ramdisk_table_builder
                                      .ramdisk_total_size)
    args.vendor_ramdisk_table_entry_num = len(vendor_ramdisk_table_builder
                                              .entries)
    args.vendor_ramdisk_table_builder = vendor_ramdisk_table_builder
    return unknown_args


def parse_cmdline():
    version_parser = ArgumentParser(add_help=False)
    version_parser.add_argument('--header_version', type=parse_int, default=0)
    if version_parser.parse_known_args()[0].header_version < 3:
        # For boot header v0 to v2, the kernel commandline field is split into
        # two fields, cmdline and extra_cmdline. Both fields are asciiz strings,
        # so we minus one here to ensure the encoded string plus the
        # null-terminator can fit in the buffer size.
        cmdline_size = BOOT_ARGS_SIZE + BOOT_EXTRA_ARGS_SIZE - 1
    else:
        cmdline_size = BOOT_ARGS_SIZE + BOOT_EXTRA_ARGS_SIZE

    parser = ArgumentParser(formatter_class=RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
                            epilog=get_vendor_boot_v4_usage())
    parser.add_argument('--kernel', type=FileType('rb'),
                        help='path to the kernel')
    parser.add_argument('--ramdisk', type=FileType('rb'),
                        help='path to the ramdisk')
    parser.add_argument('--second', type=FileType('rb'),
                        help='path to the second bootloader')
    parser.add_argument('--dtb', type=FileType('rb'), help='path to the dtb')
    dtbo_group = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
    dtbo_group.add_argument('--recovery_dtbo', type=FileType('rb'),
                            help='path to the recovery DTBO')
    dtbo_group.add_argument('--recovery_acpio', type=FileType('rb'),
                            metavar='RECOVERY_ACPIO', dest='recovery_dtbo',
                            help='path to the recovery ACPIO')
    parser.add_argument('--cmdline', type=AsciizBytes(bufsize=cmdline_size),
                        default='', help='kernel command line arguments')
    parser.add_argument('--vendor_cmdline',
                        type=AsciizBytes(bufsize=VENDOR_BOOT_ARGS_SIZE),
                        default='',
                        help='vendor boot kernel command line arguments')
    parser.add_argument('--base', type=parse_int, default=0x10000000,
                        help='base address')
    parser.add_argument('--kernel_offset', type=parse_int, default=0x00008000,
                        help='kernel offset')
    parser.add_argument('--ramdisk_offset', type=parse_int, default=0x01000000,
                        help='ramdisk offset')
    parser.add_argument('--second_offset', type=parse_int, default=0x00f00000,
                        help='second bootloader offset')
    parser.add_argument('--dtb_offset', type=parse_int, default=0x01f00000,
                        help='dtb offset')

    parser.add_argument('--os_version', type=parse_os_version, default=0,
                        help='operating system version')
    parser.add_argument('--os_patch_level', type=parse_os_patch_level,
                        default=0, help='operating system patch level')
    parser.add_argument('--tags_offset', type=parse_int, default=0x00000100,
                        help='tags offset')
    parser.add_argument('--board', type=AsciizBytes(bufsize=BOOT_NAME_SIZE),
                        default='', help='board name')
    parser.add_argument('--pagesize', type=parse_int,
                        choices=[2**i for i in range(11, 15)], default=2048,
                        help='page size')
    parser.add_argument('--id', action='store_true',
                        help='print the image ID on standard output')
    parser.add_argument('--header_version', type=parse_int, default=0,
                        help='boot image header version')
    parser.add_argument('-o', '--output', type=FileType('wb'),
                        help='output file name')
    parser.add_argument('--gki_signing_algorithm',
                        help='GKI signing algorithm to use')
    parser.add_argument('--gki_signing_key',
                        help='path to RSA private key file')
    parser.add_argument('--gki_signing_signature_args',
                        help='other hash arguments passed to avbtool')
    parser.add_argument('--gki_signing_avbtool_path',
                        help='path to avbtool for boot signature generation')
    parser.add_argument('--vendor_boot', type=FileType('wb'),
                        help='vendor boot output file name')
    parser.add_argument('--vendor_ramdisk', type=FileType('rb'),
                        help='path to the vendor ramdisk')
    parser.add_argument('--vendor_bootconfig', type=FileType('rb'),
                        help='path to the vendor bootconfig file')

    args, extra_args = parser.parse_known_args()
    if args.vendor_boot is not None and args.header_version > 3:
        extra_args = parse_vendor_ramdisk_args(args, extra_args)
    if len(extra_args) > 0:
        raise ValueError(f'Unrecognized arguments: {extra_args}')

    if args.header_version < 3:
        args.extra_cmdline = args.cmdline[BOOT_ARGS_SIZE-1:]
        args.cmdline = args.cmdline[:BOOT_ARGS_SIZE-1] + b'\x00'
        assert len(args.cmdline) <= BOOT_ARGS_SIZE
        assert len(args.extra_cmdline) <= BOOT_EXTRA_ARGS_SIZE

    return args


def add_boot_image_signature(args, pagesize):
    """Adds the boot image signature.

    Note that the signature will only be verified in VTS to ensure a
    generic boot.img is used. It will not be used by the device
    bootloader at boot time. The bootloader should only verify
    the boot vbmeta at the end of the boot partition (or in the top-level
    vbmeta partition) via the Android Verified Boot process, when the
    device boots.
    """
    args.output.flush()  # Flush the buffer for signature calculation.

    # Appends zeros if the signing key is not specified.
    if not args.gki_signing_key or not args.gki_signing_algorithm:
        zeros = b'\x00' * BOOT_IMAGE_V4_SIGNATURE_SIZE
        args.output.write(zeros)
        pad_file(args.output, pagesize)
        return

    avbtool = 'avbtool'  # Used from otatools.zip or Android build env.

    # We need to specify the path of avbtool in build/core/Makefile.
    # Because avbtool is not guaranteed to be in $PATH there.
    if args.gki_signing_avbtool_path:
        avbtool = args.gki_signing_avbtool_path

    # Need to specify a value of --partition_size for avbtool to work.
    # We use 64 MB below, but avbtool will not resize the boot image to
    # this size because --do_not_append_vbmeta_image is also specified.
    avbtool_cmd = [
        avbtool, 'add_hash_footer',
        '--partition_name', 'boot',
        '--partition_size', str(64 * 1024 * 1024),
        '--image', args.output.name,
        '--algorithm', args.gki_signing_algorithm,
        '--key', args.gki_signing_key,
        '--salt', 'd00df00d']  # TODO: use a hash of kernel/ramdisk as the salt.

    # Additional arguments passed to avbtool.
    if args.gki_signing_signature_args:
        avbtool_cmd += args.gki_signing_signature_args.split()

    # Outputs the signed vbmeta to a separate file, then append to boot.img
    # as the boot signature.
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temp_out_dir:
        boot_signature_output = os.path.join(temp_out_dir, 'boot_signature')
        avbtool_cmd += ['--do_not_append_vbmeta_image',
                        '--output_vbmeta_image', boot_signature_output]
        subprocess.check_call(avbtool_cmd)
        with open(boot_signature_output, 'rb') as boot_signature:
            if filesize(boot_signature) > BOOT_IMAGE_V4_SIGNATURE_SIZE:
                raise ValueError(
                    f'boot sigature size is > {BOOT_IMAGE_V4_SIGNATURE_SIZE}')
            write_padded_file(args.output, boot_signature, pagesize)


def write_data(args, pagesize):
    write_padded_file(args.output, args.kernel, pagesize)
    write_padded_file(args.output, args.ramdisk, pagesize)
    write_padded_file(args.output, args.second, pagesize)

    if args.header_version > 0 and args.header_version < 3:
        write_padded_file(args.output, args.recovery_dtbo, pagesize)
    if args.header_version == 2:
        write_padded_file(args.output, args.dtb, pagesize)
    if args.header_version >= 4:
        add_boot_image_signature(args, pagesize)


def write_vendor_boot_data(args):
    if args.header_version > 3:
        builder = args.vendor_ramdisk_table_builder
        builder.write_ramdisks_padded(args.vendor_boot, args.pagesize)
        write_padded_file(args.vendor_boot, args.dtb, args.pagesize)
        builder.write_entries_padded(args.vendor_boot, args.pagesize)
        write_padded_file(args.vendor_boot, args.vendor_bootconfig,
            args.pagesize)
    else:
        write_padded_file(args.vendor_boot, args.vendor_ramdisk, args.pagesize)
        write_padded_file(args.vendor_boot, args.dtb, args.pagesize)


def main():
    args = parse_cmdline()
    if args.vendor_boot is not None:
        if args.header_version not in {3, 4}:
            raise ValueError(
                '--vendor_boot not compatible with given header version')
        if args.header_version == 3 and args.vendor_ramdisk is None:
            raise ValueError('--vendor_ramdisk missing or invalid')
        write_vendor_boot_header(args)
        write_vendor_boot_data(args)
    if args.output is not None:
        if args.second is not None and args.header_version > 2:
            raise ValueError(
                '--second not compatible with given header version')
        img_id = write_header(args)
        if args.header_version > 2:
            write_data(args, BOOT_IMAGE_HEADER_V3_PAGESIZE)
        else:
            write_data(args, args.pagesize)
        if args.id and img_id is not None:
            print('0x' + ''.join(f'{octet:02x}' for octet in img_id))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```
