`tools/guard_test.c`:

```c
/*
 * The speakers' guard (bsd/dev/redwood_guard.c) on this machine, with signals made up for it:
 * what comes out, second by second, for a sustained full-scale tone at the amplifiers' levels that
 * are tried on the phone, for music-like noise, and for the tone once it stops (the cooling).
 *
 *   cc -O2 -DKERNEL -I<a directory with sys/redwood_audio.h and a sys/ioccom.h> tools/guard_test.c \
 *      xnu-src/xnu-8796.121.2/bsd/dev/redwood_guard.c -lm -o guard_test && ./guard_test
 * (tools/guard-test.sh does that.)
 */
#include <math.h>
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <sys/redwood_audio.h>

#define RATE    48000
#define BLOCK   960

static double phase, pink_scale = 1;
static uint64_t noise = 88172645463325252ull;

static double
random_uniform(void)
{
	noise ^= noise << 13;
	noise ^= noise >> 7;
	noise ^= noise << 17;
	return (double)(noise >> 11) / (double)(1ull << 53) * 2 - 1;
}

/* one block: kind 0 silence, 1 a sine at `level' (of full scale, peak), 2 noise filtered to fall 3 dB an octave, at RMS `level' */
static void
make(int16_t *frames, int kind, double level, double hz)
{
	static double b[7];

	for (int f = 0; f < BLOCK; f++) {
		double v = 0;

		if (kind == 1) {
			v = level * sin(phase);
			phase += 2 * M_PI * hz / RATE;
		} else if (kind == 2) {
			/* Paul Kellet's pink noise, scaled to about the RMS asked for */
			double w = random_uniform();

			b[0] = 0.99886 * b[0] + w * 0.0555179;
			b[1] = 0.99332 * b[1] + w * 0.0750759;
			b[2] = 0.96900 * b[2] + w * 0.1538520;
			b[3] = 0.86650 * b[3] + w * 0.3104856;
			b[4] = 0.55000 * b[4] + w * 0.5329522;
			b[5] = -0.7616 * b[5] - w * 0.0168980;
			v = (b[0] + b[1] + b[2] + b[3] + b[4] + b[5] + b[6] + w * 0.5362) * pink_scale * level;
			b[6] = w * 0.115926;
		}
		v *= 32767;
		v = v > 32767 ? 32767 : v < -32768 ? -32768 : v;
		frames[2 * f] = frames[2 * f + 1] = (int16_t)lrint(v);
	}
}

static double
decibels(double ratio)
{
	return ratio > 0 ? 10 * log10(ratio) : -99;
}

/* `seconds' of one kind of signal; a line every `every' seconds: the output's RMS and peak at the speaker, and the guard */
static void
run(const char *what, uint32_t attenuation, int kind, double level, double hz, int seconds, int every)
{
	int16_t frames[2 * BLOCK];
	bool silent = attenuation == REDWOOD_GUARD_SILENT;
	double at_speaker = silent ? 0 : pow(10, -(double)attenuation / 80.0);   /* power */

	if (silent) {
		printf("-- %s, the amplifiers off\n", what);
	} else {
		printf("-- %s, the amplifiers %.1f dB under Android's level\n", what, attenuation / 8.0);
	}
	redwood_guard_attenuation(attenuation);
	for (int s = 0; s < seconds; s++) {
		double sum = 0, peak = 0, in_sum = 0;
		struct redwood_guard_report r;

		for (int b = 0; b < RATE / BLOCK; b++) {
			make(frames, kind, level, hz);
			for (int i = 0; i < 2 * BLOCK; i++) {
				in_sum += (double)frames[i] * frames[i];
			}
			redwood_guard_process(frames, BLOCK);
			for (int i = 0; i < 2 * BLOCK; i++) {
				double v = frames[i] / 32768.0;

				sum += v * v;
				peak = fabs(v) > peak ? fabs(v) : peak;
			}
		}
		redwood_guard_take_report(&r);
		if ((s + 1) % every == 0 || s == 0) {
			/* at the speaker: relative to a full-scale square wave at Android's level */
			printf("%4d s: in %6.1f dB, out %6.1f dB (peak %6.1f dB) at the speaker; guard %5.1f dB (%u rms, %u fast, %u slow "
			    "blocks), peaks limited in %u frames; averages %.1f %.1f %.1f dB\n", s + 1,
			    decibels(in_sum / (2.0 * RATE) / (32768.0 * 32768.0) * at_speaker), decibels(sum / (2.0 * RATE) * at_speaker),
			    silent ? -99 : 20 * log10(peak > 0 ? peak : 1e-9) - attenuation / 8.0, redwood_guard_decibels(r.gain * r.gain >> 30) / 10.0,
			    r.rms_blocks, r.fast_blocks, r.slow_blocks, r.limited_frames, redwood_guard_decibels(r.rms) / 10.0,
			    redwood_guard_decibels(r.fast) / 10.0, redwood_guard_decibels(r.slow) / 10.0);
		}
	}
}

int
main(void)
{
	int16_t frames[2 * BLOCK];
	double sum = 0;

	/* the noise's own RMS, so that it can be made as loud as asked (at full scale, then scaled down in make()) */
	pink_scale = 1.0 / 32767;
	for (int b = 0; b < 500; b++) {
		make(frames, 2, 1.0, 0);
		for (int i = 0; i < 2 * BLOCK; i += 2) {
			sum += (double)frames[i] * frames[i];
		}
	}
	pink_scale = 1.0 / sqrt(sum / (500.0 * BLOCK));
	redwood_guard_configure(true, 0);
	run("a full-scale 1 kHz sine", 160, 1, 1.0, 1000, 10, 5);
	run("a full-scale 1 kHz sine", 80, 1, 1.0, 1000, 10, 5);
	run("a full-scale 1 kHz sine", 0, 1, 1.0, 1000, 120, 10);
	run("silence, the speakers cooling", REDWOOD_GUARD_SILENT, 0, 0, 0, 120, 20);
	run("the same sine again", 0, 1, 1.0, 1000, 5, 1);
	run("silence", REDWOOD_GUARD_SILENT, 0, 0, 0, 300, 300);
	run("a 100 Hz sine at full scale (the high-pass filter)", 0, 1, 1.0, 100, 4, 2);
	run("silence", REDWOOD_GUARD_SILENT, 0, 0, 0, 300, 300);
	run("pink noise at -15 dB RMS (loud music)", 0, 2, pow(10, -15 / 20.0), 0, 60, 10);
	run("pink noise at -9 dB RMS (music mastered as loud as it goes)", 0, 2, pow(10, -9 / 20.0), 0, 120, 20);
	run("silence", REDWOOD_GUARD_SILENT, 0, 0, 0, 300, 300);
	/* iOS at its top: a tone 12.6 dB under full scale, then 12 dB of gain before the guard */
	redwood_guard_configure(true, 96);
	run("iOS's top (a 440 Hz sine at -12.6 dB) with 12 dB of gain", 0, 1, pow(10, -12.6 / 20), 440, 90, 10);
	run("silence", REDWOOD_GUARD_SILENT, 0, 0, 0, 600, 600);
	run("pink noise at -24 dB RMS (loud music as iOS leaves it) with 12 dB of gain", 0, 2, pow(10, -24 / 20.0), 0, 60, 20);
	run("silence", REDWOOD_GUARD_SILENT, 0, 0, 0, 600, 600);
	run("the same with the amplifiers 90 dB under (sound_below=720)", 720, 2, pow(10, -24 / 20.0), 0, 10, 5);
	return 0;
}
```

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# In a workspace made by new-workspace.sh: print, as a patch, what was changed in the kernel tree
# since the workspace was made (new files included). Apply it elsewhere with "git apply".
set -e
cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/../xnu-src/xnu-8796.121.2"
git rev-parse -q --verify refs/redwood/baseline >/dev/null || { echo "kernel-delta.sh: not a workspace (no baseline)" >&2; exit 1; }
export GIT_INDEX_FILE=$PWD/.git/index.delta
rm -f "$GIT_INDEX_FILE"
git read-tree refs/redwood/baseline
git add -A . 2>/dev/null
git diff --cached --binary refs/redwood/baseline
rm -f "$GIT_INDEX_FILE"
```

`tools/latency.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
latency.py RUN.log [MORE.log ...] [RECORDING.raw]: how far behind the finger the phone's screen is.
(More logs: the live ones of the same run, XL_FOLLOW=N XL_FOLLOW_KEEP=1, which keep what the run's log loses.)

A run with boot-arg touch_lat=1 writes a line at every stage a touch passes on its way to the panel,
all in microseconds of mach_absolute_time (the kernel's clock, which user space reads too):

  tl: p TYPE FINGER X Y at US              the kernel posts a sample (bsd/dev/redwood_input.c)
  tl: c before US seen US read US          the touch driver finds the interrupt line low and reads the
                                           report (bsd/dev/redwood_goodix.c; only for a real finger)
  tl: i TYPE posted US read US sent US     the window server reads it and hands it to the event system
                                           (userland/src/inject.c)
  tl: g FRAME began US ended US DRAWS      the window server draws a frame (userland/src/eagl.c)
  tl: s ID at US                           it hands the frame over (SwapEnd)
  tl: v ID ready US shown US done US       the display driver: the GPU done with it, its beat come, its
                                           pixels in the panel's memory (MiniIOMobileFramebuffer.cpp)

With rec_secs=... rec_ring=1 the frames themselves are in the screen recording, each with the time it
was put in the panel's memory. A "zigzag" of rwtouch (the finger up and down over a scrolling list
without letting go) then gives the latency from end to end: the list follows the finger, and the
time by which the list's movement lags the finger's is found by fitting the one to the other (a
constant offset -- the scroll view's slop before it starts to follow -- does not matter; the turns do).
The stages are averaged over the same frames and samples, and what is left between the event
system and the frame -- the application's handling and the wait for the next frame of
CoreAnimation's clock -- is the difference.
"""
import re
import struct
import sys

import numpy as np


def micros_lines(paths):
    """The tl: lines of the logs, once each (the kernel's own also come back in its log at the end)."""
    seen, lines = set(), []
    if isinstance(paths, str):
        paths = [paths]
    for path in paths:
      with open(path, 'rb') as f:
        for raw in f:
            text = raw.decode('utf-8', 'replace')
            at = text.find('tl: ')
            if at < 0:
                continue
            line = text[at:].strip()
            if line not in seen:
                seen.add(line)
                lines.append(line)
    return lines


def parse(lines):
    samples, reads, frames, swaps, shows, chip = [], [], [], {}, {}, []
    for line in lines:
        w = line.split()
        try:
            if w[1] == 'p' and len(w) >= 8:
                samples.append((int(w[7]), int(w[2]), int(w[3]), int(w[4]), int(w[5])))
            elif w[1] == 'i' and len(w) >= 9:
                reads.append((int(w[4]), int(w[6]), int(w[8]), int(w[2])))
            elif w[1] == 'g' and len(w) >= 8:
                frames.append((int(w[4]), int(w[6]), int(w[7])))
            elif w[1] == 's' and len(w) >= 5:
                swaps[int(w[2])] = int(w[4])
            elif w[1] == 'v' and len(w) >= 9:
                shows[int(w[2])] = (int(w[4]), int(w[6]), int(w[8]))
            elif w[1] == 'c' and len(w) >= 8:
                chip.append((int(w[3]), int(w[5]), int(w[7])))
        except ValueError:
            pass
    samples.sort()
    reads.sort()
    frames.sort(key=lambda f: f[1])
    return samples, reads, frames, swaps, shows, chip


def recording(path):
    data = open(path, 'rb').read()
    magic, width, height, count, oldest = struct.unpack_from('<8sIIII', data, 0)
    if magic != b'RWREC003':
        sys.exit('latency.py: not a recording of the RWREC003 kind')
    began = struct.unpack_from('<Q', data, 24)[0]
    size = 8 + width * height * 3
    out = []
    for k in range(count):
        i = (oldest + k) % count
        at = 32 + i * size
        t = struct.unpack_from('<Q', data, at)[0]
        pixels = np.frombuffer(data, np.uint8, width * height * 3, at + 8).reshape(height, width, 3)
        out.append(((began + t) // 1000, pixels))
    out.sort(key=lambda f: f[0])
    return out, width, height


def zigzags(samples):
    """Touches with many moves, finger 0: (down time, up time, [(t, y)])."""
    out, current = [], None
    for t, kind, finger, x, y in samples:
        if finger != 0:
            continue
        if kind == 1:
            current = [(t, y)]
        elif kind == 2 and current is not None:
            current.append((t, y))
        elif kind == 3 and current is not None:
            current.append((t, y))
            ys = [p[1] for p in current]
            turns = sum(1 for i in range(1, len(ys) - 1) if (ys[i] - ys[i - 1]) * (ys[i + 1] - ys[i]) < 0)
            if len(current) > 30 and turns >= 3:
                out.append((current[0][0], t, current))
            current = None
    return out


def shift(a, b, most):
    """How far b's content has moved down from a's, in rows: the shift with the least difference."""
    h = a.shape[0]
    best, best_cost = 0, None
    for s in range(-most, most + 1):
        if s >= 0:
            pa, pb = a[0:h - s], b[s:h]
        else:
            pa, pb = a[-s:h], b[0:h + s]
        cost = np.mean(np.abs(pa - pb))
        if best_cost is None or cost < best_cost:
            best, best_cost = s, cost
    return best


def content_offsets(frames, t0, t1, height):
    """The list's position in each frame between t0 and t1, in rows of the recording, relative to the first."""
    chosen = [(t, p) for t, p in frames if t0 <= t <= t1]
    out = []
    if not chosen:
        return out
    top, bottom = int(height * 0.15), int(height * 0.90)
    previous, offset = None, 0
    for t, pixels in chosen:
        grey = pixels[top:bottom, :, :].astype(np.float32).mean(axis=2)
        grey = grey[:, grey.shape[1] // 10: grey.shape[1] * 9 // 10]
        if previous is not None:
            offset += shift(previous, grey, 48)
        out.append((t, offset))
        previous = grey
    return out


def fit_lag(offsets, touch, height):
    """The lag (us) at which the list's position best follows the finger's: least squares with an offset and a gain."""
    tt = np.array([p[0] for p in touch], dtype=np.float64)
    ty = np.array([p[1] for p in touch], dtype=np.float64) / 65535.0 * height
    ft = np.array([o[0] for o in offsets], dtype=np.float64)
    fy = np.array([o[1] for o in offsets], dtype=np.float64)
    best = None
    for lag in range(0, 250001, 500):
        at = ft - lag
        keep = (at >= tt[0]) & (at <= tt[-1])
        if keep.sum() < 10:
            continue
        x = np.interp(at[keep], tt, ty)
        y = fy[keep]
        matrix = np.vstack([x, np.ones_like(x)]).T
        coefficients, residual, _, _ = np.linalg.lstsq(matrix, y, rcond=None)
        error = float(np.mean((matrix @ coefficients - y) ** 2))
        if best is None or error < best[1]:
            best = (lag, error, coefficients[0], int(keep.sum()))
    return best


def mean(values):
    return sum(values) / len(values) if values else float('nan')


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        sys.exit(__doc__)
    logs = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if not a.endswith('.raw')]
    raws = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if a.endswith('.raw')]
    samples, reads, frames, swaps, shows, chip = parse(micros_lines(logs))
    print(f'latency.py: {len(samples)} samples, {len(reads)} read by the window server, {len(frames)} frames drawn, '
          f'{len(swaps)} handed over, {len(shows)} shown; {len(chip)} reports read from the touch chip')
    if chip:
        found = [seen - before for before, seen, read in chip if before]
        took = [read - seen for before, seen, read in chip]
        print(f'  touch chip: looked at every {mean(found) / 1000:.2f} ms (a report waits half of that on average); '
              f'reading a report takes {mean(took) / 1000:.2f} ms')
    pictures, width, height = recording(raws[0]) if raws else ([], 0, 0)
    totals = []
    for number, (down, up, touch) in enumerate(zigzags(samples)):
        moves = [p for p in touch[1:-1]]
        print(f'zigzag {number + 1}: {len(touch)} samples over {(up - down) / 1000:.0f} ms')
        result = None
        if pictures:
            offsets = content_offsets(pictures, down, up + 400000, height)
            result = fit_lag(offsets, moves, height) if len(offsets) > 10 else None
        if result is None:
            print('  (no frames of it in the recording)')
            continue
        lag, error, gain, used = result
        print(f'  END TO END: the list follows the finger {lag / 1000:.1f} ms behind, until its pixels are in the panel\'s '
              f'memory (gain {gain:.2f}, misfit {error ** 0.5:.1f} rows, {used} frames)')
        totals.append(lag)
        # the stages, over the samples and frames of this zigzag
        within = [r for r in reads if down <= r[0] <= up]
        inject = [r[1] - r[0] for r in within]
        send = [r[2] - r[1] for r in within]
        rows = []
        for sid in sorted(shows):
            if sid not in swaps or not (down <= shows[sid][2] <= up + 400000):
                continue
            swap = swaps[sid]
            drawn = [f for f in frames if f[1] <= swap]
            if not drawn:
                continue
            began, ended, draws = drawn[-1]
            ready, shown, done = shows[sid]
            rows.append((ended - began, swap - ended, ready - swap, shown - ready, done - shown))
        if rows:
            render, handover, gpu, beat, copy = (mean([r[k] for r in rows]) for k in range(5))
            rest = lag - mean(inject) - mean(send) - render - handover - gpu - beat - copy
            print(f'  kernel to window server (the touch device read):   {mean(inject) / 1000:6.2f} ms')
            print(f'  window server to event system:                      {mean(send) / 1000:6.2f} ms')
            print(f'  the application, and the wait for the next frame:   {rest / 1000:6.2f} ms  (what is left)')
            print(f'  the window server drawing the frame (GPU commands):  {render / 1000:6.2f} ms')
            print(f'  frame drawn to frame handed over (SwapEnd):         {handover / 1000:6.2f} ms')
            print(f'  waiting for the GPU to finish it:                   {gpu / 1000:6.2f} ms')
            print(f'  waiting for the display driver\'s beat:              {beat / 1000:6.2f} ms')
            print(f'  copying (scaling) it into the panel\'s memory:       {copy / 1000:6.2f} ms')
            print(f'  ({len(rows)} frames, {len(within)} samples; then the panel\'s next scan of those rows, '
                  f'0 to 8.3 ms at 120 Hz)')
    if totals:
        print(f'all zigzags: {mean(totals) / 1000:.1f} ms behind the finger on average')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

```

`tools/mk-ath11k.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# Build the driver of the phone's Wi-Fi radio for our kernel: ath11k, Qualcomm's driver for the
# WCN6750 (and its kin) as it is in Linux, unmodified, on a layer that gives it the kernel
# interfaces it expects. Three things meet here, and only the third is in the repository:
#
#   Linux's ath11k        drivers/net/wireless/ath/ath11k of a pinned release of Linux
#                         (BSD-3-Clause-Clear; the one header of ath/ it includes is ISC);
#   FreeBSD's LinuxKPI    the headers with which FreeBSD compiles Linux drivers, with the kernel
#                         headers those are written against (BSD-2-Clause, of a pinned release
#                         of FreeBSD); patched with wifi/lx/patches/*.patch. Its source files
#                         are not used: what they do is done in wifi/lx/src;
#   wifi/lx               ours: the headers LinuxKPI lacks (device tree, platform devices), the
#                         headers of FreeBSD that cannot serve under XNU as they are, and the
#                         functions underneath (locks, sleeping, work, memory, firmware, the
#                         radio's bus) written on the handful of calls that the kernel's
#                         bsd/dev/redwood_lx.c offers (bsd/sys/redwood_lx.h of the kernel tree).
#
# Not all of the driver is built yet: DRIVER below lists the files that are. What they call in
# the files that are not becomes a function that says its name in the log and answers 0
# (out/stubs.txt lists them), unless wifi/lx/src has one that does more.
#
# Everything is compiled as FreeBSD kernel code for an Apple arm64 kernel and tied into one
# object that shows nothing but its entry points; the kernel links it when it is there
# (xnu-build.sh).
#
#   VERSION   of Linux. 7.0.14: LinuxKPI's 802.11 headers follow the mac80211 of Linux 7.0, and
#             the driver has to be the one they were written for. For the WCN6750 the driver
#             asks the same of firmware and platform as in the 6.6 series.
#   FREEBSD   15.1-RELEASE, the first release whose LinuxKPI is at Linux 7.0.
#
# What comes out, in xnu-deps/build/ath11k:
#   src/ath11k/        the driver's files, untouched       freebsd/sys/   FreeBSD's, patched
#   out/ath11k.o       the object for the kernel           out/stubs.txt  what is not there yet
# Needs on this machine: curl, tar, xz, sha256sum, patch, awk, clang, and the kernel's linker
# (xnu-deps/host/bin/ld64, see xnu-deps/setup.sh). The two archives are 150 and 253 MB and are kept.
#
# usage: tools/mk-ath11k.sh [fetch]        "fetch" stops when the driver's sources are there
set -e
VERSION=7.0.14
SHA256=de9999b784d2293f00d39c62d8f92a08ab8a54bc4e80ffd250a0c09cb07a0f98
ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/.." && pwd)
B=$ROOT/xnu-deps/build/ath11k
ATH=drivers/net/wireless/ath
mkdir -p "$B"
cd "$B"

if [ "$(cat src/.release 2>/dev/null)" != "$VERSION $SHA256" ]; then
	[ -f linux-$VERSION.tar.xz ] || curl -sL --fail -o linux-$VERSION.tar.xz \
		https://cdn.kernel.org/pub/linux/kernel/v${VERSION%%.*}.x/linux-$VERSION.tar.xz
	echo "$SHA256  linux-$VERSION.tar.xz" | sha256sum -c --quiet
	rm -rf src unpacked
	mkdir unpacked
	tar xJf linux-$VERSION.tar.xz -C unpacked --strip-components=1 linux-$VERSION/$ATH/ath11k \
		linux-$VERSION/$ATH/spectral_common.h
	# every file must say itself that it may be used so: the licence is checked, not assumed
	for f in unpacked/$ATH/ath11k/*.[ch] unpacked/$ATH/spectral_common.h; do
		case "$(head -6 "$f")" in
		*"SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause-Clear"*) ;;
		*"Permission to use, copy, modify, and/or distribute this software"*) ;;      # (ISC, spelt out)
		*) echo "mk-ath11k.sh: $f does not carry the licence expected" >&2; exit 1 ;;
		esac
	done
	mkdir src
	mv unpacked/$ATH/ath11k src/ath11k
	mv unpacked/$ATH/spectral_common.h src/
	rm -rf unpacked
	echo "$VERSION $SHA256" > src/.release
fi
[ "$1" = fetch ] && { echo "mk-ath11k.sh: ath11k of Linux $VERSION: $B/src/ath11k"; exit 0; }
W=$ROOT/wifi/lx

# --- FreeBSD's LinuxKPI and the kernel headers under it, with our patches on top. When the patches
# change, the tree is taken from the archive again (as tools/mk-mesa.sh does with Mesa's).
FREEBSD=15.1
FREEBSD_SHA256=cf5762da53fd52e1eaf0f9ceee9bf58cbe314c821031d0d9ffa76823185a89e1
FSYS="compat/linuxkpi sys arm64/include net net80211 netinet netinet6 vm kern tools libkern ddb
	security fs/pseudofs crypto opencrypto geom bsm isa cam rpc xdr x86/include ofed/include
	dev/pci dev/ofw dev/fdt dev/acpica dev/usb dev/iicbus dev/backlight
	contrib/ck/include contrib/dev/acpica/include contrib/libnv"
PATCHES=$(cat "$W"/patches/*.patch 2>/dev/null | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1)
if [ "$(cat freebsd/.release 2>/dev/null)" != "$FREEBSD $FREEBSD_SHA256 $PATCHES" ]; then
	[ -f freebsd-$FREEBSD-src.txz ] || curl -sL --fail -o freebsd-$FREEBSD-src.txz \
		https://download.freebsd.org/releases/amd64/$FREEBSD-RELEASE/src.txz
	echo "$FREEBSD_SHA256  freebsd-$FREEBSD-src.txz" | sha256sum -c --quiet
	rm -rf freebsd gen obj
	mkdir freebsd
	tar xJf freebsd-$FREEBSD-src.txz -C freebsd --strip-components=2 usr/src/COPYRIGHT \
		$(for d in $FSYS; do echo usr/src/sys/$d; done)
	for p in "$W"/patches/*.patch; do
		[ -f "$p" ] && patch -s --no-backup-if-mismatch -d freebsd -p1 < "$p"
	done
	echo "$FREEBSD $FREEBSD_SHA256 $PATCHES" > freebsd/.release
fi
S=$B/freebsd/sys

# --- what FreeBSD's build would have generated: the interfaces of its device framework, and the
# option headers, which here say only that there is an Internet
if [ ! -d gen ]; then
	mkdir gen
	(
		cd gen
		ln -s $S/arm64/include machine
		for m in kern/device_if.m kern/bus_if.m dev/pci/pci_if.m dev/pci/pci_iov_if.m dev/pci/pcib_if.m \
			dev/iicbus/iicbus_if.m dev/iicbus/iicbb_if.m dev/backlight/backlight_if.m dev/usb/usb_if.m \
			dev/ofw/ofw_bus_if.m; do
			awk -f $S/tools/makeobjops.awk $S/$m -h
		done
		for o in h p q; do awk -f $S/tools/vnode_if.awk $S/kern/vnode_if.src -$o; done
		for o in $(grep -rhoE "opt_[a-z0-9_]+\.h" $S | sort -u) lkpi_iic_if.h; do : > $o; done
		printf '#define INET 1\n#define INET6 1\n' > opt_inet.h
		printf '#define INET6 1\n' > opt_inet6.h
		printf '#define SMP 1\n' > opt_global.h
	)
fi

# --- compile: the driver's files that are built so far, and ours
DRIVER="core hal qmi ce hw fw htc wmi mac reg peer dp dp_rx dp_tx hal_rx hal_tx dbring p2p"
CC="clang -target arm64-apple-ios16.5"
LD=$ROOT/xnu-deps/host/bin/ld64
CFLAGS="-mkernel -mgeneral-regs-only -fno-builtin -fno-common -ffreestanding -fno-strict-aliasing
	-funsigned-char -nostdinc -std=gnu17 -O2 -g -w
	-D__FreeBSD__=15 -D_KERNEL -DKLD_MODULE -DHAVE_KERNEL_OPTION_HEADERS -include opt_global.h
	-I$W/include -Igen -I$S -I$S/contrib/ck/include
	-I$S/compat/linuxkpi/common/include -I$S/compat/linuxkpi/dummy/include
	-include $S/compat/linuxkpi/common/include/linux/kconfig.h -DLINUXKPI_VERSION=70000"
DFLAGS="-Isrc/ath11k -Isrc -include $W/include/lx_prelude.h -DCONFIG_ATH11K_AHB -DCONFIG_ATH11K_DEBUG
	-DKBUILD_MODNAME=\"ath11k\""
# two headers are the kernel's: what it offers this object (wifi/lx/include/lx_os.h), and its QMI
# helpers (wifi/lx/include/linux/soc/qcom/qmi.h)
source "$ROOT/xnu-env.sh"
for h in lx qmi; do
	[ -f "$XNU_SRC/bsd/sys/redwood_$h.h" ] || { echo "mk-ath11k.sh: the kernel tree has no bsd/sys/redwood_$h.h" >&2; exit 1; }
done
DFLAGS="$DFLAGS -DLX_REDWOOD_LX_H=\"$XNU_SRC/bsd/sys/redwood_lx.h\" -DLX_REDWOOD_QMI_H=\"$XNU_SRC/bsd/sys/redwood_qmi.h\""
mkdir -p obj out
rm -f obj/*.err
compile() {		# compile SOURCE OBJECT [FLAGS]: only when the object is older than anything it was made of
	local src=$1 obj=$2
	shift 2
	if [ -f "$obj" ] && [ -f "$obj.d" ] && [ -z "$(find $(sed -e 's/^[^:]*://' -e 's/\\$//' "$obj.d") "$0" -newer "$obj" 2>/dev/null | head -1)" ]; then
		return
	fi
	$CC $CFLAGS "$@" -MMD -MF "$obj.d" -c "$src" -o "$obj" 2> "$obj.err" || rm -f "$obj"
}
for f in $DRIVER; do compile src/ath11k/$f.c obj/ath11k_$f.o $DFLAGS & done
for f in "$W"/src/*.c; do [ -f "$f" ] && compile "$f" obj/lx_$(basename "$f" .c).o $DFLAGS -I$W/src & done
wait
bad=
for f in obj/*.err; do
	[ -s "$f" ] && [ ! -f "${f%.err}" ] && { echo "--- $(basename "$f" .o.err)"; grep -m6 -A3 "error:" "$f"; bad=1; }
done
[ -z "$bad" ] || exit 1
OBJECTS=$(for f in $DRIVER; do echo obj/ath11k_$f.o; done; for f in "$W"/src/*.c; do echo obj/lx_$(basename "$f" .c).o; done)

# --- tie it all into one object. What it then still wants is one of three things: a call of the
# kernel's (redwood_lx.h; the QMI helpers; the handful of C library functions XNU has under the same
# names with the same meaning), a function of a part of the driver that is not built yet, or a
# mistake. The second kind gets a stub each that says its name and answers 0; anything else
# missing ends the build.
KERNEL="memcmp memcpy memmove memset strcmp strncmp strlen strchr strrchr strlcpy strlcat bzero
	snprintf vsnprintf __stack_chk_fail __stack_chk_guard"
$LD -r -arch arm64 $OBJECTS -o out/all.o 2> out/ld.err || { cat out/ld.err; exit 1; }
llvm-nm -u --format=just-symbols out/all.o | sed 's/^_//' | sort > out/undefined.txt
: > out/stubs.txt
: > out/stubs.s
missing=
for s in $(cat out/undefined.txt); do
	case " $(echo $KERNEL) " in *" $s "*) continue ;; esac
	case $s in
	lx_os_*|qmi_*|redwood_qmi_*|section\$*) continue ;;
	ath11k_*|__ath11k_*) ;;
	*) echo "mk-ath11k.sh: nothing defines $s" >&2; missing=1; continue ;;
	esac
	echo $s >> out/stubs.txt
	printf '\t.globl _%s\n_%s:\n\tadrp x0, 1f@PAGE\n\tadd x0, x0, 1f@PAGEOFF\n\tb _lx_stub\n\t.cstring\n1:\t.asciz "%s"\n\t.text\n\t.p2align 2\n' \
		$s $s $s >> out/stubs.s
done
[ -z "$missing" ] || exit 1
$CC -c out/stubs.s -o out/stubs.o
# four names are shown: where the kernel enters (lx_prepare(), lx_start(), lx_stop() and lx_transmit() of redwood_lx.h)
printf '_lx_prepare\n_lx_start\n_lx_stop\n_lx_transmit\n' > out/exported.txt
$LD -r -arch arm64 -exported_symbols_list out/exported.txt out/all.o out/stubs.o -o out/ath11k.o 2> out/ld.err ||
	{ cat out/ld.err; exit 1; }
rm -f out/all.o
echo "mk-ath11k.sh: out/ath11k.o: $(llvm-size out/ath11k.o | awk 'NR == 2 { print $1 + $2 }') bytes of code and data from" \
	"$(echo $DRIVER | wc -w) of the driver's files; $(wc -l < out/stubs.txt) functions of the others are stubs (out/stubs.txt);" \
	"asks the kernel for $(llvm-nm -u --format=just-symbols out/ath11k.o | grep -vc 'section\$') names"

```

`tools/mk-libdeflate.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# Put the decompressing half of libdeflate into the kernel tree, as bsd/miscfs/apfs/libdeflate/:
# the APFS driver inflates the zlib pieces of compressed files with it instead of libkern's zlib.
#
# Why: on the restore-ramdisk volume -- 19149 pieces, 180 MB in, 1229 MB out -- libkern's zlib
# inflates at 344 MB/s on the build machine and libdeflate at 740 MB/s, to the same bytes; and
# on the phone zlib was 3819 of the 4227 ms one reader spent in vnop_read over that volume.
#
# Taken as it is from the release, files unchanged; what the kernel lacks (an allocator, no C
# library) is in bsd/miscfs/apfs/apfs_deflate.c, which compiles these with -DFREESTANDING.
# libdeflate is Copyright 2016 Eric Biggers and 2024 Google LLC, under the MIT licence (COPYING,
# copied alongside).
set -e
VERSION=1.24
SHA256=a0dda1c4b804742066db07b9510876edd09cc0ca06cdc32c5dfe1b2016a26463
ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/.." && pwd)
OUT=${XNU_SRC:-$ROOT/xnu-src/xnu-8796.121.2}/bsd/miscfs/apfs/libdeflate
TMP=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
curl -sL --fail -o "$TMP/l.tar.gz" \
	https://github.com/ebiggers/libdeflate/releases/download/v$VERSION/libdeflate-$VERSION.tar.gz
echo "$SHA256  $TMP/l.tar.gz" | sha256sum -c --quiet
tar xzf "$TMP/l.tar.gz" -C "$TMP"
S=$TMP/libdeflate-$VERSION
rm -rf "$OUT"
mkdir -p "$OUT/lib/arm"
cp "$S/COPYING" "$S/libdeflate.h" "$S/common_defs.h" "$OUT/"
for f in lib_common.h cpu_features_common.h deflate_constants.h zlib_constants.h \
	decompress_template.h deflate_decompress.c zlib_decompress.c adler32.c; do
	cp "$S/lib/$f" "$OUT/lib/"
done
# the architecture dispatch is included unconditionally; in the kernel it settles on NEON for
# the Adler-32 and the portable code for the rest (see apfs_deflate.c)
cp "$S/lib/arm/"*.h "$OUT/lib/arm/"
echo "mk-libdeflate.sh: $OUT ($(du -sk "$OUT" | cut -f1) KB, libdeflate $VERSION)"
```

`tools/mk-wlfw.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# Give the kernel's build ath11k's descriptions of the messages a WCN6750's firmware speaks, for
# bsd/dev/redwood_wlfw.c (a stand-in for ath11k's own qmi.c: see there). They are taken out of
# the driver's sources as they are -- the structures of its qmi.h and the tables of its qmi.c --
# and written as one header into the kernel's build directory, where the compiler finds it and
# git does not: ath11k's text is BSD-3-Clause-Clear and is not kept in the repository.
# Without that header redwood_wlfw.c compiles to a line that says so.
#
# usage: tools/mk-wlfw.sh          then build the kernel (./xnu-build.sh); again after a clean build
set -e
ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/.." && pwd)
source "$ROOT/xnu-env.sh"
ATH=$ROOT/xnu-deps/build/ath11k/src/ath11k
[ -f "$ATH/qmi.c" ] || "$ROOT/tools/mk-ath11k.sh"
OUT=$XNU_SRC/BUILD/obj/DEVELOPMENT_ARM64_${MACHINE:-BCM2837}/bsd/DEVELOPMENT
[ -d "$OUT" ] || { echo "mk-wlfw.sh: no build directory $OUT: build the kernel once first" >&2; exit 1; }
python3 - "$ATH" "$(cat "$ATH/../.release" | cut -d' ' -f1)" > "$OUT/redwood_wlfw_ath11k.h.new" <<'PY'
import re
import sys

src, release = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
c = open(src + '/qmi.c').read()
h = open(src + '/qmi.h').read()
print('/* ath11k\'s qmi.h and the message tables of its qmi.c (Linux %s, BSD-3-Clause-Clear), put together by' % release)
print(' * tools/mk-wlfw.sh: not to be edited, not to be kept. */')
# the names qmi.h uses of a Linux kernel around it, outside its message definitions: nothing here does anything
print('''#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>
typedef uint8_t u8;
typedef uint16_t u16;
typedef uint32_t u32;
typedef uint64_t u64;
typedef uint16_t __le16;
typedef uint32_t __le32;
typedef uint64_t __le64;
typedef uint64_t dma_addr_t;
#define __iomem
struct list_head { struct list_head *next, *prev; };
struct work_struct { int unused; };
struct workqueue_struct;
typedef struct { int unused; } spinlock_t;
typedef struct { int unused; } wait_queue_head_t;
''')
print(re.sub(r'^#include <linux/[^>]*>\n', '', h, flags=re.M))
# every table, in the file's order (a table is used by the ones after it)
print('\n'.join(re.findall(r'static const struct qmi_elem_info \w+\[\] = \{.*?\n\};\n', c, re.S)))

# What the configuration message is made of for this chip: the two tables its entry of the
# driver's parameter list (core.c) names, from hw.c, with the definitions they are written in
# (ce.h, htc.h), and from that entry how many of each table's rows are sent.
core = open(src + '/core.c').read()
hw = open(src + '/hw.c').read()
ce = open(src + '/ce.h').read()
htc = open(src + '/htc.h').read()
entry = core[core.index('"wcn6750 hw1.0"'):]
entry = entry[:entry.index('\n\t},')]
def of(field):
    return re.search(r'\.%s = (\w+),' % field, entry).group(1)
print('/* as Linux has it on a little-endian machine, whatever this kernel\'s headers define */')
print('#undef __BIG_ENDIAN\n#define __cpu_to_le32(x) (x)')
print(re.search(r'#define CE_ATTR_BYTE_SWAP_DATA.*?#endif\n', ce, re.S).group(0))
print(''.join(re.findall(r'^#define PIPEDIR_\w+.*\n', ce, re.M)))
for name in ('service_to_pipe', 'ce_pipe_config'):
    print(re.search(r'struct %s \{.*?\n\};\n' % name, ce, re.S).group(0))
print(re.search(r'enum ath11k_htc_svc_gid \{.*?\n\};\n', htc, re.S).group(0))
print(re.search(r'#define SVC\(group, idx\).*?\n.*?\n', htc).group(0))
print(re.search(r'enum ath11k_htc_svc_id \{.*?\n\};\n', htc, re.S).group(0))
print('#undef SVC')
for kind, field in (('ce_pipe_config', 'target_ce_config'), ('service_to_pipe', 'svc_to_ce_map')):
    print('static ' + re.search(r'const struct %s %s\[\] = \{.*?\n\};\n' % (kind, of(field)), hw, re.S).group(0))
print('#define WLFW_PIPES\t\t%s\n#define WLFW_PIPE_COUNT\t\t%s' % (of('target_ce_config'), of('target_ce_count')))
print('#define WLFW_SERVICES\t\t%s\n#define WLFW_SERVICE_COUNT\t%s' % (of('svc_to_ce_map'), of('svc_to_ce_map_len')))
print('#define WLFW_SENDS_INI\t\t%d\t/* fw_wmi_diag_event */' % (of('fw_wmi_diag_event') == 'true'))
print('#define WLFW_SHADOW_REGISTERS\t%d\t/* supports_shadow_regs */' % (of('supports_shadow_regs') == 'true'))
PY
cmp -s "$OUT/redwood_wlfw_ath11k.h.new" "$OUT/redwood_wlfw_ath11k.h" 2>/dev/null && rm "$OUT/redwood_wlfw_ath11k.h.new" ||
	mv "$OUT/redwood_wlfw_ath11k.h.new" "$OUT/redwood_wlfw_ath11k.h"
echo "mk-wlfw.sh: $OUT/redwood_wlfw_ath11k.h ($(grep -c 'qmi_elem_info .*\[\] = {' "$OUT/redwood_wlfw_ath11k.h") tables)"

```

`tools/new-workspace.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# A second working copy of everything, for working on something else at the same time: its own
# branch of this repository (a git worktree), its own kernel tree and build, its own images and
# its own QEMU instance. What is big is shared with this copy through reflinks and hard links
# (btrfs or xfs), so a workspace costs about 0.5 GB, most of it the kernel's build output.
#
# usage: tools/new-workspace.sh NAME INSTANCE [DIR]
#   NAME      the branch, and the directory ../hackios-NAME unless DIR is given
#   INSTANCE  the QEMU instance number of the copy (1, 2, ...; see qemu/run-ios.sh)
#
# The kernel tree is copied as it is now, uncommitted work included, and that state is recorded
# (refs/redwood/baseline in the copy's kernel tree): tools/kernel-delta.sh, run in the workspace,
# prints what was changed in the kernel since. Files below ios165/rootfs, ios165/cryptex and
# ios165/cryptex-app are hard links to this copy's: replace them, never edit them in place.
# The phone is not part of a workspace: there is one, and ./xl belongs to the main copy.
set -e
ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/.." && pwd)
NAME=${1:?usage: new-workspace.sh NAME INSTANCE [DIR]}
INSTANCE=${2:?usage: new-workspace.sh NAME INSTANCE [DIR]}
WS=${3:-$(dirname "$ROOT")/hackios-$NAME}
[ -e "$WS" ] && { echo "new-workspace.sh: $WS already exists"; exit 1; }

git -C "$ROOT" worktree add -q -b "$NAME" "$WS"
cd "$WS"
# hackios-xnu-userland shares the tree (common/setup.sh): the copy gets its own clone of it, from this
# copy's, on a branch of the same name
if [ -d "$ROOT/.userland.git" ]; then
	USERLAND_URL="$ROOT/.userland.git" USERLAND_REF="$(git --git-dir="$ROOT/.userland.git" rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)" \
		common/setup.sh > /dev/null
	common/ugit checkout -q -b "$NAME"
fi

# the kernel tree, without build output (it is full of absolute paths)
mkdir -p xnu-src
cp -a --reflink=auto "$ROOT/xnu-src/xnu-8796.121.2" xnu-src/
K=xnu-src/xnu-8796.121.2
rm -rf $K/BUILD
(
	cd $K
	export GIT_INDEX_FILE=$PWD/.git/index.baseline
	git add -A . 2>/dev/null
	git update-ref refs/redwood/baseline "$(git commit-tree "$(git write-tree)" -p HEAD -m 'the state the workspace started from')"
	rm -f "$GIT_INDEX_FILE"
)
# what the kernel build needs besides the tree
cp -a --reflink=auto "$ROOT/xnu-deps/." xnu-deps/
# The files of iOS and the system image made of them. Every one of these is taken only if it is
# there: a main copy that has not built its images yet has no system.apfs nor root.apfs, and
# cryptex-app is unpacked only where somebody has needed it -- under "set -e" a copy of a file that
# is not there used to end the script halfway, leaving a workspace without its QEMU instance number
# and without a kernel. What a missing cryptex-app costs, when there is one to take: the images come
# out with no /System/Cryptexes/App at all, and Safari's daemons and AuthenticationServicesAgent --
# eight jobs -- then look to mkjobs.py like programs nobody has (build.sh at cryptex-app, present()).
for d in rootfs cryptex cryptex-app "20F66__iPhone10,3_6"; do
	if [ -e "$ROOT/ios165/$d" ]; then cp -al "$ROOT/ios165/$d" ios165/; fi
done
for f in system.files system.manifest var.skel .done-rootfs .done-cryptex .done-cryptex-app a2s.json; do
	if [ -e "$ROOT/ios165/$f" ]; then cp -a "$ROOT/ios165/$f" ios165/; fi
done
for f in rootfs.dmg rootfs.slt cryptex-app.dmg extracted; do
	if [ -e "$ROOT/ios165/$f" ]; then ln -s "$ROOT/ios165/$f" ios165/; fi
done
# The firmware the build puts into the images -- the radio's, the audio DSP's, the GPU's. A copy
# without them builds an image with no /fw and says nothing about it: gpu=1 then starts no GPU.
# Links, not copies: there is one set of these on this computer and they are not small.
for d in "$ROOT"/fw-*; do
	if [ -d "$d" ]; then ln -s "$d" ./; fi
done
for f in obj system.apfs root.apfs hello; do
	if [ -e "$ROOT/userland/$f" ]; then cp -a --reflink=auto "$ROOT/userland/$f" userland/; fi
done
[ -f "$ROOT/xnuloader/loader.efi" ] && cp -a "$ROOT/xnuloader/loader.efi" xnuloader/
[ -f "$ROOT/qemu/kernel.syms" ] && cp -a "$ROOT/qemu/kernel.syms" qemu/
echo "$INSTANCE" > qemu/instance
mkdir -p logs

echo "new-workspace.sh: building the kernel in $WS"
./xnu-build.sh -j"$(nproc)" -k > xnu-build.log 2>&1 || true
[ -f $K/BUILD/obj/DEVELOPMENT_ARM64_BCM2837/mach.development.bcm2837 ] ||
	{ echo "new-workspace.sh: the kernel did not build, see $WS/xnu-build.log"; exit 1; }
echo "new-workspace.sh: $WS is ready (branch $NAME, QEMU instance $INSTANCE)"

```

`tools/qmi-test/extract.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Take the message descriptions out of ath11k's qmi.c for the tests of our QMI helpers.

usage: extract.py PATH/TO/ath11k > tables.inc

qmi.c has 36 tables of struct qmi_elem_info, all static, and qmi.h has the C structures
they describe and, for most messages, the length the encoded message can have at most
(QMI_WLANFW_..._MAX_LEN). The tables are copied as they are, and a list is added that names each
message's table, structure and that length, so that the tests can go through all of them.
The output is ath11k's text (BSD-3-Clause-Clear) and is not kept in the repository.
"""
import re
import sys

src = sys.argv[1]
c = open(src + '/qmi.c').read()
h = open(src + '/qmi.h').read()

# every table, in the file's order (a table is used by the ones after it)
found = re.findall(r'static const struct qmi_elem_info \w+\[\] = \{.*?\n\};\n', c, re.S)
tables = '\n'.join(found)
print('/* from ath11k\'s qmi.c, by tools/qmi-test/extract.py: not to be edited, not to be committed */')
print(tables)

structs = set(re.findall(r'^struct (\w+) \{', h, re.M))
defines = set(re.findall(r'^#define (\w+)', h, re.M))
rows = []
for name, body in re.findall(r'static const struct qmi_elem_info (\w+)\[\] = \{(.*?)\n\};', tables, re.S):
    used = re.search(r'offsetof\(struct (\w+),', body)
    struct = used.group(1) if used else name[:-len('_ei')]
    if struct not in structs:
        # the few tables with no element in them: the structure is named a little differently
        guess = [s for s in structs if s.replace('_fw_', '_').replace('wlfw', 'wlanfw') ==
                 name[:-len('_ei')].replace('_fw_', '_').replace('wlfw', 'wlanfw')]
        struct = guess[0] if guess else None
    limit = (struct or '').upper() + '_MAX_LEN'
    rows.append((name, struct, limit if limit in defines else None))

print('static const struct test_message {')
print('\tconst char *name;\n\tconst struct qmi_elem_info *ei;\n\tsize_t size;\n\tint limit;\t/* -1: none given */\n\tbool message;\t/* not a structure inside one */')
print('} ath11k_messages[] = {')
for name, struct, limit in rows:
    size = 'sizeof(struct %s)' % struct if struct else '1'
    print('\t{ "%s", %s, %s, %s, %s },' % (name[:-len('_ei')], name, size, limit or '-1',
                                          'true' if '_msg_' in name else 'false'))
print('};')

```

`tools/qmi-test/run.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# Build and run the tests of the QMI helpers (bsd/dev/redwood_qmi.c of the kernel tree) on this
# machine, under the address and undefined-behaviour sanitizers.
#
# With ath11k's sources at hand (tools/mk-ath11k.sh fetches them; ATH11K=<directory> to say where
# else they are) its own message tables are tested too; without, only what needs none of them.
# Nothing of ath11k is kept: its tables are taken out of qmi.c into the build directory each time.
set -e
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd "$HERE/../.." && pwd)
K=$ROOT/xnu-src/xnu-8796.121.2                 # the kernel tree being worked in, or else the copies that are in git
[ -f "$K/bsd/dev/redwood_qmi.c" ] || K=$ROOT/xnu/files
ATH=${ATH11K:-$ROOT/xnu-deps/build/ath11k/src/ath11k}
B=$ROOT/xnu-deps/build/qmi-test
rm -rf "$B"
mkdir -p "$B/inc/sys"
ln -s "$K/bsd/sys/redwood_qmi.h" "$K/bsd/sys/redwood_qrtr.h" "$B/inc/sys/"
FLAGS="-std=gnu11 -O1 -g -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -pthread"
if [ -f "$ATH/qmi.c" ]; then
	"$HERE/extract.py" "$ATH" > "$B/tables.inc"
	${CC:-cc} $FLAGS -I"$B/inc" -I"$B" -I"$HERE/shim" -I"$ATH" -o "$B/test" "$HERE/test_qmi.c" "$K/bsd/dev/redwood_qmi.c"
	echo "qmi-test: with ath11k's tables from $ATH ($(cat "$ATH/../.release" 2>/dev/null | cut -d' ' -f1))"
else
	echo "qmi-test: no ath11k sources in $ATH: only the tests that need none"
	${CC:-cc} $FLAGS -DNO_ATH11K -I"$B/inc" -o "$B/test" "$HERE/test_qmi.c" "$K/bsd/dev/redwood_qmi.c"
fi
"$B/test"

```
