```c
static void
ticker(void *argument)
{
	unsigned long long began = lx_os_nanoseconds();

	for (;;) {
		struct timer_list *due = NULL;
		struct delayed_work *work = NULL;
		struct workqueue_struct *queue = NULL;

		lx_os_lock();
		lx_os_sleep(&jiffies, 2 * 1000000ull);
		jiffies = (unsigned long)((lx_os_nanoseconds() - began) / 1000000ull);
		for (unsigned i = 0; i < nitems(armed) && due == NULL; i++) {
			if (armed[i] != NULL && (long)(jiffies - armed[i]->expires) >= 0) {
				due = armed[i];
				armed[i] = NULL;
			}
		}
		for (unsigned i = 0; i < nitems(later) && work == NULL; i++) {
			if (later[i].work != NULL && (long)(jiffies - later[i].when) >= 0) {
				work = later[i].work;
				queue = later[i].queue;
				later[i].work = NULL;
			}
		}
		lx_os_unlock();
		/* (a timer that a part of the driver not built yet would have given its function has none) */
		if (due != NULL && due->function_415 != NULL) {
			due->function_415(due);
		}
		if (work != NULL) {
			linux_queue_work_on(0, queue, &work->work);
		}
	}
}

/* Work that is to be queued when some time has passed: the thread above does that. */
void
linux_init_delayed_work(struct delayed_work *dwork, work_func_t function)
{
	bzero(dwork, sizeof(*dwork));
	INIT_WORK(&dwork->work, function);
}

bool
linux_queue_delayed_work_on(int cpu, struct workqueue_struct *wq, struct delayed_work *dwork, unsigned long delay)
{
	int slot = -1;

	if (delay == 0) {
		return (linux_queue_work_on(cpu, wq, &dwork->work));
	}
	lx_os_lock();
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < nitems(later); i++) {
		if (later[i].work == dwork) {
			lx_os_unlock();
			return (false);			/* (it waits already) */
		}
		if (later[i].work == NULL && slot < 0) {
			slot = (int)i;
		}
	}
	if (slot >= 0) {
		later[slot].work = dwork;
		later[slot].queue = wq;
		later[slot].when = jiffies + delay;
	}
	lx_os_unlock();
	if (slot < 0) {
		printf("lx: no room for more work that waits for its time: one piece will not be done\n");
	}
	return (slot >= 0);
}

/* Not to be queued any more, if it waits for its time; true if it did. */
bool
linux_cancel_delayed_work(struct delayed_work *dwork)
{
	bool waited = false;

	lx_os_lock();
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < nitems(later); i++) {
		if (later[i].work == dwork) {
			later[i].work = NULL;
			waited = true;
		}
	}
	lx_os_unlock();
	return (waited);
}

/* (A timer's function that is running on the ticker's thread at this moment is not waited for.) */
int
timer_delete_sync(struct timer_list *timer)
{
	int was = 0;

	lx_os_lock();
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < nitems(armed); i++) {
		if (armed[i] == timer) {
			armed[i] = NULL;
			was = 1;
		}
	}
	lx_os_unlock();
	return (was);
}

void
lx_pause_ms(unsigned ms)
{
	static char nothing;			/* (an address nobody wakes) */

	lx_os_lock();
	lx_os_sleep(&nothing, ms * 1000000ull);
	lx_os_unlock();
}

void
callout_init(struct callout *c, int mpsafe)
{
	bzero(c, sizeof(*c));
}

int
mod_timer(struct timer_list *timer, unsigned long expires)
{
	int was = 0, slot = -1;

	lx_os_lock();
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < nitems(armed); i++) {
		if (armed[i] == timer) {
			was = 1;
			slot = (int)i;
		} else if (armed[i] == NULL && slot < 0) {
			slot = (int)i;
		}
	}
	timer->expires = expires;
	if (slot >= 0) {
		armed[slot] = timer;
	}
	lx_os_unlock();
	if (slot < 0) {
		printf("lx: no room for another timer: one will not fire\n");
	}
	return (was);
}

/* ---- locks ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ */

/*
 * LinuxKPI makes a Linux mutex of FreeBSD's "sx" and a spinlock of FreeBSD's "mtx". Both are a
 * word here that holds who has the lock; whoever finds it taken sleeps until it is given back.
 * (A spinlock that sleeps is no harm where nothing runs in an interrupt.)
 */
static void
word_lock(volatile uintptr_t *word)
{
	uintptr_t self = (uintptr_t)lx_os_thread_self();

	lx_os_lock();
	while (*word != 0) {
		if (*word == self) {
			lx_os_unlock();
			lx_os_panic("lx: a lock taken twice by the thread that has it");
		}
		lx_os_sleep(word, SLICE_NS);
	}
	*word = self;
	lx_os_unlock();
}

static void
word_unlock(volatile uintptr_t *word)
{
	lx_os_lock();
	*word = 0;
	lx_os_wakeup(word);
	lx_os_unlock();
}

void
sx_init_flags(struct sx *sx, const char *description, int opts)
{
	bzero(sx, sizeof(*sx));
	sx->lock_object.lo_name = description;
}

int
_sx_xlock(struct sx *sx, int opts, const char *file, int line)
{
	word_lock(&sx->sx_lock);
	return (0);
}

void
_sx_xunlock(struct sx *sx, const char *file, int line)
{
	word_unlock(&sx->sx_lock);
}

void
_mtx_init(volatile uintptr_t *c, const char *name, const char *type, int opts)
{
	*c = 0;
}

void
__mtx_lock_flags(volatile uintptr_t *c, int opts, const char *file, int line)
{
	word_lock(c);
}

void
__mtx_unlock_flags(volatile uintptr_t *c, int opts, const char *file, int line)
{
	word_unlock(c);
}

/* ---- waiting for something ---------------------------------------------------------------------- */

void
linux_complete_common(struct completion *c, int all)
{
	lx_os_lock();
	if (all) {
		c->done = UINT_MAX;
	} else if (c->done != UINT_MAX) {
		c->done++;
	}
	lx_os_wakeup(c);
	lx_os_unlock();
}

int
linux_completion_done(struct completion *c)
{
	return (c->done != 0);
}

/* What is left of the time when the completion comes (at least 1), or 0 if it does not. */
unsigned long
linux_wait_for_timeout_common(struct completion *c, unsigned long timeout, int flags)
{
	unsigned long long deadline = lx_os_nanoseconds() + ticks_to_ns(timeout), now;
	unsigned long left = 0;

	lx_os_lock();
	for (;;) {
		now = lx_os_nanoseconds();
		if (c->done != 0) {
			if (c->done != UINT_MAX) {
				c->done--;
			}
			left = now < deadline ? (unsigned long)((deadline - now) / 1000000ull) : 0;
			left = left == 0 ? 1 : left;
			break;
		}
		if (now >= deadline) {
			break;
		}
		lx_os_sleep(c, deadline - now < SLICE_NS ? deadline - now : SLICE_NS);
	}
	lx_os_unlock();
	return (left);
}

/*
 * wait_event...() is a loop in LinuxKPI's header: look at the condition, call this, look again.
 * It gives the whole time allowed each time round, so when the first round began is kept here.
 */
void
linux_prepare_to_wait(wait_queue_head_t *wqh, wait_queue_t *wq, int state)
{
}

void
linux_finish_wait(wait_queue_head_t *wqh, wait_queue_t *wq)
{
	lx_thread()->waiting_on = NULL;
}

int
linux_wait_event_common(wait_queue_head_t *wqh, wait_queue_t *wq, long timeout, unsigned int state, spinlock_t *lock)
{
	struct lx_thread *t = lx_thread();
	unsigned long long now = lx_os_nanoseconds(), slice = SLICE_NS;

	if (t->waiting_on != wqh) {
		t->waiting_on = wqh;
		t->deadline = timeout == MAX_SCHEDULE_TIMEOUT ? 0 : now + ticks_to_ns((unsigned long)timeout);
	}
	if (t->deadline != 0) {
		if (now >= t->deadline) {
			return (-EWOULDBLOCK);
		}
		slice = t->deadline - now < slice ? t->deadline - now : slice;
	}
	if (lock != NULL) {
		spin_unlock_irq(lock);
	}
	lx_os_lock();
	lx_os_sleep(wqh, slice);
	lx_os_unlock();
	if (lock != NULL) {
		spin_lock_irq(lock);
	}
	return (0);
}

void
linux_wake_up(wait_queue_head_t *wqh, unsigned int state, int nr, bool locked)
{
	lx_os_lock();
	lx_os_wakeup(wqh);
	lx_os_unlock();
}

int
autoremove_wake_function(wait_queue_t *wq, unsigned int state, int flags, void *key)
{
	return (1);
}

/* ---- work queues ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ */

/*
 * A queue is a thread and a list of the work waiting for it: work runs one piece at a time in
 * the order it was queued, which is what an "ordered" queue promises and more than the other
 * kinds do. A piece of work that is queued while it waits is not queued twice; one that is
 * queued while it runs runs again.
 */
enum { WORK_IDLE = 0, WORK_QUEUED = 2 };

struct lx_workqueue {
	struct workqueue_struct shown;		/* what LinuxKPI's headers know of a queue (nothing of it is used) */
	struct work_struct *waiting[64];
	unsigned first, count;
	struct work_struct *running;
	void *thread;
	char name[24];
};

static void
worker(void *argument)
{
	struct lx_workqueue *queue = argument;
	struct work_struct *work;

	queue->thread = lx_os_thread_self();
	for (;;) {
		lx_os_lock();
		queue->running = NULL;
		lx_os_wakeup(&queue->running);
		while (queue->count == 0) {
			lx_os_sleep(queue, SLICE_NS);
		}
		work = queue->waiting[queue->first];
		queue->first = (queue->first + 1) % nitems(queue->waiting);
		queue->count--;
		queue->running = work;
		atomic_set(&work->state, WORK_IDLE);
		lx_os_unlock();
		work->func(work);
	}
}

struct workqueue_struct *
linux_create_workqueue_common(const char *name, int cpus)
{
	struct lx_workqueue *queue = lx_os_alloc(sizeof(*queue));

	if (queue == NULL) {
		return (NULL);
	}
	strlcpy(queue->name, name, sizeof(queue->name));
	if (lx_os_thread(queue->name, worker, queue) != 0) {
		lx_os_free(queue, sizeof(*queue));
		return (NULL);
	}
	return (&queue->shown);
}

void
linux_destroy_workqueue(struct workqueue_struct *wq)
{
	/* (its thread stays, asleep: queues are made once here and never given up while the kernel runs) */
}

bool
linux_queue_work_on(int cpu, struct workqueue_struct *wq, struct work_struct *work)
{
	struct lx_workqueue *queue = __containerof(wq, struct lx_workqueue, shown);
	bool queued = false;

	lx_os_lock();
	if (atomic_read(&work->state) == WORK_IDLE && queue->count < nitems(queue->waiting)) {
		atomic_set(&work->state, WORK_QUEUED);
		work->work_queue = wq;
		queue->waiting[(queue->first + queue->count++) % nitems(queue->waiting)] = work;
		lx_os_wakeup(queue);
		queued = true;
	}
	lx_os_unlock();
	return (queued);
}

/* Not to run any more if it waits; and if it runs, until it has ended (unless it is the caller that runs it). */
bool
linux_cancel_work_sync(struct work_struct *work)
{
	struct lx_workqueue *queue;
	bool waited = false;

	if (work->work_queue == NULL) {
		return (false);
	}
	queue = __containerof(work->work_queue, struct lx_workqueue, shown);
	lx_os_lock();
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < queue->count; i++) {
		unsigned at = (queue->first + i) % nitems(queue->waiting);

		if (queue->waiting[at] == work) {
			for (; i + 1 < queue->count; i++) {
				queue->waiting[(queue->first + i) % nitems(queue->waiting)] =
				    queue->waiting[(queue->first + i + 1) % nitems(queue->waiting)];
			}
			queue->count--;
			atomic_set(&work->state, WORK_IDLE);
			waited = true;
			break;
		}
	}
	while (queue->running == work && queue->thread != lx_os_thread_self()) {
		lx_os_sleep(&queue->running, SLICE_NS);
		waited = true;
	}
	lx_os_unlock();
	return (waited);
}

bool
linux_cancel_delayed_work_sync(struct delayed_work *dwork)
{
	bool waited = linux_cancel_delayed_work(dwork);

	return (linux_cancel_work_sync(&dwork->work) || waited);
}

void
linux_work_fn(void *context, int pending)
{
	/* (the function FreeBSD's task queues would call; LinuxKPI's headers want its address) */
}

/* ---- memory ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

/* kmalloc(): the size goes in front, because kfree() is not told it. */
static volatile long allocations, allocated;	/* pieces out now, and their bytes: for lx_memory_say() */

void *
lkpi_kmalloc(size_t size, gfp_t flags)
{
	size_t *block = lx_os_alloc(size + 16);

	if (block == NULL) {
		return (NULL);
	}
	block[0] = size + 16;
	__sync_fetch_and_add(&allocations, 1);
	__sync_fetch_and_add(&allocated, (long)(size + 16));
	return (block + 2);
}

void
lkpi_kfree(const void *memory)
{
	size_t *block = (size_t *)(uintptr_t)memory - 2;

	if (memory != NULL) {
		__sync_fetch_and_sub(&allocations, 1);
		__sync_fetch_and_sub(&allocated, (long)block[0]);
		lx_os_free(block, block[0]);
	}
}

void *
_ioremap_attr(vm_paddr_t physical, unsigned long size, int attributes)
{
	return (lx_os_map_registers(physical, size));
}

void
iounmap(void *address)
{
}

/*
 * Memory the radio itself reads and writes: its rings, and the buffers it fills. The radio
 * reaches memory through the SoC's SMMU, which lets it see what it has been shown and nothing
 * else; so all such memory comes out of one piece, taken once, which the kernel's side shows
 * the radio and says the radio's address of (lx_os_radio_memory()). That piece is not behind
 * the processor's cache: there is nothing to do between our writing and the radio's reading,
 * or the other way round. The first part of it is handed out for good, a stretch at a time
 * (rings); the rest is slots of one size, taken and given back (buffers).
 */
#define POOL_SIZE	(44u << 20)
#define POOL_RINGS	(12u << 20)		/* (the data path's rings and link descriptors come to about 6 MB) */
#define POOL_SLOT	4096u
#define POOL_SLOTS	((POOL_SIZE - POOL_RINGS) / POOL_SLOT)

static struct {
	uint8_t *memory;
	unsigned long long address;		/* the radio's, of the first byte */
	uint32_t rings_used;
	uint32_t free_slots[POOL_SLOTS], free_count;
} pool;

int
lx_pool_init(void)
{
	if (pool.memory != NULL) {
		return (0);
	}
	pool.memory = lx_os_radio_memory(POOL_SIZE, &pool.address);
	if (pool.memory == NULL) {
		return (ENOMEM);
	}
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < POOL_SLOTS; i++) {
		pool.free_slots[i] = POOL_SLOTS - 1 - i;
	}
	pool.free_count = POOL_SLOTS;
	printf("lx: %u MB for the radio to read and write; it knows them from %#llx on\n", POOL_SIZE >> 20, pool.address);
	return (0);
}

static bool
in_pool(const void *memory, size_t size)
{
	return ((const uint8_t *)memory >= pool.memory && (const uint8_t *)memory + size <= pool.memory + POOL_SIZE);
}

void *
linux_dma_alloc_coherent(struct device *dev, size_t size, dma_addr_t *dma_handle, gfp_t flag)
{
	uint32_t at;

	size = roundup2(size, 64);
	lx_os_lock();
	at = pool.rings_used;
	if (pool.memory == NULL || at + size > POOL_RINGS) {
		lx_os_unlock();
		printf("lx: no room for %zu more bytes of rings\n", size);
		return (NULL);
	}
	pool.rings_used += size;
	lx_os_unlock();
	bzero(pool.memory + at, size);
	*dma_handle = pool.address + at;
	return (pool.memory + at);
}

void
kmem_free(void *address, vm_size_t size)
{
	/* (dma_free_coherent() ends here: rings are not given back) */
}

/*
 * Linux's memory for a device that need not be coherent: the same piece. (The data path takes a
 * few kilobytes of it for every traffic class of a station it meets, and gives them back when
 * the station goes: here they stay taken, like the rings.)
 */
void *
dma_alloc_noncoherent(struct device *dev, size_t size, dma_addr_t *handle, enum dma_data_direction direction, gfp_t gfp)
{
	return (linux_dma_alloc_coherent(dev, size, handle, gfp));
}

void
dma_free_noncoherent(struct device *dev, size_t size, void *memory, dma_addr_t handle, enum dma_data_direction direction)
{
}

/*
 * FreeBSD's question for the physical address of memory, which LinuxKPI asks before it hands
 * memory to a device. Here the answer is the radio's address, for memory of the pool; no other
 * memory has one (0, which lkpi_dma_map_phys() below then refuses).
 */
vm_paddr_t
pmap_kextract(vm_offset_t va)
{
	return (in_pool((void *)va, 1) ? pool.address + ((uint8_t *)va - pool.memory) : 0);
}

/* A buffer handed to the radio: it must be the pool's. */
dma_addr_t
lkpi_dma_map_phys(struct device *dev, vm_paddr_t address, size_t length, enum dma_data_direction direction, unsigned long attributes)
{
	if (address < pool.address || address + length > pool.address + POOL_SIZE) {
		printf("lx: memory is given to the radio that it cannot reach (%zu bytes)\n", length);
		return (DMA_MAPPING_ERROR);
	}
	return (address);
}

void
lkpi_dma_unmap(struct device *dev, dma_addr_t address, size_t length, enum dma_data_direction direction, unsigned long attributes)
{
}

void
linuxkpi_dma_sync(struct device *dev, dma_addr_t address, size_t length, bus_dmasync_op_t op)
{
}

/* ---- socket buffers --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

/* The buffer's description and what LinuxKPI keeps behind it come from kmalloc(); its data is a slot of the pool. */
struct sk_buff *
linuxkpi_dev_alloc_skb(size_t size, gfp_t gfp)
{
	size_t all = roundup2(sizeof(struct sk_buff), 64) + sizeof(struct skb_shared_info) + 64;
	struct sk_buff *skb;
	uint8_t *raw;
	uint32_t slot;

	if (size + NET_SKB_PAD > POOL_SLOT) {
		printf("lx: a buffer of %zu bytes is asked for; the slots are %u\n", size, POOL_SLOT);
		return (NULL);
	}
	raw = lkpi_kmalloc(all, gfp);
	if (raw == NULL) {
		return (NULL);
	}
	lx_os_lock();
	if (pool.free_count == 0) {
		lx_os_unlock();
		lkpi_kfree(raw);
		printf("lx: no buffer left\n");
		return (NULL);
	}
	slot = pool.free_slots[--pool.free_count];
	lx_os_unlock();
	skb = (struct sk_buff *)roundup2((uintptr_t)raw, 64);
	skb->m = raw;				/* (the field FreeBSD keeps for what is behind a buffer) */
	skb->prev = skb->next = skb;
	skb->shinfo = (struct skb_shared_info *)((uint8_t *)skb + roundup2(sizeof(struct sk_buff), 64));
	skb->truesize = size + NET_SKB_PAD;
	skb->head = skb->data = pool.memory + POOL_RINGS + (size_t)slot * POOL_SLOT;
	skb_reset_tail_pointer(skb);
	skb->end = skb->head + size + NET_SKB_PAD;
	skb_reserve(skb, NET_SKB_PAD);
	return (skb);
}

void
linuxkpi_kfree_skb(struct sk_buff *skb)
{
	if (skb == NULL) {
		return;
	}
	if (in_pool(skb->head, 1) && skb->head >= pool.memory + POOL_RINGS) {
		lx_os_lock();
		pool.free_slots[pool.free_count++] = (uint32_t)((skb->head - (pool.memory + POOL_RINGS)) / POOL_SLOT);
		lx_os_unlock();
	}
	lkpi_kfree(skb->m);
}

/* ---- firmware files ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

int
linuxkpi_firmware_request_nowarn(const struct linuxkpi_firmware **out, const char *name, struct device *dev)
{
	struct linuxkpi_firmware *fw;
	const void *data = NULL;
	unsigned long size = 0;
	int error = lx_os_firmware(name, &data, &size);

	printf("lx: the driver asks for the file \"%s\": %s\n", name, error == 0 ? "there" : "not there");
	if (error != 0) {
		return (-ENOENT);
	}
	fw = lkpi_kmalloc(sizeof(*fw), GFP_KERNEL);
	if (fw == NULL) {
		return (-ENOMEM);
	}
	fw->size = size;
	fw->data = data;
	*out = fw;
	return (0);
}

void
linuxkpi_release_firmware(const struct linuxkpi_firmware *fw)
{
	lkpi_kfree(fw);
}

/* ---- what the files built so far name and do not get to --------------------------------------------- */

/*
 * Numbered things (Linux's "idr": the driver numbers the frames it has handed to the firmware
 * and finds them again by number). Here a table that grows, hung where FreeBSD's keeps its tree.
 */
struct lx_ids {
	int size;
	void *things[];
};

void
idr_init(struct idr *idr)
{
	bzero(idr, sizeof(*idr));
}

void
idr_destroy(struct idr *idr)
{
	struct lx_ids *ids = (struct lx_ids *)idr->top;

	if (ids != NULL) {
		lx_os_free(ids, sizeof(*ids) + ids->size * sizeof(void *));
	}
	idr->top = NULL;
}

/* The lowest free number from `start` up to but not `end` (0 or less: no limit), or -ENOSPC. */
int
idr_alloc(struct idr *idr, void *thing, int start, int end, gfp_t gfp)
{
	struct lx_ids *ids, *more;
	int id, size;

	lx_os_lock();
	ids = (struct lx_ids *)idr->top;
	for (id = start < 0 ? 0 : start; ids != NULL && id < ids->size && ids->things[id] != NULL; id++) {
	}
	if (end > 0 && id >= end) {
		lx_os_unlock();
		return (-ENOSPC);
	}
	if (ids == NULL || id >= ids->size) {
		size = id + 64;
		lx_os_unlock();
		more = lx_os_alloc(sizeof(*more) + size * sizeof(void *));
		if (more == NULL) {
			return (-ENOMEM);
		}
		lx_os_lock();
		ids = (struct lx_ids *)idr->top;
		if (ids != NULL && ids->size >= size) {		/* (somebody else has made it grow meanwhile) */
			lx_os_unlock();
			lx_os_free(more, sizeof(*more) + size * sizeof(void *));
			return (idr_alloc(idr, thing, start, end, gfp));
		}
		more->size = size;
		if (ids != NULL) {
			memcpy(more->things, ids->things, ids->size * sizeof(void *));
		}
		idr->top = (struct idr_layer *)more;
		lx_os_unlock();
		if (ids != NULL) {
			lx_os_free(ids, sizeof(*ids) + ids->size * sizeof(void *));
		}
		return (idr_alloc(idr, thing, start, end, gfp));
	}
	ids->things[id] = thing;
	lx_os_unlock();
	return (id);
}

void *
idr_find(struct idr *idr, int id)
{
	struct lx_ids *ids;
	void *thing;

	lx_os_lock();
	ids = (struct lx_ids *)idr->top;
	thing = ids != NULL && id >= 0 && id < ids->size ? ids->things[id] : NULL;
	lx_os_unlock();
	return (thing);
}

void *
idr_remove(struct idr *idr, int id)
{
	struct lx_ids *ids;
	void *thing = NULL;

	lx_os_lock();
	ids = (struct lx_ids *)idr->top;
	if (ids != NULL && id >= 0 && id < ids->size) {
		thing = ids->things[id];
		ids->things[id] = NULL;
	}
	lx_os_unlock();
	return (thing);
}

int
idr_for_each(struct idr *idr, int (*function)(int id, void *p, void *data), void *data)
{
	int answer = 0;

	for (int id = 0; answer == 0; id++) {
		struct lx_ids *ids;
		void *thing;

		lx_os_lock();
		ids = (struct lx_ids *)idr->top;
		if (ids == NULL || id >= ids->size) {
			lx_os_unlock();
			break;
		}
		thing = ids->things[id];
		lx_os_unlock();
		if (thing != NULL) {
			answer = function(id, thing, data);
		}
	}
	return (answer);
}

/*
 * Things found by a key inside them (linux/rhashtable.h, ours). The chains are changed and walked
 * under the layer's lock; that a thing found stays there while it is used is the caller's
 * business, as it is under Linux.
 */
static struct rhash_head **
rht_chain(struct rhashtable *table, const void *key, unsigned length)
{
	uint32_t hash = 2166136261u;

	for (unsigned i = 0; i < length; i++) {
		hash = (hash ^ ((const uint8_t *)key)[i]) * 16777619u;
	}
	return (&table->chains[hash % nitems(table->chains)]);
}

int
rhashtable_init(struct rhashtable *table, const struct rhashtable_params *params)
{
	bzero(table, sizeof(*table));
	return (0);
}

void
rhashtable_destroy(struct rhashtable *table)
{
}

static void *
rht_find(struct rhashtable *table, const void *key, const struct rhashtable_params *params)
{
	for (struct rhash_head *head = *rht_chain(table, key, params->key_len); head != NULL; head = head->next) {
		uint8_t *thing = (uint8_t *)head - params->head_offset;

		if (memcmp(thing + params->key_offset, key, params->key_len) == 0) {
			return (thing);
		}
	}
	return (NULL);
}

void *
rhashtable_lookup_fast(struct rhashtable *table, const void *key, const struct rhashtable_params params)
{
	void *thing;

	lx_os_lock();
	thing = rht_find(table, key, &params);
	lx_os_unlock();
	return (thing);
}

void *
rhashtable_lookup_get_insert_fast(struct rhashtable *table, struct rhash_head *head, const struct rhashtable_params params)
{
	const uint8_t *key = (uint8_t *)head - params.head_offset + params.key_offset;
	struct rhash_head **chain;
	void *there;

	lx_os_lock();
	there = rht_find(table, key, &params);
	if (there == NULL) {
		chain = rht_chain(table, key, params.key_len);
		head->next = *chain;
		*chain = head;
	}
	lx_os_unlock();
	return (there);
}

int
rhashtable_remove_fast(struct rhashtable *table, struct rhash_head *head, const struct rhashtable_params params)
{
	const uint8_t *key = (uint8_t *)head - params.head_offset + params.key_offset;
	int error = -ENOENT;

	lx_os_lock();
	for (struct rhash_head **link = rht_chain(table, key, params.key_len); *link != NULL; link = &(*link)->next) {
		if (*link == head) {
			*link = head->next;
			error = 0;
			break;
		}
	}
	lx_os_unlock();
	return (error);
}

/* The numbered thing with the lowest number from *id on, and that number; or NULL. */
void *
idr_get_next(struct idr *idr, int *id)
{
	struct lx_ids *ids;
	void *thing = NULL;

	lx_os_lock();
	ids = (struct lx_ids *)idr->top;
	for (int i = *id < 0 ? 0 : *id; ids != NULL && i < ids->size; i++) {
		if (ids->things[i] != NULL) {
			thing = ids->things[i];
			*id = i;
			break;
		}
	}
	lx_os_unlock();
	return (thing);
}

void
explicit_bzero(void *memory, size_t size)
{
	bzero(memory, size);
}

/* FreeBSD's kernel log, which LinuxKPI's rate-limited messages go to. */
void
log(int level, const char *format, ...)
{
	char line[400];
	va_list list;

	va_start(list, format);
	vsnprintf(line, sizeof(line), format, list);
	va_end(list);
	lx_os_print(line);
}

void
arc4random_buf(void *buffer, size_t size)
{
	lx_os_random(buffer, size);
}

const struct dmi_system_id *
linux_dmi_first_match(const struct dmi_system_id *list)
{
	return (NULL);				/* (no table of the machine's maker here) */
}

/* What the layer holds of the kernel's memory right now: a number that keeps growing is a leak. */
void
lx_memory_say(void)
{
	lx_tell("lx: memory: %ld pieces of the kernel's out, %ld KB; of the radio's %u MB: %u KB of rings, %u of %u buffers out\n",
	    allocations, allocated >> 10, POOL_SIZE >> 20, pool.rings_used >> 10, POOL_SLOTS - pool.free_count, POOL_SLOTS);
}

int
lx_base_init(void)
{
	static bool begun;

	if (begun) {
		return (0);
	}
	begun = true;
	return (lx_os_thread("wifi-ticks", ticker, NULL));
}

```

`wifi/lx/src/lx_bus.c`:

```c
/*
 * The radio's bus, for as long as ath11k's own (ahb.c, pcic.c) is not built: what stands between
 * the driver's core and this phone's WCN6750. It does what ahb.c's probe does for this chip, in
 * its order, with what the files built so far need of it -- the chip's registers through the
 * three fixed windows, and a thread that looks at the copy engines every millisecond where the
 * driver would have their interrupts -- and it is where the driver's calls into the parts not
 * yet built are given something to do.
 *
 * Where this stage ends: qmi.c has its exchange with the firmware, core.c starts the firmware
 * in mission mode and has ce.c and hal.c set up the copy engines' rings, htc.c connects its
 * services over them and wmi.c has the firmware say what the radio is ("service ready") and,
 * given the driver's configuration, that it is ready for commands ("unified ready"); mac.c
 * registers the radio with what stands in for mac80211 (lx_80211.c) and sets the data path's
 * rings up. What the firmware said is then put in the log. With the boot-arg wifi_scan=1 the
 * station of lx_80211.c has the radio scan, and the driver is taken down again the way its own
 * removal does it (ath11k_core_deinit()); with wifi_join=1 the station joins the network the
 * kernel was given, and the driver stays up, carrying the kernel's frames, until lx_stop().
 *
 * The kernel's boot-arg wifi_lx says how far the radio's registers are touched: 1, not at all
 * (every write is said and dropped, every read is 0: the driver's own exchange and nothing
 * else); 2, for real.
 *
 * What the phone said, 13 October: all of that happens, 270 ms from the start of the bus to
 * "unified ready", with the copy engines looked at once a millisecond, and the scan hears the
 * networks around (bsd/dev/redwood_wifi.c, step_driver(), has the account).
 */
#define LX_QMI_AS_IT_IS				/* (this file is where the driver's requests go past) */
#include <linux/kernel.h>
#include <linux/device.h>
#include <linux/io.h>
#include <linux/of.h>
#include <linux/of_reserved_mem.h>
#include <linux/skbuff.h>

#include "core.h"
#include "ce.h"
#include "debug.h"
#include "hal.h"
#include "hif.h"
#include "htc.h"
#include "pcic.h"
#include "qmi.h"

#include <lx_os.h>
#include "lx.h"

static struct {
	unsigned how;				/* wifi_lx */
	bool mission;				/* the firmware has been asked for mission mode, and for no other since */
	bool closed;				/* the driver has stopped the bus: the registers are not touched again */
	unsigned reads, writes, said, refused;
	u32 last, last_value;			/* the register written last, and with what ... */
	unsigned again;				/* ... and how many writes to it in a row have not been said */
	volatile bool looking;			/* the thread that looks at the copy engines is wanted ... */
	volatile bool looks;			/* ... and runs */
	volatile bool data;			/* ... and looks at the data path's rings as well */
	unsigned same;				/* it has written a ring's pointer what it held so many times */

	/* the radio's interrupts (wifi_irq=1): what the copy engines and the data path's groups are taken care of on */
	bool irq;
	struct mutex service;			/* one thing at a time looks at the rings: an interrupt's or the thread */
	int ce_vector[CE_COUNT_MAX];		/* a copy engine's vector, -1: it has none (ce.c: CE_ATTR_DIS_INTR) */
	int group_vector[ATH11K_EXT_IRQ_GRP_NUM_MAX];
	unsigned long long late;		/* work the thread found that no interrupt had brought */
} bus;

/*
 * The radio's interrupt vectors, as pcic.c has them for this chip: 28 of the node's 32, ten for the
 * copy engines from vector 0 and eighteen for the data path's groups from vector 10.
 */
static struct ath11k_msi_user msi_users[] = {
	{ .name = "CE", .num_vectors = 10, .base_vector = 0 },
	{ .name = "DP", .num_vectors = 18, .base_vector = 10 },
};
static void irq_say(void);

static const struct ath11k_msi_config msi_config = {
	.total_vectors = 28,
	.total_users = 2,
	.users = msi_users,
	.hw_rev = ATH11K_HW_WCN6750_HW10,
};

/* ---- what the driver says ---------------------------------------------------------------------- */

static void
driver_says(const char *kind, const char *format, va_list list)
{
	char line[320];
	size_t length;

	vsnprintf(line, sizeof(line), format, list);
	length = strlen(line);
	/* (Linux ends a line for whoever has not) */
	printf("ath11k%s: %s%s", kind, line, length != 0 && line[length - 1] == '\n' ? "" : "\n");
}

void
ath11k_info(struct ath11k_base *ab, const char *format, ...)
{
	va_list list;

	va_start(list, format);
	driver_says("", format, list);
	va_end(list);
}

/* (the driver's warnings and errors are said whatever happens to the rest) */
static void
driver_complains(const char *kind, const char *format, va_list list)
{
	char line[320];

	vsnprintf(line, sizeof(line), format, list);
	lx_tell("ath11k %s: %s%s", kind, line, line[0] != 0 && line[strlen(line) - 1] == '\n' ? "" : "\n");
}

void
ath11k_warn(struct ath11k_base *ab, const char *format, ...)
{
	va_list list;

	va_start(list, format);
	driver_complains("WARNS", format, list);
	va_end(list);
}

void
ath11k_err(struct ath11k_base *ab, const char *format, ...)
{
	va_list list;

	va_start(list, format);
	driver_complains("ERROR", format, list);
	va_end(list);
}

void
__ath11k_dbg(struct ath11k_base *ab, enum ath11k_debug_mask mask, const char *format, ...)
{
	va_list list;

	va_start(list, format);
	driver_says(" (debug)", format, list);
	va_end(list);
}

void
ath11k_dbg_dump(struct ath11k_base *ab, enum ath11k_debug_mask mask, const char *msg, const char *prefix, const void *buf,
    size_t len)
{
}

/* ---- the chip's registers ---------------------------------------------------------------------- */

/*
 * As ahb.c reaches them (ath11k_ahb_get_window_start_wcn6750()): the first 512K of the block
 * the firmware names are the chip's first 512K; the second 512K show its data path's
 * registers, the third its copy engines'.
 */
static u32
window(struct ath11k_base *ab, u32 offset)
{
	if (offset < ATH11K_PCI_WINDOW_START) {
		return (offset);
	}
	if ((offset ^ HAL_SEQ_WCSS_UMAC_OFFSET) < ATH11K_PCI_WINDOW_RANGE_MASK) {
		return (ATH11K_PCI_WINDOW_START + (offset & ATH11K_PCI_WINDOW_RANGE_MASK));
	}
	if ((offset ^ HAL_SEQ_WCSS_UMAC_CE0_SRC_REG(ab)) < ATH11K_PCI_WINDOW_RANGE_MASK) {
		return (2 * ATH11K_PCI_WINDOW_START + (offset & ATH11K_PCI_WINDOW_RANGE_MASK));
	}
	return (0);				/* (refused() has kept such a one out) */
}

/*
 * The registers answer while the firmware is in mission mode and at no other time: an access
 * outside it ends the kernel (bsd/dev/redwood_wifi.c, step 16). The driver asks for that mode
 * before it first touches them; once it has stopped the bus, on its way to asking for the mode
 * "off", nothing is let through any more.
 */
static bool
refused(struct ath11k_base *ab, u32 offset)
{
	bool known = offset < ATH11K_PCI_WINDOW_START || (offset ^ HAL_SEQ_WCSS_UMAC_OFFSET) < ATH11K_PCI_WINDOW_RANGE_MASK ||
	    (offset ^ HAL_SEQ_WCSS_UMAC_CE0_SRC_REG(ab)) < ATH11K_PCI_WINDOW_RANGE_MASK;

	if (known && bus.mission && !bus.closed) {
		return (false);
	}
	if (bus.refused++ < 8) {
		lx_tell("lx: the chip's %#x is reached for %s: NOT DONE\n", offset, !known ? "which no window shows" : bus.closed ?
		    "after the bus was stopped" : "while the firmware is not in mission mode");
	}
	return (true);
}

/*
 * The accesses are said one by one, up to a number of lines; of writes to one register in a row
 * (a ring's pointer, moved once for every buffer) the first three, and then how many followed.
 */
#define SAID_FIRST	600

static void
say_repeats(void)
{
	if (bus.again != 0) {
		printf("lx: ... and %u more to the chip's %#x, the last %#x\n", bus.again, bus.last, bus.last_value);
		bus.again = 0;
	}
}

static bool
said_write(u32 offset, u32 value)
{
	static struct {
		u32 offset, value;
	} pointers[24];				/* while the copy engines are looked at: what each pointer was moved to last */
	static unsigned row;

	if (bus.looks) {
		for (unsigned i = 0; i < nitems(pointers); i++) {
			if (pointers[i].offset == offset || pointers[i].offset == 0) {
				bool moved = pointers[i].offset == 0 || pointers[i].value != value;

				pointers[i].offset = offset;
				pointers[i].value = value;
				bus.same += !moved;
				return (moved && bus.said < SAID_FIRST);
			}
		}
	}
	row = offset == bus.last ? row + 1 : 0;
	if (row >= 3) {
		bus.again++;
		bus.last_value = value;
		return (false);
	}
	say_repeats();
	bus.last = offset;
	return (bus.said < SAID_FIRST);
}

static u32
bus_read32(struct ath11k_base *ab, u32 offset)
{
	u32 value = 0;

	if (refused(ab, offset)) {
		return (0);
	}
	bus.reads++;
	if (bus.how >= 2 && ab->mem != NULL) {
		value = ioread32((u8 *)ab->mem + window(ab, offset));
	}
	if (bus.said < SAID_FIRST) {
		say_repeats();
		bus.last = ~0u;
		bus.said++;
		printf("lx: the chip's %#x reads %#x%s\n", offset, value, bus.how >= 2 ? "" : " (NOT READ: wifi_lx=1)");
	}
	return (value);
}

static void
bus_write32(struct ath11k_base *ab, u32 offset, u32 value)
{
	if (refused(ab, offset)) {
		return;
	}
	bus.writes++;
	if (said_write(offset, value)) {
		bus.said++;
		printf("lx: %s the chip's %#x (at +%#x of its block): %#x\n", bus.how >= 2 ? "about to write" : "NOT WRITTEN (wifi_lx=1):",
		    offset, window(ab, offset), value);
	}
	if (bus.how >= 2 && ab->mem != NULL) {
		__asm __volatile("dsb sy");	/* (what was written to a ring is in memory before the radio is told of it) */
		iowrite32(value, (u8 *)ab->mem + window(ab, offset));
	}
}

/*
 * In place of the radio's interrupts: each copy engine is looked at as its interrupt would have
 * ath11k do (ce.c: ath11k_ce_per_engine_service(), which takes what has been received to its
 * owner and posts fresh buffers), and once the driver has "enabled the data path's interrupts"
 * so is each of the groups its rings are in (dp.c: ath11k_dp_service_srng(), which is what the
 * driver's NAPI poll calls: frames received, frames that have been sent, errors, the reorder
 * block's answers). Once a millisecond while nothing comes; again at once while a group has
 * used up what it was allowed in one go.
 *
 * With the radio's interrupts (wifi_irq=1) the rings are looked at when one arrives, on the
 * kernel's thread for them (irq_ce(), irq_group() below), and this thread looks only every 100 ms,
 * to count what the interrupts left behind and to take care of it.
 */
#define DATA_BUDGET	64

static void
bus_looks(void *argument)
{
	struct ath11k_base *ab = argument;
	unsigned long long said = lx_os_nanoseconds();

	bus.looks = true;
	while (bus.looking) {
		bool more = false;

		if (lx_os_nanoseconds() - said > 300000000000ull) {	/* every five minutes: how the station and memory stand */
			said = lx_os_nanoseconds();
			lx_station_say();
			lx_memory_say();
			if (bus.irq) {
				irq_say();
			}
		}

		if (bus.irq) {
			mutex_lock(&bus.service);
		}
		for (unsigned i = 0; i < ab->hw_params.ce_count; i++) {
			ath11k_ce_per_engine_service(ab, i);
		}
		for (unsigned i = 0; bus.data && i < ATH11K_EXT_IRQ_GRP_NUM_MAX; i++) {
			int done = ath11k_dp_service_srng(ab, &ab->ext_irq_grp[i], DATA_BUDGET);

			more |= done >= DATA_BUDGET;
			bus.late += bus.irq && done > 0;
		}
		if (bus.irq) {
			mutex_unlock(&bus.service);
		}
		if (!more) {
			lx_pause_ms(bus.irq ? 100 : 1);
		}
	}
	bus.looks = false;
}

/*
 * The copy engines are looked at no more, and no register is touched from here on. This is what
 * the driver's "interrupts off" comes to here, and it comes in time: on its way down the driver
 * says that after its last word to the firmware over a copy engine and before it asks for the
 * mode "off".
 */
static void
bus_quiet(void)
{
	if (bus.irq && bus.looking) {
		irq_say();
	}
	if (bus.irq) {
		lx_os_irq_detach_all();
	}
	bus.data = false;
	bus.looking = false;
	while (bus.looks) {
		lx_pause_ms(1);
	}
	say_repeats();
}

/*
 * A request of the driver's to the firmware, on its way out (linux/soc/qcom/qmi.h, ours). One
 * matters here: the mode. With any mode but mission the radio's registers stop answering, and
 * the driver does not always let go of the copy engines first -- where its start fails late,
 * core.c asks for the mode "off" and stops the bus after that (ath11k_core_stop()). So the
 * copy engines are let go of here, before the request leaves.
 */
int
lx_qmi_send_request(struct qmi_handle *qmi, struct sockaddr_qrtr *sq, struct qmi_txn *txn, int msg_id, size_t largest,
    const struct qmi_elem_info *ei, const void *structure)
{
	if (msg_id == QMI_WLANFW_WLAN_MODE_REQ_V01) {
		u32 mode = ((const struct qmi_wlanfw_wlan_mode_req_msg_v01 *)structure)->mode;

		if (mode != ATH11K_FIRMWARE_MODE_NORMAL && bus.looking) {
			printf("lx: the driver asks for mode %u while the copy engines are still looked at: they are let go of first\n",
			    mode);
		}
		if (mode != ATH11K_FIRMWARE_MODE_NORMAL) {
			bus_quiet();
		}
		bus.mission = mode == ATH11K_FIRMWARE_MODE_NORMAL;
		lx_tell("lx: the firmware is asked for mode %u (0: mission, 4: off, 7: calibration)\n", mode);
	}
	return (qmi_send_request(qmi, sq, txn, msg_id, largest, ei, structure));
}

/* ---- the radio's interrupts ---------------------------------------------------------------------- */

/* A copy engine's interrupt (pcic.c: ath11k_pcic_ce_interrupt_handler() and its tasklet). */
static void
irq_ce(void *argument)
{
	struct ath11k_ce_pipe *pipe = argument;

	mutex_lock(&bus.service);
	ath11k_ce_per_engine_service(pipe->ab, pipe->pipe_num);
	mutex_unlock(&bus.service);
	lx_os_irq_enable(bus.ce_vector[pipe->pipe_num]);
}

/* A data path group's (pcic.c: ath11k_pcic_ext_interrupt_handler() and its NAPI poll, until it has less to do than allowed). */
static void
irq_group(void *argument)
{
	struct ath11k_ext_irq_grp *group = argument;
	int done;

	mutex_lock(&bus.service);
	do {
		done = bus.data ? ath11k_dp_service_srng(group->ab, group, DATA_BUDGET) : 0;
	} while (done >= DATA_BUDGET);
	mutex_unlock(&bus.service);
	if (bus.data) {
		lx_os_irq_enable(bus.group_vector[group->grp_id]);
	}
}

/* pcic.c: ath11k_pcic_config_irq(), for this chip: which vector is whose, and the functions for them, all masked */
static int
irq_attach(struct ath11k_base *ab)
{
	unsigned index = 0;
	int ret;

	for (unsigned i = 0; i < CE_COUNT_MAX; i++) {
		bus.ce_vector[i] = -1;
	}
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < ATH11K_EXT_IRQ_GRP_NUM_MAX; i++) {
		bus.group_vector[i] = -1;
	}
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < ab->hw_params.ce_count; i++) {
		if (ath11k_ce_get_attr_flags(ab, i) & CE_ATTR_DIS_INTR) {
			continue;
		}
		bus.ce_vector[i] = (int)(index++ % msi_users[0].num_vectors + msi_users[0].base_vector);
		if ((ret = lx_os_irq_attach((unsigned)bus.ce_vector[i], irq_ce, &ab->ce.ce_pipe[i])) != 0) {
			return (ret);
		}
	}
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < ATH11K_EXT_IRQ_GRP_NUM_MAX; i++) {
		const struct ath11k_hw_ring_mask *mask = ab->hw_params.ring_mask;

		ab->ext_irq_grp[i].ab = ab;
		ab->ext_irq_grp[i].grp_id = i;
		if (!(mask->tx[i] || mask->rx[i] || mask->rx_err[i] || mask->rx_wbm_rel[i] || mask->reo_status[i] ||
		    mask->rxdma2host[i] || mask->host2rxdma[i] || mask->rx_mon_status[i])) {
			continue;
		}
		bus.group_vector[i] = (int)(i % msi_users[1].num_vectors + msi_users[1].base_vector);
		if ((ret = lx_os_irq_attach((unsigned)bus.group_vector[i], irq_group, &ab->ext_irq_grp[i])) != 0) {
			return (ret);
		}
	}
	return (0);
}

/* What came, by vector: for the log. */
static void
irq_say(void)
{
	char line[400] = "";

	for (unsigned v = 0; v < msi_config.total_vectors; v++) {
		unsigned long long count = lx_os_irq_count(v);

		if (count != 0) {
			snprintf(line + strlen(line), sizeof(line) - strlen(line), " %u: %llu,", v, count);
		}
	}
	lx_tell("lx: the radio's interrupts by vector (copy engines 0-9, the data path's groups 10-27):%s the thread found %llu "
	    "times work no interrupt had brought\n", line[0] ? line : " NONE", bus.late);
}

static int
bus_get_user_msi_vector(struct ath11k_base *ab, char *user, int *count, u32 *user_base_data, u32 *base_vector)
{
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < nitems(msi_users); i++) {
		if (strcmp(user, msi_users[i].name) == 0) {
			*count = (int)msi_users[i].num_vectors;
			*base_vector = msi_users[i].base_vector;
			*user_base_data = msi_users[i].base_vector + ab->pci.msi.ep_base_data;
			return (0);
		}
	}
	return (-EINVAL);
}

static void
bus_get_msi_address(struct ath11k_base *ab, u32 *low, u32 *high)
{
	*low = ab->pci.msi.addr_lo;
	*high = ab->pci.msi.addr_hi;
}

/* pcic.c: ath11k_pcic_get_ce_msi_idx(): the copy engines with interrupts, counted */
static void
bus_get_ce_msi_idx(struct ath11k_base *ab, u32 ce_id, u32 *index)
{
	u32 n = 0;

	for (u32 i = 0; i < ab->hw_params.ce_count && i != ce_id; i++) {
		n += !(ath11k_ce_get_attr_flags(ab, i) & CE_ATTR_DIS_INTR);
	}
	*index = n;
}

/* pcic.c: ath11k_pcic_start(), with the thread above where it enables the interrupts */
static int
bus_start(struct ath11k_base *ab)
{
	int ret;

	set_bit(ATH11K_FLAG_DEVICE_INIT_DONE, &ab->dev_flags);
	printf("lx: the driver starts the bus: buffers for the copy engines that receive (%u reads and %u writes of the chip's "
	    "registers so far; the configuration the firmware was sent named %u shadow registers)\n", bus.reads, bus.writes,
	    ab->qmi.ce_cfg.shadow_reg_v2_len);
	ath11k_ce_rx_post_buf(ab);
	say_repeats();
	lx_tell("lx: the rings are set up and the copy engines have their buffers: the bus is started\n");
	/*
	 * (here and not when the driver is set up: the firmware is asked for calibration in between, and
	 * the copy engines are let go of for that, interrupts and all; see lx_qmi_send_request())
	 */
	if (bus.irq && (ret = irq_attach(ab)) != 0) {
		lx_tell("lx: wifi_irq: the radio's interrupts cannot be had (%d): its rings are looked at every 100 ms only\n", ret);
		lx_os_irq_detach_all();
	}
	if (bus.irq) {
		for (unsigned i = 0; i < CE_COUNT_MAX; i++) {
			if (bus.ce_vector[i] >= 0) {
				lx_os_irq_enable((unsigned)bus.ce_vector[i]);
			}
		}
	}
	bus.looking = true;
	if (lx_os_thread("wifi-rings", bus_looks, ab) != 0) {
		bus.looking = false;
		return (-ENOMEM);
	}
	return (0);
}

/* pcic.c: ath11k_pcic_stop() */
static void
bus_stop(struct ath11k_base *ab)
{
	bus_quiet();
	bus.closed = true;
	timer_delete_sync(&ab->rx_replenish_retry);
	ath11k_ce_cleanup_pipes(ab);
	printf("lx: the driver stops the bus (%u reads and %u writes of the chip's registers in all, %u of the writes a ring's "
	    "pointer written what it held)\n", bus.reads, bus.writes, bus.same);
}

/* pcic.c: ath11k_pcic_map_service_to_pipe(): which copy engines carry a service, by the chip's table */
static int
bus_map_service_to_pipe(struct ath11k_base *ab, u16 service, u8 *up, u8 *down)
{
	bool has_up = false, has_down = false;

	for (u32 i = 0; i < ab->hw_params.svc_to_ce_map_len; i++) {
		const struct service_to_pipe *entry = &ab->hw_params.svc_to_ce_map[i];
		u32 direction = __le32_to_cpu(entry->pipedir);

		if (__le32_to_cpu(entry->service_id) != service) {
			continue;
		}
		if (direction == PIPEDIR_IN || direction == PIPEDIR_INOUT) {
			*down = (u8)__le32_to_cpu(entry->pipenum);
			has_down = true;
		}
		if (direction == PIPEDIR_OUT || direction == PIPEDIR_INOUT) {
			*up = (u8)__le32_to_cpu(entry->pipenum);
			has_up = true;
		}
	}
	return (has_up && has_down ? 0 : -ENOENT);
}

static int
bus_power_up(struct ath11k_base *ab)
{
	return (-lx_os_rproc_boot());
}

static void
bus_power_down(struct ath11k_base *ab, bool is_suspend)
{
}

/* pcic.c: ath11k_pcic_ext_irq_enable(): the data path's rings are set up, and are looked at from here on */
static void
bus_irq_enable(struct ath11k_base *ab)
{
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < ATH11K_EXT_IRQ_GRP_NUM_MAX; i++) {
		ab->ext_irq_grp[i].ab = ab;
		ab->ext_irq_grp[i].grp_id = i;
	}
	bus.data = true;
	for (unsigned i = 0; bus.irq && i < ATH11K_EXT_IRQ_GRP_NUM_MAX; i++) {
		if (bus.group_vector[i] >= 0) {
			lx_os_irq_enable((unsigned)bus.group_vector[i]);
		}
	}
}

static void
bus_irq_disable(struct ath11k_base *ab)
{
	bus_quiet();
}

static const struct ath11k_hif_ops bus_ops = {
	.read32 = bus_read32,
	.write32 = bus_write32,
	.irq_enable = bus_irq_enable,
	.irq_disable = bus_irq_disable,
	.start = bus_start,
	.stop = bus_stop,
	.map_service_to_pipe = bus_map_service_to_pipe,
	.power_up = bus_power_up,
	.power_down = bus_power_down,
	/* (no interrupt vectors are offered: the rings are then set up without any, see ce.c) */
};

/* ... and with the radio's interrupts: the vectors, and where the radio writes to raise one */
static const struct ath11k_hif_ops bus_ops_irq = {
	.read32 = bus_read32,
	.write32 = bus_write32,
	.irq_enable = bus_irq_enable,
	.irq_disable = bus_irq_disable,
	.start = bus_start,
	.stop = bus_stop,
	.map_service_to_pipe = bus_map_service_to_pipe,
	.power_up = bus_power_up,
	.power_down = bus_power_down,
	.get_user_msi_vector = bus_get_user_msi_vector,
	.get_msi_address = bus_get_msi_address,
	.get_ce_msi_idx = bus_get_ce_msi_idx,
};

/* ---- the device tree, of which there is none ------------------------------------------------------ */

int
of_property_read_string(const struct device_node *np, const char *name, const char **out)
{
	return (-EINVAL);
}

bool
of_machine_is_compatible(const char *compatible)
{
	return (false);
}

int
of_reserved_mem_region_to_resource(const struct device_node *np, unsigned int index, struct resource *res)

	return (-ENODEV);
}

/*
 * The radio's own address, which the driver asks its device for before it falls back on what the
 * firmware says (mac.c: ath11k_mac_register()); this radio's firmware says none. The kernel has
 * it, if it was given one. Nothing here says the address.
```
