```c
int
linuxkpi_device_get_mac_address(struct device *dev, char *address)
{
	return (lx_os_radio_address((unsigned char *)address) ? 0 : -ENOENT);
}

/* ---- what the firmware has said of the radio ------------------------------------------------------- */

/* After "unified ready": what wmi.c has kept of the firmware's two announcements. */
static void
say_radio(struct ath11k_base *ab)
{
	const struct ath11k_targ_cap *t = &ab->target_caps;

	printf("lx: THE FIRMWARE SAYS OF THE RADIO: %u radio(s); %u chains (mask %#x); up to %u channels in a scan, %u MACs; "
	    "transmit power %d..%d; phy %#x, HT %#x, VHT %#x (MCS %#x), system %#x\n", ab->num_radios, t->num_rf_chains,
	    t->txrx_chainmask, t->max_num_scan_channels, t->max_supported_macs, (int)t->hw_min_tx_power, (int)t->hw_max_tx_power,
	    t->phy_capability, t->ht_cap_info, t->vht_cap_info, t->vht_supp_mcs, t->sys_cap_info);
	/* (the second number is from the same structure of "ready" as the address: it shows that was read) */
	printf("lx: its address, by the firmware: %02x:%02x:%02x:%02x:%02x:%02x (and its check sum of the packet log's "
	    "definitions: %#x)\n", ab->mac_addr[0], ab->mac_addr[1], ab->mac_addr[2], ab->mac_addr[3], ab->mac_addr[4],
	    ab->mac_addr[5], ab->pktlog_defs_checksum);
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < ab->num_radios && i < MAX_RADIOS; i++) {
		const struct ath11k_hal_reg_capabilities_ext *r = &ab->hal_reg_cap[i];
		const struct ath11k_pdev_cap *c = &ab->pdevs[i].cap;

		printf("lx: radio %u (pdev %u, phy %u): bands%s%s (%#x); 2.4 GHz %u..%u MHz, 5 GHz and up %u..%u MHz; regulatory "
		    "domain %#x, wireless modes %#x; chains tx %#x rx %#x; VHT %#x, A-MPDU density %u\n", i, ab->pdevs[i].pdev_id,
		    r->phy_id, c->supported_bands & WMI_HOST_WLAN_2G_CAP ? " 2.4 GHz" : "", c->supported_bands &
		    WMI_HOST_WLAN_5G_CAP ? " 5 GHz" : "", c->supported_bands, r->low_2ghz_chan, r->high_2ghz_chan, r->low_5ghz_chan,
		    r->high_5ghz_chan, r->eeprom_reg_domain, r->wireless_modes, c->tx_chain_mask, c->rx_chain_mask, c->vht_cap,
		    c->ampdu_density);
		for (unsigned band = 0; band < NUM_NL80211_BANDS; band++) {
			const struct ath11k_band_cap *b = &c->band[band];

			if (b->max_bw_supported == 0 && b->ht_cap_info == 0 && b->he_cap_info[0] == 0) {
				continue;
			}
			printf("lx: radio %u, band %u (0: 2.4 GHz, 1: 5 GHz, 3: 6 GHz): widest channel code %u, HT %#x, HE %#x %#x "
			    "(MCS %#x), HE at 6 GHz %#x\n", i, band, b->max_bw_supported, b->ht_cap_info, b->he_cap_info[0],
			    b->he_cap_info[1], b->he_mcs, b->he_6ghz_capa);
		}
	}
}

/* ---- the entries ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

static struct ath11k_base *volatile driver;	/* the driver, while it is up: between lx_start() and lx_stop() */

int
lx_start(void)
{
	static struct device device;
	static struct device_node node;
	struct ath11k_base *ab;
	unsigned long long began;
	bool up;
	int ret;

	bus.how = lx_os_option("wifi_lx");
	if (lx_prepare() != 0) {
		lx_tell("lx: no thread, or no memory the radio can be given\n");
		return (ENOMEM);
	}
	/* what the driver has to say while it is being looked into; not in a session that just uses the radio */
	if (lx_os_option("wifi_quiet")) {
		ath11k_debug_mask = 0;
		bus.said = SAID_FIRST;
	} else {
		ath11k_debug_mask = ATH11K_DBG_QMI | ATH11K_DBG_BOOT | ATH11K_DBG_AHB | ATH11K_DBG_WMI | ATH11K_DBG_REG | ATH11K_DBG_MAC;
	}
	/*
	 * The driver's parameter "frame_mode": Ethernet. The firmware then puts frames into 802.11
	 * and takes them out of it, and ciphers them: what passes between the driver and the layer
	 * above is what goes over a cable.
	 */
	ath11k_frame_mode = ATH11K_HW_TXRX_ETHERNET;
	device.of_node = &node;
	device.kobj.name = "wifi";

	/* ahb.c: ath11k_ahb_probe(), for this chip */
	ab = ath11k_core_alloc(&device, 0, ATH11K_BUS_AHB);
	if (ab == NULL) {
		return (ENOMEM);
	}
	ab->hif.ops = &bus_ops;
	bus.irq = false;
	if (lx_os_option("wifi_irq")) {
		unsigned long long address;
		unsigned data;

		/* (pcic.c: ath11k_pcic_init_msi_config() and what ahb.c takes from the device tree for this chip) */
		if (lx_os_irq_msi(&address, &data)) {
			mutex_init(&bus.service);
			ab->pci.msi.config = &msi_config;
			ab->pci.msi.addr_lo = (u32)address;
			ab->pci.msi.addr_hi = (u32)(address >> 32);
			ab->pci.msi.ep_base_data = data;
			set_bit(ATH11K_FLAG_MULTI_MSI_VECTORS, &ab->dev_flags);
			ab->hif.ops = &bus_ops_irq;
			bus.irq = true;
		} else {
			lx_tell("lx: wifi_irq: the radio cannot be shown where to raise an interrupt: the rings are looked at, as before\n");
		}
	}
	ab->hw_rev = ATH11K_HW_WCN6750_HW10;
	ab->fw_mode = ATH11K_FIRMWARE_MODE_NORMAL;
	if ((ret = ath11k_core_pre_init(ab)) != 0 || (ret = ath11k_hal_srng_init(ab)) != 0 || (ret = ath11k_ce_alloc_pipes(ab)) != 0) {
		lx_tell("lx: the driver does not get as far as its exchange with the firmware: %d\n", ret);
		return (-ret);
	}
	ab->qmi.ce_cfg.tgt_ce_len = ab->hw_params.target_ce_count;
	ab->qmi.ce_cfg.tgt_ce = ab->hw_params.target_ce_config;
	ab->qmi.ce_cfg.svc_to_ce_map_len = ab->hw_params.svc_to_ce_map_len;
	ab->qmi.ce_cfg.svc_to_ce_map = ab->hw_params.svc_to_ce_map;
	ab->qmi.service_ins_id = ab->hw_params.qmi_service_ins_id;
	printf("lx: the driver (\"%s\") is set up; its exchange with the firmware begins (registers: %s)\n", ab->hw_params.name,
	    bus.how >= 2 ? "for real" : "NOT TOUCHED, wifi_lx=1");
	if ((ret = ath11k_core_init(ab)) != 0) {
		lx_tell("lx: the driver's start fails: %d\n", ret);
		return (-ret);
	}

	/*
	 * The rest happens on the driver's own threads, until core.c has been through its start (it
	 * says so with the flag below, whether that went well or not) or the exchange has failed.
	 * It went well if the bus is still up: core.c stops it where it gives up.
	 */
	began = lx_os_nanoseconds();
	while (!test_bit(ATH11K_FLAG_REGISTERED, &ab->dev_flags) && !test_bit(ATH11K_FLAG_QMI_FAIL, &ab->dev_flags) &&
	    lx_os_nanoseconds() - began < 60000000000ull) {
		lx_pause_ms(10);
	}
	up = test_bit(ATH11K_FLAG_REGISTERED, &ab->dev_flags) && bus.looks;
	lx_tell("lx: %llu ms after its start the driver %s; its flags: %#lx\n", (lx_os_nanoseconds() - began) / 1000000ull,
	    up ? "IS UP as far as it is built: the firmware has said \"unified ready\"" : test_bit(ATH11K_FLAG_REGISTERED,
	    &ab->dev_flags) ? "HAS GIVEN UP on the way and wound itself down" : "HAS NOT GOT THROUGH its exchange with the firmware",
	    ab->dev_flags);
	if (!up) {
		lx_pause_ms(600);		/* (for core.c to have wound down: the mode "off") */
		ath11k_qmi_deinit_service(ab);
		return (test_bit(ATH11K_FLAG_REGISTERED, &ab->dev_flags) ? ETIMEDOUT : EIO);
	}
	lx_pause_ms(1000);			/* (for what the firmware says unasked once it is ready) */
	say_radio(ab);

	driver = ab;
	if (lx_os_option("wifi_station")) {
		/* whoever wants a network asks the kernel, and the kernel asks the station: the driver stays up until lx_stop() */
		if ((ret = lx_station_offer()) == 0) {
			return (0);
		}
	} else if (lx_os_option("wifi_join")) {
		if ((ret = lx_station_join()) == 0) {
			if (lx_os_option("wifi_hold")) {	/* (seconds to stay before returning: to see frames pass) */
				lx_pause_ms(1000 * lx_os_option("wifi_hold"));
				lx_station_say();
			}
			return (0);			/* the network is joined, and the driver stays up until lx_stop() */
		}
	} else {
		ret = lx_os_option("wifi_scan") ? lx_station_scan() : 0;
	}
	lx_stop();
	return (ret);
}

/* The thread that counts the ticks, and the memory the radio is shown: once. 0, or an errno. */
int
lx_prepare(void)
{
	return (lx_base_init() != 0 || lx_pool_init() != 0 ? ENOMEM : 0);
}

/* The network left, and the driver down as its own removal does it (the copy engines are let go of on the way: bus_quiet()). */
void
lx_stop(void)
{
	struct ath11k_base *ab = driver;

	if (ab == NULL) {
		return;
	}
	driver = NULL;
	lx_station_withdraw();
	lx_station_leave();
	ath11k_core_deinit(ab);
	lx_tell("lx: the driver is down again\n");
}

int
lx_transmit(const unsigned char *frame, unsigned long length)
{
	return (driver != NULL ? lx_station_send(frame, length) : ENETDOWN);
}

```

`wifi/lx/src/lx_wpa.c`:

```c
/*
 * The arithmetic of WPA2 with a passphrase (lx_wpa.h): SHA-1 and HMAC over it (FIPS 180, RFC
 * 2104), the key of a name and a passphrase (PBKDF2, RFC 8018), the function that makes the
 * handshake's keys out of that key, two addresses and two nonces (IEEE 802.11-2020, 12.7.1.2),
 * AES decryption and the unwrapping of a key with it (FIPS 197, RFC 3394), and the messages of
 * the four-way and the group-key handshake (12.7.6, 12.7.7; figure 12-35 is the layout).
 *
 * Nothing here is taken from another implementation; the tests in tools/wpa-test check it
 * against the standards' own examples and against Python's hashlib and "cryptography".
 * Nothing here is written for speed, and nothing here says a key in a message.
 */
#ifdef _KERNEL
#include <sys/param.h>
#include <sys/systm.h>
#else
#include <stdint.h>
#include <string.h>
#endif

#include "lx_wpa.h"

/* ---- SHA-1 ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ */

struct sha1 {
	uint32_t h[5];
	uint64_t length;			/* bytes so far */
	uint8_t block[64];
};

static uint32_t
rol(uint32_t x, unsigned n)
{
	return (x << n | x >> (32 - n));
}

static void
sha1_block(uint32_t h[5], const uint8_t *p)
{
	uint32_t w[80], a = h[0], b = h[1], c = h[2], d = h[3], e = h[4];

	for (unsigned t = 0; t < 16; t++) {
		w[t] = (uint32_t)p[4 * t] << 24 | (uint32_t)p[4 * t + 1] << 16 | (uint32_t)p[4 * t + 2] << 8 | p[4 * t + 3];
	}
	for (unsigned t = 16; t < 80; t++) {
		w[t] = rol(w[t - 3] ^ w[t - 8] ^ w[t - 14] ^ w[t - 16], 1);
	}
	for (unsigned t = 0; t < 80; t++) {
		uint32_t f = t < 20 ? ((b & c) | (~b & d)) + 0x5a827999 : t < 40 ? (b ^ c ^ d) + 0x6ed9eba1 : t < 60 ?
		    ((b & c) | (b & d) | (c & d)) + 0x8f1bbcdc : (b ^ c ^ d) + 0xca62c1d6;
		uint32_t next = rol(a, 5) + f + e + w[t];

		e = d;
		d = c;
		c = rol(b, 30);
		b = a;
		a = next;
	}
	h[0] += a;
	h[1] += b;
	h[2] += c;
	h[3] += d;
	h[4] += e;
}

static void
sha1_begin(struct sha1 *s)
{
	s->h[0] = 0x67452301;
	s->h[1] = 0xefcdab89;
	s->h[2] = 0x98badcfe;
	s->h[3] = 0x10325476;
	s->h[4] = 0xc3d2e1f0;
	s->length = 0;
}

static void
sha1_more(struct sha1 *s, const uint8_t *data, unsigned length)
{
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < length; i++) {
		s->block[s->length++ % 64] = data[i];
		if (s->length % 64 == 0) {
			sha1_block(s->h, s->block);
		}
	}
}

static void
sha1_end(struct sha1 *s, uint8_t digest[20])
{
	uint64_t bits = s->length * 8;
	uint8_t tail[8];

	sha1_more(s, (const uint8_t *)"\x80", 1);
	while (s->length % 64 != 56) {
		sha1_more(s, (const uint8_t *)"", 1);
	}
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < 8; i++) {
		tail[i] = (uint8_t)(bits >> (56 - 8 * i));
	}
	sha1_more(s, tail, 8);
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < 20; i++) {
		digest[i] = (uint8_t)(s->h[i / 4] >> (24 - 8 * (i % 4)));
	}
}

/* HMAC-SHA1 of several pieces in a row. */
static void
hmac_sha1(const uint8_t *key, unsigned key_length, const uint8_t *const pieces[], const unsigned lengths[], unsigned count,
    uint8_t digest[20])
{
	uint8_t pad[64], hashed[20], inner[20];
	struct sha1 s;

	if (key_length > 64) {
		sha1_begin(&s);
		sha1_more(&s, key, key_length);
		sha1_end(&s, hashed);
		key = hashed;
		key_length = 20;
	}
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < 64; i++) {
		pad[i] = (i < key_length ? key[i] : 0) ^ 0x36;
	}
	sha1_begin(&s);
	sha1_more(&s, pad, 64);
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < count; i++) {
		sha1_more(&s, pieces[i], lengths[i]);
	}
	sha1_end(&s, inner);
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < 64; i++) {
		pad[i] ^= 0x36 ^ 0x5c;
	}
	sha1_begin(&s);
	sha1_more(&s, pad, 64);
	sha1_more(&s, inner, 20);
	sha1_end(&s, digest);
	memset(pad, 0, sizeof(pad));
	memset(inner, 0, sizeof(inner));
}

/* ---- the key of a name and a passphrase -------------------------------------------------------- */

/* PBKDF2 with HMAC-SHA1, 4096 rounds, 32 bytes: two blocks of 20, of the second the first 12. */
void
lx_wpa_pmk(const unsigned char *passphrase, unsigned passphrase_length, const unsigned char *name, unsigned name_length,
    unsigned char pmk[32])
{
	for (unsigned block = 1; block <= 2; block++) {
		const uint8_t number[4] = { 0, 0, 0, (uint8_t)block };
		const uint8_t *first[2] = { name, number };
		const unsigned first_lengths[2] = { name_length, 4 };
		uint8_t u[20], sum[20];

		hmac_sha1(passphrase, passphrase_length, first, first_lengths, 2, u);
		memcpy(sum, u, 20);
		for (unsigned round = 1; round < 4096; round++) {
			const uint8_t *again[1] = { u };
			const unsigned again_lengths[1] = { 20 };

			hmac_sha1(passphrase, passphrase_length, again, again_lengths, 1, u);
			for (unsigned i = 0; i < 20; i++) {
				sum[i] ^= u[i];
			}
		}
		memcpy(pmk + 20 * (block - 1), sum, block == 1 ? 20 : 12);
		memset(u, 0, sizeof(u));
		memset(sum, 0, sizeof(sum));
	}
}

/* The standard's PRF: HMAC-SHA1 of (label, a zero byte, data, a counter byte), block after block. */
static void
prf(const uint8_t *key, unsigned key_length, const char *label, const uint8_t *data, unsigned data_length, uint8_t *out,
    unsigned out_length)
{
	uint8_t zero = 0, counter = 0, digest[20];
	const uint8_t *pieces[4] = { (const uint8_t *)label, &zero, data, &counter };
	const unsigned lengths[4] = { (unsigned)strlen(label), 1, data_length, 1 };

	for (unsigned done = 0; done < out_length; done += 20, counter++) {
		hmac_sha1(key, key_length, pieces, lengths, 4, digest);
		memcpy(out + done, digest, out_length - done < 20 ? out_length - done : 20);
	}
	memset(digest, 0, sizeof(digest));
}

/* ---- AES-128, decryption only, and the unwrapping of a key --------------------------------------- */

static uint8_t sbox[256], inverse_sbox[256];

static uint8_t
times(uint8_t a, uint8_t b)			/* in GF(2^8) modulo x^8 + x^4 + x^3 + x + 1 */
{
	uint8_t product = 0;

	for (; b != 0; b >>= 1) {
		if (b & 1) {
			product ^= a;
		}
		a = (uint8_t)(a << 1 ^ (a & 0x80 ? 0x1b : 0));
	}
	return (product);
}

/* FIPS 197, 5.1.1: a byte's inverse in the field, then the affine map. */
static void
aes_tables(void)
{
	if (sbox[0] != 0) {
		return;
	}
	for (unsigned x = 0; x < 256; x++) {
		uint8_t inverse = 0, s;

		for (unsigned y = 1; y < 256 && x != 0; y++) {
			if (times((uint8_t)x, (uint8_t)y) == 1) {
				inverse = (uint8_t)y;
				break;
			}
		}
		s = inverse;
		for (unsigned i = 1; i < 5; i++) {
			s ^= (uint8_t)(inverse << i | inverse >> (8 - i));
		}
		s ^= 0x63;
		sbox[x] = s;
		inverse_sbox[s] = (uint8_t)x;
	}
}

static void
aes_keys(const uint8_t key[16], uint8_t round_keys[176])
{
	uint8_t constant = 1;

	aes_tables();
	memcpy(round_keys, key, 16);
	for (unsigned i = 16; i < 176; i += 4) {
		uint8_t word[4];

		memcpy(word, round_keys + i - 4, 4);
		if (i % 16 == 0) {
			uint8_t first = word[0];

			word[0] = sbox[word[1]] ^ constant;
			word[1] = sbox[word[2]];
			word[2] = sbox[word[3]];
			word[3] = sbox[first];
			constant = times(constant, 2);
		}
		for (unsigned j = 0; j < 4; j++) {
			round_keys[i + j] = round_keys[i - 16 + j] ^ word[j];
		}
	}
}

/* FIPS 197, 5.3: the inverse cipher on one block (bytes in column order: byte r of column c is s[4c + r]). */
static void
aes_decrypt(const uint8_t round_keys[176], uint8_t s[16])
{
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < 16; i++) {
		s[i] ^= round_keys[160 + i];
	}
	for (int round = 9; round >= 0; round--) {
		uint8_t t[16];

		for (unsigned c = 0; c < 4; c++) {		/* the rows shifted back, and the bytes substituted back */
			for (unsigned r = 0; r < 4; r++) {
				t[4 * ((c + r) % 4) + r] = inverse_sbox[s[4 * c + r]];
			}
		}
		for (unsigned i = 0; i < 16; i++) {
			t[i] ^= round_keys[16 * round + i];
		}
		if (round == 0) {
			memcpy(s, t, 16);
			break;
		}
		for (unsigned c = 0; c < 4; c++) {		/* the columns mixed back */
			const uint8_t *a = t + 4 * c;

			s[4 * c + 0] = times(a[0], 14) ^ times(a[1], 11) ^ times(a[2], 13) ^ times(a[3], 9);
			s[4 * c + 1] = times(a[0], 9) ^ times(a[1], 14) ^ times(a[2], 11) ^ times(a[3], 13);
			s[4 * c + 2] = times(a[0], 13) ^ times(a[1], 9) ^ times(a[2], 14) ^ times(a[3], 11);
			s[4 * c + 3] = times(a[0], 11) ^ times(a[1], 13) ^ times(a[2], 9) ^ times(a[3], 14);
		}
	}
}

/*
 * RFC 3394, 2.2.2: `wrapped` is 8 bytes longer than what comes out, which goes to `plain`. 0, or -1
 * if the length is not one a wrapped key has or the check value does not come out.
 */
static int
aes_unwrap(const uint8_t kek[16], const uint8_t *wrapped, unsigned length, uint8_t *plain)
{
	unsigned n = length / 8 - 1;
	uint8_t round_keys[176], a[8], block[16];
	int good = 0;

	if (length % 8 != 0 || length < 24) {
		return (-1);
	}
	aes_keys(kek, round_keys);
	memcpy(a, wrapped, 8);
	memcpy(plain, wrapped + 8, 8 * n);
	for (int j = 5; j >= 0; j--) {
		for (unsigned i = n; i >= 1; i--) {
			uint64_t t = (uint64_t)n * (unsigned)j + i;

			memcpy(block, a, 8);
			for (unsigned k = 0; k < 8; k++) {
				block[7 - k] ^= (uint8_t)(t >> (8 * k));
			}
			memcpy(block + 8, plain + 8 * (i - 1), 8);
			aes_decrypt(round_keys, block);
			memcpy(a, block, 8);
			memcpy(plain + 8 * (i - 1), block + 8, 8);
		}
	}
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < 8; i++) {
		good |= a[i] ^ 0xa6;
	}
	memset(round_keys, 0, sizeof(round_keys));
	memset(block, 0, sizeof(block));
	return (good == 0 ? 0 : -1);
}

/* ---- the handshake -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

/*
 * A key message, after the four bytes every EAPOL frame begins with (version, type 3, length):
 *   4 the kind of descriptor (2: RSN)     5 what the message is (bits below)     7 key length
 *   9 replay counter (8)     17 nonce (32)     49 IV (16)     65 RSC (8)     73 reserved (8)
 *   81 MIC (16)     97 length of the key data     99 key data
 */
#define AT_KIND		4
#define AT_INFO		5
#define AT_REPLAY	9
#define AT_NONCE	17
#define AT_RSC		65
#define AT_MIC		81
#define AT_DATA_LENGTH	97
#define AT_DATA		99
#define MESSAGE_MOST	640

#define INFO_VERSION	0x0007			/* 2: HMAC-SHA1 for the MIC, the AES key wrap for the key data */
#define INFO_PAIRWISE	0x0008
#define INFO_INSTALL	0x0040
#define INFO_ACK	0x0080
#define INFO_MIC	0x0100
#define INFO_SECURE	0x0200
#define INFO_ENCRYPTED	0x1000

static void
mic_of(const struct lx_wpa *wpa, const uint8_t *message, unsigned length, uint8_t mic[16])
{
	const uint8_t zeros[16] = { 0 };
	const uint8_t *pieces[3] = { message, zeros, message + AT_MIC + 16 };
	const unsigned lengths[3] = { AT_MIC, 16, length - AT_MIC - 16 };
	uint8_t digest[20];

	hmac_sha1(wpa->kck, 16, pieces, lengths, 3, digest);
	memcpy(mic, digest, 16);
}

/* The keys of the handshake and the pairwise key, from the PMK, both addresses and both nonces. */
static void
derive(struct lx_wpa *wpa)
{
	uint8_t data[76], keys[48];
	int own_first = memcmp(wpa->own, wpa->peer, 6) < 0, own_nonce_first = memcmp(wpa->own_nonce, wpa->peer_nonce, 32) < 0;

	memcpy(data, own_first ? wpa->own : wpa->peer, 6);
	memcpy(data + 6, own_first ? wpa->peer : wpa->own, 6);
	memcpy(data + 12, own_nonce_first ? wpa->own_nonce : wpa->peer_nonce, 32);
	memcpy(data + 44, own_nonce_first ? wpa->peer_nonce : wpa->own_nonce, 32);
	prf(wpa->pmk, 32, "Pairwise key expansion", data, sizeof(data), keys, sizeof(keys));
	memcpy(wpa->kck, keys, 16);
	memcpy(wpa->kek, keys + 16, 16);
	memcpy(wpa->pairwise, keys + 32, 16);
	memset(keys, 0, sizeof(keys));
	wpa->have_keys = 1;
}

/* Our message in answer to `message`: the same counter, our bits, our nonce and key data if any, signed. */
static void
answer(const struct lx_wpa *wpa, const uint8_t *message, unsigned info, const uint8_t *nonce, const uint8_t *data,
    unsigned data_length, uint8_t *reply, unsigned *reply_length)
{
	unsigned length = AT_DATA + data_length;

	memset(reply, 0, length);
	reply[0] = message[0];
	reply[1] = 3;
	reply[2] = (uint8_t)((length - 4) >> 8);
	reply[3] = (uint8_t)(length - 4);
	reply[AT_KIND] = 2;
	reply[AT_INFO] = (uint8_t)(info >> 8);
	reply[AT_INFO + 1] = (uint8_t)info;
	memcpy(reply + AT_REPLAY, message + AT_REPLAY, 8);
	if (nonce != NULL) {
		memcpy(reply + AT_NONCE, nonce, 32);
	}
	reply[AT_DATA_LENGTH] = (uint8_t)(data_length >> 8);
	reply[AT_DATA_LENGTH + 1] = (uint8_t)data_length;
	if (data_length != 0) {
		memcpy(reply + AT_DATA, data, data_length);
	}
	mic_of(wpa, reply, length, reply + AT_MIC);
	*reply_length = length;
}

/* The group key among what message 3 (or a group message) carries: an element 0xdd of the suite 00-0f-ac, kind 1. */
static int
group_key(struct lx_wpa *wpa, const uint8_t *data, unsigned length, const uint8_t *counter)
{
	for (unsigned at = 0; at + 2 <= length && at + 2 + data[at + 1] <= length; at += 2 + data[at + 1]) {
		const uint8_t *e = data + at;

		if (e[0] == 0xdd && e[1] == 0) {
			break;				/* (padding from here on) */
		}
		if (e[0] == 0xdd && e[1] >= 6 + 5 && e[2] == 0x00 && e[3] == 0x0f && e[4] == 0xac && e[5] == 1 &&
		    e[1] - 6u <= sizeof(wpa->group)) {
			wpa->group_index = e[6] & 3;
			wpa->group_length = e[1] - 6u;
			memcpy(wpa->group, e + 8, wpa->group_length);
			memcpy(wpa->group_counter, counter, 8);
			return (0);
		}
	}
	return (-1);
}

int
lx_wpa_message(struct lx_wpa *wpa, const unsigned char *message, unsigned length, unsigned char *reply, unsigned *reply_length,
    const char **why)
{
	uint8_t mic[16], data[MESSAGE_MOST];
	unsigned info, body, data_length, difference = 0;
	const char *nothing;

	why = why != NULL ? why : &nothing;
	*why = "";
	*reply_length = 0;
	if (length < 4 || message[1] != 3) {
		return (LX_WPA_NOTHING);
	}
	body = (unsigned)message[2] << 8 | message[3];
	if (length < AT_DATA || 4 + body > length || 4 + body < AT_DATA || 4 + body > MESSAGE_MOST) {
		*why = "its length is not a key message's";
		return (LX_WPA_BAD);
	}
	length = 4 + body;
	info = (unsigned)message[AT_INFO] << 8 | message[AT_INFO + 1];
	data_length = (unsigned)message[AT_DATA_LENGTH] << 8 | message[AT_DATA_LENGTH + 1];
	if (message[AT_KIND] != 2) {
		*why = "it is not an RSN key message (WPA of the first kind?)";
		return (LX_WPA_BAD);
	}
	if ((info & INFO_VERSION) != 2) {
		*why = "its key descriptor is not version 2 (the network wants another kind of key management)";
		return (LX_WPA_BAD);
	}
	if (AT_DATA + data_length > length) {
		*why = "its key data is longer than the message";
		return (LX_WPA_BAD);
	}

	/* message 1: the access point's nonce, unsigned */
	if ((info & (INFO_PAIRWISE | INFO_ACK | INFO_MIC)) == (INFO_PAIRWISE | INFO_ACK)) {
		memcpy(wpa->peer_nonce, message + AT_NONCE, 32);
		derive(wpa);
		answer(wpa, message, 2 | INFO_PAIRWISE | INFO_MIC, wpa->own_nonce, wpa->rsn, wpa->rsn_length, reply, reply_length);
		return (LX_WPA_ANSWER);
	}

	/* everything else is signed, by an access point that has shown it has the key */
	if (!(info & INFO_MIC) || !(info & INFO_ACK)) {
		return (LX_WPA_NOTHING);
	}
	if (!wpa->have_keys) {
		*why = "it is signed, and there has been no message 1 to make the keys from";
		return (LX_WPA_BAD);
	}
	mic_of(wpa, message, length, mic);
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < 16; i++) {
		difference |= mic[i] ^ message[AT_MIC + i];
	}
	if (difference != 0) {
		*why = "its signature is not right (a wrong passphrase gives this)";
		return (LX_WPA_BAD);
	}
	if (wpa->replay_known && memcmp(message + AT_REPLAY, wpa->replay, 8) <= 0) {
		*why = "its counter is not beyond the last one's (a message played again)";
		return (LX_WPA_BAD);
	}
	if ((info & INFO_PAIRWISE) && memcmp(message + AT_NONCE, wpa->peer_nonce, 32) != 0) {
		*why = "its nonce is not message 1's";
		return (LX_WPA_BAD);
	}
	if (!(info & INFO_ENCRYPTED) || aes_unwrap(wpa->kek, message + AT_DATA, data_length, data) != 0) {
		*why = "its key data does not unwrap";
		return (LX_WPA_BAD);
	}
	if (group_key(wpa, data, data_length - 8, message + AT_RSC) != 0) {
		memset(data, 0, sizeof(data));
		*why = "there is no group key in it";
		return (LX_WPA_BAD);
	}
	memset(data, 0, sizeof(data));
	memcpy(wpa->replay, message + AT_REPLAY, 8);
	wpa->replay_known = 1;

	/* message 3 of the four, or message 1 of a new group key */
	if (info & INFO_PAIRWISE) {
		answer(wpa, message, 2 | INFO_PAIRWISE | INFO_MIC | INFO_SECURE, NULL, NULL, 0, reply, reply_length);
		return (LX_WPA_KEYS);
	}
	answer(wpa, message, 2 | INFO_MIC | INFO_SECURE, NULL, NULL, 0, reply, reply_length);
	return (LX_WPA_GROUP);
}

```

`wifi/lx/src/lx_wpa.h`:

```h
/*
 * WPA2 with a passphrase, as a station sees it: the key a name and a passphrase make, and the
 * four-way handshake in which an access point and a station prove that key to each other and
 * arrive at the keys their frames are ciphered with (IEEE 802.11-2020, 12.7; RSN, AKM "PSK",
 * key descriptor version 2: HMAC-SHA1 and the AES key wrap). lx_wpa.c is the arithmetic and
 * nothing else -- no radio, no kernel --, so that it runs on the machine the kernel is built on
 * (tools/wpa-test) as it runs in the kernel.
 */
#ifndef _LX_WPA_H_
#define _LX_WPA_H_

/* The key ("PMK") of a network's name and passphrase: 32 bytes. Slow on purpose: 8192 rounds of HMAC-SHA1. */
void lx_wpa_pmk(const unsigned char *passphrase, unsigned passphrase_length, const unsigned char *name, unsigned name_length,
    unsigned char pmk[32]);

struct lx_wpa {
	unsigned char pmk[32];
	unsigned char own[6], peer[6];		/* the station's address and the access point's */
	unsigned char own_nonce[32];		/* 32 bytes nobody can guess, fresh for every handshake */
	const unsigned char *rsn;		/* the station's RSN element as its association request had it ... */
	unsigned rsn_length;			/* ... which goes into message 2 */
	/* from here on: lx_wpa.c's */
	unsigned char peer_nonce[32];
	unsigned char kck[16], kek[16];		/* the keys the handshake's own messages are signed and ciphered with */
	unsigned char replay[8];		/* the counter of the last message accepted */
	int have_keys, replay_known;
	/* what comes out of it */
	unsigned char pairwise[16];		/* the key for frames between the two ("TK", CCMP) */
	unsigned char group[32];		/* the key the access point sends to everybody with ("GTK") ... */
	unsigned group_length, group_index;	/* ... its length, and its number (1 to 3) */
	unsigned char group_counter[8];		/* ... and the packet number its frames have got to ("RSC") */
};

/*
 * What a message of the handshake (an EAPOL frame: what follows the Ethernet header of a frame
 * of type 0x888e) calls for. `reply` has room for LX_WPA_REPLY_MOST bytes.
 */
#define LX_WPA_REPLY_MOST	256
enum {
	LX_WPA_BAD = -1,		/* not a message that can be answered: *why says what was wrong with it */
	LX_WPA_NOTHING = 0,		/* not for us to answer (not a key message) */
	LX_WPA_ANSWER = 1,		/* message 1: send the reply (message 2) */
	LX_WPA_KEYS = 2,		/* message 3: send the reply (message 4), then both keys are to be used */
	LX_WPA_GROUP = 3,		/* a new group key later on: send the reply, then use the new group key */
};
int lx_wpa_message(struct lx_wpa *wpa, const unsigned char *message, unsigned length, unsigned char *reply,
    unsigned *reply_length, const char **why);

#endif

```

`xl`:

```
#!/bin/bash
# xl — drive the XNU loader on the phone over USB (fastboot protocol).
#
#   xl enter            get the phone into the resident loader (from Android or stock fastboot)
#   xl run [N]          upload the current kernel, run it (optionally stop at checkpoint N), fetch the log
#   xl ramdisk [FILE]   upload the big system image (default userland/system.apfs) once; it stays in
#                       the phone's RAM across kernel runs and is the root filesystem (/dev/md0)
#                       ("xl ramdisk none" forgets it; the image sent with the kernel is then the root)
#   xl screenshot [F]   save what is in the phone's framebuffer as a PNG (default logs/screen.png);
#                       works during a run too (from another terminal)
#   xl recording [F]    fetch the screen recording the last run made (rec_secs=N among XL_CMDLINE) and
#                       make a video of it (default logs/recording.mp4)
#   xl sound [F]        fetch the sound the last run recorded (rec_sound=N among XL_CMDLINE: the first N
#                       seconds of what iOS played) and make a WAV file of it (default logs/sound.wav)
#   xl camera [P]       fetch the frames the last run's camera left (cam=3 and up among XL_CMDLINE) and make
#                       pictures of them (P-0.png, ...; default prefix logs/camera)
#   xl selftest         exercise only the kernel->loader return path
#   xl log              fetch the loader's current log; during a run, the kernel's log so far as well
#   xl stop             end the run in progress now (the kernel returns as when its time is up)
#   xl hang             watchdog test: make the loader hang on purpose
#   xl reboot           cold-reset the phone (back to Android)
#   xl reload           restart the phone into a freshly built loader (after changing xnuloader/)
#   xl memmap           the phone's memory map as its firmware reports it
#   xl state            where is the phone right now
#
# Logs land in logs/. Environment for `run`:
#   XL_CMDLINE  extra kernel boot-args; default "-v": the boot is shown as text on the phone's screen
#               (XL_CMDLINE="" for a blank screen, XL_CMDLINE="-v systrace=1" to trace failing syscalls)
#   XL_SECS     seconds after which the kernel returns to the loader on its own (default 8)
#   XL_SB_DELAY seconds SpringBoard waits before it starts (default 8; see userland/src/inject_sb.c)
#               Among XL_CMDLINE, for the phone: bootcpu=7 runs the kernel on the biggest core instead of
#               the small one the firmware starts on (the loader then watches from the first core, and a
#               kernel that hangs still gets its log out); cpufreq=1 sets that core to its top speed;
#               touchscreen=1 turns the touch screen on.
#   XL_RAMDISK  the image sent with the kernel: the small one that is mounted on /redwood
#               (default userland/root.apfs; "none" sends none). Without a system image in the
#               phone's RAM it is the root itself (e.g. XL_RAMDISK=userland/hello).
# One phone, several working copies: a run holds a lock, and `stop` and `reboot` from another working
# copy than the one it was started from are refused (XL_FORCE=1 to end it all the same). While a run
# is in progress every other command is refused too, `ramdisk` among them.
# The lock says whether a run is live; it says nothing about the image resident in the phone's memory,
# which outlives both the lock and any note beside it and belongs to whoever uploaded it last. So
# `ramdisk` records who uploaded what, and how big it was, in $PHONE.ramdisk, and `run` prints that
# when the last upload was not from this copy. The record starts empty -- an upload by a copy without
# this change leaves none -- and `run` says so rather than assuming.
cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")" || exit 1
# the kernel and the loader built here, or else the ones that come with the repository
K=xnu-src/xnu-8796.121.2/BUILD/obj/DEVELOPMENT_ARM64_BCM2837/mach.development.bcm2837
[ -f $K ] || K=prebuilt/mach.development.bcm2837
L=xnuloader/loader.efi
[ -f $L ] || L=prebuilt/loader.efi
mkdir -p logs
# There is one phone, whichever working copy (tools/new-workspace.sh) talks to it: the locks are
# outside all of them.
PHONE=${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/hackios-phone

# one fastboot at a time (a run in one terminal, "xl screenshot" in another): each takes the lock for itself
fb() { flock -w 90 $PHONE.lock timeout "${FB_TIMEOUT:-10}" fastboot "$@" 2>&1; }
# does the loader answer while its kernel runs (0.5 and later)? an older one answers only when the run is over
live_loader() { fb getvar version | grep -Eq 'version: 0\.([5-9]|[1-9][0-9])'; }
in_fastboot() { fastboot devices 2>/dev/null | grep -q fastboot; }
is_loader() { in_fastboot && fb getvar product | grep -q 'product: xnuloader'; }
state() {
	if is_loader; then echo loader
	elif in_fastboot; then echo fastboot
	elif [ "$(adb get-state 2>/dev/null)" = device ]; then echo android
	else echo absent; fi
}
wait_for() { # wait_for <state> <seconds>
	local i
	for ((i = 0; i < $2; i += 2)); do [ "$(state)" = "$1" ] && return 0; sleep 2; done
	return 1
}

enter() {
	case "$(state)" in
	loader) return 0 ;;
	android) adb reboot bootloader; wait_for fastboot 60 || { echo "xl: phone did not reach fastboot"; return 1; } ;;
	fastboot) ;;
	absent) echo "xl: waiting for the phone (Android or fastboot)..."
		local i; for ((i = 0; i < 180; i += 3)); do [ "$(state)" != absent ] && break; sleep 3; done
		[ "$(state)" = absent ] && { echo "xl: phone not reachable"; return 1; }
		enter; return ;;
	esac
	xnuloader/mkpayload.py -o usb-payload.bin loader.efi=$L --usb >/dev/null &&
		./mkxnuimg.py -p usb-payload.bin -o xnu-usb.img >/dev/null || { echo "xl: image build failed"; return 1; }
	# Right after the phone enters fastboot the first "boot" is sometimes not taken: try twice.
	local try
	for try in 1 2; do
		FB_TIMEOUT=40 fb boot xnu-usb.img | grep -q OKAY || { sleep 3; continue; }
		sleep 6
		wait_for loader 30 && return 0
		[ "$(state)" = fastboot ] || break
	done
	echo "xl: loader did not come up on USB (state: $(state))"; return 1
}

fetch_log() { # fetch_log <file>
	rm -f "$1"
	FB_TIMEOUT=20 fb get_staged "$1" >/dev/null
	[ -s "$1" ] && tr -d '\0' < "$1" > "$1.tmp" && mv "$1.tmp" "$1"
}

run() { # run <oem command> <label>
	enter || return 1
	exec 8> $PHONE.run
	flock -n 8 || { echo "xl: a run is in progress, started from $(cat $PHONE.who 2>/dev/null) (xl stop ends it)"; return 1; }
	pwd > $PHONE.who
	local stamp log result
	stamp=$(date +%H%M%S); log="logs/$stamp-$2.log"
	if [ "$1" != "oem selftest" ]; then
		# The kernel hands control back after XL_SECS seconds even if it is just waiting.
		local rd=${XL_RAMDISK:-userland/root.apfs}
		case "$rd" in
		none|resident) rd= ;;
		*) [ -f "$rd" ] || { echo "xl: ramdisk $rd not found"; return 1; } ;;
		esac
		case $K in prebuilt/*) echo "xl: no kernel built here, running $K" >&2 ;; esac
		# The resident image: whose it is and how big, when the last upload was not from here.
		# Both values and not just "not from here", because a foreign image of the same kind
		# changes nothing, while a foreign one of another kind makes the boot fail in a way that
		# names neither it nor its owner -- /sbin/launchd.ios: No such file or directory, with a
		# perfectly good image on this side. The warning is not a refusal: relying on another
		# copy's upload is legitimate when you know what it is, and this says what it is.
		if [ -s $PHONE.ramdisk ]; then
			local rwho rwhat rsize
			IFS=$'\t' read -r rwho rwhat rsize < $PHONE.ramdisk
			if [ "$rwho" != "$(pwd)" ]; then
				echo "xl: the resident image was uploaded from $rwho:" \
				     "$rwhat, $(( rsize / 1048576 )) MB. Upload your own" \
				     "(./xl ramdisk FILE) unless that is the one you want" >&2
			fi
		else
			echo "xl: nothing here recorded who uploaded the resident image;" \
			     "if this run needs a particular one, upload it" >&2
		fi
		# A run about Wi-Fi is given the radio's own address, which is this phone's and so is kept in a
		# file that is not in the repository: fw-wifi/mac, one line, six bytes in hexadecimal with colons.
		local args=${XL_CMDLINE--v}
		case " $args " in
		*" wifi="*|*" wifi_step="*) [ -s fw-wifi/mac ] && args="$args wifi_mac=$(tr -d ' \n\r' < fw-wifi/mac)" ;;
		esac
		xnuloader/mkpayload.py -o run-payload.bin kernel=$K ${rd:+ramdisk=$rd} --cmdline "loader_return_after=${XL_SECS:-8} epoch=$(date +%s) sb_delay=${XL_SB_DELAY:-8} $args" >/dev/null || return 1
		FB_TIMEOUT=30 fb stage run-payload.bin | grep -q OKAY || { echo "xl: upload failed"; return 1; }
	fi
	local live=; live_loader && live=1
	fb $1 >/dev/null
	if [ -n "$live" ] && [ "$1" != "oem selftest" ]; then
		# the loader goes on answering: ask every two seconds until the result is no longer "running".
		# XL_FOLLOW=N: fetch the log as it stands every N seconds as well, so that a phone that
		# resets without a word leaves all it said up to then ($log.live)
		local deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + ${XL_SECS:-8} + 100 )) followed=$(date +%s)
		while :; do
			result=$(FB_TIMEOUT=15 fb getvar result | grep '^result:')
			case "$result" in ""|*running*) ;; *) break ;; esac
			[ "$(date +%s)" -ge "$deadline" ] && { result=; break; }
			if [ -n "$XL_FOLLOW" ] && [ $(( $(date +%s) - followed )) -ge "$XL_FOLLOW" ]; then
				followed=$(date +%s)
				# (XL_FOLLOW_KEEP=1: every one kept, $log.live.1, .2, ...: a long run's middle, which the log
				# itself loses once more than a megabyte follows it, is then all there)
				followed_n=$(( ${followed_n:-0} + 1 ))
				fb oem log | grep -q OKAY && fetch_log "$log.live" && { [ -z "$XL_FOLLOW_KEEP" ] || cp "$log.live" "$log.live.$followed_n"; }
			fi
			sleep 2
		done
	else
		result=$(FB_TIMEOUT=$(( ${XL_SECS:-8} + 100 )) fb getvar result | grep '^result:')
	fi
	if [ -z "$result" ]; then
		echo "xl: no answer — the kernel hung; waiting for the watchdog to reset the phone"
		wait_for android 120 && echo "xl: phone is back in Android" || echo "xl: phone did not come back (state: $(state))"
		return 2
	fi
	fetch_log "$log"
	ln -sf "$(basename "$log")" logs/last.log
	echo "$result  [$log]"
	case "$result" in
	*hung*|*no-such-core*)
		# (bootcpu=N) the kernel is stuck on the core it was given and nothing can take the core back
		echo "xl: the kernel did not come back from its core; restarting the phone"
		fb reboot >/dev/null
		return 2 ;;
	esac
}

recording() { # recording [file.mp4]
	enter || return 1
	local out=${1:-logs/recording.mp4}
	fb oem recording | grep -q OKAY || { echo "xl: the last run left no recording (boot-arg rec_secs=N)"; return 1; }
	FB_TIMEOUT=120 fb get_staged logs/recording.raw >/dev/null
	# (XL_REC_KEEP=1: the recording itself stays in logs/recording.raw, for tools/recording.py --frames)
	tools/recording.py logs/recording.raw "$out" && { [ -n "$XL_REC_KEEP" ] || rm -f logs/recording.raw; }
}

sound() { # sound [file.wav]
	enter || return 1
	local out=${1:-logs/sound.wav}
	fb oem sound | grep -q OKAY || { echo "xl: the last run left no sound recording (boot-arg rec_sound=N)"; return 1; }
	FB_TIMEOUT=120 fb get_staged logs/sound.raw >/dev/null
	tools/sound.py logs/sound.raw "$out" && rm -f logs/sound.raw
}

camera() { # camera [prefix]: the frames the last run's camera left (boot-arg cam=3 and up), as pictures
	enter || return 1
	local out=${1:-logs/camera}
	fb oem recording | grep -q OKAY || { echo "xl: the last run left no frames (boot-arg cam=3)"; return 1; }
	FB_TIMEOUT=120 fb get_staged logs/camera.raw >/dev/null
	tools/camraw.py logs/camera.raw "$out"
}

ramdisk() { # ramdisk [<file>|none]
	enter || return 1
	if [ "$1" = none ]; then
		fb oem ramdisk none >/dev/null; rm -f $PHONE.ramdisk
		echo "xl: resident ramdisk dropped"; return
	fi
	set -- "${1:-userland/system.apfs}"
	[ -f "$1" ] || { echo "xl: $1 not found"; return 1; }
	local t0=$(date +%s) size=$(stat -c %s "$1")
	fb oem ramdisk | grep -q OKAY || { echo "xl: the loader refused (no memory window?)"; return 1; }
	FB_TIMEOUT=1800 fb stage "$1" | grep -q OKAY || { echo "xl: upload failed"; return 1; }
	local dt=$(( $(date +%s) - t0 )); [ $dt -lt 1 ] && dt=1
	echo "xl: $(( size / 1048576 )) MB uploaded in $dt s ($(( size / 1048576 / dt )) MB/s)"
	# Who put what there, for `run` to warn about below. The resident image is a third state of
	# the phone that neither the lock nor the note describes: it stays in memory across runs and
	# across working copies, so a run that uploads nothing boots against whatever the last upload
	# left -- which may be another copy's, of another kind. That cost two runs on 20 October, and
	# the only thing that distinguished them on sight was the loader's own "resident image at pa
	# ... size 400000" against "size 97308000". The size is recorded for exactly that reason: a
	# foreign image of the same kind is harmless, a foreign one of another kind kills the run and
	# says nothing.
	printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$(pwd)" "$1" "$size" > $PHONE.ramdisk 2>/dev/null
}

screenshot() { # screenshot [file.png]
	enter || return 1
	local out=${1:-logs/screen.png} geom
	geom=$(fb getvar screen | sed -n 's/^screen: //p')
	[ -n "$geom" ] && fb oem screenshot | grep -q OKAY || { echo "xl: the loader has no display"; return 1; }
	FB_TIMEOUT=60 fb get_staged logs/screen.raw >/dev/null
	python3 - logs/screen.raw "$out" $geom <<'PY' && rm -f logs/screen.raw && echo "xl: $out ($geom)"
import struct, sys, zlib
raw, out, width, height, stride = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], *map(int, sys.argv[3:6])
data = open(raw, 'rb').read()
rows = bytearray()
for y in range(height):
    line = data[y * stride:y * stride + width * 4]
    rows.append(0)                                    # PNG filter type: none
    rgb = bytearray(width * 3)
    rgb[0::3], rgb[1::3], rgb[2::3] = line[2::4], line[1::4], line[0::4]   # the panel is BGRX
    rows += rgb
def chunk(kind, body):
    return struct.pack('>I', len(body)) + kind + body + struct.pack('>I', zlib.crc32(kind + body))
with open(out, 'wb') as f:
    f.write(b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n' + chunk(b'IHDR', struct.pack('>IIBBBBB', width, height, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0)) +
            chunk(b'IDAT', zlib.compress(bytes(rows), 6)) + chunk(b'IEND', b''))
PY
}

# stop and reboot end a run. One that was started from another working copy is somebody else's work
# (an agent's measurement, a long session): not ended from here unless XL_FORCE=1 says so.
not_anothers_run() { # not_anothers_run <command>
	flock -n $PHONE.run true 2>/dev/null && return 0
	[ "$(cat $PHONE.who 2>/dev/null)" = "$(pwd)" ] || [ -n "$XL_FORCE" ] && return 0
	echo "xl: a run started from $(cat $PHONE.who 2>/dev/null) is in progress; XL_FORCE=1 ./xl $1 ends it all the same" >&2
	return 1
}

# While a run is in progress the loader takes only what does not disturb the kernel: state, screenshot,
# log, stop, reboot. Anything else would wait for nothing.
case "$1" in
""|run|selftest|state|screenshot|log|stop|reboot) ;;
*)	if ! flock -n $PHONE.run true 2>/dev/null; then
		echo "xl: a run is in progress: only state, screenshot, log, stop and reboot now" >&2; exit 1
	fi ;;
esac

case "$1" in
enter) enter && echo "xl: loader is up" ;;
screenshot) screenshot "$2" ;;
recording) recording "$2" ;;
camera) camera "$2" ;;
sound) sound "$2" ;;
ramdisk) ramdisk "$2" ;;
run) run "oem run $2" "run${2:+-cp$2}" ;;
selftest) run "oem selftest" selftest ;;
log) enter && fb oem log >/dev/null && fetch_log logs/loader.log && cat logs/loader.log ;;
stop) not_anothers_run stop && fb oem stop | grep -q OKAY && echo "xl: asked the kernel to come back" ;;
memmap) enter && fb oem memmap >/dev/null && fb oem log >/dev/null && fetch_log logs/loader.log && sed -n '/^memory map/,$p' logs/loader.log ;;
hang) enter && fb oem hang; echo "xl: waiting for the watchdog..."; t0=$(date +%s); wait_for android 150 && echo "xl: back in Android after $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) s" || echo "xl: not back (state: $(state))" ;;
reboot) not_anothers_run reboot && fb reboot ;;
reload) [ "$(state)" = loader ] && { fb reboot >/dev/null; wait_for android 120; }; enter && echo "xl: loader is up" ;;
state) state ;;
*) awk 'NR > 1 && /^#/ { print; next } NR > 1 { exit }' "$0" ;;
esac

```

`xnu-build.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# Build XNU for redwood on Linux. Extra make args are passed through.
source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/xnu-env.sh"
cd "$XNU_SRC" || exit 1
# The Wi-Fi driver's object (tools/mk-ath11k.sh) is linked into the kernel when it is there; make
# does not see it change, so the linked kernel is thrown away when it has.
LX=$XNUDEPS/build/ath11k/out/ath11k.o
STAMP=BUILD/obj/redwood-objects
if [ -f "$LX" ]; then now="$LX $(stat -c %Y "$LX")"; else LX= now=; fi
if [ -d BUILD/obj ] && [ "$(cat $STAMP 2>/dev/null)" != "$now" ]; then
	rm -f BUILD/obj/*/mach.*.unstripped
	echo "$now" > $STAMP
fi
exec make REDWOOD_OBJECTS="$LX" SDKROOT=iphoneos ARCH_CONFIGS=ARM64 MACHINE_CONFIGS=${MACHINE:-BCM2837} KERNEL_CONFIGS=DEVELOPMENT \
  ARCH_STRING_FOR_CURRENT_MACHINE_CONFIG=arm64 BUILD_WERROR=0 BUILD_LTO=0 DO_CTFMERGE=0 \
  HOST_CC="clang -include $XNUDEPS/hostinc/hostcompat.h -I$XNUDEPS/hostinc -Wno-unused-command-line-argument -Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" HOST_FLEX=flex HOST_BISON=bison HOST_GM4=m4 CC=xnu-clang CXX=xnu-clang++ LOGCOLORS=n "$@"
```

`xnu-deps/build/lzbitmap/libzbitmap.c`:

```c
// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0+ OR MIT
/*
 * Copyright (C) 2022 Corellium LLC
 *
 * Author: Ernesto A. Fernández <ernesto@corellium.com>
 *
 * Ported from libzbitmap (https://github.com/eafer/libzbitmap). Only the
 * decompression code is included.
 */

#include <errno.h>
#include <string.h>
#include "libzbitmap.h"

#define ZBM_MAGIC       "ZBM\x09"
#define ZBM_MAGIC_SZ    4

#define ZBM_MAX_DECMP_CHUNK_SIZE        0x8000
#define ZBM_MAX_DECMP_CHUNK_SIZE_BITS   15

struct uint24 {
    uint8_t     low;
    uint8_t     mid;
    uint8_t     hig;
};

/* This header is shared by both compressed and decompressed chunks */
struct zbm_chunk_hdr {
    struct uint24   len;        /* Length of the chunk */
    struct uint24   decmp_len;  /* Length of the chunk after decompression */
};

/* The full header for compressed chunks */
struct zbm_cmp_chunk_hdr {
    /* Shared with decompressed chunks */
    struct zbm_chunk_hdr hdr;

    /* Offset for each of the three metadata areas */
    struct uint24   meta_off_1;
    struct uint24   meta_off_2;
    struct uint24   meta_off_3;
};

/* Pointer to a half-byte */
struct nybl_ptr {
    uint8_t         *addr;  /* Address of the byte */
    int             nibble; /* Which of the two nibbles? */
};

/* 0-2 and 0xf are not real bitmap indexes */
#define ZBM_BITMAP_COUNT        (16 - 1 - 3)
#define ZBM_BITMAP_BASE         3
#define ZBM_BITMAP_BYTECNT      17
#define ZBM_MAX_PERIOD_BYTECNT  2

struct zbm_bmap {
    uint8_t     bitmap;         /* The bitmap */
    uint8_t     period_bytecnt; /* Read this many bytes to get the new period */
};

struct zbm_state {
    /* Updated during a chunk read */
    uint8_t         *dest;      /* Write the next byte here */
    size_t          dest_left;  /* Room left in destination buffer */
    uint32_t        written;    /* Bytes written so far for current chunk */
    uint16_t        period;     /* Repetition period for decompression, in bytes */

    /* Updated right before a chunk read */
    const uint8_t   *src_end;   /* End of current chunk */
    uint32_t        len;        /* Length of the chunk */
    uint32_t        decmp_len;  /* Expected chunk length after decompression */

    /* Updated after a chunk read */
    const uint8_t   *src;       /* Start of buffer, or current chunk if any */
    size_t          src_left;   /* Room left in the source buffer */
    size_t          prewritten; /* Bytes written for previous chunks */

    /* Current position in data and metadata areas for this chunk */
    const uint8_t   *data;
    const uint8_t   *meta_1;
    const uint8_t   *meta_2;
    struct nybl_ptr meta_3;

    /* Array of bitmaps for the current chunk */
    struct zbm_bmap bitmaps[ZBM_BITMAP_COUNT];
};

static int zbm_check_magic(struct zbm_state *state)
{
    if(state->src_left < ZBM_MAGIC_SZ)
        return -EINVAL;

    if(memcmp(state->src, ZBM_MAGIC, ZBM_MAGIC_SZ))
        return -EINVAL;

    state->src += ZBM_MAGIC_SZ;
    state->src_left -= ZBM_MAGIC_SZ;
    return 0;
}

static uint32_t zbm_u24_to_u32(struct uint24 n)
{
    uint32_t res;

    res = n.hig;
    res <<= 8;
    res += n.mid;
    res <<= 8;
    res += n.low;
    return res;
}

/* Some chunks just have regular uncompressed data, but with a header */
static int zbm_chunk_is_uncompressed(struct zbm_state *state)
{
    return state->len == state->decmp_len + sizeof(struct zbm_chunk_hdr);
}

static int zbm_handle_uncompressed_chunk(struct zbm_state *state)
{
    state->meta_1 = state->meta_2 = NULL;
    state->meta_3.addr = NULL;
    state->meta_3.nibble = 0;
    state->data = state->src + sizeof(struct zbm_chunk_hdr);
    memcpy(state->dest, state->data, state->decmp_len);

    state->dest += state->decmp_len;
    state->dest_left -= state->decmp_len;
    state->written = state->decmp_len;
    return 0;
}

static int zbm_read_nibble(struct nybl_ptr *nybl, const uint8_t *limit, uint8_t *result)
{
    if(nybl->addr >= limit)
        return -EINVAL;

    if(nybl->nibble == 0) {
        *result = *nybl->addr & 0xf;
        nybl->nibble = 1;
    } else {
        *result = (*nybl->addr >> 4) & 0xf;
        nybl->nibble = 0;
        ++nybl->addr;
    }
    return 0;
}

static void zbm_rewind_nibble(struct nybl_ptr *nybl)
{
    if(nybl->nibble == 0) {
        nybl->nibble = 1;
        --nybl->addr;
    } else {
        nybl->nibble = 0;
    }
}

static int zbm_apply_bitmap(struct zbm_state *state, struct zbm_bmap *bitmap)
{
    int i;

    /* The periods are stored in the first metadata area */
    if(bitmap->period_bytecnt) {
        state->period = 0;
        for(i = 0; i < bitmap->period_bytecnt; ++i) {
            if(state->meta_1 >= state->src_end)
                return -EINVAL;
            state->period |= *state->meta_1 << i * 8;
            ++state->meta_1;
        }
    }
    if(state->period == 0)
        return -EINVAL;

    for(i = 0; i < 8; ++i) {
        if(state->written == state->decmp_len)
            break;
        if(bitmap->bitmap & 1 << i) {
            if(state->data >= state->src_end)
                return -EINVAL;
            *state->dest = *state->data;
            ++state->data;
        } else {
            if(state->prewritten + state->written < state->period)
                return -EINVAL;
            *state->dest = *(state->dest - state->period);
        }
        ++state->dest;
        --state->dest_left;
        ++state->written;
    }

    return 0;
}

static int zbm_apply_bitmap_number(struct zbm_state *state, uint8_t bmp_num)
{
    struct zbm_bmap next = {0};

    /* Not a valid bitmap number (it signals a repetition) */
    if(bmp_num == 0xf)
        return -EINVAL;

    /* An actual index in the bitmap array */
    if(bmp_num > ZBM_MAX_PERIOD_BYTECNT)
        return zbm_apply_bitmap(state, &state->bitmaps[bmp_num - ZBM_BITMAP_BASE]);

    /* For < 2, use the next bitmap in the second metadata area */
    if(state->meta_2 >= state->src_end)
        return -EINVAL;
    next.bitmap = *state->meta_2;
    next.period_bytecnt = bmp_num;
    ++state->meta_2;
    return zbm_apply_bitmap(state, &next);
}

/* Find out how many times we need to repeat the current bitmap operation */
static int zbm_read_repetition_count(struct zbm_state *state, uint16_t *repeat)
{
    uint8_t nibble;
    uint16_t total;
    int err;

    /* Don't confuse the trailing bitmaps with a repetition count */
    if(state->decmp_len - state->written <= 8) {
        *repeat = 1;
        return 0;
    }

    err = zbm_read_nibble(&state->meta_3, state->src_end, &nibble);
    if(err)
        return err;

    if(nibble != 0xf) {
        /* No repetition count: the previous bitmap number gets applied once */
        zbm_rewind_nibble(&state->meta_3);
        *repeat = 1;
        return 0;
    }

    /*
     * Under this scheme, repeating a bitmap number 3 times wouldn't save any
     * space, so the repetition count starts from 4.
     */
    total = 4;
    while(nibble == 0xf) {
        err = zbm_read_nibble(&state->meta_3, state->src_end, &nibble);
        if(err)
            return err;
        total += nibble;
        if(total < nibble)
            return -EINVAL;
    }

    *repeat = total;
    return 0;
}

static int zbm_decompress_single_bitmap(struct zbm_state *state)
{
    uint8_t bmp_num;
    uint16_t repeat;
    int i;
    int err;

    /* The current nibble is the offset of the next bitmap to apply */
    err = zbm_read_nibble(&state->meta_3, state->src_end, &bmp_num);
    if(err)
        return err;

    err = zbm_read_repetition_count(state, &repeat);
    if(err)
        return err;

    for(i = 0; i < repeat; ++i) {
        err = zbm_apply_bitmap_number(state, bmp_num);
        if(err)
            return err;
    }
    return 0;
}

/* Pointer to a bit */
struct bit_ptr {
    uint8_t         *addr;  /* Address of the byte */
    int             offset; /* Bit number */
};

/* This function does not perform boundary checks, the caller must do it */
static int zbm_read_single_bit(struct bit_ptr *bit)
{
    int res = *bit->addr >> bit->offset & 1;

    ++bit->offset;
    if(bit->offset != 8)
        return res;
    bit->offset = 0;
    ++bit->addr;
    return res;
}

static int zbm_read_single_bitmap(struct bit_ptr *bit, const uint8_t *limit, struct zbm_bmap *result)
{
    int i;

    result->bitmap = 0;
    result->period_bytecnt = 0;

    /* The bitmap itself */
    for(i = 0; i < 8; ++i) {
        if(bit->addr >= limit)
            return -EINVAL;
        result->bitmap |= zbm_read_single_bit(bit) << i;
    }

    /*
     * The two trailing bits tell us how many bytes to read for the next
     * repetition period
     */
    for(i = 0; i < 2; ++i) {
        if(bit->addr >= limit)
            return -EINVAL;
        result->period_bytecnt |= zbm_read_single_bit(bit) << i;
    }

    return 0;
}

static int zbm_read_bitmaps(struct zbm_state *state)
{
    struct bit_ptr bmap = {0};
    int err, i;

    if(state->len < ZBM_BITMAP_BYTECNT)
        return -EINVAL;

    bmap.addr = (uint8_t *)state->src_end - ZBM_BITMAP_BYTECNT;
    bmap.offset = 0;

    for(i = 0; i < ZBM_BITMAP_COUNT; ++i) {
        err = zbm_read_single_bitmap(&bmap, state->src_end, &state->bitmaps[i]);
        if(err)
            return err;
        if(state->bitmaps[i].period_bytecnt > ZBM_MAX_PERIOD_BYTECNT)
            return -EINVAL;
    }
    return 0;
}

static int zbm_handle_compressed_chunk(struct zbm_state *state)
{
    const struct zbm_cmp_chunk_hdr *hdr = NULL;
    uint32_t meta_off_1, meta_off_2, meta_off_3;
    int err;

    state->written = 0;
    state->period = 8;

    if(state->len < sizeof(*hdr))
        return -EINVAL;
    hdr = (struct zbm_cmp_chunk_hdr *)state->src;
    state->data = state->src + sizeof(*hdr);

    meta_off_1 = zbm_u24_to_u32(hdr->meta_off_1);
    meta_off_2 = zbm_u24_to_u32(hdr->meta_off_2);
    meta_off_3 = zbm_u24_to_u32(hdr->meta_off_3);
    if(meta_off_1 >= state->len || meta_off_2 >= state->len || meta_off_3 >= state->len)
        return -EINVAL;
    state->meta_1 = state->src + meta_off_1;
    state->meta_2 = state->src + meta_off_2;
    state->meta_3.addr = (uint8_t *)state->src + meta_off_3;
    state->meta_3.nibble = 0;

    err = zbm_read_bitmaps(state);
    if(err)
        return err;

    while(state->written < state->decmp_len) {
        err = zbm_decompress_single_bitmap(state);
        if(err)
            return err;
    }

    return 0;
}

static int zbm_handle_chunk(struct zbm_state *state)
{
    const struct zbm_chunk_hdr *decmp_hdr = NULL;

    if(state->src_left < sizeof(*decmp_hdr))
        return -EINVAL;
    decmp_hdr = (struct zbm_chunk_hdr *)state->src;

    state->len = zbm_u24_to_u32(decmp_hdr->len);
    if(state->len > state->src_left)
        return -EINVAL;
    state->src_end = state->src + state->len;

    state->decmp_len = zbm_u24_to_u32(decmp_hdr->decmp_len);
    if(state->decmp_len > ZBM_MAX_DECMP_CHUNK_SIZE)
        return -EINVAL;
    if(!state->dest) /* We just wanted the length, so we are done */
        return 0;
    if(state->decmp_len > state->dest_left)
        return -ERANGE;

    if(zbm_chunk_is_uncompressed(state))
        return zbm_handle_uncompressed_chunk(state);

    return zbm_handle_compressed_chunk(state);
}

int zbm_decompress(void *dest, size_t dest_size, const void *src, size_t src_size, size_t *out_len)
{
    struct zbm_state state = {0};
    int err;

    state.src = src;
    state.src_left = src_size;
    state.dest = dest;
    state.dest_left = dest_size;
    state.prewritten = 0;

    err = zbm_check_magic(&state);
    if(err)
        return err;

    /* The final chunk has zero decompressed length */
    do {
        err = zbm_handle_chunk(&state);
        if(err)
            return err;
        state.src += state.len;
        state.src_left -= state.len;
        state.prewritten += state.decmp_len;
    } while(state.decmp_len != 0);

    *out_len = state.prewritten;
    return 0;
}

```

`xnu-deps/build/lzbitmap/unzbm.c`:

```c
/*
 * unzbm: finish what 7z leaves undone for files compressed with LZBITMAP.
 *
 * 7z extracts such a file from an APFS image as an empty file plus its two
 * attributes, "NAME:com.apple.decmpfs" (the compression header) and
 * "NAME:com.apple.ResourceFork" (the compressed data, in 64K blocks behind a
 * table of offsets). For every NAME given, this writes the real contents and
 * removes the two attribute files.
 *
 * The decompressor is libzbitmap (Ernesto A. Fernandez, GPL-2.0+ OR MIT),
 * as shipped with the linux-apfs-rw driver.
 */
#include <errno.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#include "libzbitmap.h"

#define BLOCK 0x10000u
#define LZBITMAP_RSRC 14

static uint8_t *
slurp(const char *path, size_t *size)
{
	FILE *f = fopen(path, "rb");
	uint8_t *data;

	if (!f) {
		return NULL;
	}
	fseek(f, 0, SEEK_END);
	*size = (size_t)ftell(f);
	rewind(f);
	data = malloc(*size + 1);
	if (fread(data, 1, *size, f) != *size) {
		free(data);
		data = NULL;
	}
	fclose(f);
	return data;
}

static uint32_t
le32(const uint8_t *p)
{
	return p[0] | p[1] << 8 | p[2] << 16 | (uint32_t)p[3] << 24;
}

static int
expand(const char *name)
{
	char header_path[4096], fork_path[4096];
	size_t header_size, fork_size;
	uint8_t *header, *fork, *out;
	uint64_t size, blocks;
	FILE *f;

	snprintf(header_path, sizeof(header_path), "%s:com.apple.decmpfs", name);
	snprintf(fork_path, sizeof(fork_path), "%s:com.apple.ResourceFork", name);
	header = slurp(header_path, &header_size);
	fork = slurp(fork_path, &fork_size);
	if (!header || !fork || header_size < 16 || memcmp(header, "fpmc", 4) != 0 || le32(header + 4) != LZBITMAP_RSRC) {
		fprintf(stderr, "unzbm: %s: not an LZBITMAP resource-fork file\n", name);
		return 1;
	}
	size = le32(header + 8) | (uint64_t)le32(header + 12) << 32;
	blocks = (size + BLOCK - 1) / BLOCK;
	if ((blocks + 1) * 4 > fork_size) {
		fprintf(stderr, "unzbm: %s: block table does not fit\n", name);
		return 1;
	}
	out = malloc(size ? size : 1);
	for (uint64_t b = 0; b < blocks; b++) {
		uint32_t from = le32(fork + 4 * b), to = le32(fork + 4 * (b + 1));
		size_t want = size - b * BLOCK > BLOCK ? BLOCK : (size_t)(size - b * BLOCK), got = 0;

		/* a block that did not shrink is stored as it is behind one byte, 0xff */
		if (from < to && to <= fork_size && to - from == want + 1 && fork[from] == 0xff) {
			memcpy(out + b * BLOCK, fork + from + 1, want);
			continue;
		}
		if (from > to || to > fork_size || zbm_decompress(out + b * BLOCK, want, fork + from, to - from, &got) != 0 ||
		    got != want) {
			fprintf(stderr, "unzbm: %s: block %llu does not decompress\n", name, (unsigned long long)b);
			return 1;
		}
	}
	f = fopen(name, "wb");
	if (!f || fwrite(out, 1, size, f) != size || fclose(f) != 0) {
		fprintf(stderr, "unzbm: %s: %s\n", name, strerror(errno));
		return 1;
	}
	unlink(header_path);
	unlink(fork_path);
	free(out);
	free(fork);
	free(header);
	return 0;
}

int
main(int argc, char **argv)
{
	int failed = 0;

	for (int i = 1; i < argc; i++) {
		failed += expand(argv[i]);
	}
	return failed != 0;
}

```

`xnu-deps/build/pthread/build.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# Build the open-source pthread kernel extension (libpthread/kern) as a static
# library that gets linked into the XNU kernel image (there is no kext loader
# in this setup). Requires an XNU build tree for the exported kernel headers.
set -e
# The two -D renames below avoid clashes with kernel symbols of the same name:
# as a real kext these live in a separate link unit.
cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")"
source ../../../xnu-env.sh
X=$XNU_SRC; E=$X/BUILD/obj/EXPORT_HDRS; P=$XNUDEPS/libpthread
[ -d $E/osfmk ] || { echo "pthread kext: no exported kernel headers in $E (run: xnu-build.sh exporthdrs)" >&2; exit 1; }
mkdir -p $XNU_SDK_PATH/usr/local/lib/kernel
for f in kern_init kern_support kern_synch; do
  xnu-clang -arch arm64 -c -Os -mkernel -nostdinc -fno-builtin -fno-common -Wno-int-conversion \
    -DKERNEL=1 -DKERNEL_PRIVATE=1 -DPRIVATE=1 -D__PTHREAD_EXPOSE_INTERNALS__=1 -Dpthread_kern=pthread_kext_kern -Dcurrent_uthread=pthread_kext_current_uthread -D__DARWIN_64_BIT_INO_T=1 -DARM64_BOARD_CONFIG_BCM2837 \
    -Iinc -I$P -I$E/osfmk -I$E/bsd -I$E/libkern -I$E/pexpert -I$E/iokit -I$E/security -I$X/EXTERNAL_HEADERS \
    -I$P/include -I$P/private -o pthread_$f.o $P/kern/$f.c
done
libtool -static -o $XNU_SDK_PATH/usr/local/lib/kernel/libpthread_kext.a pthread_kern_init.o pthread_kern_support.o pthread_kern_synch.o
ls -la $XNU_SDK_PATH/usr/local/lib/kernel/libpthread_kext.a
```

`xnu-deps/gen-iig-stubs.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Generate stand-in DriverKit implementation files for the XNU build.

Apple's `iig` tool (closed source) normally generates <Class>.iig.cpp: the RPC
marshalling for DriverKit (user-space driver) interfaces. Without it the kernel
fails to link. This script reads the linker's undefined-symbol list and emits:
  * metaclass definitions for classes that only exist as DriverKit interfaces
  * a stub returning kIOReturnUnsupported for every remaining generated method
The kernel then links and runs; user-space DriverKit drivers are non-functional.

usage: gen-iig-stubs.py <undefined.txt> <outdir> [kernel-symbols (nm -n output)]
"""
import re, sys, os

undefined = [l.strip() for l in open(sys.argv[1]) if l.strip()]
outdir = sys.argv[2]

# class -> superclass, for classes whose OSMetaClass the generated code owns
META = {
    'IODispatchSource': ('OSObject', True),
    'IOEventLink': ('OSObject', False),
    'IOWorkGroup': ('OSObject', False),
    'IODispatchQueue': ('OSObject', False),
    'OSAction': ('OSObject', False),
    'IODataQueueDispatchSource': ('IODispatchSource', False),
    'IOInterruptDispatchSource': ('IODispatchSource', False),
    'IOServiceNotificationDispatchSource': ('IODispatchSource', False),
    'IOServiceStateNotificationDispatchSource': ('IODispatchSource', False),
}

meta_needed, funcs = [], []
for sym in undefined:
    m = re.match(r'__ZN(\d+)', sym)
    if not m:
        continue
    n = int(m.group(1)); cls = sym[len(m.group(0)):len(m.group(0)) + n]
    if sym.endswith('9metaClassE') and sym == '__ZN%d%s9metaClassE' % (n, cls):
        meta_needed.append(cls)
    else:
        funcs.append(sym)
vt = [s for s in undefined if s.startswith('__ZTV')]

out = ['/* Generated by gen-iig-stubs.py: stand-in for iig output. Do not edit. */',
       '#include <IOKit/IOLib.h>', '#include <IOKit/IOReturn.h>', '#include <IOKit/IOService.h>',
       '#include <IOKit/IOUserClient.h>', '#include <IOKit/IOUserServer.h>',
       '#include <DriverKit/IODispatchSource.h>', '#include <DriverKit/IODispatchQueue.h>',
       '#include <DriverKit/IOEventLink.h>', '#include <DriverKit/IOWorkGroup.h>', '#include <DriverKit/OSAction.h>',
       '#include <DriverKit/IODataQueueDispatchSource.h>', '#include <DriverKit/IOInterruptDispatchSource.h>',
       '#include <DriverKit/IOServiceNotificationDispatchSource.h>',
       '#include <DriverKit/IOServiceStateNotificationDispatchSource.h>', '']
want = set(meta_needed)
if any(META.get(c, ('', 0))[0] == 'IODispatchSource' for c in want) or vt:
    want.add('IODispatchSource')
for cls, (sup, abstract) in META.items():
    if cls in want:
        macro = 'OSDefineMetaClassAndAbstractStructors' if abstract else 'OSDefineMetaClassAndStructors'
        out.append('%s(%s, %s);' % (macro, cls, sup))
out.append('')
# Kernel-implemented methods: the real generated wrapper marshals the call into
# an RPC and dispatches it back to Class::Method_Impl(). For objects that live
# in the kernel that round trip is equivalent to calling _Impl directly, and
# the kernel itself relies on it (e.g. IOService::StateNotificationItemCreate).
# The wrapper only has one extra trailing argument (the "supermethod"), so a
# tail branch is argument-compatible on arm64.
SUPER = 'PFiP15OSMetaClassBase5IORPCE'
defined = set()
if len(sys.argv) > 3:
    for line in open(sys.argv[3]):
        parts = line.split()
        if len(parts) == 3 and parts[1] in 'tTsS':  # kernel text lives in __TEXT_EXEC, which nm reports as 'S'
            defined.add(parts[2])

def impl_name(sym):
    m = re.match(r'__ZN(\d+)', sym)
    if not m or not sym.endswith(SUPER):
        return None
    pos = len(m.group(0)) + int(m.group(1))
    m2 = re.match(r'(\d+)', sym[pos:])
    if not m2:
        return None
    mlen = int(m2.group(1)); mstart = pos + len(m2.group(1))
    method = sym[mstart:mstart + mlen]
    rest = sym[mstart + mlen:]
    if not rest.startswith('E'):
        return None
    params = rest[1:-len(SUPER)] or 'v'
    return '%s%d%s_ImplE%s' % (sym[:pos], mlen + 5, method, params)

direct, unsupported = [], []
for sym in sorted(set(funcs)):
    impl = impl_name(sym)
    if impl and impl in defined:
        direct.append((sym, impl))
    else:
        unsupported.append(sym)

out.append('/* wrappers forwarded straight to their kernel implementation */')
for sym, impl in direct:
    out.append('__asm__(".text\\n.globl %s\\n.p2align 2\\n%s:\\n\\tb %s\\n");' % (sym, sym, impl))
out.append('')
out.append('/* everything else (RPC dispatch, user-space-only methods) is not available */')
out.append('extern "C" {')
for i, sym in enumerate(unsupported):
    # sym carries the Mach-O leading underscore already
    out.append('kern_return_t __iig_stub_%d(void) __asm__("%s");' % (i, sym))
    out.append('kern_return_t __iig_stub_%d(void) { return kIOReturnUnsupported; }' % i)
out.append('}')
os.makedirs(outdir, exist_ok=True)
open(os.path.join(outdir, 'OSObject.iig.cpp'), 'w').write('\n'.join(out) + '\n')
print('metaclasses:', len(want), 'forwarded to _Impl:', len(direct), 'unsupported stubs:', len(unsupported))

```

`xnu-deps/host/bin/iig`:

```
#!/bin/bash
# Stand-in for Apple's closed-source iig (DriverKit interface generator).
# Headers: taken pre-generated from the macOS 13.3 SDK (same xnu-8796 family).
# Implementation: taken from $XNUDEPS/iig-impl/<name>.iig.cpp if present, else an empty TU.
XNUDEPS=${XNUDEPS:-$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)}
SDKH="$XNUDEPS/MacOSX13.3.sdk/System/Library/Frameworks/Kernel.framework/Headers"
def=""; hdr=""; impl=""
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do case "$1" in
  --def) def="$2"; shift 2;; --header) hdr="$2"; shift 2;; --impl) impl="$2"; shift 2;;
  --) break;; *) shift;; esac; done
name="$(basename "$def" .iig)"
src="$(find "$SDKH" -name "$name.h" -path '*DriverKit*' | head -1)"
[ -z "$src" ] && src="$(find "$SDKH" -name "$name.h" | xargs grep -l 'iig(DriverKit' 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
if [ -z "$src" ]; then echo "iig shim: no pre-generated header for $name" >&2; exit 1; fi
cp "$src" "$hdr"
if [ -f "$XNUDEPS/iig-impl/$name.iig.cpp" ]; then cp "$XNUDEPS/iig-impl/$name.iig.cpp" "$impl"
else echo "/* $name: no DriverKit implementation generated (iig shim) */" > "$impl"; fi

```

`xnu-deps/host/bin/xcrun`:

```
#!/bin/bash
# Minimal xcrun replacement for building XNU on Linux
HB="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
sdk=""; find=""; show=""
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do case "$1" in
  -sdk) sdk="$2"; shift 2;; -verbose) shift;;
  -find|--find|-f) find="$2"; shift 2;;
  -show-sdk-path|--show-sdk-path) show=path; shift;;
  -show-sdk-version|--show-sdk-version) show=version; shift;;
  -show-sdk-platform-path|--show-sdk-platform-path) show=platform; shift;;
  -show-sdk-platform-version) show=version; shift;;
  *) break;; esac; done
SDKP="${XNU_SDK_PATH:?XNU_SDK_PATH not set}"
case "$show" in
  path) case "$sdk" in /*) echo "$sdk";; *) echo "$SDKP";; esac; exit 0;;
  version) echo "${XNU_SDK_VERSION:-16.5}"; exit 0;;
  platform) echo "${XNU_PLATFORM_PATH:-/Platforms/iPhoneOS.platform}"; exit 0;;
esac
if [ -n "$find" ]; then
  for d in "$HB" /usr/bin; do [ -x "$d/$find" ] && { echo "$d/$find"; exit 0; }; done
  exit 1
fi
[ $# -gt 0 ] && exec "$@"
```

`xnu-deps/host/bin/xnu-clang`:

```
#!/bin/bash
# clang wrapper for cross-building XNU on Linux:
#  - forces an Apple Mach-O target (stock Linux clang defaults to ELF)
#  - drops flags only Apple's clang understands
#  - links with the cctools ld64
HB="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
case "$(basename "$0")" in *++) drv=clang++; extra=(-fno-use-cxa-atexit);; *) drv=clang; extra=();; esac
args=()
for a in "$@"; do
  case "$a" in
    -enable-trivial-auto-var-init-zero-knowing-it-will-be-removed-from-clang) ;;
    -fapple-kext-vtable-verify|-Wno-vla-cxx-extension) ;;
    -Werror|-Werror=*|-Weverything|-pedantic-errors) ;;
    *) args+=("$a");;
  esac
done
exec /usr/bin/$drv -include "$HB/../../hostinc/xnu_clang_compat.h" -target arm64-apple-ios${XNU_SDK_VERSION:-16.5} --ld-path="$HB/ld64" \
  -w "${extra[@]}" "${args[@]}"
```

`xnu-deps/hostinc/copyfile.h`:

```h
#ifndef HOST_COPYFILE_H
#define HOST_COPYFILE_H
#include <unistd.h>
#define COPYFILE_DATA 8
typedef void *copyfile_state_t;
static inline int fcopyfile(int from, int to, copyfile_state_t s, unsigned flags) {
	char buf[65536]; ssize_t n;
	(void)s; (void)flags;
	while ((n = read(from, buf, sizeof buf)) > 0) {
		char *p = buf; while (n > 0) { ssize_t w = write(to, p, n); if (w < 0) return -1; p += w; n -= w; }
	}
	return n < 0 ? -1 : 0;
}
#endif
```

```h
/*
 * This header file describes the structures of the file format for "fat"
 * architecture specific file (wrapper design).  At the begining of the file
 * there is one fat_header structure followed by a number of fat_arch
 * structures.  For each architecture in the file, specified by a pair of
 * cputype and cpusubtype, the fat_header describes the file offset, file
 * size and alignment in the file of the architecture specific member.
 * The padded bytes in the file to place each member on it's specific alignment
 * are defined to be read as zeros and can be left as "holes" if the file system
 * can support them as long as they read as zeros.
 *
 * All structures defined here are always written and read to/from disk
 * in big-endian order.
 */

/*
 * <mach/machine.h> is needed here for the cpu_type_t and cpu_subtype_t types
 * and contains the constants for the possible values of these types.
 */
#include <stdint.h>
#include <mach/machine.h>
#include <architecture/byte_order.h>

#define FAT_MAGIC	0xcafebabe
#define FAT_CIGAM	0xbebafeca	/* NXSwapLong(FAT_MAGIC) */

struct fat_header {
	uint32_t	magic;		/* FAT_MAGIC */
	uint32_t	nfat_arch;	/* number of structs that follow */
};

struct fat_arch {
	cpu_type_t	cputype;	/* cpu specifier (int) */
	cpu_subtype_t	cpusubtype;	/* machine specifier (int) */
	uint32_t	offset;		/* file offset to this object file */
	uint32_t	size;		/* size of this object file */
	uint32_t	align;		/* alignment as a power of 2 */
};

#endif /* _MACH_O_FAT_H_ */

```

```h
#ifndef _MACHO_LOADER_H_
```
