```c
/* ---- the layouts ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ */

#define CHANNEL_20MHZ           0x2u
#define CHANNEL_2GHZ            0x8u
#define CHANNEL_5GHZ            0x10u
#define CHANNEL_ACTIVE          0x80u           /* the radio may send there */
#define CHANNEL_DFS             0x100u

struct apple80211_channel {
	uint32_t version, channel, flags;
};

/* SUPPORTED_CHANNELS (27) and HW_SUPPORTED_CHANNELS (254): 4824 bytes */
struct apple80211_channels {
	uint32_t version, count;
	struct apple80211_channel channels[401];
	uint32_t unused;
};

/* CHANNELS_INFO (207): 10016 bytes; of each channel a byte in each of several rows, and a word of flags */
struct apple80211_channels_info {
	uint8_t unknown_0[12];
	uint16_t count;
	uint8_t unknown_1[800];
	uint8_t number[400], indoor[400], dfs[400], passive[400], wide_40[400], wide_80[400];
	uint8_t unknown_2[1602];
	uint32_t flags[400];
	uint8_t unknown_3[3600];
} __attribute__((packed));

/* SCAN_REQ (10): 5456 bytes */
struct apple80211_scan_request {
	uint32_t version, bss_type;
	uint8_t bssid[6], unused_0[2];
	uint32_t ssid_length;
	uint8_t ssid[32];
	uint32_t scan_type;                     /* 1: asking, 2: listening only */
	uint32_t phy_mode;
	uint16_t dwell_ms, unused_1;
	uint32_t rest_ms;
	uint32_t channel_count;
	struct apple80211_channel channels[400];
	uint64_t flags;
	uint32_t unused_2;
	uint32_t name_count;                    /* networks asked for by name, each in 56 bytes */
	uint8_t names[10][56];
	uint32_t short_ssid, unused_3;
};

/* SCAN_RESULT (11) and CURRENT_NETWORK (103): 1164 bytes */
struct apple80211_scan_result {
	uint32_t version;
	struct apple80211_channel channel;
	uint16_t noise_known;
	int16_t noise, snr, rssi;
	uint16_t beacon_interval, capability;
	uint8_t bssid[6];
	uint8_t rate_count, unused_0;
	uint32_t rates[15];                     /* Mbit/s */
	uint8_t ssid_length, ssid[32], unused_1[3];
	uint32_t age_ms;
	uint8_t flags, unused_2;
	uint16_t elements_length;               /* comes in as the room there is */
	uint8_t elements[1024];
};

/* ASSOCIATE (20): 592 bytes; of what follows the key (the RSN element wifid built, flags) nothing is used */
struct apple80211_assoc {
	uint32_t version;
	uint16_t mode, auth_lower, auth_upper, unused_0;
	uint32_t ssid_length;
	uint8_t ssid[32];
	uint8_t bssid[6], unused_1[2];
	uint32_t key_version, key_length, key_cipher;   /* cipher 10: a passphrase as typed; 6: the key (from 64 hex digits) */
	uint16_t key_flags, key_index;
	uint8_t key[64];
	uint8_t rest[0x250 - 0x88];
};

#define CIPHER_PMK              6
#define CIPHER_PASSPHRASE       10

/* the link event's data (at least 32 bytes, or the framework drops the event) */
struct apple80211_link_changed {
	uint8_t down, unused_0[3];
	int32_t rssi;
	uint16_t snr, noise;
	uint8_t unused_1[4];
	uint8_t involuntary, unused_2[3];
	uint32_t reason, subreason;
	uint8_t unused_3[4];
};

_Static_assert(sizeof(struct apple80211_assoc) == 592 && offsetof(struct apple80211_assoc, key) == 0x48,
    "the association request as iOS 16.5 has it");
_Static_assert(sizeof(struct apple80211_link_changed) == 32 && offsetof(struct apple80211_link_changed, reason) == 0x14,
    "the link event as iOS 16.5 reads it");
_Static_assert(sizeof(struct apple80211_channels) == 4824, "the channel list as iOS 16.5 has it");
_Static_assert(sizeof(struct apple80211_channels_info) == 10016 && offsetof(struct apple80211_channels_info, number) == 0x32e &&
    offsetof(struct apple80211_channels_info, flags) == 0x12d0, "the channels' description as iOS 16.5 has it");
_Static_assert(sizeof(struct apple80211_scan_request) == 5456 && offsetof(struct apple80211_scan_request, channels) == 0x48 &&
    offsetof(struct apple80211_scan_request, flags) == 0x1308 && offsetof(struct apple80211_scan_request, names) == 0x1318,
    "the scan request as iOS 16.5 has it");
_Static_assert(sizeof(struct apple80211_scan_result) == 1164 && offsetof(struct apple80211_scan_result, ssid_length) == 0x60 &&
    offsetof(struct apple80211_scan_result, age_ms) == 0x84 && offsetof(struct apple80211_scan_result, elements) == 0x8c,
    "a scan's result as iOS 16.5 has it");

/* Apple80211's events (APPLE80211_M_...) */
enum { EVENT_POWER_CHANGED = 1, EVENT_SSID_CHANGED = 2, EVENT_BSSID_CHANGED = 3, EVENT_LINK_CHANGED = 4, EVENT_ASSOC_DONE = 9,
       EVENT_SCAN_DONE = 10 };

static const char interface_name[16] = "en0";   /* (bsd/dev/redwood_net.c makes one interface, and that is its name) */

static LCK_GRP_DECLARE(apple80211_lock_group, "redwood-apple80211");
static LCK_MTX_DECLARE(apple80211_lock, &apple80211_lock_group);
static unsigned result_next;                    /* which of what the last scan heard a SCAN_RESULT request gets next */
static uint32_t join_result;                    /* of the last join asked for: 0 while it runs, then Apple80211's number */

/* ---- channels ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

static unsigned
channel_number(unsigned frequency)
{
	return frequency == 2484 ? 14 : frequency < 4000 ? (frequency - 2407) / 5 : (frequency - 5000) / 5;
}

static unsigned
channel_frequency(const struct apple80211_channel *channel)
{
	bool low = channel->flags & CHANNEL_2GHZ ? true : channel->flags & CHANNEL_5GHZ ? false : channel->channel <= 14;

	if (channel->channel == 0 || channel->channel > 196 || (channel->flags & 0x2000)) {     /* (0x2000: 6 GHz) */
		return 0;
	}
	return low ? (channel->channel == 14 ? 2484 : 2407 + 5 * channel->channel) : 5000 + 5 * channel->channel;
}

static void
channel_fill(struct apple80211_channel *channel, unsigned frequency, unsigned flags)
{
	channel->version = 1;
	channel->channel = channel_number(frequency);
	channel->flags = CHANNEL_20MHZ | (frequency < 4000 ? CHANNEL_2GHZ : CHANNEL_5GHZ) | (flags & REDWOOD_STA_CHANNEL_PASSIVE ?
	    0 : CHANNEL_ACTIVE) | (flags & REDWOOD_STA_CHANNEL_RADAR ? CHANNEL_DFS : 0);
}

/* ---- what the caller is given back ------------------------------------------------------------------- */

/* At most as many bytes as it has room for. */
static int
give(const struct apple80211req *request, const void *data, size_t length)
{
	return request->req_data == USER_ADDR_NULL ? 0 : copyout(data, request->req_data, length < request->req_len ? length :
	       request->req_len);
}

/* An access point in the form a scan's result has; the caller has said how much room for elements there is. */
static int
give_network(const struct apple80211req *request, const struct redwood_sta_bss *bss)
{
	struct apple80211_scan_result *result = kalloc_data(sizeof(*result), Z_WAITOK | Z_ZERO);
	unsigned room = sizeof(result->elements);
	int error;

	if (result == NULL) {
		return ENOMEM;
	}
	if (request->req_len >= sizeof(*result) && copyin(request->req_data, result, offsetof(struct apple80211_scan_result,
	    elements)) == 0 && result->elements_length < room) {
		room = result->elements_length;
	}
	bzero(result, sizeof(*result));
	result->version = 1;
	channel_fill(&result->channel, bss->frequency, 0);
	result->rssi = bss->rssi;
	result->beacon_interval = bss->beacon_interval;
	result->capability = bss->capability;
	memcpy(result->bssid, bss->bssid, sizeof(result->bssid));
	result->ssid_length = bss->ssid_length;
	memcpy(result->ssid, bss->ssid, bss->ssid_length);
	result->age_ms = bss->age_ms;
	result->elements_length = (uint16_t)(bss->elements_length <= room ? bss->elements_length : 0);
	memcpy(result->elements, bss->elements, result->elements_length);
	/* the rates it says it has (elements 1 and 50: units of 500 kbit/s, the top bit marks the ones everybody must have) */
	for (unsigned at = 0; at + 2 <= bss->elements_length && at + 2 + bss->elements[at + 1] <= bss->elements_length;
	    at += 2 + bss->elements[at + 1]) {
		for (unsigned i = 0; (bss->elements[at] == 1 || bss->elements[at] == 50) && i < bss->elements[at + 1]; i++) {
			unsigned rate = (bss->elements[at + 2 + i] & 0x7f) / 2;

			if (rate != 0 && rate <= 54 && result->rate_count < 15) {
				result->rates[result->rate_count++] = rate;
			}
		}
	}
	error = give(request, result, sizeof(*result));
	kfree_data(result, sizeof(*result));
	return error;
}

/* ---- get ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

static int
get(struct apple80211req *request)
{
	struct redwood_sta_state *state;
	int error = 0;

	switch (request->req_type) {
	case 43:
	case 44: {                              /* the driver's and the hardware's name: the text alone, in 256 bytes */
		static const char name[256] = "redwood: ath11k for the WCN6750";

		return give(request, name, sizeof(name));
	}
	case 12: {
		/*
		 * What the card can do, a bit each (apple80211_var.h: APPLE80211_CAP_*): the 13 bytes are the
		 * bits alone, from the first (the framework hands in a buffer that begins after the old
		 * header's version word). AES, AES-CCM, power management, short slot and preamble, WPA2, WME,
		 * short guard interval at 20 MHz. Read wrong, the framework sees no WPA2 and builds no join
		 * for a WPA2 network ("Unable to join").
		 */
		uint8_t bits[13] = { 0 };
		static const uint8_t has[] = { 2, 3, 6, 9, 10, 14, 17, 19 };

		for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof(has); i++) {
			bits[has[i] / 8] |= (uint8_t)(1u << (has[i] % 8));
		}
		return give(request, bits, sizeof(bits));
	}
	case 19: {                              /* the radio's power: one radio. Until the driver is up it counts as on: it */
		struct {                        /* is being brought up, and iOS asks this once, early */
			uint32_t version, radios, state[4];
		} answer = { .version = 1, .radios = 1, .state = { !redwood_sta_present() || redwood_sta_powered() } };

		return give(request, &answer, sizeof(answer));
	}
	case 15:                                /* the mode: a station (APPLE80211_M_STA) */
		request->req_val = 1;
		return 0;
	case 27:
	case 254: {                             /* the channels the radio may tune to */
		struct apple80211_channels *answer;
		struct redwood_sta_channel channels[96];
		unsigned count = redwood_sta_channels(channels, 96);

		if (count == 0 || (answer = kalloc_data(sizeof(*answer), Z_WAITOK | Z_ZERO)) == NULL) {
			return count == 0 ? ENXIO : ENOMEM;
		}
		answer->version = 1;
		answer->count = count;
		for (unsigned i = 0; i < count; i++) {
			channel_fill(&answer->channels[i], channels[i].frequency, channels[i].flags);
		}
		error = give(request, answer, sizeof(*answer));
		kfree_data(answer, sizeof(*answer));
		return error;
	}
	case 207: {                             /* ... and more of each */
		struct apple80211_channels_info *answer;
		struct redwood_sta_channel channels[96];
		unsigned count = redwood_sta_channels(channels, 96);

		if (count == 0 || (answer = kalloc_data(sizeof(*answer), Z_WAITOK | Z_ZERO)) == NULL) {
			return count == 0 ? ENXIO : ENOMEM;
		}
		answer->count = (uint16_t)count;
		for (unsigned i = 0; i < count; i++) {
			struct apple80211_channel channel;

			channel_fill(&channel, channels[i].frequency, channels[i].flags);
			answer->number[i] = (uint8_t)channel.channel;
			answer->dfs[i] = (channels[i].flags & REDWOOD_STA_CHANNEL_RADAR) != 0;
			answer->passive[i] = (channels[i].flags & REDWOOD_STA_CHANNEL_PASSIVE) != 0;
			answer->flags[i] = channel.flags;
		}
		error = give(request, answer, sizeof(*answer));
		kfree_data(answer, sizeof(*answer));
		return error;
	}
	case 21:                                /* how the last join went (0: not over yet) */
		lck_mtx_lock(&apple80211_lock);
		request->req_val = (int32_t)join_result;
		lck_mtx_unlock(&apple80211_lock);
		return 0;
	case 11: {                              /* what the last scan heard, one access point a request; EIO: that was all */
		struct redwood_sta_bss *bss = kalloc_data(sizeof(*bss), Z_WAITOK);
		unsigned index;
		bool there;

		if (bss == NULL) {
			return ENOMEM;
		}
		lck_mtx_lock(&apple80211_lock);
		index = result_next++;
		lck_mtx_unlock(&apple80211_lock);
		there = redwood_sta_heard(index, bss);
		error = there ? give_network(request, bss) : EIO;
		kfree_data(bss, sizeof(*bss));
		return error;
	}
	default:
		break;
	}

	/* the rest is about the network joined, and there is none unless the station says so */
	if ((state = kalloc_data(sizeof(*state), Z_WAITOK)) == NULL) {
		return ENOMEM;
	}
	redwood_sta_state(state);
	switch (request->req_type) {
	case 13:                                /* the state: APPLE80211_S_INIT 0, _SCAN 1, _AUTH 2, _ASSOC 3, _RUN 4 */
		request->req_val = state->phase == REDWOOD_STA_JOINED ? 4 : state->phase == REDWOOD_STA_JOINING ? 2 :
		    state->phase == REDWOOD_STA_SCANNING ? 1 : 0;
		break;
	case 1:                                 /* its name; the length goes back in the request */
		if (state->phase != REDWOOD_STA_JOINED) {
			error = ENXIO;
		} else if ((error = give(request, state->bss.ssid, state->bss.ssid_length)) == 0) {
			request->req_len = state->bss.ssid_length;
		}
		break;
	case 9:                                 /* its access point's address */
		error = state->phase != REDWOOD_STA_JOINED ? ENXIO : give(request, state->bss.bssid, 6);
		break;
	case 4: {                               /* its channel */
		struct {
			uint32_t version;
			struct apple80211_channel channel;
		} answer = { .version = 1 };

		if (state->phase != REDWOOD_STA_JOINED) {
			error = ENXIO;
		} else {
			channel_fill(&answer.channel, state->bss.frequency, 0);
			error = give(request, &answer, sizeof(answer));
		}
		break;
	}
	case 16: {                              /* how strongly it is heard: dBm, per radio and all together, twice over */
		struct {
			uint32_t version, radios, unit;
			int32_t each[4], all, each_ext[4], all_ext;
		} answer = { .version = 1, .radios = 1, .each = { state->bss.rssi }, .all = state->bss.rssi,
			     .each_ext = { state->bss.rssi }, .all_ext = state->bss.rssi };

		error = state->phase != REDWOOD_STA_JOINED ? ENXIO : give(request, &answer, sizeof(answer));
		break;
	}
	case 103:                               /* all of it, as a scan's result */
		error = state->phase != REDWOOD_STA_JOINED ? ENXIO : give_network(request, &state->bss);
		break;
	case 2: {                               /* how it was joined: open system, then WPA2 with a passphrase */
		struct {
			uint32_t version, lower, upper, extended;
		} answer = { .version = 1, .lower = 1, .upper = 8 };

		error = state->phase != REDWOOD_STA_JOINED ? ENXIO : give(request, &answer, sizeof(answer));
		break;
	}
	default:
		error = EOPNOTSUPP;
		break;
	}
	kfree_data(state, sizeof(*state));
	return error;
}

/* ---- set ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

static int
set_scan(const struct apple80211req *request, char *said, size_t said_size)
{
	struct apple80211_scan_request *asked;
	struct redwood_sta_scan *what;
	unsigned unknown = 0;
	int error;

	if (request->req_len != sizeof(*asked)) {
		return EINVAL;
	}
	if (!redwood_sta_present()) {
		return EBUSY;                   /* (the radio is still being brought up: the framework tries again) */
	}
	asked = kalloc_data(sizeof(*asked), Z_WAITOK);
	what = kalloc_data(sizeof(*what), Z_WAITOK | Z_ZERO);
	if (asked == NULL || what == NULL || (error = copyin(request->req_data, asked, sizeof(*asked))) != 0) {
		error = asked == NULL || what == NULL ? ENOMEM : error;
		goto out;
	}
	if (asked->ssid_length <= sizeof(what->ssid)) {
		what->ssid_length = (uint8_t)asked->ssid_length;
		memcpy(what->ssid, asked->ssid, asked->ssid_length);
	}
	what->passive = asked->scan_type == 2;
	what->dwell_ms = asked->dwell_ms;
	/* (more channels than there is room to name: every channel) */
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < asked->channel_count && i < 400 && asked->channel_count <= 64; i++) {
		unsigned frequency = channel_frequency(&asked->channels[i]);

		if (frequency != 0) {
			what->frequencies[what->frequency_count++] = (uint16_t)frequency;
		} else {
			unknown++;
		}
	}
	snprintf(said, said_size, " (a scan: type %u, %u channels of which %u are not the radio's, %u ms on each, a name of %u bytes, "
	    "%u more names, flags %#llx)", asked->scan_type, asked->channel_count, unknown, asked->dwell_ms, asked->ssid_length,
	    asked->name_count, asked->flags);
	if (asked->channel_count != 0 && asked->channel_count <= 64 && what->frequency_count == 0) {
		error = EINVAL;                 /* (nothing of what is asked for is a channel of this radio's) */
	} else {
		lck_mtx_lock(&apple80211_lock);
		result_next = 0;
		lck_mtx_unlock(&apple80211_lock);
		error = redwood_sta_ask_scan(what);
	}
out:
	if (asked != NULL) {
		kfree_data(asked, sizeof(*asked));
	}
	if (what != NULL) {
		kfree_data(what, sizeof(*what));
	}
	return error;
}

static int
set_join(const struct apple80211req *request, char *said, size_t said_size)
{
	struct apple80211_assoc *asked;
	struct redwood_sta_join *what;
	int error;

	if (request->req_len < offsetof(struct apple80211_assoc, rest)) {
		return EINVAL;
	}
	asked = kalloc_data(sizeof(*asked), Z_WAITOK | Z_ZERO);
	what = kalloc_data(sizeof(*what), Z_WAITOK | Z_ZERO);
	if (asked == NULL || what == NULL || (error = copyin(request->req_data, asked, offsetof(struct apple80211_assoc, rest))) != 0) {
		error = asked == NULL || what == NULL ? ENOMEM : error;
		goto out;
	}
	/* (lengths and kinds only: the name, the access point and the key stay out of the log) */
	snprintf(said, said_size, " (a join: a name of %u bytes, %s access point, authentication %#x/%#x, a key of %u bytes of kind %u)",
	    asked->ssid_length, asked->bssid[0] | asked->bssid[1] | asked->bssid[2] | asked->bssid[3] | asked->bssid[4] |
	    asked->bssid[5] ? "a given" : "any", asked->auth_lower, asked->auth_upper, asked->key_length, asked->key_cipher);
	if (asked->ssid_length == 0 || asked->ssid_length > sizeof(what->ssid)) {
		error = EINVAL;
		goto out;
	}
	what->ssid_length = (uint8_t)asked->ssid_length;
	memcpy(what->ssid, asked->ssid, asked->ssid_length);
	memcpy(what->bssid, asked->bssid, sizeof(what->bssid));
	if (asked->key_length == 0) {
		what->security = REDWOOD_STA_OPEN;
	} else if (asked->key_cipher == CIPHER_PASSPHRASE && asked->key_length >= 8 && asked->key_length <= 63) {
		what->security = REDWOOD_STA_WPA2_PSK;
		what->passphrase_length = (uint8_t)asked->key_length;
		memcpy(what->passphrase, asked->key, asked->key_length);
	} else if (asked->key_cipher == CIPHER_PMK && asked->key_length == sizeof(what->pmk)) {
		what->security = REDWOOD_STA_WPA2_PSK;
		memcpy(what->pmk, asked->key, sizeof(what->pmk));
	} else {
		error = EINVAL;
		goto out;
	}
	lck_mtx_lock(&apple80211_lock);
	join_result = 0;
	lck_mtx_unlock(&apple80211_lock);
	error = redwood_sta_ask_join(what);
out:
	if (asked != NULL) {
		memset_s(asked, sizeof(*asked), 0, sizeof(*asked));
		kfree_data(asked, sizeof(*asked));
	}
	if (what != NULL) {
		memset_s(what, sizeof(*what), 0, sizeof(*what));
		kfree_data(what, sizeof(*what));
	}
	return error;
}

static int
set(const struct apple80211req *request, char *said, size_t said_size)
{
	switch (request->req_type) {
	case 20:
		return set_join(request, said, said_size);
	case 22:                                /* leave the network */
		return redwood_sta_ask_leave();
	case 19: {                              /* the radio's power */
		struct {
			uint32_t version, radios, state[4];
		} asked;
		int error;

		if (request->req_len < sizeof(asked) || (error = copyin(request->req_data, &asked, sizeof(asked))) != 0) {
			return request->req_len < sizeof(asked) ? EINVAL : error;
		}
		snprintf(said, said_size, " (power: %s)", asked.state[0] ? "on" : "off");
		return redwood_sta_ask_power(asked.state[0] != 0);
	}
	case 10:
		return set_scan(request, said, said_size);
	default:
		return EOPNOTSUPP;
	}
}

/* ---- events -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

static void
post(uint32_t code, const void *data, uint32_t length)
{
	struct kev_msg message = { .vendor_code = KEV_VENDOR_APPLE, .kev_class = KEV_IEEE80211_CLASS, .kev_subclass = 1,
		                   .event_code = code };
	char name[16];

	memcpy(name, interface_name, sizeof(name));
	message.dv[0].data_length = sizeof(name);
	message.dv[0].data_ptr = name;
	if (length != 0) {
		message.dv[1].data_length = length;
		message.dv[1].data_ptr = __DECONST(void *, data);
	}
	kev_post_msg(&message);
}

/* What the station side says has happened (bsd/dev/redwood_sta.c calls this, on its thread or the station's). */
void
redwood_apple80211_event(enum redwood_sta_event event, int status)
{
	static unsigned said;

	if (said < 200) {
		said++;
		printf("apple80211: the station says: %s, %d\n", event == REDWOOD_STA_POWER ? "power" : event == REDWOOD_STA_SCAN_DONE ?
		    "a scan is over" : event == REDWOOD_STA_JOIN_DONE ? "a join is over" : "the link", status);
	}
	switch (event) {
	case REDWOOD_STA_POWER:
		post(EVENT_POWER_CHANGED, NULL, 0);
		break;
	case REDWOOD_STA_SCAN_DONE:
		lck_mtx_lock(&apple80211_lock);
		result_next = 0;
		lck_mtx_unlock(&apple80211_lock);
		post(EVENT_SCAN_DONE, NULL, 0);
		break;
	case REDWOOD_STA_JOIN_DONE:
		lck_mtx_lock(&apple80211_lock);
		join_result = status == 0 ? 1 : status == EAUTH ? 21 : status == ETIMEDOUT ? 9 : 2;
		lck_mtx_unlock(&apple80211_lock);
		post(EVENT_ASSOC_DONE, NULL, 0);
		break;
	case REDWOOD_STA_LINK: {
		struct apple80211_link_changed link = { .down = status != 1, .involuntary = status != 1 && status != 0,
			                                .reason = status != 1 && status != 0 ? 4 : 0 };      /* (4: gone, not asked) */
		struct redwood_sta_state *state = kalloc_data(sizeof(*state), Z_WAITOK | Z_ZERO);

		if (state != NULL) {
			redwood_sta_state(state);
			link.rssi = status == 1 ? state->bss.rssi : 0;
			kfree_data(state, sizeof(*state));
		}
		post(EVENT_SSID_CHANGED, NULL, 0);
		post(EVENT_BSSID_CHANGED, NULL, 0);
		post(EVENT_LINK_CHANGED, &link, sizeof(link));
		break;
	}
	}
}

/* ---- the requests as they arrive --------------------------------------------------------------------- */

/*
 * How often each kind of request came and how it fared: said when the run ends, because the
 * lines said along the way can be lost with the middle of a long log.
 */
static struct {
	int32_t type;
	bool set;
	unsigned times, answered;
	int last_error;
} kinds[96];
static unsigned kind_count;

static void
note(const struct apple80211req *request, bool is_set, int error)
{
	unsigned i;

	lck_mtx_lock(&apple80211_lock);
	for (i = 0; i < kind_count && !(kinds[i].type == request->req_type && kinds[i].set == is_set); i++) {
	}
	if (i < sizeof(kinds) / sizeof(kinds[0])) {
		if (i == kind_count) {
			kinds[kind_count++] = (typeof(kinds[0])) { .type = request->req_type, .set = is_set };
		}
		kinds[i].times++;
		kinds[i].answered += error == 0;
		kinds[i].last_error = error != 0 ? error : kinds[i].last_error;
	}
	lck_mtx_unlock(&apple80211_lock);
}

void
redwood_apple80211_summary(void)
{
	static bool said;

	if (said) {
		return;
	}
	said = true;
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < kind_count; i++) {
		printf("apple80211: in this run: %s %d (%s) %u times, answered %u times%s", kinds[i].set ? "set" : "get", kinds[i].type,
		    type_name(kinds[i].type), kinds[i].times, kinds[i].answered, kinds[i].last_error == 0 ? "\n" : "");
		if (kinds[i].last_error != 0) {
			printf("; the last refusal: %d%s\n", kinds[i].last_error, kinds[i].last_error == EOPNOTSUPP ? " (not built)" : "");
		}
	}
}

/* An Apple80211 request for the radio's interface, from the process that is running now. */
errno_t
redwood_apple80211_ioctl(u_long command, void *data)
{
	static unsigned said;
	struct apple80211req *request = data;
	char who[32] = "?", what[200] = "";
	bool is_set = command == SIOCSA80211;
	int error;

	if (command != SIOCSA80211 && command != SIOCGA80211) {
		return EOPNOTSUPP;
	}
	proc_selfname(who, sizeof(who));
	error = is_set ? set(request, what, sizeof(what)) : get(request);
	note(request, is_set, error);
	/* (a request that is repeated for ever is said a few hundred times) */
	if (said < 800) {
		said++;
		printf("apple80211: %s %s %d (%s), value %d, %u bytes%s: %s", who, is_set ? "sets" : "gets", request->req_type,
		    type_name(request->req_type), request->req_val, request->req_len, what, error == 0 ? "answered\n" : error ==
		    EOPNOTSUPP ? "REFUSED\n" : "");
		if (error != 0 && error != EOPNOTSUPP) {
			printf("error %d\n", error);
		}
	}
	return error;
}

```

`xnu/files/bsd/dev/redwood_audio.c`:

```c
/*
 * /dev/redwood-audio: the sound that iOS plays (see sys/redwood_audio.h).
 *
 * What is written goes two ways:
 *
 *   to a sink   a driver that plays it: the virtio sound device under QEMU
 *               (redwood_virtio_sound.c). On the phone there is none yet (redwood_speaker.c
 *               is where it begins).
 *
 *   into a recording, with boot-arg rec_sound=N: the first N seconds of sound are also kept
 *               in one piece of memory that is left in place when the kernel returns to the
 *               loader, which hands it to the host ("xl sound"; under QEMU, the monitor's
 *               pmemsave), where tools/sound.py makes a WAV file of it. Only what is played
 *               takes room, the silence in between does not: every write is stored with the
 *               time it was made.
 *
 *                 struct rec_header, then per write: struct rec_block, frames * 4 bytes
 *
 *               With rec_sound_fed=1 as well, the recording has instead what the speakers' guard
 *               let through (redwood_guard.c, on the phone): what reaches the amplifiers. With
 *               rec_sound_mic=1, what the main microphone hears (redwood_mic.c, mic=3), in both
 *               channels.
 *
 * When the writer has stopped, a line in the log says how long it wrote, at what rate, how much
 * of it was not silence and how loud: the only way to "hear" a machine one cannot listen to.
 * (The audio server writes for as long as its device runs, a second or two beyond the sound.)
 */
#include <kern/clock.h>
#include <kern/locks.h>
#include <kern/thread_call.h>
#include <libkern/libkern.h>
#include <mach/mach_types.h>
#include <mach/vm_param.h>
#include <miscfs/devfs/devfs.h>
#include <pexpert/pexpert.h>
#include <sys/conf.h>
#include <sys/errno.h>
#include <sys/proc.h>
#include <sys/redwood_audio.h>
#include <sys/systm.h>
#include <sys/uio.h>
#include <vm/vm_kern.h>

extern uint64_t kvtophys(vm_offset_t va);       /* pmap_paddr_t */

#define CHUNK_FRAMES    1024            /* what one pass of write() moves */
#define QUIET_MS        500             /* no write for this long: the writer has stopped */
#define SILENCE         8               /* samples no larger than this are silence */
#define REC_MAX_SECONDS 1200            /* 220 MB */

struct rec_header {
	char     magic[8];              /* "RWSND001" */
	uint32_t rate, channels;        /* REDWOOD_AUDIO_RATE, REDWOOD_AUDIO_CHANNELS; the samples are 16-bit */
	uint32_t blocks;
	uint32_t reserved;
};
struct rec_block {
	uint64_t nanoseconds;           /* when it was written, since the kernel started */
	uint32_t frames;
	uint32_t reserved;
};

/* { physical address, bytes, kernel address } of the recording, for the loader: osfmk/arm64/loader_return.c */
extern uint64_t loader_sound[3];

static LCK_GRP_DECLARE(audio_lck_grp, "redwood-audio");
static LCK_MTX_DECLARE(audio_lock, &audio_lck_grp);

static redwood_audio_sink_t audio_sink;

static uint8_t *rec_base;
static bool rec_fed;                    /* boot-arg rec_sound_fed=1: what the guard let through is recorded, not what was written */
static bool rec_mic;                    /* boot-arg rec_sound_mic=1: what the microphone hears (redwood_mic.c) */
static uint64_t rec_size, rec_used;
static uint64_t rec_frames, rec_frames_max;

/* the stretch of writing in progress */
static uint64_t stretch_first, stretch_last;    /* mach_absolute_time() of its first and its latest write */
static uint64_t stretch_frames, stretch_latest; /* frames written, and how many of them by the latest write */
static uint64_t stretch_sound, stretch_lost;    /* frames in writes that were not silence; frames the sink did not take */
static uint32_t stretch_peak;                   /* the largest sample, as an absolute value */
static thread_call_t report_call;
static bool report_armed;

static void
audio_report(__unused thread_call_param_t p0, __unused thread_call_param_t p1)
{
	uint64_t frames, latest, sound, lost, deadline, since = 0, lasted = 0;
	uint32_t loudest;

	lck_mtx_lock(&audio_lock);
	absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(mach_absolute_time() - stretch_last, &since);
	if (since < QUIET_MS * NSEC_PER_MSEC) {
		/* still writing: look again later */
		clock_interval_to_deadline(2 * QUIET_MS, NSEC_PER_MSEC, &deadline);
		thread_call_enter_delayed(report_call, deadline);
		lck_mtx_unlock(&audio_lock);
		return;
	}
	absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(stretch_last - stretch_first, &lasted);
	frames = stretch_frames;
	latest = stretch_latest;
	sound = stretch_sound;
	lost = stretch_lost;
	loudest = stretch_peak;
	stretch_frames = stretch_sound = stretch_lost = 0;
	stretch_peak = 0;
	report_armed = false;
	lck_mtx_unlock(&audio_lock);

	printf("redwood-audio: %llu.%02llu s written", frames / REDWOOD_AUDIO_RATE,
	    frames % REDWOOD_AUDIO_RATE * 100 / REDWOOD_AUDIO_RATE);
	if (lasted >= NSEC_PER_SEC) {
		/* what was written before the latest write took the time between the first and the latest */
		printf(" at %llu frames a second", (frames - latest) * NSEC_PER_SEC / lasted);
	}
	printf(", %llu.%02llu s of it sound, peak %u%% of full scale", sound / REDWOOD_AUDIO_RATE,
	    sound % REDWOOD_AUDIO_RATE * 100 / REDWOOD_AUDIO_RATE, loudest * 100 / 32768);
	if (lost) {
		printf(", %llu ms lost (the sink was full)", lost * 1000 / REDWOOD_AUDIO_RATE);
	}
	printf("\n");
}

/* With audio_lock held. */
static void
audio_record(const int16_t *frames, uint32_t count)
{
	struct rec_header *header = (struct rec_header *)rec_base;
	struct rec_block *block;
	uint64_t bytes = (uint64_t)count * REDWOOD_AUDIO_FRAME;

	if (rec_base == NULL || rec_frames >= rec_frames_max || rec_used + sizeof(*block) + bytes > rec_size) {
		return;
	}
	block = (struct rec_block *)(rec_base + rec_used);
	absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(mach_absolute_time(), &block->nanoseconds);
	block->frames = count;
	block->reserved = 0;
	memcpy(block + 1, frames, bytes);
	rec_used += sizeof(*block) + bytes;
	rec_frames += count;
	header->blocks++;
	loader_sound[1] = rec_used;
	if (rec_frames >= rec_frames_max) {
		printf("redwood-audio: recording finished: %llu s in %u writes\n", rec_frames / REDWOOD_AUDIO_RATE, header->blocks);
	}
}

bool
redwood_audio_recording_fed(void)
{
	return rec_fed && rec_base != NULL && rec_frames < rec_frames_max;
}

bool
redwood_audio_recording_mic(void)
{
	return rec_mic && rec_base != NULL && rec_frames < rec_frames_max;
}

/* From the speakers' feeder: what the guard let through, into the recording (rec_sound_fed=1). */
void
redwood_audio_record_fed(const int16_t *frames, uint32_t count)
{
	lck_mtx_lock(&audio_lock);
	audio_record(frames, count);
	lck_mtx_unlock(&audio_lock);
}

static void
audio_play(const int16_t *frames, uint32_t count)
{
	uint32_t loudest = 0, taken = 0;
	uint64_t deadline;

	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count * REDWOOD_AUDIO_CHANNELS; i++) {
		uint32_t level = frames[i] < 0 ? -(int32_t)frames[i] : frames[i];

		if (level > loudest) {
			loudest = level;
		}
	}
	lck_mtx_lock(&audio_lock);
	if (!rec_fed && !rec_mic) {
		audio_record(frames, count);
	}
	if (audio_sink != NULL) {
		taken = audio_sink(frames, count);
		stretch_lost += count - taken;
	}
	stretch_last = mach_absolute_time();
	if (stretch_frames == 0) {
		stretch_first = stretch_last;
	}
	stretch_frames += count;
	stretch_latest = count;
	if (loudest > SILENCE) {
		stretch_sound += count;
	}
	if (loudest > stretch_peak) {
		stretch_peak = loudest;
	}
	if (!report_armed && report_call != NULL) {
		report_armed = true;
		clock_interval_to_deadline(2 * QUIET_MS, NSEC_PER_MSEC, &deadline);
		thread_call_enter_delayed(report_call, deadline);
	}
	lck_mtx_unlock(&audio_lock);
}

void
redwood_audio_set_sink(const char *name, redwood_audio_sink_t sink)
{
	lck_mtx_lock(&audio_lock);
	audio_sink = sink;
	lck_mtx_unlock(&audio_lock);
	printf("redwood-audio: sound goes to %s\n", name);
}

static int
audio_open(__unused dev_t dev, __unused int flags, __unused int devtype, __unused struct proc *p)
{
	return 0;
}

static int
audio_close(__unused dev_t dev, __unused int flags, __unused int devtype, __unused struct proc *p)
{
	return 0;
}

static int
audio_write(__unused dev_t dev, struct uio *uio, __unused int ioflag)
{
	int16_t frames[CHUNK_FRAMES * REDWOOD_AUDIO_CHANNELS];
	int error = 0;

	while (uio_resid(uio) >= REDWOOD_AUDIO_FRAME) {
		user_ssize_t bytes = uio_resid(uio);

		if (bytes > (user_ssize_t)sizeof(frames)) {
			bytes = sizeof(frames);
		}
		bytes -= bytes % REDWOOD_AUDIO_FRAME;
		error = uiomove((caddr_t)frames, (int)bytes, uio);
		if (error) {
			break;
		}
		audio_play(frames, (uint32_t)(bytes / REDWOOD_AUDIO_FRAME));
	}
	return error;
}

/* the speakers' volume, as iOS sets it (sys/redwood_audio.h): kept for the sink's driver to look at */
static uint32_t volume_below, volume_generation;
static bool volume_muted;

static int
audio_ioctl(__unused dev_t dev, u_long command, caddr_t data, __unused int flags, __unused struct proc *p)
{
	const struct redwood_audio_volume *volume = (const struct redwood_audio_volume *)data;

	if (command != REDWOOD_AUDIO_SET_VOLUME) {
		return ENOTTY;
	}
	lck_mtx_lock(&audio_lock);
	volume_below = volume->below;
	volume_muted = volume->muted != 0;
	volume_generation++;
	lck_mtx_unlock(&audio_lock);
	printf("redwood-audio: the volume: %s%u.%03u dB under the loudest\n", volume->muted ? "muted; " : "", volume->below / 8,
	    volume->below % 8 * 125);
	return 0;
}

bool
redwood_audio_volume(uint32_t *below, bool *muted, uint32_t *generation)
{
	lck_mtx_lock(&audio_lock);
	*below = volume_below;
	*muted = volume_muted;
	*generation = volume_generation;
	lck_mtx_unlock(&audio_lock);
	return *generation != 0;
}

static const struct cdevsw audio_cdevsw = {
	.d_open = audio_open, .d_close = audio_close, .d_read = eno_rdwrt, .d_write = audio_write,
	.d_ioctl = audio_ioctl, .d_stop = eno_stop, .d_reset = eno_reset, .d_select = eno_select,
	.d_mmap = eno_mmap, .d_strategy = eno_strat, .d_type = 0
};

static void
audio_recording_init(void)
{
	struct rec_header *header;
	uint32_t seconds = 0, fed = 0;
	vm_offset_t memory = 0;
	uint64_t size;

	if (!PE_parse_boot_argn("rec_sound", &seconds, sizeof(seconds)) || seconds == 0) {
		return;
	}
	if (seconds > REC_MAX_SECONDS) {
		seconds = REC_MAX_SECONDS;
	}
	/* the samples, and a block header for every write of ten milliseconds or more */
	size = sizeof(*header) + (uint64_t)seconds * (REDWOOD_AUDIO_RATE * REDWOOD_AUDIO_FRAME + 100 * sizeof(struct rec_block));
	size = round_page(size);
	/* one piece of physical memory: the loader will send it over USB as it lies */
	if (kmem_alloc_contig(kernel_map, &memory, size, PAGE_MASK, 0, 0, KMA_KOBJECT | KMA_ZERO | KMA_DATA,
	    VM_KERN_MEMORY_IOKIT) != KERN_SUCCESS) {
		printf("redwood-audio: no memory for a recording of %u s (%llu MB)\n", seconds, size >> 20);
		return;
	}
	header = (struct rec_header *)memory;
	memcpy(header->magic, "RWSND001", 8);
	header->rate = REDWOOD_AUDIO_RATE;
	header->channels = REDWOOD_AUDIO_CHANNELS;
	rec_size = size;
	rec_used = sizeof(*header);
	rec_frames_max = (uint64_t)seconds * REDWOOD_AUDIO_RATE;
	rec_base = (uint8_t *)memory;
	loader_sound[0] = kvtophys(memory);
	loader_sound[1] = rec_used;
	loader_sound[2] = (uint64_t)memory;
	PE_parse_boot_argn("rec_sound_fed", &fed, sizeof(fed));
	rec_fed = fed != 0;
	fed = 0;
	PE_parse_boot_argn("rec_sound_mic", &fed, sizeof(fed));
	rec_mic = fed != 0;
	printf("redwood-audio: recording the first %u s of sound%s, into %llu MB at %#llx\n", seconds,
	    rec_fed ? " as the speakers' guard lets it through" : rec_mic ? " the microphone hears (in both channels)" : "", size >> 20,
	    loader_sound[0]);
}

void
redwood_audio_init(void)
{
	int major = cdevsw_add(-1, &audio_cdevsw);

	if (major < 0 || devfs_make_node(makedev(major, 0), DEVFS_CHAR, UID_ROOT, GID_WHEEL, 0666, "redwood-audio") == NULL) {
		printf("redwood-audio: cannot create the device\n");
		return;
	}
	report_call = thread_call_allocate(audio_report, NULL);
	audio_recording_init();
	redwood_virtio_sound_init();
	redwood_speaker_init();
	redwood_haptic_init();
	redwood_torch_init();
	redwood_camera_init();
}
```

`xnu/files/bsd/dev/redwood_battery.c`:

```c
/*
 * Battery monitor for Xiaomi redwood (POCO X5 Pro).
 *
 * Redwood selects PM7325B and qcom,battery-charger over PMIC GLINK/ADSP, not
 * the local PM7250B/QG layout.  The resident UEFI contains the matching
 * Qualcomm charger drivers.  xnuloader owns that firmware context on core 0,
 * polls it, and publishes a read-only cache; XNU only consumes that cache.
 * Charger limits and JEITA protection therefore remain firmware-owned.
 */
#include <kern/clock.h>
#include <kern/thread.h>
#include <libkern/libkern.h>
#include <mach/mach_types.h>
#include <pexpert/pexpert.h>
#include <sys/redwood_input.h>
#include <sys/sysctl.h>
#include <sys/systm.h>

extern vm_offset_t ml_io_map(vm_offset_t phys_addr, vm_size_t size);

#define LOADER_BATTERY_MAGIC            0x2154544142574452ULL
#define LOADER_BATTERY_VERSION          1
#define LOADER_BATTERY_VALID            (1u << 0)
#define LOADER_BATTERY_PRESENT          (1u << 1)
#define LOADER_BATTERY_CHARGER_PRESENT  (1u << 2)
#define LOADER_BATTERY_VOLTAGE_VALID    (1u << 3)
#define LOADER_BATTERY_CHARGING         (1u << 4)
#define LOADER_BATTERY_SOC_ESTIMATED    (1u << 5)
#define LOADER_PAGE_SIZE                0x4000UL

struct loader_battery {
	uint64_t magic;
	uint32_t version, size;
	volatile uint32_t sequence;
	uint32_t flags;
	int32_t soc_percent, voltage_mv, current_ma, temperature_c;
	uint32_t charger_action, polls, failures, reserved;
};

static volatile struct loader_battery *shared_battery;
static int battery_soc_percent = -1, battery_voltage_mv = -1, battery_current_ma;
static int battery_temperature_c = -273, battery_present, battery_charger_present;
static int battery_charging, battery_soc_estimated, battery_charger_action = -1;
static uint64_t battery_updates, battery_failures;

/* for others in the kernel (the flashlight's thermal guard): -273 while it is not known */
int
redwood_battery_temperature(void)
{
	return battery_temperature_c;
}

SYSCTL_NODE(_kern, OID_AUTO, redwood, CTLFLAG_RW | CTLFLAG_LOCKED, 0, "redwood phone bits");
SYSCTL_INT(_kern_redwood, OID_AUTO, battery_soc, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED,
    &battery_soc_percent, 0, "battery state of charge, 0..100 percent, or -1 if unknown");
SYSCTL_INT(_kern_redwood, OID_AUTO, battery_voltage_mv, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED,
    &battery_voltage_mv, 0, "battery voltage in millivolts, or -1 if unknown");
SYSCTL_INT(_kern_redwood, OID_AUTO, battery_current_ma, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED,
    &battery_current_ma, 0, "battery current reported by Qualcomm firmware, in milliamps");
SYSCTL_INT(_kern_redwood, OID_AUTO, battery_temperature_c, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED,
    &battery_temperature_c, 0, "battery temperature reported by Qualcomm firmware, in Celsius");
SYSCTL_INT(_kern_redwood, OID_AUTO, battery_present, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED,
    &battery_present, 0, "1 if Qualcomm firmware reports a battery");
SYSCTL_INT(_kern_redwood, OID_AUTO, battery_charger_present, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED,
    &battery_charger_present, 0, "1 if Qualcomm firmware reports an attached charger");
SYSCTL_INT(_kern_redwood, OID_AUTO, battery_charging, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED,
    &battery_charging, 0, "1 while an attached charger is charging a non-full battery");
SYSCTL_INT(_kern_redwood, OID_AUTO, battery_soc_estimated, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED,
    &battery_soc_estimated, 0, "1 only when SOC had to be estimated from voltage");
SYSCTL_INT(_kern_redwood, OID_AUTO, battery_charger_action, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED,
    &battery_charger_action, 0, "last Qualcomm charger action, for diagnostics");

static bool
battery_snapshot(struct loader_battery *out)
{
	uint32_t before, after;

	for (unsigned retry = 0; retry < 4; retry++) {
		before = shared_battery->sequence;
		if (before & 1) continue;
		__asm__ volatile ("dmb ishld" ::: "memory");
		memcpy(out, (const void *)(uintptr_t)shared_battery, sizeof(*out));
		__asm__ volatile ("dmb ishld" ::: "memory");
		after = shared_battery->sequence;
		if (before == after && !(after & 1)) return true;
	}
	return false;
}

static void
battery_poll(void)
{
	struct loader_battery sample;

	if (!battery_snapshot(&sample) || sample.magic != LOADER_BATTERY_MAGIC ||
	    sample.version != LOADER_BATTERY_VERSION || sample.size < sizeof(sample) ||
	    !(sample.flags & LOADER_BATTERY_VALID) || sample.soc_percent < 0 || sample.soc_percent > 100) {
		battery_failures++;
		return;
	}
	battery_soc_percent = sample.soc_percent;
	battery_voltage_mv = (sample.flags & LOADER_BATTERY_VOLTAGE_VALID) ? sample.voltage_mv : -1;
	battery_current_ma = sample.current_ma;
	battery_temperature_c = sample.temperature_c;
	battery_present = (sample.flags & LOADER_BATTERY_PRESENT) != 0;
	battery_charger_present = (sample.flags & LOADER_BATTERY_CHARGER_PRESENT) != 0;
	battery_charging = (sample.flags & LOADER_BATTERY_CHARGING) != 0;
	battery_soc_estimated = (sample.flags & LOADER_BATTERY_SOC_ESTIMATED) != 0;
	battery_charger_action = (int)sample.charger_action;
	battery_updates++;
}

/*
 * What the audio DSP's battery manager says (bsd/dev/redwood_adsp.c, with adsp=1 unless battmgr=0):
 * the values that Android shows, from where Android takes them. They are kept here for the sysctls
 * and passed on to the power source that iOS reads (iokit/Kernel/RedwoodBattery.cpp).
 */
static int battery_full_uah, battery_design_uah, battery_cycles, battery_source_dsp;

SYSCTL_INT(_kern_redwood, OID_AUTO, battery_full_uah, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED,
    &battery_full_uah, 0, "the battery's full charge as the fuel gauge has learnt it, in uAh (0 if unknown)");
SYSCTL_INT(_kern_redwood, OID_AUTO, battery_design_uah, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED,
    &battery_design_uah, 0, "the battery's charge as designed, in uAh (0 if unknown)");
SYSCTL_INT(_kern_redwood, OID_AUTO, battery_cycles, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED,
    &battery_cycles, 0, "the battery's charge cycles (0 if unknown)");
SYSCTL_INT(_kern_redwood, OID_AUTO, battery_from_dsp, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED,
    &battery_source_dsp, 0, "1 when the values come from the audio DSP's battery manager");

extern void RedwoodBatteryReport(const void *state, unsigned size);     /* iokit/Kernel/RedwoodBattery.cpp */

void
redwood_battery_report(const struct redwood_battery_state *b)
{
	int percent = (b->percent_hundredths + 50) / 100;

	battery_soc_percent = percent < 0 ? 0 : percent > 100 ? 100 : percent;
	battery_voltage_mv = b->voltage_uv / 1000;
	battery_current_ma = b->current_ua / 1000;
	battery_temperature_c = (b->temperature_hundredths + 50) / 100;
	battery_present = b->present != 0;
	battery_charger_present = b->external != 0;
	battery_charging = b->status == 1;      /* POWER_SUPPLY_STATUS_CHARGING */
	battery_soc_estimated = 0;
	battery_charger_action = b->status;
	if (b->full_uah > 0) {
		battery_full_uah = b->full_uah;
	}
	if (b->design_uah > 0) {
		battery_design_uah = b->design_uah;
	}
	if (b->cycles > 0) {
		battery_cycles = b->cycles;
	}
	battery_source_dsp = 1;
	battery_updates++;
	RedwoodBatteryReport(b, sizeof(*b));
}

static void
battery_thread(__unused void *parameter, __unused wait_result_t result)
{
	for (unsigned tick = 0;; tick++) {
		battery_poll();
		if (tick % 12 == 0) {
			printf("battery: SOC=%d%%%s, V=%d mV, I=%d mA, T=%d C, battery=%d charger=%d charging=%d "
			    "action=%d (%llu reads, %llu failed)\n", battery_soc_percent,
			    battery_soc_estimated ? " (voltage estimate)" : "", battery_voltage_mv,
			    battery_current_ma, battery_temperature_c, battery_present, battery_charger_present,
			    battery_charging, battery_charger_action, battery_updates, battery_failures);
		}
		delay_for_interval(5000, NSEC_PER_MSEC);
	}
}

void
redwood_battery_init(void)
{
	uint32_t enabled = 0;
	uint64_t shared_pa = 0;
	vm_offset_t page;
	thread_t thread;

	if (!PE_parse_boot_argn("battery", &enabled, sizeof(enabled)) || !enabled) return;
	if (!PE_parse_boot_argn("battery_shared_pa", &shared_pa, sizeof(shared_pa)) || shared_pa == 0) {
		printf("battery: xnuloader did not provide battery_shared_pa\n");
		return;
	}
	page = ml_io_map((vm_offset_t)(shared_pa & ~(LOADER_PAGE_SIZE - 1)), LOADER_PAGE_SIZE);
	shared_battery = (volatile struct loader_battery *)(page + (shared_pa & (LOADER_PAGE_SIZE - 1)));
	if (shared_battery->magic != LOADER_BATTERY_MAGIC || shared_battery->version != LOADER_BATTERY_VERSION ||
	    shared_battery->size < sizeof(struct loader_battery)) {
		printf("battery: bad xnuloader cache at %#llx (magic %#llx version %u size %u)\n", shared_pa,
		    shared_battery->magic, shared_battery->version, shared_battery->size);
		return;
	}
	printf("battery: Qualcomm UEFI cache at pa %#llx; polling every 5 seconds\n", shared_pa);
	if (kernel_thread_start(battery_thread, NULL, &thread) == KERN_SUCCESS) thread_deallocate(thread);
}
```

`xnu/files/bsd/dev/redwood_buttons.c`:

```c
/*
 * The buttons of the POCO X5 Pro (redwood) -- power, volume up, volume down -- as a source of
 * button records for /dev/redwood-touch (sys/redwood_input.h). Only with boot-arg buttons=1:
 * every address below belongs to this phone.
 *
 * None of the three is a pin of the SoC. They are inputs of two of the power management chips:
 *   power        KPDPWR_N of the power-on block ("PON") of the PMK8350
 *   volume down  RESIN_N of the same block
 *   volume up    GPIO6 of the PM7325, pulled up; the key pulls it low
 * Both chips sit on the SPMI bus (slaves 0 and 1), and the way to that bus is the SoC's "PMIC
 * arbiter": it owns the bus and gives each of the systems on the chip (this one, the modem, the
 * always-on processor, TrustZone...) a set of registers per PMIC peripheral -- a "channel" -- to
 * ask for a transfer with. Reads go through the "observer" channels, which every system has for
 * every peripheral, whoever owns it.
 *
 * THIS DRIVER ONLY READS. Nothing is written to either chip, neither a register of a PMIC nor
 * the configuration of the pin: the PMICs make the phone's supplies, and a wrong write there
 * can switch one off. The firmware reads the same keys itself (volume down and volume up choose
 * between fastboot and recovery) and has left both inputs as they are needed; the driver checks
 * that before it believes them, and where it finds something else it says so and leaves that
 * key alone. The only thing written is the command word that asks the arbiter for a read.
 *
 * What a press is: the PON's "real time status" has a bit per key, set while the key is held
 * (after the block's own debouncing); the GPIO's has the level of the pin. A thread reads the
 * two registers 60 times a second, and a key has changed when two looks in a row say so. A key
 * that reads as held before it has ever been seen released is not believed (a pin that is not
 * what it was taken for must not become a volume key held down for the whole session).
 * No interrupt is used; what one would take is said at the end of this file.
 *
 * The mapping: the phone has what the iPhone X has, whose user space runs here -- a side button
 * and two volume keys, no home button. Power is the side button (REDWOOD_BUTTON_LOCK).
 *
 * The bring-up is made in steps, each said in the log before it is made. Boot-arg
 * buttons_steps=N stops after the first N:
 *   1  map the arbiter and read its version             (the first access to that block)
 *   2  find the channels of the two peripherals         (reads of the arbiter's tables)
 *   3  ask each peripheral what it is                   (the first transfers on the bus)
 *   4  read how the keys' inputs are set up, and what they say now
 *   5  watch them                                       (the default)
 *
 * Register layouts: Linux drivers/spmi/spmi-pmic-arb.c (arbiter version 5),
 * drivers/input/misc/pm8941-pwrkey.c (the "pmk8350" kind), drivers/pinctrl/qcom/pinctrl-spmi-gpio.c,
 * and the phone's own device tree (qcom,spmi@c440000, pon_hlos@1300, gpio_keys).
 */
#include <kern/clock.h>
#include <kern/locks.h>
#include <kern/thread.h>
#include <libkern/libkern.h>
#include <mach/mach_types.h>
#include <pexpert/pexpert.h>
#include <sys/redwood_input.h>
#include <sys/systm.h>

extern vm_offset_t ml_io_map(vm_offset_t phys_addr, vm_size_t size);
extern kern_return_t thread_terminate(thread_t thread);

/*
 * Every line goes to the loader's log directly as well: without -v the kernel's own messages
 * reach that log only at the end of a run (with the kernel's message buffer), and "xl log"
 * during a run is to show a press when it happens.
 */
extern void loader_log_putc(char c);

static int say(const char *format, ...) __printflike(1, 2);

static int
say(const char *format, ...)
{
	char line[400];
	va_list list;

	va_start(list, format);
	vsnprintf(line, sizeof(line), format, list);
	va_end(list);
	for (const char *c = line; *c != 0; c++) {
		loader_log_putc(*c);
	}
	return printf("%s", line);
}
#define printf say

static inline uint32_t
rd(vm_offset_t address)
{
	return *(volatile uint32_t *)address;
}

static inline void
wr(vm_offset_t address, uint32_t value)
{
	*(volatile uint32_t *)address = value;
}

/* ---- the PMIC arbiter ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

#define ARB_CORE_PHYS           0x0c440000UL    /* "core": the version, and which peripheral each channel is */
#define ARB_CORE_SIZE           0x1100UL
#define ARB_CNFG_PHYS           0x0c40a000UL    /* "cnfg": which system owns each channel */
#define ARB_CNFG_SIZE           0x1000UL
#define ARB_OBSERVER_PHYS       0x0e600000UL    /* "obsrvr": 0x10000 per system, 0x80 per channel in it */
#define ARB_OBSERVER_SIZE       0x10000UL       /* ours is the first */
#define ARB_SYSTEM              0               /* who we are to the arbiter: the device tree's "qcom,ee" */

#define ARB_VERSION             0x000
#define ARB_VERSION_5           0x50000000u     /* what follows is version 5's; 7 moved things again */
#define ARB_VERSION_7           0x70000000u
#define ARB_FEATURES            0x004           /* [10:0] the number of channels */
#define ARB_CHANNEL(n)          (0x900 + 4 * (n))       /* core: [19:8] slave and peripheral, [24] interrupts go to the owner */
#define ARB_CHANNEL_INTERRUPTS  (1u << 24)
#define ARB_OWNER(n)            (0x700 + 4 * (n))       /* cnfg: [2:0] the system that may write through channel n */
#define ARB_MAX_CHANNELS        512

#define OBSERVER_COMMAND        0x00
#define OBSERVER_STATUS         0x08
#define OBSERVER_DATA0          0x18            /* the bytes read, the first in the lowest byte */
#define OBSERVER_DATA1          0x1c
#define STATUS_DONE             0x1
#define STATUS_FAILURE          0x2
#define STATUS_DENIED           0x4
#define STATUS_DROPPED          0x8
#define COMMAND_READ            (1u << 27)      /* "extended register read long"; [11:4] register, [2:0] bytes - 1 */
#define READ_TIMEOUT_US         2000            /* a read takes some tens of microseconds */

static vm_offset_t arb_core, arb_cnfg, arb_observer;

/*
 * One transfer at a time through the arbiter for this system, whoever asks (the flashlight's
 * driver, bsd/dev/redwood_torch.c, as well): with two at once the arbiter drops one ("the transfer
 * was dropped"), as Linux never lets happen (one lock for the bus).
 */
static LCK_GRP_DECLARE(spmi_lck_grp, "redwood-spmi");
static LCK_SPIN_DECLARE(spmi_lock, &spmi_lck_grp);

void
redwood_spmi_lock(void)
{
	lck_spin_lock(&spmi_lock);
}

void
redwood_spmi_unlock(void)
{
	lck_spin_unlock(&spmi_lock);
}

struct peripheral {
	const char *    name;
	uint16_t        id;             /* slave << 8 | peripheral: the high byte of its register addresses */
	uint16_t        channel;
	bool            found;
};
static struct peripheral pon = { .name = "the PMK8350's power-on block", .id = 0x013 };          /* registers 0x1300 of slave 0 */
static struct peripheral pin = { .name = "GPIO6 of the PM7325", .id = 0x18d };                   /* registers 0x8d00 of slave 1 */

/* How the reads have gone: said once a minute. */
static struct {
	uint64_t reads, failed, total_ns, longest_ns, last_ns;
} bus;

/*
 * Read `count` (1 to 8) registers of a peripheral, from register `reg` on. Returns NULL, or what
 * went wrong.
 */
static const char *
spmi_read(const struct peripheral *p, uint8_t reg, uint8_t *bytes, uint32_t count)
{
	vm_offset_t channel = arb_observer + 0x10000UL * ARB_SYSTEM + 0x80UL * p->channel;
	uint64_t start = mach_absolute_time(), now, interval, taken;
	uint32_t status, data[2];
	const char *problem = NULL;

	nanoseconds_to_absolutetime(READ_TIMEOUT_US * (uint64_t)NSEC_PER_USEC, &interval);
	redwood_spmi_lock();
	wr(channel + OBSERVER_COMMAND, COMMAND_READ | (uint32_t)reg << 4 | (count - 1));
	do {
		status = rd(channel + OBSERVER_STATUS);
		now = mach_absolute_time();
	} while (!(status & STATUS_DONE) && now - start < interval);
	data[0] = rd(channel + OBSERVER_DATA0);
	data[1] = count > 4 ? rd(channel + OBSERVER_DATA1) : 0;
	redwood_spmi_unlock();

	if (!(status & STATUS_DONE)) {
		problem = "no answer from the arbiter";
	} else if (status & STATUS_DENIED) {
		problem = "the arbiter refuses";
	} else if (status & STATUS_FAILURE) {
		problem = "the transfer failed (nobody at that address?)";
	} else if (status & STATUS_DROPPED) {
		problem = "the transfer was dropped";
	} else {
		for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
			bytes[i] = (uint8_t)(data[i / 4] >> (8 * (i % 4)));
		}
	}
	absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(now - start, &taken);
	bus.reads++;
	bus.total_ns += taken;
	bus.last_ns = taken;
	if (taken > bus.longest_ns) {
		bus.longest_ns = taken;
	}
	if (problem != NULL) {
		bus.failed++;
	}
	return problem;
}

/*
 * Which channel is that peripheral's. Several can be: one per system that may write to it. As
 * Linux chooses: the first, unless a later one is ours to write through.
 */
static void
find_channel(struct peripheral *p, uint32_t channels)
{
	for (uint32_t n = 0; n < channels; n++) {
		uint32_t map = rd(arb_core + ARB_CHANNEL(n)), owner;

		if (map == 0 || ((map >> 8) & 0xfff) != p->id) {
			continue;
		}
		owner = rd(arb_cnfg + ARB_OWNER(n)) & 7;
		printf("buttons: channel %u is %s (%#x); written by system %u%s\n", n, p->name, map, owner,
		    (map & ARB_CHANNEL_INTERRUPTS) ? ", which also gets its interrupts" : "");
		if (!p->found || owner == ARB_SYSTEM) {
			p->found = true;
			p->channel = (uint16_t)n;
		}
	}
	if (!p->found) {
		printf("buttons: no channel of the arbiter is %s (slave %u, peripheral %#x)\n", p->name, p->id >> 8, p->id & 0xff);
	}
}

/* ---- the two peripherals ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

/* every peripheral of these PMICs */
#define REG_TYPE                0x04
#define REG_SUBTYPE             0x05
#define REG_RT_STATUS           0x10            /* the inputs as they are now */
#define REG_INT_SET_TYPE        0x11            /* interrupts: a bit per input in each of these */
#define REG_INT_POLARITY_HIGH   0x12
#define REG_INT_POLARITY_LOW    0x13
#define REG_INT_ENABLED         0x15
#define REG_INT_LATCHED         0x18
#define REG_INT_PENDING         0x19

/* the power-on block, of the kind that is split in two ("generation 3"): this is its half for the operating system */
#define PON_TYPE                0x01
#define PON_SUBTYPE_HLOS        0x09
#define PON_KPDPWR              0x80            /* in the status and in the interrupt registers */
#define PON_RESIN               0x40

/* a GPIO of the low or medium voltage kind */
#define GPIO_TYPE               0x10
#define GPIO_SUBTYPE_LV         0x10
#define GPIO_SUBTYPE_MV_VIN3    0x13            /* 0x10 to 0x13: one layout */
#define GPIO_LEVEL              0x01            /* in the status */
#define GPIO_REG_MODE           0x40            /* [1:0]: 0 input, 1 output, 2 both, 3 analog */
#define GPIO_REG_SUPPLY         0x41
#define GPIO_REG_PULL           0x42            /* [2:0]: 0 to 3 up (30, 1.5, 31.5 uA, 1.5 with a boost), 4 down, 5 none */
#define GPIO_REG_ENABLE         0x46            /* [7] */

#define POLL_MS                 16
#define MINUTE_TICKS            (60 * 1000 / POLL_MS)

static struct button {
	const char *    name;
	uint32_t        record;         /* REDWOOD_BUTTON_* */
	bool            usable;         /* its input is what it was taken for */
	bool            live;           /* it has been seen released */
	bool            last;           /* the look before this one */
	bool            down;           /* as reported */
	uint64_t        since;          /* when it went down */
	uint32_t        presses;
} power = { .name = "power", .record = REDWOOD_BUTTON_LOCK },
    volume_up = { .name = "volume up", .record = REDWOOD_BUTTON_VOLUME_UP },
    volume_down = { .name = "volume down", .record = REDWOOD_BUTTON_VOLUME_DOWN };

/* "12.345 s (08:13:05.918 UTC)": since boot as in the log's own stamps, and as the daemons' lines have it */
static void
now_text(char *text, size_t size, uint64_t now)
{
	clock_sec_t seconds;
	clock_usec_t micro;
	uint64_t up;

	absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(now, &up);
	clock_get_calendar_microtime(&seconds, &micro);
	snprintf(text, size, "%llu.%03llu s (%02u:%02u:%02u.%03u UTC)", up / NSEC_PER_SEC, up / NSEC_PER_MSEC % 1000,
	    (unsigned)(seconds / 3600 % 24), (unsigned)(seconds / 60 % 60), (unsigned)(seconds % 60), (unsigned)(micro / 1000));
}

static void
button_look(struct button *b, bool pressed)
{
	uint64_t now = mach_absolute_time(), held;
	bool steady = pressed == b->last;
	char when[64];

	b->last = pressed;
	if (!b->usable || !steady) {
		return;
	}
	if (!b->live) {
		if (!pressed) {
			b->live = true;
			printf("buttons: %s is released now: believed from here on\n", b->name);
		}
		return;
	}
	if (pressed == b->down) {
		return;
	}
	b->down = pressed;
	now_text(when, sizeof(when), now);
	if (pressed) {
		b->since = now;
		b->presses++;
		printf("buttons: %s PRESSED at %s\n", b->name, when);
	} else {
		absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(now - b->since, &held);
		printf("buttons: %s released at %s, after %llu ms\n", b->name, when, held / NSEC_PER_MSEC);
	}
	redwood_touch_post(pressed ? REDWOOD_BUTTON_DOWN : REDWOOD_BUTTON_UP, b->record, 0, 0);
}

/* One look at both peripherals. */
static void
buttons_poll(void)
{
	static unsigned said;
	const char *problem;
	uint8_t status;

	if (power.usable || volume_down.usable) {
		problem = spmi_read(&pon, REG_RT_STATUS, &status, 1);
		if (problem == NULL) {
			button_look(&power, status & PON_KPDPWR);
			button_look(&volume_down, status & PON_RESIN);
		} else if (said < 8) {
			said++;
			printf("buttons: reading %s: %s\n", pon.name, problem);
		}
	}
	if (volume_up.usable) {
		problem = spmi_read(&pin, REG_RT_STATUS, &status, 1);
		if (problem == NULL) {
			button_look(&volume_up, !(status & GPIO_LEVEL));
		} else if (said < 8) {
			said++;
			printf("buttons: reading %s: %s\n", pin.name, problem);
		}
	}
}

/* Step 3: is each peripheral what the registers above are those of? */
static bool
identify(const struct peripheral *p, uint8_t type, uint8_t subtype_from, uint8_t subtype_to)
{
	const char *problem;
	uint8_t is[2];

	if (!p->found) {
		return false;
	}
	printf("buttons: next: read the type of %s through channel %u (2 registers, 0x%02x04)\n", p->name, p->channel, p->id & 0xff);
	problem = spmi_read(p, REG_TYPE, is, 2);
	if (problem != NULL) {
		printf("buttons: %s: %s\n", p->name, problem);
		return false;
	}
	printf("buttons: %s says type %#x, subtype %#x (the read took %llu us)\n", p->name, is[0], is[1], bus.last_ns / 1000);
	if (is[0] != type || is[1] < subtype_from || is[1] > subtype_to) {
		printf("buttons: ... which is not what this driver knows (type %#x, subtype %#x to %#x): left alone\n", type,
		    subtype_from, subtype_to);
		return false;
	}
	return true;
}

/* Step 4 for the power-on block: nothing to check but what it says now; its interrupt setup goes to the log. */
static void
pon_inputs(void)
{
	const char *problem;
	uint8_t r[8], more[2];

	printf("buttons: next: read the status and the interrupt setup of %s (registers 0x1310 to 0x1319)\n", pon.name);
	problem = spmi_read(&pon, REG_RT_STATUS, r, 8);
	if (problem == NULL) {
		problem = spmi_read(&pon, REG_INT_LATCHED, more, 2);
	}
	if (problem != NULL) {
		printf("buttons: %s: %s\n", pon.name, problem);
		return;
	}
	printf("buttons: power-on block: status %#x (power %s, volume down %s); interrupts: edge %#x, high %#x, low %#x, "
	    "enabled %#x, latched %#x, pending %#x\n", r[0], (r[0] & PON_KPDPWR) ? "HELD" : "released",
	    (r[0] & PON_RESIN) ? "HELD" : "released", r[REG_INT_SET_TYPE - REG_RT_STATUS], r[REG_INT_POLARITY_HIGH - REG_RT_STATUS],
	    r[REG_INT_POLARITY_LOW - REG_RT_STATUS], r[REG_INT_ENABLED - REG_RT_STATUS], more[0], more[1]);
	power.usable = volume_down.usable = true;
	power.last = r[0] & PON_KPDPWR;
	volume_down.last = r[0] & PON_RESIN;
}

/* Step 4 for the pin: it is volume up only if it is an input with a pull-up, and switched on. */
static void
pin_input(void)
{
	const char *problem;
	uint8_t c[8], status = 0;
	unsigned mode, pull;

	printf("buttons: next: read the setup and the level of %s (registers 0x8d40 to 0x8d47, 0x8d10)\n", pin.name);
	problem = spmi_read(&pin, GPIO_REG_MODE, c, 8);
	if (problem == NULL) {
		problem = spmi_read(&pin, REG_RT_STATUS, &status, 1);
	}
	if (problem != NULL) {
		printf("buttons: %s: %s\n", pin.name, problem);
		return;
	}
	mode = c[0] & 3;
	pull = c[GPIO_REG_PULL - GPIO_REG_MODE] & 7;
	printf("buttons: volume up's pin: mode %u (%s), supply %u, pull %u (%s), %s; registers 0x40.. = %02x %02x %02x %02x %02x %02x "
	    "%02x %02x; level %s\n", mode, mode == 0 ? "input" : mode == 1 ? "output" : mode == 2 ? "input and output" : "analog",
	    c[GPIO_REG_SUPPLY - GPIO_REG_MODE] & 7, pull, pull < 4 ? "up" : pull == 4 ? "down" : "none",
	    (c[GPIO_REG_ENABLE - GPIO_REG_MODE] & 0x80) ? "enabled" : "DISABLED", c[0], c[1], c[2], c[3], c[4], c[5], c[6], c[7],
	    (status & GPIO_LEVEL) ? "high (released)" : "LOW (held)");
	if (mode != 0 || pull >= 4 || !(c[GPIO_REG_ENABLE - GPIO_REG_MODE] & 0x80)) {
		printf("buttons: volume up's pin is not an enabled input with a pull-up. Making it one is a write to the PMIC, "
		    "which this driver does not do: volume up is left alone\n");
		return;
	}
	volume_up.usable = true;
	volume_up.last = !(status & GPIO_LEVEL);
}

static void
say_summary(void)
{
	printf("buttons: so far %u presses of power, %u of volume up, %u of volume down; now%s%s%s%s; %llu reads of the bus, "
	    "%llu us each (the longest %llu), %llu failed\n", power.presses, volume_up.presses, volume_down.presses,
	    power.down ? " power" : "", volume_up.down ? " volume-up" : "", volume_down.down ? " volume-down" : "",
	    (power.down || volume_up.down || volume_down.down) ? " held" : " none held", bus.reads,
	    bus.reads ? bus.total_ns / bus.reads / 1000 : 0, bus.longest_ns / 1000, bus.failed);
}

static void
buttons_thread(void *parameter, __unused wait_result_t result)
{
	uint32_t steps = (uint32_t)(uintptr_t)parameter, version, channels;
	bool pon_known, pin_known;

	printf("buttons: step 1: map the PMIC arbiter (%#lx, %#lx, %#lx) and read its version\n", ARB_CORE_PHYS, ARB_CNFG_PHYS,
	    ARB_OBSERVER_PHYS);
	arb_core = ml_io_map(ARB_CORE_PHYS, ARB_CORE_SIZE);
	arb_cnfg = ml_io_map(ARB_CNFG_PHYS, ARB_CNFG_SIZE);
	arb_observer = ml_io_map(ARB_OBSERVER_PHYS, ARB_OBSERVER_SIZE);
	version = rd(arb_core + ARB_VERSION);
	channels = rd(arb_core + ARB_FEATURES) & 0x7ff;
	printf("buttons: PMIC arbiter version %#x, %u channels\n", version, channels);
	if (version < ARB_VERSION_5 || version >= ARB_VERSION_7) {
		printf("buttons: this driver knows version 5 of the arbiter only: no buttons\n");
		goto out;
	}
	if (channels == 0 || channels > ARB_MAX_CHANNELS) {
		channels = ARB_MAX_CHANNELS;
	}
	if (steps < 2) {
		goto out;
	}

	printf("buttons: step 2: look through the arbiter's table for the channels of the two peripherals\n");
	find_channel(&pon, channels);
	find_channel(&pin, channels);
	if (steps < 3) {
		goto out;
	}

	printf("buttons: step 3: the first transfers on the SPMI bus\n");
	pon_known = identify(&pon, PON_TYPE, PON_SUBTYPE_HLOS, PON_SUBTYPE_HLOS);
	pin_known = identify(&pin, GPIO_TYPE, GPIO_SUBTYPE_LV, GPIO_SUBTYPE_MV_VIN3);
	if (steps < 4) {
		goto out;
	}

	printf("buttons: step 4: how the keys' inputs are set up\n");
	if (pon_known) {
		pon_inputs();
	}
	if (pin_known) {
		pin_input();
	}
	if (!power.usable && !volume_up.usable) {
		printf("buttons: nothing that can be read: no buttons\n");
		goto out;
	}
	if (power.last || volume_down.last || volume_up.last) {
		printf("buttons: a key reads as held before anything was watched:%s%s%s. It is not reported until it has been "
		    "seen released\n", power.last ? " power" : "", volume_up.last ? " volume-up" : "",
		    volume_down.last ? " volume-down" : "");
	}
	/* (a key that is released now is believed at once) */
	power.live = power.usable && !power.last;
	volume_down.live = volume_down.usable && !volume_down.last;
	volume_up.live = volume_up.usable && !volume_up.last;
	if (steps < 5) {
		goto out;
	}

	printf("buttons: step 5: watching%s%s%s, every %u ms: power is the side button\n", power.usable ? " power" : "",
	    volume_up.usable ? " volume-up" : "", volume_down.usable ? " volume-down" : "", POLL_MS);
	for (unsigned tick = 1;; tick++) {
		buttons_poll();
		/* once early on as well: a short run is to say what the reads cost too */
		if (tick % MINUTE_TICKS == 0 || tick == 10 * 1000 / POLL_MS) {
			say_summary();
		}
		if (bus.failed >= 1000 && bus.failed * 2 > bus.reads) {
			printf("buttons: more than half of %llu reads have failed: giving up\n", bus.reads);
			break;
		}
		delay_for_interval(POLL_MS, NSEC_PER_MSEC);
	}
out:
	if (steps < 5) {
		printf("buttons: stopping here (buttons_steps=%u)\n", steps);
	}
	thread_terminate(current_thread());
}

void
redwood_buttons_init(void)
{
	uint32_t enabled = 0, steps = 5;
	thread_t thread;

	/*
	 * On with the touch screen (the phone, somebody at it) unless buttons=0 says otherwise: a hand
	 * has pressed all three keys and each press and release was read as it was made.
	 */
	if (!PE_parse_boot_argn("buttons", &enabled, sizeof(enabled))) {
		uint32_t touch_screen = 0;

		enabled = PE_parse_boot_argn("touchscreen", &touch_screen, sizeof(touch_screen)) && touch_screen != 0;
	}
	if (!enabled) {
		return;
	}
	PE_parse_boot_argn("buttons_steps", &steps, sizeof(steps));
	if (steps == 0) {
		return;
	}
	if (kernel_thread_start(buttons_thread, (void *)(uintptr_t)steps, &thread) == KERN_SUCCESS) {
		thread_deallocate(thread);
	}
}

/*
 * What interrupts would take, instead of looking 60 times a second:
 *
 *   - The arbiter has one interrupt line for all the PMICs' peripherals ("periph_irq": through the
 *     power domain controller's pin 1 to the interrupt controller's SPI 481). This kernel has no
 *     driver that takes a hardware interrupt other than the timer's so far; that is the first
 *     thing to add (a handler registered for one more interrupt of the GICv3 the kernel already
 *     drives, and that line unmasked and set to level, high).
 *   - Per channel, the arbiter has an enable bit ("ACC_ENABLE"), a status and a clear register
 *     (in the "chnls" region: 0x100, 0x104, 0x108 of 0x10000 per channel), and per system a
 *     summary of which channels have something. Those are writes to the arbiter, not to a PMIC.
 *   - But the peripheral must be told to raise them as well: for each key a bit in "interrupt
 *     type" (edge), "polarity high" and "polarity low" (both edges), and "enable set". Those are
 *     WRITES TO THE PMIC -- to the power-on block for power and volume down, to the GPIO for
 *     volume up -- unless the firmware has left them set; step 4 prints what it finds there.
 *     After an interrupt the peripheral's latched status is cleared by another write to it.
 *   - Only the system that owns a peripheral's channel gets its interrupts (step 2 prints the
 *     owners).
 * Looking costs two reads of some tens of microseconds each, 60 times a second (the minute's
 * summary line says what they really take), so the reason to want interrupts would not be
 * processor time; it would be a system that sleeps and is to be woken by a key, and this one
 * does not sleep.
 */

```

`xnu/files/bsd/dev/redwood_camera.c`:

```c
/*
 * The cameras of the POCO X5 Pro (redwood): the macro one, an OmniVision OV02B10 (2 MP, Android's
 * camera 2, "redwood_aac_ov02b10_macro"), the wide one, a Samsung S5KHM2SD (108 MP, Android's
 * camera 0, "redwood_sunny_s5khm2sd_wide"), the front one and the ultra-wide one. Every address and
 * number below belongs to this phone, from Android's own device tree (cam-sensor0 to cam-sensor3 and
 * what they point to), the sensors' module files of Android's camera stack (/vendor/lib64/camera/com.qti.sensormodule.redwood_*.bin: the
 * slave address, the chip ID and where it is read, the power sequence, the tables) and the drivers
 * of the phone's kernel (MiCode redwood-s-oss: cam_sensor_util.c, qcom_pm8008-regulator.c,
 * camcc-yupik.c, gdsc-regulator.c, pinctrl-yupik.c, pinctrl-spmi-gpio.c, cam_csiphy_*), read as
 * data. The macro one (the others' differences are in sensors[] below and capture_sensor()):
 *
 *   the sensor     on CCI 1, master 0 (GPIO 73 data, 74 clock, function cci_i2c, internal pull-ups),
 *                  slave address 0x3c; done by hand here, as the other drivers do their I2C (the
 *                  two pins taken for each transaction and given back as they were found)
 *   chip ID        Android reads it as a 16-bit register at the 16-bit address 0x0203 and wants
 *                  0x002b (mask 0xffff); done the same way here
 *   reset          GPIO 77, high = running
 *   MCLK           camcc's mclk2 (RCG 0xe038, branch 0xe050) at 19.2 MHz on GPIO 66 (function
 *                  cam_mclk, 4 mA); Android takes the 19.2 MHz from camcc's PLL2 (M/N 1/75), here
 *                  it is the crystal's own 19.2 MHz (the RCG's source 0), with no PLL to start.
 *                  Before it Android switches on the camera's top power domain ("cam_clk":
 *                  titan_top_gdsc, camcc 0xc194), and so does this.
 *   VDIG (DOVDD)   PM8008i's LDO6 at 1.8 V; VANA (AVDD) its LDO7 at 2.8 V (the device tree's
 *                  voltages, normal power mode for the load Android asks). The PM8008i is on the
 *                  serial engine 1's I2C (GPIO 4 data, 5 clock; addresses 0x08 for the chip, 0x09
 *                  for the regulators, 16-bit registers), done by hand too; its reset pin is
 *                  PM8350C GPIO 3 (output high, as Android's pinctrl "pm8008i_active" has it)
 *   power-up       (the module file's): reset low, 1 ms; VDIG on; VANA on, 2 ms; MCLK on, 4 ms;
 *                  reset high, 9 ms. Power-down: MCLK off; reset low, 1 ms; VANA off, 7 ms; VDIG off.
 *                  (Both are read from the sensor's table at run time, as the wide one's are.)
 *
 * The wide one: CCI 0 master 1 (GPIO 71/72), slave address 0x20, chip ID 0xfad2 at 0x0000, reset
 * GPIO 21, MCLK1 (RCG 0xe01c, branch 0xe034, GPIO 65); VDIG the PM8008i's LDO1 at 1.0 V, VIO its
 * LDO5 at 1.8 V, VANA a fixed 2.8 V regulator that GPIO 106 switches; three C-PHY trios into
 * CSIPHY 1.
 *
 * The front one, an OmniVision OV16A1Q (16 MP, cam-sensor1): CCI 0 master 0 (GPIO 69/70), slave
 * 0x10, chip ID 0x1641 at 0x300b, reset GPIO 20, MCLK0 (GPIO 64); VANA LDO3 at 2.8 V, VDIG LDO2 at
 * 1.2 V, VIO LDO5 at 1.8 V; four D-PHY lanes into CSIPHY 0.
 *
 * The ultra-wide one, a Samsung S5K4H7 (8 MP, cam-sensor3): CCI 1 master 1 (GPIO 75/76), slave
 * 0x2d, chip ID 0x487b at 0x0000, reset GPIO 78, MCLK3 (GPIO 67) at the 24 MHz its module file
 * asks for, from camcc's PLL2 (Android's 1440 MHz Zonda configuration); VANA LDO4 at 2.8 V, VIO
 * LDO5 at 1.8 V, VDIG a fixed 1.2 V regulator that GPIO 108 switches; four D-PHY lanes into CSIPHY 3.
 *
 * Nothing here is done unless a boot-arg asks for it:
 *
 *   cam=1   a look, reading only: the camera's clocks and power domain as they are, the pins, the
 *           PM8008i's reset pin, and if it is out of reset the PM8008i itself (its chip enable and
 *           the two LDOs)
 *   cam=2   ... and the sensor powered up as Android powers it, its chip ID read, and powered
 *           down again (every write read back)
 *   cam=3   the CSID's test pattern through RDI 0 and IFE-lite 0 into memory, which the loader hands
 *           to the host after the run (xl camera): the camera subsystem's rails, PLL, clocks, SMMU
 *           and blocks without the sensor (capture_tpg() below)
 *   cam=4   the sensor's own frames that way, through its CSIPHY (capture_sensor() below)
 *
 * Boot-arg cam_sensor=wide picks the wide sensor; without it, the macro one.
 *
 * Limits, whatever asks: Android's voltages only (the device tree's: 1.8 and 2.8 V for the macro
 * one, 1.0 and 1.8 V for the wide one, 1.2, 1.8 and 2.8 V for the front one, 1.8 and 2.8 V for the
 * ultra-wide one; nothing else is ever written to the LDOs' set points); only the registers named above are written (a list each, checked at every
 * write) and each is read back; any write that does not read back, a regulator that is not ready
 * in time or reports over-current, a byte nobody acknowledges, and everything is switched off again
 * in the power-down's order and nothing more is done. At the run's end (and on a panic's way out)
 * whatever was switched on is switched off. Everything that was found switched on is left on.
 * The camera subsystem's own registers (camcc's PLL0 and the clocks named there, the sensor's CSIPHY,
 * CSID-lite 0, IFE-lite 0, one match register and context of the SMMU) are written the same way, read back
 * where they keep what they are given, and taken back in the reverse order.
 */
#include <kern/clock.h>
#include <kern/locks.h>
#include <kern/thread.h>
#include <vm/vm_kern.h>
#include <libkern/libkern.h>
#include <mach/mach_types.h>
#include <machine/machine_routines.h>
#include <pexpert/pexpert.h>
#include <vm/memory_types.h>
#include <sys/systm.h>
#include <sys/conf.h>
#include <sys/uio.h>
#include <miscfs/devfs/devfs.h>
#include <sys/redwood_audio.h>
#include <sys/redwood_camera.h>
#include <sys/redwood_input.h>

extern vm_offset_t ml_io_map(vm_offset_t phys_addr, vm_size_t size);
extern kern_return_t thread_terminate(thread_t thread);
extern void loader_log_putc(char c);

static uint32_t level;
static bool broken, leaving;

static int say(const char *format, ...) __printflike(1, 2);

/* every line to the loader's log as well (and to the console when that may be written) */
static int
say(const char *format, ...)
{
	char line[300];
	va_list list;
	int length;

	va_start(list, format);
	length = vsnprintf(line, sizeof(line), format, list);
	va_end(list);
	for (const char *c = line; *c != '\0'; c++) {
		loader_log_putc(*c);
	}
	if (!leaving && ml_get_interrupts_enabled()) {
		printf("%s", line);
	}
	return length;
}

static inline uint32_t
rd(vm_offset_t address)
{
	return *(volatile uint32_t *)address;
}

static inline void
wr(vm_offset_t address, uint32_t value)
{
	*(volatile uint32_t *)address = value;
}

static void
spin_us(uint32_t us)
{
	uint64_t until;

	nanoseconds_to_absolutetime((uint64_t)us * NSEC_PER_USEC, &until);
	until += mach_absolute_time();
	while (mach_absolute_time() < until) {
	}
}

static void
wait_ms(uint32_t ms)
{
	if (leaving) {
		spin_us(ms * 1000);
	} else {
		delay_for_interval(ms, NSEC_PER_MSEC);
	}
}

static void
give_up(const char *why)
{
	if (!broken) {
		broken = true;
		say("camera: %s: nothing more is written in this run\n", why);
	}
}

/* ---- pins ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ */

#define TLMM_PHYS               0x0f100000UL
#define TLMM_SIZE               0x100000UL
#define GPIO_CFG(n)             (tlmm + 0x1000UL * (n))         /* [1:0] pull, [5:2] function, [8:6] drive, [9] output */
#define GPIO_IO(n)              (tlmm + 0x1000UL * (n) + 4)     /* bit 0 in, bit 1 out */
#define CFG_PULL_UP             3
#define CFG_OUTPUT              (1u << 9)
#define CFG_FUNCTION(f)         ((uint32_t)(f) << 2)
#define CFG_DRIVE_MA(ma)        ((uint32_t)((ma) / 2 - 1) << 6)

#define PIN_PMIC_SDA            4       /* the serial engine 1's I2C: the PM8008i */
#define PIN_PMIC_SCL            5

static vm_offset_t tlmm;

/*
 * The four sensors, as Android's device tree has them (cam-sensor2 the macro, cam-sensor0 the wide,
 * cam-sensor1 the front, cam-sensor3 the ultra-wide): the pins of their CCI master (taken by hand),
 * the reset, MCLK (camcc RCG and branch, the pin and its function 1, cam_mclk, at 4 mA), the supplies
 * the module file's power sequence switches (a PM8008i LDO at the device tree's voltage, or a GPIO
 * that switches a fixed regulator), the CSIPHY with its clocks, and how the sensor's exposure
 * registers are laid out. Boot-arg cam_sensor=macro|wide|front|ultra picks one (default: the macro,
 * and for cam=5 the wide).
 */
enum { SUPPLY_NONE, SUPPLY_LDO, SUPPLY_GPIO };
struct supply {
	uint8_t         kind, ldo;      /* SUPPLY_LDO: PM8008i LDO n ... */
	uint16_t        mv;             /* ... at this set point (the device tree's) */
	uint16_t        gpio, ramp_us;  /* SUPPLY_GPIO: the pin, active high, and the regulator's ramp */
};
struct sensor_hw {
	const char *    name;
	const char *    tab;            /* in fw/ of the small image (tools/camsensor.py) */
	const char *    bus_name;
	unsigned        sda, scl, reset;
	uint32_t        mclk_cmd, mclk_cbcr;
	unsigned        mclk_pin;
	struct supply   vana, vdig, vio;
	unsigned        csiphy;
	uint32_t        phy_cbcr, timer_cmd, timer_cbcr;
	uint8_t         regs;           /* the exposure registers: REGS_OV_PAGED, REGS_SMIA or REGS_OV16 */
	uint8_t         bayer;          /* the picture's order as it comes here (camraw.py's codes: 1 GRBG, 3 BGGR) */
	uint8_t         pattern_bayer;  /* ... and its own colour bars' (its module file's "tpgon") */
	const char *    chip;           /* for the frames' header */
	uint16_t        gain_unity, gain_max;   /* the analog gain register's 1x, and the most it is given */
};
enum {
	REGS_OV_PAGED,                  /* OmniVision, 8-bit registers in pages (0xfd): exposure 0x0e/0x0f, gain 0x22, VTS 0x14/0x15 */
	REGS_SMIA,                      /* SMIA: frame length 0x0340, coarse integration 0x0202, analog gain 0x0204, hold 0x0104 */
	REGS_OV16,                      /* OmniVision, 16-bit addresses: exposure 0x3500.., gain 0x3508, VTS 0x380e, hold 0x3208 */
};
static const struct sensor_hw sensors[] = {
	{       /* cam-sensor2: OV02B10, CCI 1 master 0 (GPIO 73/74), reset GPIO 77, MCLK2 (GPIO 66), csiphy 2 */
		.name = "macro (OV02B10)", .tab = "camera-ov02b10.tab", .bus_name = "CCI 1 master 0", .sda = 73, .scl = 74, .reset = 77,

		.csiphy = 2, .phy_cbcr = 0xe110, .timer_cmd = 0xe0f4, .timer_cbcr = 0xe10c, .regs = REGS_OV_PAGED, .bayer = 3,
		.pattern_bayer = 2, .chip = "OV02B10", .gain_unity = 16, .gain_max = 0xf8,
	},
	{       /* cam-sensor0: S5KHM2SD, CCI 0 master 1 (GPIO 71/72), reset GPIO 21, MCLK1 (GPIO 65), csiphy 1;

		.name = "wide (S5KHM2SD)", .tab = "camera-s5khm2sd.tab", .bus_name = "CCI 0 master 1", .sda = 71, .scl = 72, .reset = 21,

static const struct sensor_hw *hw = &sensors[0];
static unsigned hw_index;

static void
```
