`xnu/files/bsd/dev/redwood_haptic.c`:

```c
/*
 * The vibration motor of the POCO X5 Pro (redwood): a linear resonant actuator driven by an
 * Awinic AW86927 (chip ID 0x9270), Android's "haptic_hv" (Xiaomi's driver aw8692x, version 1.7.0).
 * Every address and number below belongs to this phone, from Android's own device tree, its
 * kernel's log and the chip's registers as Android leaves them (read from sysfs, read-only):
 *
 *   I2C        the serial engine 9 (qupv3_se9_i2c at 0xa84000, function qup11 on GPIO 36 data and
 *              37 clock, internal pull-ups, 400 kHz under Android), address 0x5a; done by hand here
 *              as for the amplifiers (redwood_speaker.c), the two pins taken for each transaction
 *              and given back as they were found
 *   reset      GPIO 35, high = running (Android: low for 5 ms, then high, at its driver's start)
 *   interrupt  GPIO 18, pulled up, low when the chip has something to say (not used: polled)
 *   the motor  f0 175.5 Hz as Android calibrated it (f0_pre 170.0 Hz, calibration data 0x0d)
 *   effects    Android's RAM waveforms, /vendor/firmware/aw8697_haptic.bin of the phone (fw-haptic/
 *              here, not in the repository; userland/build.sh puts it into /fw of the system image):
 *              eleven of them, 1..10 short (Android's effects 0..9), 11 the one looped for a
 *              vibration of some length
 *
 * Nothing here is done unless a boot-arg asks for it:
 *
 *   haptic=1   a look, reading only: the pins, and whether the chip answers (its ID and registers,
 *              against what Android leaves in them). Out of Android's bootloader the reset pin is an
 *              input with a pull-down: the chip is held in reset and does not answer.
 *   haptic=2   ... and the reset released as Android's driver releases it (low 5 ms, then high; it
 *              stays released until the run ends), and the chip's registers read as they come out
 *              of reset, against Android's. Nothing is written to the chip.
 *   haptic=3   ... and Android's configuration written (every write read back), Android's
 *              waveforms loaded into its RAM and read back; then standby. Nothing moves.
 *   haptic=4   ... and one short effect played (haptic_effect=N, default 1: Android's effect 0)
 *   haptic=5   ... configured and loaded as for 3, and instead of the effect the motor for iOS until
 *              the run ends: what iOS plays on its "Actuator" device (the HAL plug-in's,
 *              userland/src/audio_plugin.c: the system's feedbacks and vibrations, CoreHaptics'
 *              patterns, UIKit's feedbacks) is written to /dev/redwood-haptic as samples of one
 *              channel, and the motor plays Android's waveforms by it: each waveform of iOS's (a
 *              stretch of samples after a pause) a short tap (waveform 1), and one that goes on for
 *              longer than a tap the waveform Android loops for vibrations (11), until it ends -- or
 *              for HAPTIC_MAX_MS at most, after which the motor rests for as long before it plays
 *              again. The gain follows how loud iOS's waveform is: Android's own (0x80) from a third
 *              of full scale up, five eighths of it for the softest, never above it (gain_for()).
 *
 * Limits, whatever asks: Android's own values only (its gain 0x80, its boost and drive levels, its
 * waveforms); no effect longer than HAPTIC_MAX_MS, and the chip is told to stop and put into
 * standby when that is over whether it has stopped or not; any fault the chip reports (under-
 * voltage, over-current, over-temperature, the boost's short circuit or over-voltage), a write that
 * does not read back or a byte nobody acknowledges, and the chip is put into reset and nothing more
 * is done for the rest of the run. At the run's end (and on a panic's way out) the chip goes back
 * into reset. Nothing is written anywhere but to the chip's registers and its RAM.
 */
#include <kern/clock.h>
#include <kern/thread.h>
#include <libkern/libkern.h>
#include <mach/mach_types.h>
#include <machine/machine_routines.h>
#include <pexpert/pexpert.h>
#include <miscfs/devfs/devfs.h>
#include <sys/conf.h>
#include <sys/systm.h>
#include <sys/uio.h>
#include <sys/redwood_audio.h>
#include <sys/redwood_input.h>

extern vm_offset_t ml_io_map(vm_offset_t phys_addr, vm_size_t size);
extern kern_return_t thread_terminate(thread_t thread);
extern void loader_log_putc(char c);

static vm_offset_t tlmm;
static uint32_t level;
static bool broken, released, leaving;

/* every line to the loader's log as well (and to the console when that may be written) */
static int say(const char *format, ...) __printflike(1, 2);

static int
say(const char *format, ...)
{
	char line[300];
	va_list list;
	int length;

	va_start(list, format);
	length = vsnprintf(line, sizeof(line), format, list);
	va_end(list);
	for (const char *c = line; *c != 0; c++) {
		loader_log_putc(*c);
	}
	if (!leaving && ml_get_interrupts_enabled()) {
		printf("%s", line);
	}
	return length;
}

static inline uint32_t
rd(vm_offset_t address)
{
	return *(volatile uint32_t *)address;
}

static inline void
wr(vm_offset_t address, uint32_t value)
{
	*(volatile uint32_t *)address = value;
}

static void
spin_us(uint32_t us)
{
	uint64_t until;

	nanoseconds_to_absolutetime((uint64_t)us * NSEC_PER_USEC, &until);
	until += mach_absolute_time();
	while (mach_absolute_time() < until) {
	}
}

static void
wait_ms(uint32_t ms)
{
	if (leaving) {
		spin_us(ms * 1000);
	} else {
		delay_for_interval(ms, NSEC_PER_MSEC);
	}
}

/* ---- pins ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ */

#define TLMM_PHYS               0x0f100000UL
#define TLMM_SIZE               0x100000UL
#define GPIO_CFG(n)             (tlmm + 0x1000UL * (n))         /* [1:0] pull, [5:2] function, [8:6] drive, [9] output */
#define GPIO_IO(n)              (tlmm + 0x1000UL * (n) + 4)     /* bit 0 in, bit 1 out */
#define CFG_PULL_UP             3
#define CFG_OUTPUT              (1u << 9)

#define PIN_SDA                 36      /* the serial engine's first pin is the data line, the second the clock */
#define PIN_SCL                 37
#define PIN_RESET               35
#define PIN_INT                 18

static void
show_pins(void)
{
	static const struct {
		unsigned pin;
		const char *what;
	} pins[] = { { PIN_SDA, "I2C data" }, { PIN_SCL, "I2C clock" }, { PIN_RESET, "reset" }, { PIN_INT, "interrupt" } };

	for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof(pins) / sizeof(pins[0]); i++) {
		uint32_t cfg = rd(GPIO_CFG(pins[i].pin)), io = rd(GPIO_IO(pins[i].pin));

		say("haptic: gpio%u (%s): function %u, pull %u, %u mA, %s, reads %u\n", pins[i].pin, pins[i].what, (cfg >> 2) & 15,
		    cfg & 3, (((cfg >> 6) & 7) + 1) * 2, (cfg & CFG_OUTPUT) ? (io & 2 ? "drives high" : "drives low") : "input", io & 1);
	}
}

/* the reset pin as an output of the GPIO function, driving `high' (2 mA, no pull, as Android has it) */
static void
reset_pin(bool high)
{
	wr(GPIO_IO(PIN_RESET), high ? 2 : 0);
	wr(GPIO_CFG(PIN_RESET), CFG_OUTPUT);
	released = high;
}

/* ---- I2C by hand (as in redwood_speaker.c) ---------------------------------------------------------- */

static void
half_bit(void)
{
	spin_us(5);                     /* 100 kHz at most */
}

static void
line(unsigned pin, bool high)
{
	wr(GPIO_IO(pin), 0);
	wr(GPIO_CFG(pin), CFG_PULL_UP | (high ? 0 : CFG_OUTPUT));
}

static bool
level_of(unsigned pin)
{
	return rd(GPIO_IO(pin)) & 1;
}

static void
i2c_start(void)
{
	line(PIN_SDA, true);
	line(PIN_SCL, true);
	half_bit();
	line(PIN_SDA, false);
	half_bit();
	line(PIN_SCL, false);
	half_bit();
}

static void
i2c_stop(void)
{
	line(PIN_SDA, false);
	half_bit();
	line(PIN_SCL, true);
	half_bit();
	line(PIN_SDA, true);
	half_bit();
}

static bool
i2c_bit(bool out)
{
	bool in;

	line(PIN_SDA, out);
	half_bit();
	line(PIN_SCL, true);
	for (unsigned stretched = 0; !level_of(PIN_SCL) && stretched < 100; stretched++) {
		half_bit();
	}
	half_bit();
	in = level_of(PIN_SDA);
	line(PIN_SCL, false);
	return in;
}

static bool
i2c_write(uint8_t byte)
{
	for (int bit = 7; bit >= 0; bit--) {
		i2c_bit((byte >> bit) & 1);
	}
	return !i2c_bit(true);
}

static uint8_t
i2c_read(bool more)
{
	uint8_t byte = 0;

	for (int bit = 7; bit >= 0; bit--) {
		byte = (uint8_t)(byte << 1 | i2c_bit(true));
	}
	i2c_bit(!more);
	return byte;
}

static uint32_t taken_cfg[2], taken_io[2];

static bool
bus_take(void)
{
	taken_cfg[0] = rd(GPIO_CFG(PIN_SDA));
	taken_cfg[1] = rd(GPIO_CFG(PIN_SCL));
	taken_io[0] = rd(GPIO_IO(PIN_SDA));
	taken_io[1] = rd(GPIO_IO(PIN_SCL));
	line(PIN_SDA, true);
	line(PIN_SCL, true);
	half_bit();
	if (!level_of(PIN_SDA) || !level_of(PIN_SCL)) {
		wr(GPIO_IO(PIN_SDA), taken_io[0] & 2);
		wr(GPIO_IO(PIN_SCL), taken_io[1] & 2);
		wr(GPIO_CFG(PIN_SDA), taken_cfg[0]);
		wr(GPIO_CFG(PIN_SCL), taken_cfg[1]);
		say("haptic: the I2C bus is not at rest (gpio%u reads %u, gpio%u reads %u): not touched\n", PIN_SDA,
		    level_of(PIN_SDA), PIN_SCL, level_of(PIN_SCL));
		return false;
	}
	return true;
}

static void
bus_give_back(void)
{
	wr(GPIO_IO(PIN_SDA), taken_io[0] & 2);
	wr(GPIO_IO(PIN_SCL), taken_io[1] & 2);
	wr(GPIO_CFG(PIN_SDA), taken_cfg[0]);
	wr(GPIO_CFG(PIN_SCL), taken_cfg[1]);
}

#define AW_ADDRESS              0x5a

/* `count' 8-bit registers from `reg' on (the chip's address counts up, but for its RAM data port) */
static bool
regs_read(uint8_t reg, uint8_t *values, unsigned count)
{
	bool answered;

	if (!bus_take()) {
		return false;
	}
	i2c_start();
	answered = i2c_write(AW_ADDRESS << 1) && i2c_write(reg);
	if (answered) {
		i2c_start();
		answered = i2c_write(AW_ADDRESS << 1 | 1);
	}
	for (unsigned i = 0; answered && i < count; i++) {
		values[i] = i2c_read(i + 1 < count);
	}
	i2c_stop();
	bus_give_back();
	return answered;
}

static bool
regs_write(uint8_t reg, const uint8_t *values, unsigned count)
{
	bool answered;

	if (!bus_take()) {
		return false;
	}
	i2c_start();
	answered = i2c_write(AW_ADDRESS << 1) && i2c_write(reg);
	for (unsigned i = 0; answered && i < count; i++) {
		answered = i2c_write(values[i]);
	}
	i2c_stop();
	bus_give_back();
	return answered;
}

/* ---- the chip -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

#define AW_RSTCFG               0x00            /* 0xaa: a soft reset */
#define AW_SYSST                0x01
#define AW_SYSINT               0x02            /* read: cleared */
#define AW_SYSINTM              0x03
#define AW_PLAYCFG1             0x06            /* [7] boost on, [6:0] its voltage */
#define AW_PLAYCFG2             0x07            /* the gain */
#define AW_PLAYCFG3             0x08            /* [1:0] the play mode: 0 RAM */
#define AW_PLAYCFG4             0x09            /* [1] stop, [0] go */
#define AW_WAVCFG1              0x0a            /* the first waveform to play, 1..127 (0: the end) */
#define AW_WAVCFG2              0x0b
#define AW_WAVCFG9              0x12            /* [7:4] how often the first is repeated, 15: until told to stop */
#define AW_BASEADDRH            0x2d
#define AW_BASEADDRL            0x2e
#define AW_GLBRD5               0x3f            /* [3:0] the state: 0 standby */
#define AW_RAMADDRH             0x40
#define AW_RAMADDRL             0x41
#define AW_RAMDATA              0x42
#define AW_SYSCTRL3             0x45            /* [5] standby, [2] the RAM open for loading */
#define AW_TMCFG                0x5b            /* 0x7d opens the analog registers 0x70.. for writing, 0 closes them */
#define AW_TRIM_LRA             0x79            /* the motor's f0 calibration */
#define AW_CHIPIDH              0x57
#define AW_CHIPIDL              0x58
#define AW_CHIPID               0x9270

#define SYSINT_FAULTS           0xe6            /* boost short circuit and over-voltage, under-voltage, over-current, over-temperature */
#define HAPTIC_MAX_MS           1000

static void
give_up(const char *why)
{
	broken = true;
	say("haptic: %s: THE CHIP IS PUT INTO RESET (gpio%u low) and nothing more is done\n", why, PIN_RESET);
	if (tlmm != 0) {
		reset_pin(false);
	}
}

static bool
get(uint8_t reg, uint8_t *value)
{
	if (!regs_read(reg, value, 1)) {
		say("haptic: %#04x NOT READ\n", reg);
		return false;
	}
	return true;
}

/* One register written and read back. */
static bool
put(uint8_t reg, uint8_t value)
{
	uint8_t after = 0;

	if (broken) {
		return false;
	}
	if (!regs_write(reg, &value, 1)) {
		say("haptic: %#04x <- %#04x NOT ACKNOWLEDGED\n", reg, value);
		give_up("a write was not acknowledged");
		return false;
	}
	if (!regs_read(reg, &after, 1)) {
		give_up("a register could not be read back");
		return false;
	}
	say("haptic: %#04x <- %#04x, reads %#04x%s\n", reg, value, after, after == value ? "" : ": NOT AS WRITTEN");
	if (after != value) {
		give_up("a register did not read back as written");
		return false;
	}
	return true;
}

/* The chip's interrupt flags (reading clears them): false, and the chip given up on, if one is a fault. */
static bool
healthy(const char *when)
{
	uint8_t flags = 0;

	if (!get(AW_SYSINT, &flags)) {
		give_up("the flags could not be read");
		return false;
	}
	if (flags & SYSINT_FAULTS) {
		say("haptic: %s: the chip reports %#04x:%s%s%s%s%s\n", when, flags, flags & 0x80 ? " BOOST SHORT CIRCUIT" : "",
		    flags & 0x40 ? " BOOST OVER-VOLTAGE" : "", flags & 0x20 ? " UNDER-VOLTAGE" : "", flags & 0x04 ? " OVER-CURRENT" : "",
		    flags & 0x02 ? " OVER-TEMPERATURE" : "");
		give_up("a fault");
		return false;
	}
	return true;
}

/* Android's registers as its driver leaves them, read from the phone's sysfs (fw-haptic/android/haptic-sysfs.txt) */
static const uint8_t android_regs[0x7d] = {
	[0x00] = 0x82, [0x01] = 0x10, [0x02] = 0x11, [0x03] = 0x59, [0x04] = 0x09, [0x05] = 0x00, [0x06] = 0x47, [0x07] = 0x80,
	[0x08] = 0x07, [0x09] = 0x00, [0x0a] = 0x0b, [0x12] = 0xf0, [0x18] = 0x1e, [0x19] = 0x8d, [0x1a] = 0x71, [0x1b] = 0x06,
	[0x1c] = 0x58, [0x1d] = 0xcf, [0x1e] = 0x28, [0x1f] = 0x04, [0x20] = 0x06, [0x21] = 0x08, [0x22] = 0x0c, [0x23] = 0x0c,
	[0x24] = 0x62, [0x25] = 0x08, [0x26] = 0xa0, [0x27] = 0x08, [0x28] = 0x8c, [0x2d] = 0x08, [0x2f] = 0x46, [0x33] = 0x01,
	[0x34] = 0x01, [0x35] = 0x01, [0x36] = 0x02, [0x37] = 0x02, [0x38] = 0x02, [0x3b] = 0x05, [0x3c] = 0x08, [0x3e] = 0x1b,
	[0x40] = 0x08, [0x41] = 0x03, [0x45] = 0x12, [0x46] = 0x09, [0x47] = 0x5a, [0x49] = 0x28, [0x4a] = 0xbf, [0x4b] = 0x32,
	[0x4d] = 0x24, [0x4e] = 0x04, [0x4f] = 0x0a, [0x51] = 0x07, [0x57] = 0x92, [0x58] = 0x70, [0x59] = 0x04, [0x5a] = 0x98,
	[0x5d] = 0xf5, [0x5e] = 0x0d, [0x5f] = 0xf5, [0x60] = 0x41, [0x61] = 0xf6, [0x62] = 0x5c, [0x63] = 0x0e, [0x64] = 0xf9,
	[0x68] = 0x05, [0x69] = 0x21, [0x6b] = 0x02, [0x6c] = 0x15, [0x6d] = 0x89, [0x6e] = 0xc2, [0x6f] = 0x48, [0x70] = 0x0f,
	[0x71] = 0x93, [0x72] = 0x69, [0x73] = 0xa4, [0x74] = 0x89, [0x75] = 0x88, [0x77] = 0x40, [0x79] = 0x0d,
};

/* What the chip holds now, against Android's (registers 0x00..0x7c; 0x32 and 0x42 are data ports, not read). */
static void
show_registers(void)
{
	unsigned differ = 0;

	for (unsigned reg = 0; reg <= 0x7c; reg++) {
		uint8_t value = 0;

		if (reg == 0x32 || reg == 0x42) {
			continue;
		}
		if (!regs_read((uint8_t)reg, &value, 1)) {
			say("haptic: %#04x NOT READ\n", reg);
			return;
		}
		if (value != android_regs[reg]) {
			differ++;
			say("haptic: %#04x = %#04x (Android leaves %#04x)\n", reg, value, android_regs[reg]);
		}
	}
	say("haptic: %u registers differ from what Android leaves in them\n", differ);
}

static bool
chip_answers(void)
{
	uint8_t id[2] = { 0, 0 };

	if (!regs_read(AW_CHIPIDH, id, 2)) {
		say("haptic: nobody answers at %#x on the bus of gpio%u/%u\n", AW_ADDRESS, PIN_SDA, PIN_SCL);
		return false;
	}
	say("haptic: the chip at %#x is %#06x%s\n", AW_ADDRESS, id[0] << 8 | id[1], (id[0] << 8 | id[1]) == AW_CHIPID ? ", an AW86927" :
	    ": NOT THE AW86927 EXPECTED");
	return (id[0] << 8 | id[1]) == AW_CHIPID;
}

/*
 * Android's configuration: the registers its driver sets (and the mainline Linux driver aw86927.c sets the
 * same way), with Android's values -- those that differ from the chip's own after a reset, as the phone
 * showed (haptic=2). Not written: the status and interrupt flags, the RAM's address and data ports, the
 * results of the chip's measurements (0x25..0x28: they do not take what is written, they are what its f0
 * tracking found under Android; 0x4f, 0x51, 0x59, 0x5a likewise), and what is set for each playing (0x08 the mode,
 * 0x0a/0x12 the waveform and its repeats). The values are all read from the chip as Android leaves it.
 */
static const uint8_t android_config[][2] = {
	{ 0x03, 0x59 },         /* the interrupt mask */
	{ 0x06, 0x47 },         /* PLAYCFG1: the boost in bypass, its voltage setting 0x47 (Android's vmax 7938 mV) */
	{ 0x1a, 0x71 },         /* CONTCFG3 */
	{ 0x1d, 0xcf },         /* CONTCFG6: f0 tracking on, the first drive level 0x4f */
	{ 0x1e, 0x28 },         /* CONTCFG7: the second drive level */
	{ 0x2f, 0x46 },         /* the FIFO's thresholds */
	{ 0x36, 0x02 }, { 0x37, 0x02 }, { 0x38, 0x02 },  /* the trigger pins' waveforms (the triggers stay off) */
	{ 0x39, 0x00 }, { 0x3a, 0x00 },  /* ... and off */
	{ 0x46, 0x09 },         /* SYSCTRL4: 24 kHz waveforms, the gain applied as it is */
	{ 0x47, 0x5a },
};
/*
 * ... and the analog ones, behind AW_TMCFG (the boost: skip mode, peak current 3.45 A, peak back, slew).
 * These too are Android's: what the phone's registers hold under Android (they differ from the chip's
 * own after a reset, so Android's driver set them); mainline Linux's aw86927.c sets the same values.
 */
static const uint8_t android_analog[][2] = {
	{ 0x70, 0x0f }, { 0x71, 0x93 }, { 0x72, 0x69 }, { 0x74, 0x89 }, { 0x75, 0x88 },
	{ AW_TRIM_LRA, 0x0d },  /* Android's f0 calibration of this motor (its log: "f0_cali_data = 0x0D") */
};

/* The analog registers opened or closed for writing (AW_TMCFG reads back as 0 either way: what tells is that the writes stick). */
static bool
unlock(bool open)
{
	uint8_t value = open ? 0x7d : 0x00;

	if (broken || !regs_write(AW_TMCFG, &value, 1)) {
		give_up("the analog registers could not be opened");
		return false;
	}
	say("haptic: %#04x <- %#04x (the analog registers %s)\n", AW_TMCFG, value, open ? "opened" : "closed");
	return true;
}

static bool
configure(void)
{
	say("haptic: Android's configuration is written\n");
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof(android_config) / sizeof(android_config[0]); i++) {
		if (!put(android_config[i][0], android_config[i][1])) {
			return false;
		}
	}
	if (!unlock(true)) {
		return false;
	}
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof(android_analog) / sizeof(android_analog[0]); i++) {
		if (!put(android_analog[i][0], android_analog[i][1])) {
			(void)unlock(false);
			return false;
		}
	}
	return unlock(false) && healthy("after the configuration");
}

static uint32_t states_seen;           /* the GLBRD5 states seen by the last wait, a bit each */

/* until the chip says it is in standby (GLBRD5 state 0), at most `ms' */
static bool
wait_standby(unsigned ms)
{
	states_seen = 0;
	for (unsigned waited = 0; waited <= ms; waited += 2) {
		uint8_t state = 0xff;

		if (!get(AW_GLBRD5, &state)) {
			return false;
		}
		states_seen |= 1u << (state & 0x0f);
		if ((state & 0x0f) == 0) {
			return true;
		}
		wait_ms(2);
	}
	return false;
}

/*
 * Android's waveforms into the chip's RAM: the file is a checksum (16 bits, of all that follows), the
 * address the RAM's contents begin at (0x0800), and those contents -- a version byte, the start and end
 * address of each waveform, the waveforms. Written through the data port with the address counting up,
 * then read back the same way and compared.
 */
static bool
load_waveforms(void)
{
	uint64_t size = 0;
	const uint8_t *file = redwood_wifi_file("aw8697_haptic.bin", &size);
	uint32_t sum = 0, base, length;
	uint8_t address[2], back[64];

	if (file == NULL || size < 8) {
		say("haptic: no aw8697_haptic.bin in fw/ of the small image (fw-haptic/ when it is built)\n");
		return false;
	}
	for (uint64_t i = 2; i < size; i++) {
		sum += file[i];
	}
	if ((sum & 0xffff) != (uint32_t)(file[0] << 8 | file[1])) {
		say("haptic: aw8697_haptic.bin does not add up (%#x, it says %#x): not loaded\n", sum & 0xffff, file[0] << 8 | file[1]);
		return false;
	}
	base = (uint32_t)(file[2] << 8 | file[3]);
	length = (uint32_t)size - 4;
	say("haptic: Android's waveforms: %u bytes from %#x on, %u waveforms\n", length, base, (unsigned)(((file[5] << 8 | file[6]) -
	    base - 1) / 4));
	if (!wait_standby(250) || !put(AW_SYSCTRL3, (uint8_t)(android_regs[AW_SYSCTRL3] | 0x04))) {
		give_up("the RAM could not be opened");
		return false;
	}
	address[0] = (uint8_t)(base >> 8);
	address[1] = (uint8_t)base;
	if (!put(AW_BASEADDRH, address[0]) || !put(AW_BASEADDRL, address[1]) || !regs_write(AW_RAMADDRH, address, 2)) {
		give_up("the RAM's address could not be set");
		return false;
	}
	for (uint32_t at = 0; at < length; at += 32) {
		unsigned n = length - at < 32 ? length - at : 32;

		if (!regs_write(AW_RAMDATA, file + 4 + at, n)) {
			give_up("the RAM could not be written");
			return false;
		}
	}
	if (!regs_write(AW_RAMADDRH, address, 2)) {
		give_up("the RAM's address could not be set again");
		return false;
	}
	for (uint32_t at = 0; at < length; at += sizeof(back)) {
		unsigned n = length - at < sizeof(back) ? length - at : sizeof(back);

		if (!regs_read(AW_RAMDATA, back, n) || memcmp(back, file + 4 + at, n) != 0) {
			say("haptic: the RAM reads back differently at %#x\n", base + at);
			give_up("the waveforms did not load");
			return false;
		}
	}
	if (!put(AW_SYSCTRL3, android_regs[AW_SYSCTRL3])) {
		return false;
	}
	say("haptic: Android's waveforms are in the chip's RAM and read back as written\n");
	return healthy("after the waveforms");
}

/* One waveform played once (Android's effect `effect' - 1), stopped at HAPTIC_MAX_MS at the latest. */
static bool
play_effect(unsigned effect)
{
	uint64_t began = mach_absolute_time(), ended;
	bool done;

	say("haptic: waveform %u is played once, at Android's gain %#x\n", effect, android_regs[AW_PLAYCFG2]);
	if (!wait_standby(250) || !put(AW_PLAYCFG3, 0x04) || !put(AW_WAVCFG1, (uint8_t)effect) || !put(AW_WAVCFG2, 0x00) ||
	    !put(AW_WAVCFG9, 0x00) || !put(AW_PLAYCFG2, android_regs[AW_PLAYCFG2]) || !healthy("before playing")) {
		return false;
	}
	{
		uint8_t go = 0x01;

		if (!regs_write(AW_PLAYCFG4, &go, 1)) {
			give_up("the start was not acknowledged");
			return false;
		}
	}
	wait_ms(2);
	done = wait_standby(HAPTIC_MAX_MS);
	absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(mach_absolute_time() - began, &ended);
	if (!done) {
		uint8_t stop = 0x02;

		say("haptic: STILL PLAYING after %u ms: stopped\n", HAPTIC_MAX_MS);
		(void)regs_write(AW_PLAYCFG4, &stop, 1);
		if (!wait_standby(50)) {
			give_up("it does not stop");
			return false;
		}
	}
	say("haptic: the waveform has played: back in standby after %llu ms (states seen meanwhile: %#x, a bit each; 0 is "
	    "standby)\n", ended / NSEC_PER_MSEC, states_seen);
	return healthy("after playing");
}

/* ---- haptic=5: the motor for iOS ------------------------------------------------------------------- */

#define ACTIVE_US               30000           /* a write that was not silence counts for this long */
#define SILENT_BELOW            256             /* of 32768: samples no larger are silence */
#define TAP_US                  60000           /* longer than this, and it is a vibration, not a tap */
#define SETTLE_US               8000            /* how long iOS's waveform is listened to before a tap: its loudness */
#define FOLLOW_US               20000           /* how often a vibration's strength follows iOS's */

#define TOLD_EVENTS             24              /* the first so many taps and vibrations are each said */

static volatile uint64_t heard_us;              /* when the last write that was not silence came */
static volatile uint64_t quiet_us;              /* when the last write that was silence came */
static volatile uint64_t onset_us;              /* when iOS's last waveform began: the first write not silence after a pause */
static volatile uint32_t heard_peak;            /* the largest sample of that waveform, or since the service last looked */
static uint64_t written_frames;
static unsigned taps, loops, capped;            /* what has been played, for the run's end */

static uint64_t
now_us(void)
{
	uint64_t ns;

	absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(mach_absolute_time(), &ns);
	return ns / NSEC_PER_USEC;
}

/* From the audio server's I/O thread: never waits. */
static int
haptic_write(__unused dev_t dev, struct uio *uio, __unused int ioflag)
{
	int16_t samples[256];
	int error = 0;

	while (uio_resid(uio) >= 2) {
		user_ssize_t bytes = uio_resid(uio);
		uint32_t peak = 0;

		if (bytes > (user_ssize_t)sizeof(samples)) {
			bytes = sizeof(samples);
		}
		bytes &= ~(user_ssize_t)1;
		if ((error = uiomove((caddr_t)samples, (int)bytes, uio)) != 0) {
			break;
		}
		for (unsigned i = 0; i < bytes / 2; i++) {
			uint32_t v = samples[i] < 0 ? (uint32_t)-(int32_t)samples[i] : (uint32_t)samples[i];

			peak = v > peak ? v : peak;
		}
		written_frames += (uint64_t)bytes / 2;
		if (peak > SILENT_BELOW) {
			uint64_t now = now_us();

			if (heard_us == 0 || quiet_us > heard_us || now - heard_us >= ACTIVE_US) {
				onset_us = now;
				heard_peak = 0;
			}
			heard_us = now;
			if (peak > heard_peak) {
				heard_peak = peak;
			}
		} else {
			quiet_us = now_us();
		}
	}
	return error;
}

/*
 * A test's stand-in for iOS's waveform (redwood_mic.c, mic_tap=1: the microphone hears the motor): as if
 * a write of this loudness (of 32767) had just come, or silence for 0. The service plays it with all its
 * own limits, as it plays iOS's.
 */
void
redwood_haptic_pretend(uint32_t peak)
{
	uint64_t now = now_us();

	if (peak <= SILENT_BELOW) {
		quiet_us = now;
		return;
	}
	if (heard_us == 0 || quiet_us > heard_us || now - heard_us >= ACTIVE_US) {
		onset_us = now;
		heard_peak = 0;
	}
	heard_us = now;
	if (peak > heard_peak) {
		heard_peak = peak;
	}
}

static int
haptic_open(__unused dev_t dev, __unused int flags, __unused int type, __unused struct proc *p)
{
	return 0;
}

static const struct cdevsw haptic_cdevsw = {
	.d_open = haptic_open, .d_close = haptic_open, .d_read = eno_rdwrt, .d_write = haptic_write,
	.d_ioctl = eno_ioctl, .d_stop = eno_stop, .d_reset = eno_reset, .d_select = eno_select,
	.d_mmap = eno_mmap, .d_strategy = eno_strat, .d_type = 0
};

/* Start a waveform without waiting for it: once, or (`forever') until stopped. */
static bool
start_waveform(unsigned waveform, bool forever, uint8_t gain)
{
	uint8_t go = 0x01;

	if (!put(AW_PLAYCFG3, 0x04) || !put(AW_WAVCFG1, (uint8_t)waveform) || !put(AW_WAVCFG2, 0x00) ||
	    !put(AW_WAVCFG9, forever ? 0xf0 : 0x00) || !put(AW_PLAYCFG2, gain)) {
		return false;
	}
	if (!regs_write(AW_PLAYCFG4, &go, 1)) {
		give_up("the start was not acknowledged");
		return false;
	}
	return true;
}

static bool
stop_waveform(void)
{
	uint8_t stop = 0x02;

	if (!regs_write(AW_PLAYCFG4, &stop, 1) || !wait_standby(50)) {
		give_up("it does not stop");
		return false;
	}
	return true;
}

/* the chip's state (GLBRD5: 0 standby, 7 and 11 seen while a waveform plays), 0xff if it cannot be read */
static unsigned
chip_state(void)
{
	uint8_t state = 0xff;

	return get(AW_GLBRD5, &state) ? state & 0x0f : 0xff;
}

/*
 * How strong to play what iOS plays. iOS drives its Taptic Engine with waveforms far under full
 * scale for most feedbacks (a tap's peak anywhere from 1000 to 33000 of 32768, a vibration's
 * about 17000), and followed in proportion (gain = Android's * peak / full scale) most of them came
 * out at a tenth of Android's gain or less: not felt at all. Android plays its own clicks and
 * vibrations at its gain, 0x80. So: Android's gain from a third of full scale up, and below that
 * down to five eighths of it for the softest -- never above Android's.
 */
static uint8_t
gain_for(uint32_t peak)
{
	uint32_t top = android_regs[AW_PLAYCFG2], low = top * 5 / 8, third = 32767 / 3;

	return (uint8_t)(peak >= third ? top : low + (top - low) * peak / third);
}

static void
serve(void)
{
	enum { IDLE, TAP, LOOP, REST } state = IDLE;
	uint64_t since = 0, rest_until = 0, last_look = 0, tap_onset = 0, followed = 0;
	uint8_t playing_gain = 0;
	unsigned follows = 0;                   /* how often the vibration playing now has changed strength */
	int major = cdevsw_add(-1, &haptic_cdevsw);

	if (major < 0 || devfs_make_node(makedev(major, 0), DEVFS_CHAR, UID_ROOT, GID_WHEEL, 0666, "redwood-haptic") == NULL) {
		say("haptic: /dev/redwood-haptic cannot be made\n");
		return;
	}
	say("haptic: THE MOTOR PLAYS WHAT IOS PLAYS ON ITS ACTUATOR (/dev/redwood-haptic) from here on, until the run ends\n");
	while (!broken) {
		uint64_t now = now_us();
		bool active = heard_us != 0 && now - heard_us < ACTIVE_US;
		uint32_t peak = heard_peak;
		uint8_t gain = gain_for(peak);

		switch (state) {
		case IDLE:
		case TAP:
			/*
			 * A waveform of iOS's that has begun (after a pause: a tap of a series is a tap of its own) is
			 * a tap -- once its first milliseconds are heard: a waveform begins softly, and they say how
			 * loud it is; one that goes on without a pause, a vibration.
			 */
			if (active && onset_us != tap_onset && now - onset_us >= SETTLE_US) {
				uint64_t began = onset_us;

				if (state == TAP && !wait_standby(0) && !stop_waveform()) {
					break;
				}
				if (!start_waveform(1, false, gain ? gain : 1)) {
					break;
				}
				state = TAP;
				since = now;
				tap_onset = began;
				taps++;
				if (taps + loops <= TOLD_EVENTS) {
					wait_ms(4);
					say("haptic: tap %u: iOS's waveform peaks at %u of 32768: Android's waveform 1 at gain %#04x; the "
					    "chip's state %u\n", taps, peak, gain ? gain : 1, chip_state());
				}
				break;
			}
			if (state == IDLE) {
				break;
			}
			if (active && quiet_us < tap_onset && now - since > TAP_US) {
				if (stop_waveform() && start_waveform(11, true, gain ? gain : 1)) {
					state = LOOP;
					since = followed = now;
					playing_gain = gain ? gain : 1;
					follows = 0;
					loops++;
					heard_peak = 0;
					if (taps + loops <= TOLD_EVENTS) {
						wait_ms(4);
						say("haptic: vibration %u: iOS goes on playing (peak %u): Android's waveform 11 over and over at "
						    "gain %#04x, %u ms at most; the chip's state %u\n", loops, peak, gain ? gain : 1,
						    HAPTIC_MAX_MS, chip_state());
					}
				}
			} else if (!active && now - since > TAP_US) {
				state = wait_standby(0) || stop_waveform() ? IDLE : state;
			}
			break;
		case LOOP:
			/* as strong as iOS's waveform is now (Android's gain at full scale, never more) */
			if (active && now - followed >= FOLLOW_US) {
				followed = now;
				heard_peak = 0;
				if (peak != 0 && (gain > playing_gain + 8 || gain + 8 < playing_gain)) {
					if (!put(AW_PLAYCFG2, gain)) {
						break;
					}
					playing_gain = gain;
					follows++;
				}
			}
			if (!active || now - since > HAPTIC_MAX_MS * 1000ull) {
				bool cut = now - since > HAPTIC_MAX_MS * 1000ull;

				if (cut) {
					capped++;
					rest_until = now + HAPTIC_MAX_MS * 1000ull;
				}
				if (stop_waveform()) {
					state = rest_until > now ? REST : IDLE;
					if (taps + loops <= TOLD_EVENTS + 1) {
						say("haptic: vibration %u: %s after %llu ms (its strength changed %u times, last to gain %#04x); "
						    "the chip is in standby\n", loops, cut ? "CUT at the limit" : "iOS stopped, and so does the motor",
						    (now - since) / 1000, follows, playing_gain);
					}
				}
			}
			break;
		case REST:
			if (now >= rest_until) {
				state = IDLE;
			}
			break;
		}
		if (state != IDLE && state != REST && now - last_look > 50000) {
			last_look = now;
			if (!healthy("while playing")) {
				break;
			}
		}
		wait_ms(4);
	}
	say("haptic: the motor is given up on (%u taps and %u vibrations played, %u cut at %u ms)\n", taps, loops, capped,
	    HAPTIC_MAX_MS);
}

static void
haptic_thread(__unused void *parameter, __unused wait_result_t result)
{
	tlmm = ml_io_map(TLMM_PHYS, TLMM_SIZE);
	say("haptic: level %u: %s\n", level, level == 1 ? "a look, reading only" : level == 2 ? "the reset released, registers read" :
	    level == 3 ? "the chip configured and its waveforms loaded, nothing played" : level == 4 ? "one effect played" :
	    "the motor for iOS");
	show_pins();
	if (level >= 2 && !((rd(GPIO_CFG(PIN_RESET)) & CFG_OUTPUT) && (rd(GPIO_IO(PIN_RESET)) & 2))) {
		/* (Android's driver: the pin low, 5 ms, high, and the chip ready for I2C 8 ms later) */
		say("haptic: the reset is released: gpio%u low for 5 ms, then high\n", PIN_RESET);
		reset_pin(false);
		wait_ms(5);
		reset_pin(true);
		wait_ms(8);
	}
	if (!chip_answers()) {
		say("haptic: (the reset pin %s)\n", (rd(GPIO_CFG(PIN_RESET)) & CFG_OUTPUT) && (rd(GPIO_IO(PIN_RESET)) & 2) ?
		    "drives high: the chip should answer" : "does not drive high: the chip is held in reset or not powered");
		if (released) {
			give_up("the chip does not answer");
		}
	} else {
		show_registers();
		if (level >= 3 && configure() && load_waveforms() && level == 4) {
			uint32_t effect = 1;

			PE_parse_boot_argn("haptic_effect", &effect, sizeof(effect));
			if (effect < 1 || effect > 10) {
				effect = 1;     /* (the short ones only) */
			}
			(void)play_effect(effect);
		} else if (level == 5 && !broken) {
			serve();
		}
	}
	say("haptic: done\n");
	thread_terminate(current_thread());
}

void
redwood_haptic_init(void)
{
	thread_t thread;

	if (!PE_parse_boot_argn("haptic", &level, sizeof(level)) || level == 0) {
		return;
	}
	if (level > 5) {
		level = 5;
	}
	if (kernel_thread_start(haptic_thread, NULL, &thread) == KERN_SUCCESS) {
		thread_deallocate(thread);
	}
}

/* At the run's end and on a panic's way out: the chip back into reset, if it was let out. */
void
redwood_haptic_quiesce(void)
{
	if (released && tlmm != 0) {
		leaving = true;
		reset_pin(false);
		if (level == 5) {
			say("haptic: at the run's end: %u taps and %u vibrations played (%u cut at %u ms), from %llu frames iOS "
			    "wrote; the chip is held in reset\n", taps, loops, capped, HAPTIC_MAX_MS, written_frames);
		}
	}
}
```

`xnu/files/bsd/dev/redwood_image.c`:

```c
/*
 * A file of one of this port's RAM disks, by path, for the drivers that want one before there is
 * a root or without asking it: the GPU's firmware (redwood_adreno.c), the Wi-Fi DSP's
 * (redwood_wifi.c), the audio DSP's (redwood_adsp.c) -- "fw/NAME" of the image that travels with
 * the kernel (md1; md0 when there is nothing else) or of the resident one (md0).
 *
 * The image is an APFS container (tools/apfs/mkapfs.py: what userland/build.sh makes).  A file
 * stored as it is in one piece is used where it lies in the RAM disk's memory, as the drivers
 * always did (build.sh has mkapfs.py store fw/ that way: --plain fw).
 * Any other APFS file is read out once by apfs_lib -- the same code as the volume's when
 * mounted, compressed or not -- into memory of its own, and kept: firmware is asked for once
 * or twice a session and its driver keeps it while the phone runs, so nothing gives it back.
 */
#include <kern/kalloc.h>
#include <kern/locks.h>
#include <libkern/libkern.h>
#include <sys/errno.h>
#include <sys/param.h>
#include <sys/stat.h>
#include <sys/systm.h>
#include <miscfs/apfs/apfs_lib.h>

extern dev_t mdevlookup(int devid);
extern int mdevgetkernelrange(dev_t dev, vm_offset_t *base, uint64_t *size);

const uint8_t *redwood_image_file(const char *dir, const char *name, uint64_t *size, int *disk_out);

/* ---- APFS ---- */

struct mem_dev {
	const uint8_t *base;
	uint64_t       length;
};

static int
mem_read(void *ctx, uint64_t off, void *buf, size_t len)
{
	struct mem_dev *m = ctx;

	if (off > m->length || len > m->length - off) {
		return EIO;
	}
	memcpy(buf, m->base + off, len);
	return 0;
}

static LCK_GRP_DECLARE(image_lck_grp, "redwood_image");
static LCK_MTX_DECLARE(image_lock, &image_lck_grp);    /* kept[]: the drivers start beside each other */
static struct {
	int       disk;
	char      path[96];
	uint8_t  *data;
	uint64_t  size;
} kept[64];

static const uint8_t *
apfs_file(int disk, const uint8_t *base, uint64_t length, const char *dir, const char *name, uint64_t *size)
{
	struct mem_dev m = { .base = base, .length = length };
	struct apfs_dev dev = { .ctx = &m, .size = length, .read = mem_read, .read_data = mem_read };
	struct apfs_nx *nx = NULL;
	struct apfs_vol *vol = NULL;
	struct apfs_inode ino;
	struct apfs_cfile cf;
	char path[96];
	uint64_t id = 0, fsize = 0, off = 0;
	uint8_t dt = 0, *data = NULL;
	uint32_t i;
	int error;

	if (length < 4096 || memcmp(base + 32, "NXSB", 4) != 0) {
		return NULL;
	}
	snprintf(path, sizeof(path), "/%s/%s", dir, name);
	lck_mtx_lock(&image_lock);
	for (i = 0; i < sizeof(kept) / sizeof(kept[0]) && kept[i].data != NULL; i++) {
		if (kept[i].disk == disk && strcmp(kept[i].path, path) == 0) {
			*size = kept[i].size;
			lck_mtx_unlock(&image_lock);
			return kept[i].data;
		}
	}
	nx = kalloc_type(struct apfs_nx, Z_WAITOK | Z_ZERO);
	vol = kalloc_type(struct apfs_vol, Z_WAITOK | Z_ZERO);
	if (nx == NULL || vol == NULL) {
		goto out;
	}
	if (apfs_nx_open(nx, &dev) != 0) {
		kfree_type(struct apfs_nx, nx);
		nx = NULL;
		goto out;
	}
	error = ENOENT;
	for (uint32_t v = 0; v < APFS_NX_MAX_FILE_SYSTEMS && error != 0; v++) {
		if (nx->fs_oid[v] != 0 && apfs_vol_open(nx, v, vol) == 0) {
			error = apfs_path_lookup(vol, path, &id, &dt);
		}
	}
	if (error == 0) {
		error = apfs_inode_get(vol, id, &ino);
	}
	if (error == 0 && (ino.mode & APFS_S_IFMT) != APFS_S_IFREG) {
		error = EISDIR;
	}
	if (error == 0) {
		error = apfs_inode_size(vol, &ino, &fsize);
	}
	if (error == 0 && (fsize == 0 || fsize > 256 * 1024 * 1024)) {
		error = EFBIG;
	}
	if (error == 0) {
		uint64_t addr = 0;

		/* in one piece as it is: where it lies, no copy */
		if (apfs_file_in_place(vol, &ino, &addr) == 0 && addr <= length / nx->block_size &&
		    fsize <= length - addr * nx->block_size) {
			apfs_nx_close(nx);
			*size = fsize;
			data = __DECONST(uint8_t *, base) + addr * nx->block_size;
			goto out;
		}
		if (i == sizeof(kept) / sizeof(kept[0])) {
			printf("redwood_image: %s of /dev/md%d: kept %lu files already, no room for a copy of another\n", path, disk,
			    (unsigned long)i);
			error = ENOSPC;
		}
	}
	if (error == 0) {
		data = kalloc_data((vm_size_t)fsize, Z_WAITOK);
		error = data == NULL ? ENOMEM : 0;
	}
	memset(&cf, 0, sizeof(cf));
	cf.held = APFS_NO_PIECE;
	while (error == 0 && off < fsize) {
		size_t got = 0;

		error = apfs_read_file(vol, &ino, &cf, off, data + off, (size_t)(fsize - off), &got);
		if (error == 0 && got == 0) {
			error = EIO;
		}
		off += got;
	}
	apfs_cfile_fini(&cf);
	apfs_nx_close(nx);
	if (error == 0) {
		kept[i].disk = disk;
		strlcpy(kept[i].path, path, sizeof(kept[i].path));
		kept[i].size = fsize;
		kept[i].data = data;            /* (last: a reader of the table sees all of it or none) */
		*size = fsize;
	} else if (data != NULL) {
		kfree_data(data, (vm_size_t)fsize);
		data = NULL;
	}
out:
	lck_mtx_unlock(&image_lock);
	if (vol != NULL) {
		kfree_type(struct apfs_vol, vol);
	}
	if (nx != NULL) {
		kfree_type(struct apfs_nx, nx);
	}
	return data;
}

const uint8_t *
redwood_image_file(const char *dir, const char *name, uint64_t *size, int *disk_out)
{
	for (int disk = 1; disk >= 0; disk--) {
		vm_offset_t base = 0;
		uint64_t length = 0;
		const uint8_t *data;
		dev_t dev = mdevlookup(disk);

		if (dev == (dev_t)-1 || mdevgetkernelrange(dev, &base, &length) != 0) {
			continue;
		}
		data = apfs_file(disk, (const uint8_t *)base, length, dir, name, size);
		if (data != NULL) {
			if (disk_out != NULL) {
				*disk_out = disk;
			}
			return data;
		}
	}
	return NULL;
}
```

`xnu/files/bsd/dev/redwood_input.c`:

```c
/*
 * /dev/redwood-touch: a queue of touch samples (see sys/redwood_input.h).
 */
#include <kern/clock.h>
#include <kern/locks.h>
#include <kern/thread_call.h>
#include <libkern/libkern.h>
#include <miscfs/devfs/devfs.h>
#include <sys/conf.h>
#include <sys/errno.h>
#include <sys/proc.h>
#include <sys/redwood_input.h>
#include <sys/systm.h>
#include <sys/uio.h>
#include <pexpert/pexpert.h>

#define TOUCH_QUEUE     512             /* records; a power of two */

/*
 * Boot-arg touch_lat=1: for measuring how long a touch takes to reach the panel, a line for every
 * sample posted ("tl: p TYPE FINGER X Y at US", the time in microseconds of mach_absolute_time),
 * to be matched with the window server's lines about reading it (userland/src/inject.c), drawing
 * (eagl.c) and the display driver's about the frame (MiniIOMobileFramebuffer.cpp): see
 * tools/latency.py.
 */
static uint32_t touch_lat = 2;          /* 2: not yet looked up */

extern void loader_log_line(const char *line);

/*
 * A "tl:" line, for the kernel's drivers: into the loader's log as it is written -- the kernel's own
 * log keeps only the last of a run, and a live look at the loader's (XL_FOLLOW) then misses nothing.
 */
void redwood_tl(const char *format, ...) __printflike(1, 2);

void
redwood_tl(const char *format, ...)
{
	char line[192];
	va_list list;

	va_start(list, format);
	vsnprintf(line, sizeof(line), format, list);
	va_end(list);
	loader_log_line(line);
}

static bool
latency_lines(void)
{
	if (touch_lat == 2) {
		uint32_t on = 0;

		touch_lat = PE_parse_boot_argn("touch_lat", &on, sizeof(on)) && on != 0;
	}
	return touch_lat != 0;
}

static LCK_GRP_DECLARE(touch_lck_grp, "redwood-touch");
static LCK_MTX_DECLARE(touch_lock, &touch_lck_grp);
static struct redwood_touch touch_queue[TOUCH_QUEUE];
static uint32_t touch_head, touch_tail;        /* read from head, add at tail */

/*
 * The way out when nothing else is at hand: five fingers held on the screen for a second and a
 * half end the run -- control goes back to the loader, as when loader_return_after expires.
 * Only a driver's fingers count, not samples a program writes to the device.
 */
#define EXIT_FINGERS    5
#define EXIT_HOLD_MS    1500

extern void loader_return(void);

static thread_call_t exit_call;
static uint32_t fingers_down;           /* one bit for each finger a driver says is down */

static void
exit_hold_elapsed(__unused thread_call_param_t p0, __unused thread_call_param_t p1)
{
	printf("\n--- %d fingers held on the screen for %d ms: back to the loader ---\n", EXIT_FINGERS, EXIT_HOLD_MS);
	redwood_adreno_stop();
	loader_return();
}

/* With touch_lock held. */
static void
count_fingers(uint32_t type, uint32_t finger)
{
	int before = __builtin_popcount(fingers_down), now;
	uint64_t deadline;

	if (finger >= 32 || exit_call == NULL || (type != REDWOOD_TOUCH_DOWN && type != REDWOOD_TOUCH_UP)) {
		return;
	}
	if (type == REDWOOD_TOUCH_DOWN) {
		fingers_down |= 1u << finger;
	} else {
		fingers_down &= ~(1u << finger);
	}
	now = __builtin_popcount(fingers_down);
	if (now >= EXIT_FINGERS && before < EXIT_FINGERS) {
		clock_interval_to_deadline(EXIT_HOLD_MS, NSEC_PER_MSEC, &deadline);
		thread_call_enter_delayed(exit_call, deadline);
	} else if (now < EXIT_FINGERS && before >= EXIT_FINGERS) {
		thread_call_cancel(exit_call);
	}
}

static void
touch_post(uint32_t type, uint32_t finger, uint32_t x, uint32_t y, bool from_driver)
{
	struct redwood_touch *t;

	lck_mtx_lock(&touch_lock);
	if (touch_tail - touch_head == TOUCH_QUEUE) {
		touch_head++;                   /* nobody reads: drop the oldest */
	}
	t = &touch_queue[touch_tail++ % TOUCH_QUEUE];
	t->time = mach_absolute_time();
	if (latency_lines()) {
		uint64_t ns;

		absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(t->time, &ns);
		redwood_tl("tl: p %u %u %u %u at %llu\n", type, finger, x, y, ns / 1000);
	}
	t->type = type;
	t->finger = finger;
	t->x = x > 65535 ? 65535 : x;
	t->y = y > 65535 ? 65535 : y;
	if (from_driver) {
		count_fingers(type, finger);
	}
	lck_mtx_unlock(&touch_lock);
	wakeup(&touch_queue);
}

void
redwood_touch_post(uint32_t type, uint32_t finger, uint32_t x, uint32_t y)
{
	touch_post(type, finger, x, y, true);
}

static int
touch_open(__unused dev_t dev, __unused int flags, __unused int devtype, __unused struct proc *p)
{
	return 0;
}

static int
touch_close(__unused dev_t dev, __unused int flags, __unused int devtype, __unused struct proc *p)
{
	return 0;
}

static int
touch_read(__unused dev_t dev, struct uio *uio, __unused int ioflag)
{
	struct redwood_touch t;
	int error = 0, moved = 0;

	lck_mtx_lock(&touch_lock);
	while (touch_head == touch_tail) {
		error = msleep(&touch_queue, &touch_lock, PZERO | PCATCH, "redwood-touch", NULL);
		if (error) {
			lck_mtx_unlock(&touch_lock);
			return error;
		}
	}
	while (touch_head != touch_tail && uio_resid(uio) >= (user_ssize_t)sizeof(t)) {
		t = touch_queue[touch_head++ % TOUCH_QUEUE];
		lck_mtx_unlock(&touch_lock);
		error = uiomove((caddr_t)&t, sizeof(t), uio);
		lck_mtx_lock(&touch_lock);
		if (error) {
			break;
		}
		moved++;
	}
	lck_mtx_unlock(&touch_lock);
	return moved ? 0 : error;
}

static int
touch_write(__unused dev_t dev, struct uio *uio, __unused int ioflag)
{
	struct redwood_touch t;
	int error = 0;

	while (uio_resid(uio) >= (user_ssize_t)sizeof(t)) {
		error = uiomove((caddr_t)&t, sizeof(t), uio);
		if (error) {
			break;
		}
		if (t.type < REDWOOD_TOUCH_DOWN || t.type > REDWOOD_BUTTON_UP) {
			return EINVAL;
		}
		touch_post(t.type, t.finger, t.x, t.y, false);
	}
	return error;
}

static const struct cdevsw touch_cdevsw = {
	.d_open = touch_open, .d_close = touch_close, .d_read = touch_read, .d_write = touch_write,
	.d_ioctl = eno_ioctl, .d_stop = eno_stop, .d_reset = eno_reset, .d_select = eno_select,
	.d_mmap = eno_mmap, .d_strategy = eno_strat, .d_type = 0
};

void
redwood_input_init(void)
{
	int major = cdevsw_add(-1, &touch_cdevsw);

	if (major < 0 || devfs_make_node(makedev(major, 0), DEVFS_CHAR, UID_ROOT, GID_WHEEL, 0666, "redwood-touch") == NULL) {
		printf("redwood-touch: cannot create the device\n");
	}
	exit_call = thread_call_allocate(exit_hold_elapsed, NULL);
	redwood_cpufreq_init();
	redwood_virtio_input_init();
	redwood_goodix_init();
	redwood_buttons_init();
	redwood_battery_init();
	redwood_ufs_init();
	redwood_net_init();
	redwood_adreno_init();
	redwood_wifi_init();
	redwood_adsp_init();
}

```

`xnu/files/bsd/dev/redwood_lx.c`:

```c
/*
 * Darwin-on-redwood: the kernel's side of the Wi-Fi driver's object.
 *
 * The driver of the phone's radio is Linux's ath11k, compiled unmodified outside this tree on a
 * layer that gives it the kernel interfaces it expects, and tied into one object that the
 * kernel links when it is there (tools/mk-ath11k.sh and wifi/lx in the repository; the kernel
 * is built with that object when xnu-build.sh finds it). The object shows one name, lx_start(),
 * and asks for the calls of sys/redwood_lx.h, which are here: memory, time, threads, one lock
 * to sleep under, the kernel's options. What it asks of the radio itself -- its firmware's
 * files, its view of memory, the processor its firmware runs on -- is redwood_wifi.c's to
 * answer, which knows the phone.
 *
 * A kernel built without the object has the lx_start() at the end of this file, which says so.
 */
#include <kern/clock.h>
#include <kern/kalloc.h>
#include <kern/locks.h>
#include <kern/sched_prim.h>
#include <kern/thread.h>
#include <os/atomic_private.h>
#include <libkern/libkern.h>
#include <mach/mach_types.h>
#include <mach/vm_param.h>
#include <pexpert/pexpert.h>
#include <sys/errno.h>
#include <sys/random.h>
#include <sys/redwood_input.h>
#include <sys/redwood_lx.h>
#include <sys/redwood_net.h>
#include <sys/systm.h>
#include <vm/memory_types.h>
#include <vm/vm_kern.h>

extern vm_offset_t ml_io_map_unmappable(vm_offset_t phys_addr, vm_size_t size, unsigned int flags);
extern uint64_t kvtophys(vm_offset_t va);       /* pmap_paddr_t */
extern kern_return_t thread_terminate(thread_t thread);
extern void thread_set_thread_name(thread_t thread, const char *name);

#define say redwood_wifi_say

static LCK_GRP_DECLARE(lx_lock_group, "redwood-lx");
static LCK_MTX_DECLARE(lx_lock, &lx_lock_group);

/* ---- memory ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ */

void *
lx_os_alloc(unsigned long size)
{
	return kalloc_data(size, Z_WAITOK | Z_ZERO);
}

void
lx_os_free(void *memory, unsigned long size)
{
	kfree_data(memory, size);
}

/*
 * In one physical piece, so that it can be mapped a second time without this processor's cache
 * in between (as redwood_adreno.c does with what it shares with the GPU); the first, cached
 * view is written out and never used again.
 */
void *
lx_os_radio_memory(unsigned long size, unsigned long long *address)
{
	vm_offset_t cached = 0, uncached;
	uint64_t physical;

	size = round_page(size);
	if (kmem_alloc_contig(kernel_map, &cached, size, 0, 0, 0, KMA_KOBJECT | KMA_ZERO | KMA_DATA, VM_KERN_MEMORY_IOKIT) !=
	    KERN_SUCCESS) {
		say("lx: no %lu bytes of memory in one piece\n", size);
		return NULL;
	}
	physical = kvtophys(cached);
	bzero((void *)cached, size);
	for (vm_offset_t line = cached; line < cached + size; line += 64) {
		__asm__ volatile ("dc civac, %0" : : "r" (line));
	}
	__asm__ volatile ("dsb sy");
	uncached = ml_io_map_unmappable(physical, size, VM_WIMG_WCOMB);
	if (uncached == 0 || !redwood_wifi_radio_map(physical, size, address)) {
		return NULL;
	}
	return (void *)uncached;
}

void *
lx_os_map_registers(unsigned long long physical, unsigned long size)
{
	unsigned long long page = trunc_page(physical);
	vm_offset_t mapped = ml_io_map_unmappable(page, round_page(physical + size) - page, VM_WIMG_IO);

	return mapped == 0 ? NULL : (void *)(mapped + (physical - page));
}

/* ---- saying things ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

void
lx_os_print(const char *text)
{
	say("%s", text);
}

void
lx_os_tell(const char *text)
{
	redwood_wifi_tell("%s", text);
}

void
lx_os_panic(const char *text)
{
	panic("%s", text);
}

/* ---- time, threads, sleeping --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

unsigned long long
lx_os_nanoseconds(void)
{
	uint64_t nanoseconds;

	absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(mach_absolute_time(), &nanoseconds);
	return nanoseconds;
}

void *
lx_os_thread_self(void)
{
	return current_thread();
}

struct lx_thread {
	void (*function)(void *);
	void *argument;
};

static void
lx_thread_runs(void *parameter, __unused wait_result_t result)
{
	struct lx_thread start = *(struct lx_thread *)parameter;

	kfree_type(struct lx_thread, parameter);
	start.function(start.argument);
	thread_terminate(current_thread());
}

int
lx_os_thread(const char *name, void (*function)(void *), void *argument)
{
	struct lx_thread *start = kalloc_type(struct lx_thread, Z_WAITOK | Z_ZERO);
	thread_t thread;

	if (start == NULL) {
		return ENOMEM;
	}
	start->function = function;
	start->argument = argument;
	if (kernel_thread_start(lx_thread_runs, start, &thread) != KERN_SUCCESS) {
		kfree_type(struct lx_thread, start);
		return EAGAIN;
	}
	thread_set_thread_name(thread, name);
	thread_deallocate(thread);
	return 0;
}

void
lx_os_lock(void)
{
	lck_mtx_lock(&lx_lock);
}

void
lx_os_unlock(void)
{
	lck_mtx_unlock(&lx_lock);
}

int
lx_os_sleep(const void *address, unsigned long long nanoseconds)
{
	uint64_t deadline;

	if (nanoseconds == 0) {
		return lck_mtx_sleep(&lx_lock, LCK_SLEEP_DEFAULT, (event_t)address, THREAD_UNINT) == THREAD_TIMED_OUT;
	}
	nanoseconds_to_absolutetime(nanoseconds, &deadline);
	deadline += mach_absolute_time();
	return lck_mtx_sleep_deadline(&lx_lock, LCK_SLEEP_DEFAULT, (event_t)address, THREAD_UNINT, deadline) == THREAD_TIMED_OUT;
}

void
lx_os_wakeup(const void *address)
{
	thread_wakeup((event_t)address);
}

/* ---- the rest of the machine ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

void
lx_os_random(void *buffer, unsigned long size)
{
	read_random(buffer, (u_int)size);
}

unsigned
lx_os_option(const char *name)
{
	return redwood_wifi_option(name);
}

int
lx_os_firmware(const char *name, const void **data, unsigned long *size)
{
	uint64_t length = 0;
	const uint8_t *file = redwood_wifi_driver_file(name, &length);

	if (file == NULL) {
		return ENOENT;
	}
	*data = file;
	*size = (unsigned long)length;
	return 0;
}

int
lx_os_rproc_boot(void)
{
	return redwood_wifi_dsp_is_up() ? 0 : ENXIO;
}

int
lx_os_radio_address(unsigned char *address)
{
	return redwood_wifi_radio_address(address);
}

int
lx_os_network(unsigned char *name, unsigned *name_length, unsigned char *passphrase, unsigned *passphrase_length)
{
	return redwood_wifi_network(name, name_length, passphrase, passphrase_length);
}

/* ---- frames: the radio as the link behind en0 (sys/redwood_net.h) ------------------------------------ */

/*
 * A frame from the network stack comes on whatever thread sends it, and the driver's side keeps
 * a record of every thread that enters it: so frames are put in a queue here, and one thread of
 * ours takes them to the driver. A queue that is full drops what comes (TCP sends it again).
 */
#define LX_QUEUE        256

struct lx_frame {
	uint16_t length;
	uint8_t bytes[REDWOOD_NET_FRAME_MAX];
};

static bool lx_link_attached;
static LCK_MTX_DECLARE(lx_queue_lock, &lx_lock_group);
static struct lx_frame *lx_queue;
static uint32_t lx_queue_in, lx_queue_out;      /* frames put in and taken out, counted from the start */
static uint64_t lx_queue_dropped;

static void
lx_queue_runs(__unused void *parameter, __unused wait_result_t result)
{
	for (;;) {
		struct lx_frame *frame;

		lck_mtx_lock(&lx_queue_lock);
		while (lx_queue_in == lx_queue_out) {
			lck_mtx_sleep(&lx_queue_lock, LCK_SLEEP_DEFAULT, (event_t)&lx_queue_in, THREAD_UNINT);
		}
		frame = &lx_queue[lx_queue_out % LX_QUEUE];     /* (stays ours until lx_queue_out moves) */
		lck_mtx_unlock(&lx_queue_lock);
		lx_transmit(frame->bytes, frame->length);
		lck_mtx_lock(&lx_queue_lock);
		lx_queue_out++;
		lck_mtx_unlock(&lx_queue_lock);
	}
}

static bool
lx_link_transmit(mbuf_t packet, size_t length)
{
	struct lx_frame *frame;

	lck_mtx_lock(&lx_queue_lock);
	if (length > REDWOOD_NET_FRAME_MAX || lx_queue_in - lx_queue_out == LX_QUEUE) {
		lx_queue_dropped++;
		lck_mtx_unlock(&lx_queue_lock);
		return false;
	}
	frame = &lx_queue[lx_queue_in % LX_QUEUE];
	if (mbuf_copydata(packet, 0, length, frame->bytes) != 0) {
		lck_mtx_unlock(&lx_queue_lock);
		return false;
	}
	frame->length = (uint16_t)length;
	lx_queue_in++;
	lck_mtx_unlock(&lx_queue_lock);
	thread_wakeup((event_t)&lx_queue_in);
	return true;
}

static struct redwood_net_link lx_link = {
	.name = "the phone's radio (ath11k)",
	.wireless = true,
	.transmit = lx_link_transmit,
};

void
lx_os_net_attach(const unsigned char *address)
{
	thread_t thread;

	if (lx_link_attached) {
		return;
	}
	lx_queue = kalloc_data(LX_QUEUE * sizeof(*lx_queue), Z_WAITOK | Z_ZERO);
	if (lx_queue == NULL || kernel_thread_start(lx_queue_runs, NULL, &thread) != KERN_SUCCESS) {
		say("lx: no memory or no thread for the frames to send: the radio's frames go nowhere\n");
		return;
	}
	thread_set_thread_name(thread, "wifi-send");
	thread_deallocate(thread);
	memcpy(lx_link.address, address, sizeof(lx_link.address));
	lx_link_attached = redwood_net_attach(&lx_link);
	say("lx: %s\n", lx_link_attached ? "the radio is the link behind en0" : "EN0 HAS A LINK ALREADY: the radio's frames go "
	    "nowhere");
}

/*
 * With wifi=1 the interface is made when the kernel starts, before the radio is up: iOS's Wi-Fi
 * side looks for it and for its registry entry as soon as it runs, once, and a radio that
 * turns up twelve seconds later is one it has already failed to open.
 */
void
redwood_lx_net_early(void)
{
	uint8_t address[6];

	if (redwood_wifi_radio_address(address)) {
		lx_os_net_attach(address);
	}
}

void
lx_os_net_link(int up)
{
	if (lx_link_attached) {
		redwood_net_link_state(up != 0);
	}
}

void
lx_os_net_input(const unsigned char *frame, unsigned long length)
{
	if (lx_link_attached && length <= REDWOOD_NET_FRAME_MAX) {
		redwood_net_input(frame, length);
	}
}

/* ---- the radio's interrupts ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

extern kern_return_t gic_v3_spi_attach(uint32_t intid, bool edge, void (*handler)(void *context, uint32_t intid), void *context);
extern void gic_v3_spi_mask(uint32_t intid);
extern void gic_v3_spi_unmask(uint32_t intid);
extern void gic_v3_spi_detach(uint32_t intid);
extern uint64_t gic_v3_spi_count(uint32_t intid);

#define LX_VECTORS      32

static struct {
	void (*function)(void *);
	void *argument;
	bool attached;
} lx_vector[LX_VECTORS];
static uint32_t lx_irq_first;                   /* the GIC's number of vector 0; 0: no interrupts */
static uint32_t lx_irq_pending;                 /* the vectors that have fired and are not dealt with yet */
static uint32_t lx_irq_running;                 /* the vectors whose function the thread is in */
static thread_t lx_irq_thread;
static LCK_MTX_DECLARE(lx_irq_lock, &lx_lock_group);

/* In interrupt context: the vector masked, and the thread told. */
static void
lx_irq_arrived(__unused void *context, uint32_t intid)
{
	gic_v3_spi_mask(intid);
	os_atomic_or(&lx_irq_pending, 1u << (intid - lx_irq_first), relaxed);
	thread_wakeup((event_t)&lx_irq_pending);
}

static void
lx_irq_runs(__unused void *parameter, __unused wait_result_t result)
{
	for (;;) {
		uint32_t pending;

		for (;;) {
			assert_wait((event_t)&lx_irq_pending, THREAD_UNINT);
			if ((pending = os_atomic_xchg(&lx_irq_pending, 0, acquire)) != 0) {
				clear_wait(current_thread(), THREAD_AWAKENED);
				break;
			}
			thread_block(THREAD_CONTINUE_NULL);
		}
		for (unsigned v = 0; v < LX_VECTORS; v++) {
			if (!(pending & 1u << v)) {
				continue;
			}
			lck_mtx_lock(&lx_irq_lock);
			if (!lx_vector[v].attached) {
				lck_mtx_unlock(&lx_irq_lock);
				continue;
			}
			lx_irq_running |= 1u << v;
			lck_mtx_unlock(&lx_irq_lock);
			lx_vector[v].function(lx_vector[v].argument);
			lck_mtx_lock(&lx_irq_lock);
			lx_irq_running &= ~(1u << v);
			lck_mtx_unlock(&lx_irq_lock);
			thread_wakeup((event_t)&lx_irq_running);
		}
	}
}

int
lx_os_irq_msi(unsigned long long *address, unsigned *data)
{
	uint32_t first = 0;

	if (!redwood_wifi_radio_msi(address, data, &first)) {
		return 0;
	}
	lx_irq_first = first;
	return 1;
}

int
lx_os_irq_attach(unsigned vector, void (*function)(void *), void *argument)
{
	kern_return_t kr;

	if (vector >= LX_VECTORS || lx_irq_first == 0 || function == NULL) {
		return EINVAL;
	}
	if (lx_irq_thread == THREAD_NULL) {
		redwood_wifi_tell("lx: wifi_irq: THE GIC'S DISTRIBUTOR IS WRITTEN for the radio's interrupts: each vector's SPI (%u + v) edge-"
		    "triggered, group 1, routed to this processor, then enabled\n", lx_irq_first);
		if (kernel_thread_start(lx_irq_runs, NULL, &lx_irq_thread) != KERN_SUCCESS) {
			lx_irq_thread = THREAD_NULL;
			return ENOMEM;
		}
		thread_set_thread_name(lx_irq_thread, "wifi-irq");
	}
	lck_mtx_lock(&lx_irq_lock);
	lx_vector[vector].function = function;
	lx_vector[vector].argument = argument;
	lx_vector[vector].attached = true;
	lck_mtx_unlock(&lx_irq_lock);
	if ((kr = gic_v3_spi_attach(lx_irq_first + vector, true, lx_irq_arrived, NULL)) != KERN_SUCCESS) {
		lck_mtx_lock(&lx_irq_lock);
		lx_vector[vector].attached = false;
		lck_mtx_unlock(&lx_irq_lock);
		return kr == KERN_NAME_EXISTS ? EBUSY : EINVAL;
	}
	gic_v3_spi_mask(lx_irq_first + vector);
	return 0;
}

void
lx_os_irq_enable(unsigned vector)
{
	if (vector < LX_VECTORS && lx_vector[vector].attached) {
		gic_v3_spi_unmask(lx_irq_first + vector);
	}
}

void
lx_os_irq_disable(unsigned vector)
{
	if (vector >= LX_VECTORS || !lx_vector[vector].attached) {
		return;
	}
	gic_v3_spi_mask(lx_irq_first + vector);
	if (current_thread() == lx_irq_thread) {
		return;                         /* (from the vector's own function, or another's: nothing to wait for) */
	}
	lck_mtx_lock(&lx_irq_lock);
	while (lx_irq_running & 1u << vector) {
		lck_mtx_sleep(&lx_irq_lock, LCK_SLEEP_DEFAULT, (event_t)&lx_irq_running, THREAD_UNINT);
	}
	lck_mtx_unlock(&lx_irq_lock);
}

void
lx_os_irq_detach_all(void)
{
	for (unsigned v = 0; v < LX_VECTORS; v++) {
		if (lx_vector[v].attached) {
			gic_v3_spi_detach(lx_irq_first + v);
		}
	}
	lck_mtx_lock(&lx_irq_lock);
	for (unsigned v = 0; v < LX_VECTORS; v++) {
		lx_vector[v].attached = false;
	}
	while (lx_irq_running != 0 && current_thread() != lx_irq_thread) {
		lck_mtx_sleep(&lx_irq_lock, LCK_SLEEP_DEFAULT, (event_t)&lx_irq_running, THREAD_UNINT);
	}
	lck_mtx_unlock(&lx_irq_lock);
	os_atomic_store(&lx_irq_pending, 0, relaxed);
}

unsigned long long
lx_os_irq_count(unsigned vector)
{
	return vector < LX_VECTORS && lx_irq_first != 0 ? gic_v3_spi_count(lx_irq_first + vector) : 0;
}

}

}

```

`xnu/files/bsd/dev/redwood_mic.c`:

```c
/*
 * The phone's microphones, through the audio DSP. Every address and number below belongs to the
 * POCO X5 Pro (redwood), from Android's own live device tree, its mixer paths (fw-audio/android/)
 * and Xiaomi's kernel (redwood-s-oss, techpack/audio: asoc/codecs/bolero/, asoc/codecs/wcd938x/,
 * soc/swr-mstr-ctrl.c, soc/pinctrl-lpi.c, dsp/q6afe.c, asoc/codecs/audio-ext-clk-up.c). Nothing
 * here happens unless boot-arg mic=N asks for it, with adsp=1 (redwood_adsp.c), which calls
 * redwood_mic_dsp_up() once the DSP's audio services are up.
 *
 * The main microphone under Android (mixer paths "handset-mic" = "amic1", "audio-record"): the
 * analog microphone at ADC1 of the WCD938x codec, whose samples go over SoundWire (the TX master
 * of the LPASS's digital codec, "bolero") into decimator 1 of the TX macro, out of it through the
 * codec DMA interface TX_CDC_DMA_TX_3, the AFE's port, into a stream that is read (ASM). Before any
 * of it: the LPASS's own clocks, which the DSP gives out (Android's audio-ref-clk nodes):
 *   lpass_core_hw_vote   AFE_CMD_REMOTE_LPASS_CORE_HW_VOTE_REQUEST, block 3 ("LPASS_HW_MACRO")
 *   lpass_audio_hw_vote  the same, block 4 ("LPASS_HW_DCODEC")
 *   tx_core_clk          AFE clock 0x30c at 19.2 MHz (qcom,codec-lpass-clk-id, -ext-clk-freq)
 *   tx_npl_clk           AFE clock 0x30d at 19.2 MHz
 * Without them the macros' registers are not to be touched at all: an access to a block without
 * its clock may hang the bus.
 *
 *   mic=1    a look: the votes and the two clocks asked for, then -- only if all four were given --
 *            the registers of the TX and VA macros, of the TX SoundWire master, of the LPASS pins
 *            the master uses and of the codec's reset pin read (nothing written to any of them);
 *            then the clocks and the votes given back
 *   mic=2    ... and the codec brought up far enough to answer on SoundWire, nothing of it set:
 *            its supplies as the boot chain leaves them (L18B and BoB are on: the codec answers; nothing
 *            of the PMICs is touched), its reset released (GPIO83 low 20 us, then high, 16 mA:
 *            msm-cdc-pinctrl's two states), the master's pins to their active state (LPASS GPIOs
 *            0, 1, 2, 14: function 1, 2 mA, slew rate 1; the clock without a pull, the data with a
 *            keeper), the TX macro's clocks as tx_macro_tx_va_mclk_enable() starts them (bolero's
 *            "fs-gen-sequence" in the VA macro, FREQ_MCLK, MCLK_CONTROL, FS_CNT_CONTROL, the
 *            SoundWire clock with a reset), the master started as swrm_runtime_resume() and
 *            swrm_master_init() start it (the frame 50 rows x 2 columns, auto-enumeration, its
 *            interrupts' masks), the codec's TX device waited for (ID 0x000d01170223, the tree's
 *            wcd938x-tx-slave) and its chip ID read over SoundWire. Then all of it undone, in reverse:
 *            the codec back in reset, the pins and registers as they were found
 *   mic=3    ... and the main microphone listened to for mic_secs seconds (default 10, at most 600)
 *            the way Android records from it: the codec set up as wcd938x_bind() and
 *            wcd938x_init_reg() set it up (its interrupts as edges, the mic biases' 2750 mV, its
 *            bias and sleep registers); the DSP's side (a stream read through our memory, ASM
 *            session 2; a device path for recording, ADM; the codec DMA port TX_CDC_DMA_TX_3, AFE
 *            port 0xB037, 48 kHz, 16 bits, one channel: decimator 1); the TX macro's decimator 1 fed
 *            from SWR_MIC0 (the mixer controls "TX DEC1 MUX" SWR_MIC, "TX SMIC MUX1" SWR_MIC0, and
 *            tx_macro_enable_dec()); "MIC BIAS1" and ADC1 in "low power" mode, "ADC1 Volume" 6 (Xiaomi's
 *            mixer paths); the SoundWire port with the bus as Android has it for its handset
 *            microphones (see datapath_on()); then the decimator unmuted after 200 ms and its
 *            filter settled after 300 ms, as tx-macro's delayed work does. Each second's level goes
 *            to the log; with rec_sound=N rec_sound_mic=1 the samples go into the recording that
 *            ./xl sound fetches. Every register write is read back (a few registers that read 0
 *            whatever is written, as on Android, are said so); any mismatch or a DSP command
 *            refused stops it all. Tests: mic_input=0 (decimator 1 fed from ZERO: exact silence),
 *            mic_adc=0 (ADC1 left off), mic_test=1 (no mic bias), mic_test=2 (ADC1's input held),
 *            mic_main=1 (the bus and ports of Android's one-microphone tables: a tone, not the room),
 *            mic_tap=1 with haptic=5 (the vibration motor from 2 s to 3 s of listening: the motor's
 *            175.5 Hz in the samples)
 *
 * What is asked for is given back at the end, and before the DSP is shut down (redwood_mic_dsp_down()).
 */
#include <kern/clock.h>
#include <kern/locks.h>
#include <kern/thread.h>
#include <libkern/libkern.h>
#include <libkern/OSAtomic.h>
#include <kern/kalloc.h>
#include <mach/mach_types.h>
#include <miscfs/devfs/devfs.h>
#include <pexpert/pexpert.h>
#include <sys/conf.h>
#include <sys/redwood_audio.h>
#include <sys/redwood_input.h>
#include <sys/systm.h>
#include <sys/uio.h>

extern vm_offset_t ml_io_map(vm_offset_t phys_addr, vm_size_t size);
extern kern_return_t thread_terminate(thread_t thread);
extern void loader_log_putc(char c);

static LCK_GRP_DECLARE(mic_lock_group, "redwood-mic");
static LCK_MTX_DECLARE(mic_lock, &mic_lock_group);      /* what is asked for, and given back */

static uint32_t level;
static bool running;

static int say(const char *format, ...) __printflike(1, 2);

/*
 * Every line is kept as well, and all of them said again at the run's end (redwood_mic_quiesce()):
 * the log of a run keeps its beginning and its end, and this happens in between.
 */
#define KEPT_LINES              400
static char kept[KEPT_LINES][168];
static unsigned kept_count;

static int
say(const char *format, ...)
{
	char line[400];
	va_list list;
	int length;

	va_start(list, format);
	length = vsnprintf(line, sizeof(line), format, list);
	va_end(list);
	for (const char *c = line; *c != 0; c++) {
		loader_log_putc(*c);
	}
	printf("%s", line);
	strlcpy(kept[kept_count++ % KEPT_LINES], line, sizeof(kept[0]));
	return length;
}

/* A line that says all went as it should: not said again in iOS's later recordings (mic=4), where it is the same each time. */
static bool quiet;
#define note(...)       do { if (!quiet) { say(__VA_ARGS__); } } while (0)

void
redwood_mic_quiesce(void)
{
	if (kept_count == 0) {
		return;
	}
	for (const char *c = "mic: what happened in this run, again:\n"; *c != 0; c++) {
		loader_log_putc(*c);
	}
	for (unsigned i = kept_count > KEPT_LINES ? kept_count - KEPT_LINES : 0; i < kept_count; i++) {
		loader_log_putc('>');
		loader_log_putc(' ');
		for (const char *c = kept[i % KEPT_LINES]; *c != 0; c++) {
			loader_log_putc(*c);
		}
		if (kept[i % KEPT_LINES][strlen(kept[i % KEPT_LINES]) - 1] != '\n') {
			loader_log_putc('\n');
		}
	}
}

static void
sleep_ms(uint32_t ms)
{
	delay_for_interval(ms, NSEC_PER_MSEC);
}

static uint32_t __attribute__((noinline))
rd(vm_offset_t address)
{
	uint32_t value;

	__asm__ volatile ("ldr %w0, [%1]" : "=r" (value) : "r" (address) : "memory");
	return value;
}

static void __attribute__((noinline))
wr(vm_offset_t address, uint32_t value)
{
	__asm__ volatile ("str %w0, [%1]" : : "r" (value), "r" (address) : "memory");
}

static void
spin_us(uint32_t us)
{
	uint64_t until;

	nanoseconds_to_absolutetime((uint64_t)us * NSEC_PER_USEC, &until);
	until += mach_absolute_time();
	while (mach_absolute_time() < until) {
	}
}

static bool broken;                     /* a write that did not read back: nothing more is written, all is undone */
static char last_write[120] = "nothing written";

struct block {
	const char *name;
	uint32_t phys, size;
	vm_offset_t base;
};

static uint32_t
get(struct block *b, const char *name, uint32_t offset)
{
	uint32_t value;

	if (b->base == 0) {
		b->base = ml_io_map(b->phys, b->size);
	}
	value = rd(b->base + offset);
	note("mic: %s %s (%#x) = %#x\n", b->name, name, b->phys + offset, value);
	return value;
}

/*
 * A register written (and read back, unless `check' is 0: some bits clear themselves). A write that
 * does not read back as written (in the bits of `check') stops the bring-up.
 */
static bool
put(struct block *b, const char *name, uint32_t offset, uint32_t value, uint32_t check)
{
	uint32_t back;

	if (broken) {
		return false;
	}
	if (b->base == 0) {
		b->base = ml_io_map(b->phys, b->size);
	}
	snprintf(last_write, sizeof(last_write), "%#x to %s %s (%#x)", value, b->name, name, b->phys + offset);
	wr(b->base + offset, value);
	back = rd(b->base + offset);
	if ((back & check) != (value & check)) {
		say("mic: %s %s (%#x) <- %#x, but it reads %#x: STOPPING HERE\n", b->name, name, b->phys + offset, value, back);
		broken = true;
		return false;
	}
	note("mic: %s %s (%#x) <- %#x%s\n", b->name, name, b->phys + offset, value, check ? ", reads back" : "");
	return true;
}

/* only the bits of `mask' changed */
static bool
put_bits(struct block *b, const char *name, uint32_t offset, uint32_t mask, uint32_t value)
{
	uint32_t now;

	if (b->base == 0) {
		b->base = ml_io_map(b->phys, b->size);
	}
	now = rd(b->base + offset);
	return put(b, name, offset, (now & ~mask) | (value & mask), mask);
}

/* ---- the DSP: votes and clocks ------------------------------------------------------------------- */

#define APR_SVC_AFE                             4
#define APR_BASIC_RSP_RESULT                    0x000110e8u
#define APR_WAIT_MS                             1000
#define AFE_SVC_CMD_SET_PARAM                   0x000100f3u
#define AFE_MODULE_CLOCK_SET                    0x0001028fu
#define AFE_PARAM_ID_CLOCK_SET                  0x00010290u
#define AFE_CMD_REMOTE_LPASS_CORE_HW_VOTE_REQUEST       0x000100f4u
#define AFE_CMD_RSP_REMOTE_LPASS_CORE_HW_VOTE_REQUEST   0x000100f5u
#define AFE_CMD_REMOTE_LPASS_CORE_HW_DEVOTE_REQUEST     0x000100f6u
#define LPASS_HW_MACRO_BLOCK                    3
#define LPASS_HW_DCODEC_BLOCK                   4
#define CLOCK_TX_CORE                           0x30c
#define CLOCK_TX_NPL                            0x30d
#define CLOCK_HZ                                19200000
#define CLOCK_COUPLE_NO                         1

static const char *
dsp_error(uint32_t status)
{
	static const char *const names[] = { "ok", "failed", "bad parameter", "unsupported", "version", "unexpected", "panic",
		                             "no resource", "bad handle", "already", "not ready", "pending", "busy", "aborted",
		                             "preempted", "continue", "immediate", "not implemented", "need more", "no memory",
		                             "not there" };

	return status < sizeof(names) / sizeof(names[0]) ? names[status] : "an error this does not know";
}

static bool
command(const char *what, uint8_t service, uint32_t opcode, const void *payload, uint32_t length, uint32_t wanted,
    struct redwood_apr_answer *answer)
{
	struct redwood_apr_answer local;

	if (answer == NULL) {
		answer = &local;
	}
	if (!redwood_adsp_apr(service, 0, 0, opcode, payload, length, APR_WAIT_MS, answer)) {
		say("mic: %s (opcode %#x): NO ANSWER\n", what, opcode);
		return false;
	}
	if (answer->opcode == APR_BASIC_RSP_RESULT && answer->words[0] == opcode) {
		if (answer->words[1] == 0) {
			note("mic: %s: done\n", what);
		} else {
			say("mic: %s: REFUSED: %s\n", what, dsp_error(answer->words[1]));
		}
		return answer->words[1] == 0 && wanted == 0;
	}
	if (wanted != 0 && answer->opcode == wanted) {
		return true;
	}
	say("mic: %s: an answer not expected: opcode %#x, %u bytes: %#x %#x\n", what, answer->opcode, answer->length,
	    answer->words[0], answer->words[1]);
	return false;
}

struct afe_param {
	uint32_t module, param;
	uint16_t size, reserved;
} __attribute__((packed));

struct afe_clock_set {
	uint32_t version, id, hz;
	uint16_t attribute, root;
	uint32_t enable;
} __attribute__((packed));

static bool
afe_service_param(const char *what, uint32_t module, uint32_t param, const void *data, uint16_t size)
{
	uint8_t packet[16 + sizeof(struct afe_param) + 64];
	uint32_t *head = (uint32_t *)packet;
	struct afe_param *p = (struct afe_param *)(packet + 16);

	bzero(packet, sizeof(packet));
	head[0] = (uint32_t)sizeof(*p) + size;          /* payload size; address 0 and handle 0: in band */
	p->module = module;
	p->param = param;
	p->size = size;
	memcpy(packet + 16 + sizeof(*p), data, size);
	return command(what, APR_SVC_AFE, AFE_SVC_CMD_SET_PARAM, packet, 16 + (uint32_t)sizeof(*p) + size, 0, NULL);
}

static bool
afe_clock(const char *what, uint32_t id, bool on)
{
	struct afe_clock_set clock = { 1, id, CLOCK_HZ, CLOCK_COUPLE_NO, 0, on };

	return afe_service_param(what, AFE_MODULE_CLOCK_SET, AFE_PARAM_ID_CLOCK_SET, &clock, sizeof(clock));
}

static uint32_t vote_handle[5];
static bool voted[5], core_clock, npl_clock;

static bool
vote(uint32_t block, const char *client)
{
	struct {
		uint32_t block;
		char client[8];
	} __attribute__((packed)) request = { block, { 0 } };
	struct redwood_apr_answer answer;
	char what[80];

	strlcpy(request.client, client, sizeof(request.client));
	snprintf(what, sizeof(what), "the LPASS's vote for block %u (\"%s\")", block, client);
	if (!command(what, APR_SVC_AFE, AFE_CMD_REMOTE_LPASS_CORE_HW_VOTE_REQUEST, &request, sizeof(request),
	    AFE_CMD_RSP_REMOTE_LPASS_CORE_HW_VOTE_REQUEST, &answer)) {
		return false;
	}
	vote_handle[block] = answer.words[0];
	voted[block] = true;
	say("mic: %s: given, handle %u\n", what, vote_handle[block]);
	return true;
}

static void
devote(uint32_t block)
{
	uint32_t request[2] = { block, vote_handle[block] };
	char what[64];

	if (!voted[block]) {
		return;
	}
	snprintf(what, sizeof(what), "the LPASS's vote for block %u, given back", block);
	(void)command(what, APR_SVC_AFE, AFE_CMD_REMOTE_LPASS_CORE_HW_DEVOTE_REQUEST, request, sizeof(request), 0, NULL);
	voted[block] = false;
}

static bool
clocks_on(void)
{
	if (!vote(LPASS_HW_MACRO_BLOCK, "LPASS_HW_MACRO") || !vote(LPASS_HW_DCODEC_BLOCK, "LPASS_HW_DCODEC")) {
		return false;
	}
	core_clock = afe_clock("the TX macro's core clock (0x30c) at 19.2 MHz, on", CLOCK_TX_CORE, true);
	if (!core_clock) {
		return false;
	}
	npl_clock = afe_clock("the TX macro's NPL clock (0x30d) at 19.2 MHz, on", CLOCK_TX_NPL, true);
	return npl_clock;
}

static void
clocks_off(void)
{
	if (npl_clock) {
		(void)afe_clock("the TX macro's NPL clock, off", CLOCK_TX_NPL, false);
		npl_clock = false;
	}
	if (core_clock) {
		(void)afe_clock("the TX macro's core clock, off", CLOCK_TX_CORE, false);
		core_clock = false;
	}
	devote(LPASS_HW_DCODEC_BLOCK);
	devote(LPASS_HW_MACRO_BLOCK);
}

/* ---- the blocks, read ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ */

static struct block tx_macro = { "the TX macro", 0x03220000, 0x1000 };
static struct block va_macro = { "the VA macro", 0x03370000, 0x1000 };
static struct block tx_swr = { "the TX SoundWire master", 0x03230000, 0x2000 };
static struct block tx_hctl = { "the TX SoundWire master's HCTL", 0x032a9000, 0x1000 };
static struct block lpi = { "the LPASS pins", 0x033c0000, 0x10000 };
static struct block lpi_high = { "the LPASS pins", 0x033ce000, 0x1000 };
static struct block tlmm = { "the pin controller", 0x0f100000, 0x100000 };

static void
look(void)
{
	static const struct { const char *name; uint32_t offset; } tx[] = {
		{ "MCLK_CONTROL", 0x000 }, { "FS_CNT_CONTROL", 0x004 }, { "SWR_CONTROL", 0x008 }, { "TOP_CFG0", 0x080 },
		{ "SWR_CTRL", 0x088 }, { "FREQ_MCLK", 0x090 }, { "SWR_AMIC0_CTL", 0x0d0 }, { "SWR_AMIC1_CTL", 0x0d4 },
	}, va[] = {
		{ "MCLK_CONTROL", 0x000 }, { "FS_CNT_CONTROL", 0x004 }, { "TOP_CFG0", 0x080 },
	}, swr[] = {
		{ "COMP_HW_VERSION", 0x000 }, { "COMP_CFG", 0x004 }, { "COMP_STATUS", 0x014 }, { "COMP_PARAMS", 0x100 },
		{ "COMP_MASTER_ID", 0x104 }, { "INTERRUPT_STATUS", 0x200 }, { "ENUMERATOR_CFG", 0x500 },
		{ "ENUMERATOR_STATUS", 0x504 }, { "MCP_FRAME_CTRL_BANK0", 0x101c }, { "MCP_BUS_CTRL", 0x1044 },
		{ "MCP_CFG", 0x1048 }, { "MCP_STATUS", 0x104c }, { "MCP_SLV_STATUS", 0x1090 },
	};
	static const unsigned pins[] = { 0, 1, 2 };

	for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof(tx) / sizeof(tx[0]); i++) {
		(void)get(&tx_macro, tx[i].name, tx[i].offset);
	}
	for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof(va) / sizeof(va[0]); i++) {
		(void)get(&va_macro, va[i].name, va[i].offset);
	}
	for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof(pins) / sizeof(pins[0]); i++) {
		char name[48];

		snprintf(name, sizeof(name), "gpio%u config (SoundWire TX)", pins[i]);
		(void)get(&lpi, name, 0x1000 * pins[i]);
		snprintf(name, sizeof(name), "gpio%u in/out", pins[i]);
		(void)get(&lpi, name, 0x1000 * pins[i] + 4);
	}
	(void)get(&lpi_high, "gpio14 config (SoundWire TX data 2)", 0);
	(void)get(&lpi_high, "gpio14 in/out", 4);
	(void)get(&tlmm, "gpio83 config (the codec's reset)", 0x1000 * 83);
	(void)get(&tlmm, "gpio83 in/out", 0x1000 * 83 + 4);
	/* (last: the master is a block of its own, and not yet known; with its version above 1.5.1 the votes are all it needs) */
	for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof(swr) / sizeof(swr[0]); i++) {
		(void)get(&tx_swr, swr[i].name, swr[i].offset);
	}
	(void)get(&tx_hctl, "HCTL (0x32a90a8)", 0x0a8);
}

/* ---- the codec's reset, the master's pins ------------------------------------------------------------ */

#define TLMM_CFG_83             (0x1000 * 83)
#define TLMM_IO_83              (0x1000 * 83 + 4)
static uint32_t found_reset_cfg, found_reset_io;
static bool reset_taken;

static bool
reset_release(void)
{
	if (tlmm.base == 0) {
		tlmm.base = ml_io_map(tlmm.phys, tlmm.size);
	}
	found_reset_cfg = rd(tlmm.base + TLMM_CFG_83);
	found_reset_io = rd(tlmm.base + TLMM_IO_83);
	reset_taken = true;
	/* the sleep state: gpio, 16 mA, no pull, output low; 20 us; the active state: output high */
	if (!put(&tlmm, "gpio83 out (the codec's reset)", TLMM_IO_83, 0, 2) ||
	    !put(&tlmm, "gpio83 config: gpio, 16 mA, no pull, output", TLMM_CFG_83, 0x3c0, 0x3ff)) {
		return false;
	}
	spin_us(30);
	if (!put(&tlmm, "gpio83 out: high (the codec out of reset)", TLMM_IO_83, 2, 2)) {
		return false;
	}
	spin_us(30);
	return true;
}

static void
reset_restore(void)
{
	if (!reset_taken) {
		return;
	}
	broken = false;         /* (putting back is done whatever went before) */
	(void)put(&tlmm, "gpio83 out: low (the codec in reset)", TLMM_IO_83, 0, 2);
	(void)put(&tlmm, "gpio83 config, as it was found", TLMM_CFG_83, found_reset_cfg, 0x3ff);
	(void)put(&tlmm, "gpio83 out, as it was found", TLMM_IO_83, found_reset_io & 2, 2);
	reset_taken = false;
}

static struct block lpi_slew = { "the LPASS pins' slew rates", 0x0355a000, 0x1000 };
static const struct { unsigned pin, slew_bit; uint32_t pull; const char *name; } swr_pins[] = {
	{ 0, 0, 0, "gpio0 (SoundWire TX clock)" }, { 1, 2, 2, "gpio1 (data 0)" }, { 2, 4, 2, "gpio2 (data 1)" },
	{ 14, 6, 2, "gpio14 (data 2)" },
};
#define SWR_PINS                (sizeof(swr_pins) / sizeof(swr_pins[0]))
```
