
`xnu/files/bsd/dev/redwood_speaker.c`:

```c
/*
 * The speakers of the POCO X5 Pro (redwood): their two amplifiers. Every address below belongs
 * to this phone, and nothing here is touched unless a boot-arg asks for it.
 *
 * Each speaker has an amplifier of its own, an Awinic AW88261 (chip ID 0x2113, a "smart PA"),
 * set up over I2C -- the bus of the SoC's serial engine 3, GPIO 12 data and 13 clock, on which
 * Android's device tree and its running kernel have these two and nothing else -- and fed by
 * the SoC's first TDM interface ("MI2S 0": GPIO 97 bit clock, 100 frame sync, 99 data out),
 * which the audio DSP drives (redwood_sound.c). In Android's tree the amplifier at 0x35 is
 * "sound-channel 0" and takes slot 0 of the frame (the left channel), the one at 0x34 is
 * channel 1 and takes slot 1; neither has a reset pin.
 *
 * Two uses:
 *
 *   speaker_probe=1    reads registers and nothing else: the pins, the power names (below)
 *   speaker_probe=2    ... and asks the amplifiers who they are (I2C, below)
 *
 *   redwood_speaker_prepare() and the rest (sys/redwood_audio.h), for boot-arg sound=3 of
 *   redwood_sound.c: the amplifiers set up and run exactly as Android's own driver does it
 *   (Xiaomi's redwood-s-oss kernel, techpack/audio/asoc/codecs/aw88263s_m20: aw882xx_device.c,
 *   aw882xx_init.c and aw882xx_pid_2113_reg.h; the phone runs its version 2.0.0), with the
 *   registers' values from Android's own configuration file -- /vendor/etc/aw882xx_acf.bin of
 *   the phone, which userland/build.sh puts into /fw of the system image from fw-audio/ and
 *   which is not in this repository. Its "Music" profile is what Android plays the speakers
 *   with (tinymix: aw_dev_0_prof, aw_dev_1_prof); 55 of its 57 registers read back from the
 *   idle chips under Android exactly as the file has them, and the other two as the driver
 *   leaves them (0x04 powered down and muted, 0x08 with the feedback off).
 *
 * What the driver does and this does the same way, per amplifier:
 *
 *   prepare  reads the chip ID and the four fuse registers; a soft reset (0x55aa into
 *            register 0); the profile's registers, every one but three as the file has them:
 *            0x04 keeps the power-down, amplifier power-down and mute bits as they are and
 *            sets the mute of the power stage ("ULS"), 0x08 has the feedback off, and 0x05 (the
 *            volume) is turned down to the lowest, -90 dB, right after; 0x50 gets the value the
 *            driver works out from the fuses (8192 * (1000 + icalk) / (1000 + vcalk)), which for
 *            this phone's two chips is the value Android left in them
 *   start    only while the TDM clock runs: power-down off, 2 ms, the PLL locked (status bits 0
 *            and 4); amplifier power-down off, 1 ms, the status as the driver wants it (bits 0, 4,
 *            8, 9); the feedback on; the two mutes off; the interrupts read away; the volume
 *            stays at the lowest
 *   volume   stepwise, 6 dB a step (the driver takes one every 100 us), to `below' eighths of a dB
 *            under Android's own level (the profile's 0x05, -2.1 dB, with Android's
 *            aw_dev_N_volume 0) and never above it
 *   stop     the power stage muted, the volume stepped down to the lowest, muted, the feedback
 *            off, 1 ms, amplifier power-down, power-down
 *
 * Every write is said in the log and read back; a value that does not read back as written, a
 * byte nobody acknowledges, or a fault in the status register (under-voltage, over-current of
 * the boost or the output, over-temperature, no clock, the watchdog, over-voltage) has both
 * amplifiers powered down at once (amplifier power-down and power-down, bits 1 and 0 of 0x04)
 * and nothing more done. What is not done, compared with Android: the DSP's Awinic algorithm,
 * which protects the speakers with their calibration (aw882xx_rx_switch); in its place the
 * samples go through redwood_guard.c on their way here. The driver's monitor is done
 * (redwood_speaker_monitor(), below): once a second the chips' temperature and the battery's
 * voltage, and the reduction that the file's table asks for at either.
 *
 * I2C is done by hand: a pin is either pulled low or let go (and the pull-ups raise it), at 100
 * kHz at most. For each register read or written the two pins are taken from the serial engine
 * (function qup03) as GPIOs and given back as they were found right after.
 *
 * Register layouts: the files above, and Linux's sound/soc/codecs/aw88261.c; pins:
 * drivers/pinctrl/qcom/pinctrl-yupik.c of the same kernel and the phone's own device tree.
 */
#include <kern/clock.h>
#include <kern/thread.h>
#include <libkern/libkern.h>
#include <mach/mach_types.h>
#include <pexpert/pexpert.h>
#include <sys/systm.h>
#include <sys/redwood_audio.h>

extern vm_offset_t ml_io_map(vm_offset_t phys_addr, vm_size_t size);
extern vm_offset_t ml_io_map_wcomb(vm_offset_t phys_addr, vm_size_t size);
extern kern_return_t thread_terminate(thread_t thread);
extern void loader_log_putc(char c);

static vm_offset_t tlmm, gcc, cmd_db;
static uint32_t probe_level;
static bool leaving;                    /* on a panic's way out: nothing sleeps, nothing is said but to the loader */

/* Every line to the loader's log as well: what is written to the amplifiers should be known even if the kernel dies. */
static int say(const char *format, ...) __printflike(1, 2);

static int
say(const char *format, ...)
{
	char line[300];
	va_list list;
	int length;

	va_start(list, format);
	length = vsnprintf(line, sizeof(line), format, list);
	va_end(list);
	for (const char *c = line; *c != 0; c++) {
		loader_log_putc(*c);
	}
	if (!leaving) {
		printf("%s", line);
	}
	return length;
}

static inline uint32_t
rd(vm_offset_t address)
{
	return *(volatile uint32_t *)address;
}

static inline void
wr(vm_offset_t address, uint32_t value)
{
	*(volatile uint32_t *)address = value;
}

/* Waits without sleeping (also with interrupts off, on a panic's way out). */
static void
spin_us(uint32_t us)
{
	uint64_t until;

	nanoseconds_to_absolutetime((uint64_t)us * NSEC_PER_USEC, &until);
	until += mach_absolute_time();
	while (mach_absolute_time() < until) {
	}
}

static void
wait_ms(uint32_t ms)
{
	if (leaving) {
		spin_us(ms * 1000);
	} else {
		delay_for_interval(ms, NSEC_PER_MSEC);
	}
}

/* ---- pins ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ */

#define TLMM_PHYS               0x0f100000UL
#define TLMM_SIZE               0x100000UL
#define GPIO_CFG(n)             (tlmm + 0x1000UL * (n))         /* [1:0] pull, [5:2] function, [8:6] drive, [9] output */
#define GPIO_IO(n)              (tlmm + 0x1000UL * (n) + 4)     /* bit 0 in, bit 1 out */
#define CFG_PULL_UP             3
#define CFG_OUTPUT              (1u << 9)

#define PIN_SDA                 12      /* the serial engine's first pin is the data line, the second the clock */
#define PIN_SCL                 13

static const struct {
	unsigned pin;
	const char *what;
} pins[] = {
	{ 12, "I2C data" }, { 13, "I2C clock" }, { 97, "MI2S 0 bit clock" }, { 100, "MI2S 0 word select" },
	{ 98, "MI2S 0 data 0" }, { 99, "MI2S 0 data 1" }, { 102, "the amplifier 0x35's interrupt" },
	{ 45, "the amplifier 0x34's interrupt" },
};

static void
show_pins(void)
{
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof(pins) / sizeof(pins[0]); i++) {
		uint32_t cfg = rd(GPIO_CFG(pins[i].pin)), io = rd(GPIO_IO(pins[i].pin));

		say("speaker: gpio%u (%s): function %u, pull %u, %u mA, %s, reads %u\n", pins[i].pin, pins[i].what,
		    (cfg >> 2) & 15, cfg & 3, (((cfg >> 6) & 7) + 1) * 2, (cfg & CFG_OUTPUT) ? (io & 2 ? "drives high" : "drives low") :
		    "input", io & 1);
	}
}

/* ---- I2C by hand ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

static void
half_bit(void)
{
	spin_us(5);                     /* 100 kHz at most, I2C's standard mode; the bus does not mind slower */
}

/* A line is pulled low (the pin drives 0) or let go (the pin is an input and the pull-up raises it). */
static void
line(unsigned pin, bool high)
{
	wr(GPIO_IO(pin), 0);
	wr(GPIO_CFG(pin), CFG_PULL_UP | (high ? 0 : CFG_OUTPUT));
}

static bool
level(unsigned pin)
{
	return rd(GPIO_IO(pin)) & 1;
}

static void
i2c_start(void)
{
	line(PIN_SDA, true);
	line(PIN_SCL, true);
	half_bit();
	line(PIN_SDA, false);
	half_bit();
	line(PIN_SCL, false);
	half_bit();
}

static void
i2c_stop(void)
{
	line(PIN_SDA, false);
	half_bit();
	line(PIN_SCL, true);
	half_bit();
	line(PIN_SDA, true);
	half_bit();
}

/* One bit out (the other side's bit in, if we let the data line go): the clock goes up and down once. */
static bool
i2c_bit(bool out)
{
	bool in;

	line(PIN_SDA, out);
	half_bit();
	line(PIN_SCL, true);
	for (unsigned stretched = 0; !level(PIN_SCL) && stretched < 100; stretched++) {
		half_bit();             /* (a device may hold the clock low until it is ready) */
	}
	half_bit();
	in = level(PIN_SDA);
	line(PIN_SCL, false);
	return in;
}

/* Returns true if the byte was acknowledged. */
static bool
i2c_write(uint8_t byte)
{
	for (int bit = 7; bit >= 0; bit--) {
		i2c_bit((byte >> bit) & 1);
	}
	return !i2c_bit(true);
}

static uint8_t
i2c_read(bool more)
{
	uint8_t byte = 0;

	for (int bit = 7; bit >= 0; bit--) {
		byte = (uint8_t)(byte << 1 | i2c_bit(true));
	}
	i2c_bit(!more);                 /* acknowledge all but the last byte */
	return byte;
}

/*
 * The two pins taken from the serial engine for one transaction, and given back as found. False
 * if the bus is not at rest: then nothing is driven.
 */
static uint32_t taken_cfg[2], taken_io[2];

static bool
bus_take(void)
{
	taken_cfg[0] = rd(GPIO_CFG(PIN_SDA));
	taken_cfg[1] = rd(GPIO_CFG(PIN_SCL));
	taken_io[0] = rd(GPIO_IO(PIN_SDA));
	taken_io[1] = rd(GPIO_IO(PIN_SCL));
	line(PIN_SDA, true);
	line(PIN_SCL, true);
	half_bit();
	if (!level(PIN_SDA) || !level(PIN_SCL)) {
		wr(GPIO_IO(PIN_SDA), taken_io[0] & 2);
		wr(GPIO_IO(PIN_SCL), taken_io[1] & 2);
		wr(GPIO_CFG(PIN_SDA), taken_cfg[0]);
		wr(GPIO_CFG(PIN_SCL), taken_cfg[1]);
		return false;
	}
	return true;
}

static void
bus_give_back(void)
{
	wr(GPIO_IO(PIN_SDA), taken_io[0] & 2);
	wr(GPIO_IO(PIN_SCL), taken_io[1] & 2);
	wr(GPIO_CFG(PIN_SDA), taken_cfg[0]);
	wr(GPIO_CFG(PIN_SCL), taken_cfg[1]);
}

/* A 16-bit register of an Awinic amplifier, most significant byte first. Returns false if nobody answers. */
static bool
register_read(uint8_t address, uint8_t reg, uint16_t *value)
{
	bool answered;

	if (!bus_take()) {
		say("speaker: the I2C bus is not at rest (gpio%u reads %u, gpio%u reads %u): not touched\n", PIN_SDA,
		    level(PIN_SDA), PIN_SCL, level(PIN_SCL));
		return false;
	}
	i2c_start();
	answered = i2c_write((uint8_t)(address << 1)) && i2c_write(reg);
	if (answered) {
		i2c_start();
		answered = i2c_write((uint8_t)(address << 1 | 1));
	}
	if (answered) {
		*value = (uint16_t)(i2c_read(true) << 8);
		*value |= i2c_read(false);
	}
	i2c_stop();
	bus_give_back();
	return answered;
}

static bool
register_write(uint8_t address, uint8_t reg, uint16_t value)
{
	bool answered;

	if (!bus_take()) {
		say("speaker: the I2C bus is not at rest (gpio%u reads %u, gpio%u reads %u): not touched\n", PIN_SDA,
		    level(PIN_SDA), PIN_SCL, level(PIN_SCL));
		return false;
	}
	i2c_start();
	answered = i2c_write((uint8_t)(address << 1)) && i2c_write(reg) && i2c_write((uint8_t)(value >> 8)) &&
	    i2c_write((uint8_t)value);
	i2c_stop();
	bus_give_back();
	return answered;
}

static const char *
amplifier_name(uint16_t id)
{
	switch (id) {
	case 0x1852: return "AW88194/AW88195";
	case 0x2013: return "AW88264";
	case 0x2032: return "AW88266";
	case 0x2049: return "AW88395";
	case 0x2055: return "AW88256";
	case 0x2066: return "AW88166";
	case 0x2071: return "AW88350";
	case 0x2113: return "AW88261";
	case 0x2183: return "AW88399";
	case 0x2308: return "AW88230";
	}
	return "an amplifier this list does not know";
}

/* ---- the amplifiers, as Android's driver runs them -------------------------------------------------- */

#define AW_ID                   0x00            /* reads the chip ID; 0x55aa written resets the chip */
#define AW_ID_AW88261           0x2113
#define AW_SOFT_RESET           0x55aa
#define AW_SYSST                0x01
#define AW_SYSINT               0x02            /* read: cleared */
#define AW_SYSINTM              0x03
#define AW_SYSCTRL              0x04
#define AW_SYSCTRL2             0x05            /* [9:0] the volume, attenuation: [9:6] 6 dB steps, [5:0] eighths of a dB */
#define AW_I2SCTRL3             0x08
#define AW_VBAT                 0x21            /* [9:0] the battery's voltage as the amplifier sees it: x 6025 / 1023 mV */
#define AW_TEMP                 0x22            /* [9:0] the amplifier's temperature, degrees Celsius, two's complement */
#define AW_PVDD                 0x23            /* [9:0] its boosted supply */
#define AW_ISNDAT               0x24            /* the current and voltage sense, as last measured */
#define AW_VSNDAT               0x25
#define AW_DBGCTRL              0x14
#define AW_VSNTM1               0x50
#define AW_EFRH4                0x78
#define AW_EFRH3                0x79
#define AW_EFRL4                0x7c
#define AW_EFRL3                0x7d

#define SYSCTRL_PWDN            (1u << 0)
#define SYSCTRL_AMPPD           (1u << 1)
#define SYSCTRL_HMUTE           (1u << 8)
#define SYSCTRL_ULS_HMUTE       (1u << 14)
#define I2SCTRL3_TXEN           (1u << 6)
#define DBGCTRL_EF_OR           (1u << 3)       /* the fuses' two copies are or-ed; else and-ed */
#define SYSINTM_DEFAULT         0xffff

#define SYSST_PLLS              (1u << 0)
#define SYSST_OTHS              (1u << 1)
#define SYSST_OCDS              (1u << 3)
#define SYSST_CLKS              (1u << 4)
#define SYSST_NOCLKS            (1u << 5)
#define SYSST_WDS               (1u << 6)
#define SYSST_SWS               (1u << 8)
#define SYSST_BSTS              (1u << 9)
#define SYSST_BSTOCS            (1u << 11)
#define SYSST_UVLS              (1u << 14)
#define SYSST_OVP2S             (1u << 15)
#define SYSST_PLL_CHECK         (SYSST_CLKS | SYSST_PLLS)
#define SYSST_CHECK             (SYSST_BSTS | SYSST_SWS | SYSST_CLKS | SYSST_PLLS)
#define SYSST_FAULTS            (SYSST_OVP2S | SYSST_UVLS | SYSST_BSTOCS | SYSST_WDS | SYSST_NOCLKS | SYSST_OCDS | SYSST_OTHS)

#define VOLUME_LOWEST           (90 * 8)        /* the driver's "mute volume", in eighths of a dB */
#define VOLUME_STEP             (6 * 8)
#define STATUS_TRIES            10              /* the driver's AW_DEV_SYSST_CHECK_MAX, 2 ms apart */

/* Android's configuration file ("ACF", Awinic's format; Linux: sound/soc/codecs/aw88395/aw88395_lib.c) */
#define ACF_PROFILE_MUSIC       0
#define ACF_DATA_REGISTERS      4               /* a block with a header of its own and registers in it */
#define ACF_DATA_MONITOR        10              /* the driver's "monitor": what to do when the chip is cold or the battery low */
#define MONITOR_ROWS            8
#define ACF_BLOCK_HEADER        0x3c

struct amplifier {
	uint8_t address;
	unsigned device;                /* the file's device number for it (Android's sound-channel) */
	const char *where;
	uint16_t profile[64][2];        /* register, value */
	unsigned count;
	uint16_t sysctrl;               /* what the profile has for 0x04, 0x08 and 0x05 */
	uint16_t i2sctrl3;
	uint16_t volume_at;             /* Android's level: from the profile's 0x05, in eighths of a dB of attenuation */
	uint16_t volume;                /* where it is now */
	uint16_t volume_high;           /* the profile's bits 15:10 of 0x05, which the volume leaves as they are */
	bool prepared, started;
	/* the monitor's tables (from the file) and what was last seen */
	struct { int16_t min, max; uint16_t less; } temp_rows[MONITOR_ROWS], vbat_rows[MONITOR_ROWS];
	unsigned temp_count, vbat_count, looks;
	int temps[3], vbats[3];
	int temp_row, vbat_row;
};

static struct amplifier amplifiers[2] = {
	{ .address = 0x35, .device = 0, .where = "0x35, slot 0", .temp_row = -1, .vbat_row = -1 },
	{ .address = 0x34, .device = 1, .where = "0x34, slot 1", .temp_row = -1, .vbat_row = -1 },
};
static bool broken;                     /* something went wrong: both have been powered down, nothing more is done */

static uint32_t
le32(const uint8_t *p)
{
	return (uint32_t)p[0] | (uint32_t)p[1] << 8 | (uint32_t)p[2] << 16 | (uint32_t)p[3] << 24;
}

/*
 * The driver's monitor for one amplifier (Android has it on: aw_dev_N_monitor), from the file: every second it
 * reads the chip's temperature and the battery's voltage, and a table says what to do for each range of them.
 * This file's: at 7 to 100 degrees nothing; at 2 to 5 degrees 3 dB less, at -2 to 0 4.5 dB, at -50 to -5 8 dB (and
 * a lower current limit for the boost, which is not done here); from 3.85 V nothing, at 3.65 to 3.75 V and up to
 * 3.55 V a lower "vmax" for the DSP's algorithm, which does not run here. In its temperature rows a vmax goes with
 * each reduction of the volume, so the battery rows' vmax is turned into a volume reduction in the same proportion
 * (the first temperature row's: 3 dB for its vmax): 1.6 and 3.1 dB. Between the ranges the last one holds.
 *   block: checksum (of the bytes after it), version, chip name[16], ui version, the time and count of looks,
 *   switches, then for the temperatures and for the voltages each: a value, the number of rows, a row's size and
 *   the rows' offset; a row: int16 lowest, int16 highest, uint16 boost current, uint16 reduction (eighths of a
 *   dB), int32 vmax
 */
static void
acf_monitor(uint16_t device, const uint8_t *block, uint32_t length)
{
	struct amplifier *a = NULL;
	uint32_t sum = 0, temp_count, temp_size, temp_at, vbat_count, vbat_size, vbat_at;
	int64_t per_eighth = 0;

	for (unsigned i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
		if (amplifiers[i].device == device) {
			a = &amplifiers[i];
		}
	}
	if (a == NULL || length < 0x48) {
		return;
	}
	for (uint32_t i = 4; i < length; i++) {
		sum += block[i];
	}
	temp_count = le32(block + 0x2c);
	temp_size = le32(block + 0x30);
	temp_at = le32(block + 0x34);
	vbat_count = le32(block + 0x3c);
	vbat_size = le32(block + 0x40);
	vbat_at = le32(block + 0x44);
	if (sum != le32(block) || temp_size < 12 || vbat_size < 12 || temp_count > MONITOR_ROWS || vbat_count > MONITOR_ROWS ||
	    temp_at + temp_count * temp_size > length || vbat_at + vbat_count * vbat_size > length) {
		say("speaker: device %u's monitor table is not of the shape known: not used\n", device);
		return;
	}
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < temp_count; i++) {
		const uint8_t *row = block + temp_at + i * temp_size;
		int32_t vmax = (int32_t)le32(row + 8);

		a->temp_rows[i].min = (int16_t)(row[0] | row[1] << 8);
		a->temp_rows[i].max = (int16_t)(row[2] | row[3] << 8);
		a->temp_rows[i].less = (uint16_t)(row[6] | row[7] << 8);
		if (per_eighth == 0 && a->temp_rows[i].less != 0 && vmax < 0) {
			per_eighth = -(int64_t)vmax / a->temp_rows[i].less;
		}
	}
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < vbat_count; i++) {
		const uint8_t *row = block + vbat_at + i * vbat_size;
		int32_t vmax = (int32_t)le32(row + 8);

		a->vbat_rows[i].min = (int16_t)(row[0] | row[1] << 8);
		a->vbat_rows[i].max = (int16_t)(row[2] | row[3] << 8);
		a->vbat_rows[i].less = (uint16_t)(row[6] | row[7] << 8);
		if (vmax < 0 && per_eighth > 0) {
			a->vbat_rows[i].less += (uint16_t)((-(int64_t)vmax + per_eighth / 2) / per_eighth);
		}
	}
	a->temp_count = temp_count;
	a->vbat_count = vbat_count;
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < temp_count; i++) {
		say("speaker: the amplifier %s's monitor: at %d to %d degrees, %u.%03u dB less\n", a->where, a->temp_rows[i].min,
		    a->temp_rows[i].max, a->temp_rows[i].less / 8, a->temp_rows[i].less % 8 * 125);
	}
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < vbat_count; i++) {
		say("speaker: the amplifier %s's monitor: at %d to %d mV, %u.%03u dB less\n", a->where, a->vbat_rows[i].min,
		    a->vbat_rows[i].max, a->vbat_rows[i].less / 8, a->vbat_rows[i].less % 8 * 125);
	}
}

/* The "Music" profile of every amplifier, from the file; false if the file is not of the shape known. */
static bool
acf_profiles(const uint8_t *acf, uint64_t size)
{
	uint32_t entry_size, entries, at;

	if (size < 0x50 || size > 0x100000) {
		say("speaker: the configuration file is %llu bytes: not one of Awinic's\n", size);
		return false;
	}
	entry_size = le32(acf + 0x34);
	entries = le32(acf + 0x38);
	at = le32(acf + 0x3c);
	if (entries == 0 || entries > 64 || entry_size % entries != 0 || entry_size / entries < 0x30 ||
	    (uint64_t)at + entry_size > size) {
		say("speaker: the configuration file's table (%u entries, %u bytes at %#x) is not of a shape known\n", entries,
		    entry_size, at);
		return false;
	}
	for (uint32_t e = 0; e < entries; e++) {
		const uint8_t *entry = acf + at + e * (entry_size / entries);
		char name[17];
		uint16_t device = (uint16_t)(entry[20] | entry[21] << 8), profile = (uint16_t)(entry[26] | entry[27] << 8);
		uint32_t kind = le32(entry + 28), length = le32(entry + 32), offset = le32(entry + 36);
		uint32_t checksum, sum = 0, data_length, count;
		const uint8_t *block = acf + offset;
		struct amplifier *a = NULL;

		memcpy(name, entry + 4, 16);
		name[16] = 0;
		if (kind == ACF_DATA_MONITOR) {
			acf_monitor(device, acf + offset, (uint64_t)offset + length <= size ? length : 0);
			continue;
		}
		if (kind != ACF_DATA_REGISTERS || profile != ACF_PROFILE_MUSIC || strcmp(name, "aw88261") != 0) {
			continue;
		}
		for (unsigned i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
			if (amplifiers[i].device == device) {
				a = &amplifiers[i];
			}
		}
		if (a == NULL || (uint64_t)offset + length > size || length < ACF_BLOCK_HEADER + 4) {
			say("speaker: the configuration file's entry %u (device %u) does not fit\n", e, device);
			return false;
		}
		checksum = le32(block);
		data_length = le32(block + 0x10);
		count = le32(block + ACF_BLOCK_HEADER);
		if (ACF_BLOCK_HEADER + data_length > length || data_length != 4 + 4 * count || count > 64 ||
		    le32(block + 0x20) != 2 || le32(block + 0x24) != 2) {
			say("speaker: device %u's Music profile is not a list of 16-bit registers (%u bytes, %u registers)\n", device,
			    data_length, count);
			return false;
		}
		for (uint32_t i = 4; i < ACF_BLOCK_HEADER + data_length; i++) {
			sum += block[i];
		}
		if (sum != checksum) {
			say("speaker: device %u's Music profile does not add up (%#x, the file says %#x)\n", device, sum, checksum);
			return false;
		}
		a->count = count;
		for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
			const uint8_t *pair = block + ACF_BLOCK_HEADER + 4 + 4 * i;

			a->profile[i][0] = (uint16_t)(pair[0] | pair[1] << 8);
			a->profile[i][1] = (uint16_t)(pair[2] | pair[3] << 8);
		}
	}
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
		struct amplifier *a = &amplifiers[i];
		bool have[3] = { false, false, false };

		for (unsigned r = 0; r < a->count; r++) {
			uint16_t reg = a->profile[r][0], value = a->profile[r][1];

			if (reg == AW_SYSCTRL) {
				a->sysctrl = value;
				have[0] = true;
			} else if (reg == AW_I2SCTRL3) {
				a->i2sctrl3 = value;
				have[1] = true;
			} else if (reg == AW_SYSCTRL2) {
				/* the driver's aw_pid_2113_reg_val_to_db() */
				a->volume_at = (uint16_t)(((value & 0x3ff) >> 6) * VOLUME_STEP + (value & 0x3f));
				a->volume_high = value & 0xfc00;
				have[2] = true;
			} else if (reg == AW_ID || reg >= 0x70) {
				say("speaker: device %u's Music profile writes register %#x, which is not one of the configuration's\n",
				    a->device, reg);
				return false;
			}
		}
		if (a->count == 0 || !have[0] || !have[1] || !have[2] || a->volume_at >= VOLUME_LOWEST) {
			say("speaker: no usable Music profile for device %u (the amplifier at %#x) in the configuration file\n",
			    a->device, a->address);
			return false;
		}
		say("speaker: the amplifier %s: Music profile of %u registers; Android's volume there is -%u.%03u dB (%#x)\n", a->where,
		    a->count, a->volume_at / 8, a->volume_at % 8 * 125, a->volume_at);
	}
	return true;
}

/* Both powered down at once, without the driver's ceremony: a fault, or a value that did not stick. */
static void
power_down_now(const char *why)
{
	broken = true;
	say("speaker: %s: BOTH AMPLIFIERS ARE POWERED DOWN AT ONCE (0x04: amplifier power-down and power-down set)\n", why);
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
		struct amplifier *a = &amplifiers[i];
		uint16_t value = 0, after = 0;

		if (!a->prepared && !a->started) {
			continue;
		}
		if (!register_read(a->address, AW_SYSCTRL, &value)) {
			value = a->sysctrl;
		}
		value |= SYSCTRL_PWDN | SYSCTRL_AMPPD | SYSCTRL_HMUTE;
		if (!register_write(a->address, AW_SYSCTRL, value) || !register_read(a->address, AW_SYSCTRL, &after)) {
			say("speaker: the amplifier %s: 0x04 <- %#06x NOT ACKNOWLEDGED\n", a->where, value);
		} else {
			say("speaker: the amplifier %s: 0x04 <- %#06x, reads %#06x\n", a->where, value, after);
		}
		a->started = false;
	}
}

/* One register written, said and read back; false (and both powered down) if it did not stick. */
static bool
put(struct amplifier *a, uint8_t reg, uint16_t value)
{
	uint16_t after = 0;

	if (broken) {
		return false;
	}
	if (!register_write(a->address, reg, value)) {
		say("speaker: the amplifier %s: %#04x <- %#06x NOT ACKNOWLEDGED\n", a->where, reg, value);
		power_down_now("a write was not acknowledged");
		return false;
	}
	if (!register_read(a->address, reg, &after)) {
		say("speaker: the amplifier %s: %#04x <- %#06x, NOT READ BACK\n", a->where, reg, value);
		power_down_now("a register could not be read back");
		return false;
	}
	say("speaker: the amplifier %s: %#04x <- %#06x, reads %#06x%s\n", a->where, reg, value, after, after == value ? "" :
	    ": NOT AS WRITTEN");
	if (after != value) {
		power_down_now("a register did not read back as written");
		return false;
	}
	return true;
}

static bool
get(struct amplifier *a, uint8_t reg, uint16_t *value)
{
	if (!register_read(a->address, reg, value)) {
		say("speaker: the amplifier %s: %#04x NOT READ\n", a->where, reg);
		return false;
	}
	return true;
}

/* The bits of 0x04 named in `bits' set or cleared, the rest as they read. */
static bool
sysctrl(struct amplifier *a, uint16_t bits, bool set)
{
	uint16_t value;

	if (broken || !get(a, AW_SYSCTRL, &value)) {
		return false;
	}
	return put(a, AW_SYSCTRL, set ? (value | bits) : (value & ~bits));
}

/* The volume register at `volume' eighths of a dB of attenuation (the driver's aw_pid_2113_set_volume()). */
static bool
set_volume(struct amplifier *a, uint16_t volume)
{
	uint16_t value;

	if (volume > VOLUME_LOWEST) {
		volume = VOLUME_LOWEST;
	}
	if (volume < a->volume_at) {
		volume = a->volume_at;  /* never louder than Android */
	}
	/* (the other bits as the profile has them and as they were written: not read first, for a quick fade) */
	value = (uint16_t)(a->volume_high | (volume / VOLUME_STEP) << 6 | volume % VOLUME_STEP);
	if (broken || !put(a, AW_SYSCTRL2, value)) {
		return false;
	}
	a->volume = volume;
	return true;
}

/* What the status register says, and whether it says a fault. */
static bool
faulty(struct amplifier *a, uint16_t *status)
{
	if (!get(a, AW_SYSST, status)) {
		return true;
	}
	return (*status & SYSST_FAULTS) != 0;
}

bool
redwood_speaker_prepare(const uint8_t *acf, uint64_t size)
{
	if (tlmm == 0) {
		tlmm = ml_io_map(TLMM_PHYS, TLMM_SIZE);
	}
	broken = false;
	say("speaker: the amplifiers are prepared as Android's driver prepares them; the I2C pins as found:\n");
	show_pins();
	if (!acf_profiles(acf, size)) {
		return false;
	}
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
		struct amplifier *a = &amplifiers[i];
		uint16_t id = 0, h4 = 0, h3 = 0, l4 = 0, l3 = 0, icalk_bits, vcalk_bits;
		int icalk, vcalk;
		uint16_t vcalb, ef_or = 0;

		if (!get(a, AW_ID, &id)) {
			say("speaker: nobody at I2C address %#x: not powered, or not there\n", a->address);
			power_down_now("an amplifier does not answer");
			return false;
		}
		say("speaker: the amplifier %s: chip ID %#06x, %s\n", a->where, id, amplifier_name(id));
		if (id != AW_ID_AW88261) {
			return false;
		}
		if (!get(a, AW_EFRH4, &h4) || !get(a, AW_EFRH3, &h3) || !get(a, AW_EFRL4, &l4) || !get(a, AW_EFRL3, &l3)) {
			return false;
		}
		for (unsigned r = 0; r < a->count; r++) {
			if (a->profile[r][0] == AW_DBGCTRL) {
				ef_or = a->profile[r][1] & DBGCTRL_EF_OR;
			}
		}
		/* the driver's aw_dev_get_icalk(), aw_dev_get_vcalk() and aw_dev_set_vcalb() */
		icalk_bits = ef_or ? ((h4 & 0x3ff) | (l4 & 0x3ff)) : ((h4 & 0x3ff) & (l4 & 0x3ff));
		vcalk_bits = ef_or ? ((h3 & 0x3ff) | (l3 & 0x3ff)) : ((h3 & 0x3ff) & (l3 & 0x3ff));
		icalk = 1000 + ((icalk_bits & 0x200) ? (int)icalk_bits - 0x400 : (int)icalk_bits);
		vcalk = 1000 + ((vcalk_bits & 0x200) ? (int)vcalk_bits - 0x400 : (int)vcalk_bits);
		if (vcalk <= 0 || icalk <= 0) {
			say("speaker: the amplifier %s: fuses %#x %#x %#x %#x make no sense\n", a->where, h4, h3, l4, l3);
			return false;
		}
		vcalb = (uint16_t)(8192 * icalk / vcalk);
		say("speaker: the amplifier %s: fuses %#06x %#06x %#06x %#06x: icalk %d, vcalk %d, so 0x50 is to be %#06x\n", a->where,
		    h4, h3, l4, l3, icalk, vcalk, vcalb);

		say("speaker: the amplifier %s: soft reset (0x00 <- 0x55aa), as the driver does it first\n", a->where);
		a->prepared = true;
		if (!register_write(a->address, AW_ID, AW_SOFT_RESET)) {
			power_down_now("the soft reset was not acknowledged");
			return false;
		}
		wait_ms(2);
		for (unsigned r = 0; r < a->count; r++) {
			uint8_t reg = (uint8_t)a->profile[r][0];
			uint16_t value = a->profile[r][1], now;

			switch (reg) {
			case AW_SYSINTM:
				value = SYSINTM_DEFAULT;
				break;
			case AW_SYSCTRL:
				/* the three power and mute bits stay as they are; the power stage's mute on */
				if (!get(a, AW_SYSCTRL, &now)) {
					power_down_now("0x04 could not be read");
					return false;
				}
				value = (uint16_t)((value & ~(SYSCTRL_PWDN | SYSCTRL_AMPPD | SYSCTRL_HMUTE)) |
				    (now & (SYSCTRL_PWDN | SYSCTRL_AMPPD | SYSCTRL_HMUTE)) | SYSCTRL_ULS_HMUTE);
				break;
			case AW_I2SCTRL3:
				value &= (uint16_t)~I2SCTRL3_TXEN;
				break;
			case AW_VSNTM1:
				continue;
			}
			if (!put(a, reg, value)) {
				return false;
			}
		}
		if (!put(a, AW_VSNTM1, vcalb) || !set_volume(a, VOLUME_LOWEST)) {
			return false;
		}
	}
	say("speaker: BOTH AMPLIFIERS ARE CONFIGURED as Android's Music profile has them: powered down, muted, at the lowest volume\n");
	return true;
}

bool
redwood_speaker_start(void)
{
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
		struct amplifier *a = &amplifiers[i];
		uint16_t status = 0, interrupts = 0;
		unsigned tries;

		if (broken || !a->prepared) {
			return false;
		}
		say("speaker: the amplifier %s: power-down off\n", a->where);
		a->started = true;
		if (!sysctrl(a, SYSCTRL_PWDN, false)) {
			return false;
		}
		wait_ms(2);
		for (tries = 0; tries < STATUS_TRIES; tries++) {
			if (!get(a, AW_SYSST, &status)) {
				power_down_now("the status could not be read");
				return false;
			}
			if ((status & SYSST_PLL_CHECK) == SYSST_PLL_CHECK) {
				break;
			}
			wait_ms(2);
		}
		say("speaker: the amplifier %s: status %#06x: its PLL %s\n", a->where, status, tries < STATUS_TRIES ?
		    "IS LOCKED to the bit clock" : "DOES NOT LOCK: no clock?");
		if (tries == STATUS_TRIES) {
			power_down_now("an amplifier's PLL does not lock");
			return false;
		}
		say("speaker: the amplifier %s: amplifier power-down off\n", a->where);
		if (!sysctrl(a, SYSCTRL_AMPPD, false)) {
			return false;
		}
		wait_ms(1);
		for (tries = 0; tries < STATUS_TRIES; tries++) {
			if (faulty(a, &status)) {
				break;
			}
			if ((status & SYSST_CHECK) == SYSST_CHECK) {
				break;
			}
			wait_ms(2);
		}
		say("speaker: the amplifier %s: status %#06x\n", a->where, status);
		if ((status & SYSST_FAULTS) != 0 || (status & SYSST_CHECK) != SYSST_CHECK) {
			power_down_now((status & SYSST_FAULTS) ? "an amplifier reports a fault" : "an amplifier's status is not as "
			    "the driver wants it");
			return false;
		}
		if (!put(a, AW_I2SCTRL3, a->i2sctrl3) ||        /* the feedback on, as the profile has it */
		    !sysctrl(a, SYSCTRL_ULS_HMUTE, false) || !sysctrl(a, SYSCTRL_HMUTE, false)) {
			return false;
		}
		if (!get(a, AW_SYSINT, &interrupts) || !get(a, AW_SYSINT, &interrupts) || !put(a, AW_SYSINTM, SYSINTM_DEFAULT)) {
			power_down_now("the interrupts could not be read");
			return false;
		}
		if (faulty(a, &status)) {
			say("speaker: the amplifier %s: status %#06x\n", a->where, status);
			power_down_now("an amplifier reports a fault");
			return false;
		}
		say("speaker: THE AMPLIFIER %s RUNS, unmuted at the lowest volume (status %#06x)\n", a->where, status);
	}
	return true;
}

bool
redwood_speaker_volume(uint32_t below, uint32_t step_ms)
{
	uint16_t status;

	for (unsigned i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
		struct amplifier *a = &amplifiers[i];
		uint32_t target = a->volume_at + below;

		if (broken || !a->started) {
			return false;
		}
		if (target > VOLUME_LOWEST) {
			target = VOLUME_LOWEST;
		}
		say("speaker: the amplifier %s: the volume to -%u.%03u dB (Android's level less %u.%03u dB), 6 dB a step every %u ms\n",
		    a->where, target / 8, target % 8 * 125, (target - a->volume_at) / 8, (target - a->volume_at) % 8 * 125, step_ms);
	}
	/* both together, a step every step_ms, the status looked at after every step */
	for (;;) {
		bool moved = false;

		for (unsigned i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
			struct amplifier *a = &amplifiers[i];
			uint32_t target = a->volume_at + below, next;

			if (target > VOLUME_LOWEST) {
				target = VOLUME_LOWEST;
			}
			if (a->volume == target) {
				continue;
			}
			next = a->volume > target ? (a->volume - target > VOLUME_STEP ? a->volume - VOLUME_STEP : target) :
			    (target - a->volume > VOLUME_STEP ? a->volume + VOLUME_STEP : target);
			if (!set_volume(a, (uint16_t)next)) {
				return false;
			}
			/* (a slow fade looks at the status after every step, a quick one once it is over) */
			if (step_ms >= 10 && faulty(a, &status)) {
				say("speaker: the amplifier %s: status %#06x\n", a->where, status);
				power_down_now("an amplifier reports a fault");
				return false;
			}
			moved = true;
		}
		if (!moved) {
			break;
		}
		if (step_ms) {
			wait_ms(step_ms);
		}
	}
	return redwood_speaker_healthy();
}

bool
redwood_speaker_healthy(void)
{
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
		struct amplifier *a = &amplifiers[i];
		uint16_t status;

		if (broken) {
			return false;
		}
		if (!a->started) {
			continue;
		}
		if (faulty(a, &status)) {
			say("speaker: the amplifier %s: status %#06x\n", a->where, status);
			power_down_now("an amplifier reports a fault");
			return false;
		}
	}
	return true;
}

/* the row of a monitor table that a value falls in; between rows, the one before */
static int
monitor_row(const struct amplifier *a, bool temperature, int value, int before)
{
	unsigned count = temperature ? a->temp_count : a->vbat_count;

	for (unsigned i = 0; i < count; i++) {
		int min = temperature ? a->temp_rows[i].min : a->vbat_rows[i].min;
		int max = temperature ? a->temp_rows[i].max : a->vbat_rows[i].max;

		if (value >= min && value <= max) {
			return (int)i;
		}
	}
	return before;
}

/*
 * The driver's monitor, once: the temperature and the battery voltage of every amplifier that runs (the average of
 * the last three looks, as the file's count says), and the reduction their tables ask for, the larger of the two
 * amplifiers'. With `tell', what was read (also the boosted supply and the current and voltage sense, raw).
 */
uint32_t
redwood_speaker_monitor(bool tell)
{
	uint32_t wanted = 0;

	for (unsigned i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
		struct amplifier *a = &amplifiers[i];
		uint16_t vbat = 0, temp = 0, pvdd = 0, isn = 0, vsn = 0;
		int t = 0, v = 0;
		uint32_t less = 0;

		if (broken || !a->started) {
			continue;
		}
		if (!get(a, AW_VBAT, &vbat) || !get(a, AW_TEMP, &temp)) {
			continue;
		}
		a->temps[a->looks % 3] = (temp & 0x200) ? (int)(temp & 0x3ff) - 0x400 : (int)(temp & 0x3ff);
		a->vbats[a->looks % 3] = (int)(vbat & 0x3ff) * 6025 / 1023;
		a->looks++;
		for (unsigned k = 0; k < 3 && k < a->looks; k++) {
			t += a->temps[k];
			v += a->vbats[k];
		}
		t /= (int)(a->looks < 3 ? a->looks : 3);
		v /= (int)(a->looks < 3 ? a->looks : 3);
		a->temp_row = monitor_row(a, true, t, a->temp_row);
		a->vbat_row = monitor_row(a, false, v, a->vbat_row);
		less = (a->temp_row >= 0 ? a->temp_rows[a->temp_row].less : 0) + (a->vbat_row >= 0 ? a->vbat_rows[a->vbat_row].less : 0);
		if (less > wanted) {
			wanted = less;
		}
		if (tell) {
			(void)get(a, AW_PVDD, &pvdd);
			(void)get(a, AW_ISNDAT, &isn);
			(void)get(a, AW_VSNDAT, &vsn);
			say("speaker: the amplifier %s: %d degrees, the battery %d mV (%#05x, %#05x; supply %#05x, sense %#06x %#06x): "
			    "%u.%03u dB less\n", a->where, t, v, temp, vbat, pvdd, isn, vsn, less / 8, less % 8 * 125);
		}
	}
	return wanted;
}

void
redwood_speaker_stop(void)
{
	if (broken) {
		return;                 /* (already powered down) */
	}
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
		struct amplifier *a = &amplifiers[i];

		if (!a->started) {
			continue;
		}
		say("speaker: the amplifier %s is stopped as Android's driver stops it\n", a->where);
		if (!sysctrl(a, SYSCTRL_ULS_HMUTE, true)) {
			return;
		}
		while (a->volume < VOLUME_LOWEST) {
			if (!set_volume(a, (uint16_t)(a->volume + VOLUME_STEP > VOLUME_LOWEST ? VOLUME_LOWEST : a->volume +
			    VOLUME_STEP))) {
				return;
			}
			wait_ms(1);
		}
		if (!sysctrl(a, SYSCTRL_HMUTE, true) || !put(a, AW_I2SCTRL3, (uint16_t)(a->i2sctrl3 & ~I2SCTRL3_TXEN))) {
			return;
		}
		wait_ms(1);
		if (!sysctrl(a, SYSCTRL_AMPPD, true) || !sysctrl(a, SYSCTRL_PWDN, true)) {
			return;
		}
		a->started = false;
		say("speaker: THE AMPLIFIER %s IS POWERED DOWN\n", a->where);
	}
}

void
redwood_speaker_quiesce(void)
{
	bool any = false;

	for (unsigned i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
		any |= amplifiers[i].started;
	}
	if (!any || tlmm == 0) {
		return;
	}
	leaving = true;
	power_down_now("the kernel is on its way out");
}

/* ---- speaker_probe=N: a look ------------------------------------------------------------------------ */

static void
show_amplifiers(void)
{
	/* the chip ID, then registers that every chip of the family has at the same place and that reading does not change */
	static const struct {
		uint8_t reg;
		const char *name;
	} more[] = { { 0x01, "status" }, { 0x04, "system control" }, { 0x06, "I2S control" } };

	for (unsigned i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
		uint16_t id = 0, value = 0;

		if (!register_read(amplifiers[i].address, AW_ID, &id)) {
			say("speaker: nobody at I2C address %#x: not powered, or not there\n", amplifiers[i].address);
			continue;
		}
		say("speaker: the amplifier %s is there: chip ID %#06x, %s\n", amplifiers[i].where, id, amplifier_name(id));
		for (unsigned r = 0; r < sizeof(more) / sizeof(more[0]); r++) {
			if (register_read(amplifiers[i].address, more[r].reg, &value)) {
				say("speaker:   register %#04x (%s) = %#06x\n", more[r].reg, more[r].name, value);
			}
		}
	}
}

/* ---- power names of the audio subsystem ------------------------------------------------------------- */

#define CMD_DB_PHYS             0x80860000UL
#define CMD_DB_SIZE             0x20000UL
#define GCC_PHYS                0x00100000UL
#define GCC_SIZE                0x60000UL

struct cmd_db_slave {
	uint16_t id, header_offset, data_offset, count, version, reserved[3];
};
struct cmd_db_header {
	uint32_t version;
	uint8_t magic[4];
	struct cmd_db_slave slave[8];
	uint32_t checksum, reserved;
	uint8_t data[];
};
struct cmd_db_entry {
	char id[8];
	uint32_t priority[2];
	uint32_t address;
	uint16_t length, offset;
};

/* The RPMh address of a resource by its name in the command database the boot loader left; 0 = none. */
static uint32_t
rpmh_address(const char *name)
{
	const struct cmd_db_header *db = (const struct cmd_db_header *)cmd_db;
	char id[8] = { 0 };

	if (db->magic[0] != 0xdb || db->magic[1] != 0x30 || db->magic[2] != 0x03 || db->magic[3] != 0x0c) {
		return 0;
	}
	strlcpy(id, name, sizeof(id));
	for (unsigned s = 0; s < 8; s++) {
		const struct cmd_db_slave *slave = &db->slave[s];
		const struct cmd_db_entry *entry = (const struct cmd_db_entry *)(db->data + slave->header_offset);

		if (slave->id == 0 || slave->header_offset >= CMD_DB_SIZE - 0x1000 || slave->count > 512) {
			continue;
		}
		for (unsigned i = 0; i < slave->count; i++) {
			if (memcmp(entry[i].id, id, sizeof(id)) == 0) {
				return entry[i].address;
			}
		}
	}
	return 0;
}

static void
show_power(void)
{
	/* the subsystem's two supplies and, for the DSP, the processor's own two and the crystal */
	static const char *const supplies[] = { "lcx.lvl", "lmx.lvl", "cx.lvl", "mx.lvl", "xo.lvl" };

	for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof(supplies) / sizeof(supplies[0]); i++) {
		uint32_t address = rpmh_address(supplies[i]);

		if (address) {
			say("speaker: supply \"%s\" can be asked for at RPMh address %#x\n", supplies[i], address);
		} else {
			say("speaker: no supply \"%s\" in the command database\n", supplies[i]);
		}
	}
	/*
	 * (The audio subsystem's bus clock, GCC_CFG_NOC_LPASS_CBCR, is not read: on the phone that read
	 * stops the kernel with a synchronous external abort -- the register is not the main processors'
	 * to read while the audio subsystem belongs to its DSP.)
	 */
}

static void
probe_thread(__unused void *parameter, __unused wait_result_t result)
{
	if (tlmm == 0) {
		tlmm = ml_io_map(TLMM_PHYS, TLMM_SIZE);
	}
	gcc = ml_io_map(GCC_PHYS, GCC_SIZE);
	cmd_db = ml_io_map_wcomb(CMD_DB_PHYS, CMD_DB_SIZE);      /* memory, not registers: no alignment rules */
	say("speaker: a look at the phone's sound hardware (level %u; nothing is switched on)\n", probe_level);
	show_pins();
	show_power();
	if (probe_level >= 2) {
		show_amplifiers();
	}
	say("speaker: done\n");
	thread_terminate(current_thread());
}

void
redwood_speaker_init(void)
{
	thread_t thread;

	if (!PE_parse_boot_argn("speaker_probe", &probe_level, sizeof(probe_level)) || probe_level == 0) {
		return;
	}
	if (kernel_thread_start(probe_thread, NULL, &thread) == KERN_SUCCESS) {
		thread_deallocate(thread);
	}
}
```

`xnu/files/bsd/dev/redwood_sta.c`:

```c
/*
 * Darwin-on-redwood: what stands between the two sides of the station boundary
 * (sys/redwood_sta.h).
 *
 * Whoever wants a network asks from wherever it happens to be: an ioctl of wifid's, the thread
 * that brings the radio up. The station side wants to be called by one thread, one call at a
 * time, and a scan or a join takes seconds. So what is asked for is noted here and done by a
 * thread of this file's; the asker returns at once and hears the outcome as an event. One
 * request of each kind can wait: a second scan asked for while the first has not begun
 * replaces it, as does a second join.
 *
 * What the last scan heard is kept here, so that it can be read without entering the station
 * side, and so is the list of channels.
 *
 * The network the kernel was given in a file is a standing request: joined at the start, and
 * again whenever the radio is turned back on (Settings' switch), until somebody asks for
 * another network -- as iOS itself rejoins the networks it knows. If that other network cannot
 * be joined (a wrong passphrase), the standing one is joined again.
 */
#include <kern/kalloc.h>
#include <kern/locks.h>
#include <kern/sched_prim.h>
#include <kern/thread.h>
#include <libkern/libkern.h>
#include <mach/mach_types.h>
#include <sys/errno.h>
#include <sys/redwood_input.h>
#include <sys/redwood_sta.h>
#include <sys/systm.h>

extern void thread_set_thread_name(thread_t thread, const char *name);

#define HEARD_MOST      128
#define CHANNELS_MOST   96

static LCK_GRP_DECLARE(sta_lock_group, "redwood-sta");
static LCK_MTX_DECLARE(sta_lock, &sta_lock_group);

static const struct redwood_sta_ops *sta_ops;   /* the station side, while there is one */
static bool sta_thread_made;
static bool sta_calls;                          /* the thread is in a call of the station side's */
static unsigned sta_reads;                      /* ... and so many others are in its state() */
static bool sta_on;                             /* the radio's power, as last asked for */

/* what has been asked for and not begun */
static bool asked_power, asked_power_on, asked_scan, asked_join, asked_leave;
static struct redwood_sta_scan asked_scan_what;
static struct redwood_sta_join asked_join_what;
static struct redwood_sta_join standing;        /* the network joined whenever the radio comes on (ssid_length 0: none) */
static struct redwood_sta_join fallback;        /* ... as it was before a join that has not come through yet */

static struct redwood_sta_bss *heard;           /* by the last scan that came to an end */
static unsigned heard_count;
static struct redwood_sta_channel channels[CHANNELS_MOST];
static unsigned channel_count;

static void
heard_one(const struct redwood_sta_bss *bss, __unused void *context)
{
	/* (only the thread writes the list, and it reads the count without the lock) */
	if (heard_count < HEARD_MOST) {
		lck_mtx_lock(&sta_lock);
		heard[heard_count++] = *bss;
		lck_mtx_unlock(&sta_lock);
	}
}

static void
sta_runs(__unused void *parameter, __unused wait_result_t result)
{
	static struct redwood_sta_scan scan;
	static struct redwood_sta_join join;

	for (;;) {
		const struct redwood_sta_ops *ops;
		bool power = false, power_on = false, leave = false, do_join = false, do_scan = false;
		int error = 0;

		lck_mtx_lock(&sta_lock);
		while (sta_ops == NULL || !(asked_power || asked_leave || asked_join || asked_scan)) {
			lck_mtx_sleep(&sta_lock, LCK_SLEEP_DEFAULT, (event_t)&sta_ops, THREAD_UNINT);
		}
		ops = sta_ops;
		/* one thing at a time, in the order that makes sense when several wait */
		if (asked_power) {
			power = true;
			power_on = asked_power_on;
			asked_power = false;
		} else if (asked_leave) {
			leave = true;
			asked_leave = false;
		} else if (asked_join) {
			do_join = true;
			join = asked_join_what;
			bzero(&asked_join_what, sizeof(asked_join_what));
			asked_join = false;
		} else {
			do_scan = true;
			scan = asked_scan_what;
			asked_scan = false;
		}
		sta_calls = true;
		lck_mtx_unlock(&sta_lock);

		if (power) {
			struct redwood_sta_state *state = kalloc_data(sizeof(*state), Z_WAITOK | Z_ZERO);
			bool was_joined = false;

			if (state != NULL) {
				ops->state(state);
				was_joined = state->phase == REDWOOD_STA_JOINED;
				kfree_data(state, sizeof(*state));
			}
			error = ops->power(power_on);
			if (!power_on && was_joined) {
				redwood_apple80211_event(REDWOOD_STA_LINK, 0);
			}
			redwood_apple80211_event(REDWOOD_STA_POWER, error == 0 ? power_on : !power_on);
			lck_mtx_lock(&sta_lock);
			if (error == 0 && power_on && standing.ssid_length != 0 && !asked_join) {
				asked_join_what = standing;
				asked_join = true;
			}
			lck_mtx_unlock(&sta_lock);
		} else if (leave) {
			ops->leave();
			redwood_apple80211_event(REDWOOD_STA_LINK, 0);
		} else if (do_join) {
			error = ops->join(&join);
			bzero(&join, sizeof(join));
			redwood_apple80211_event(REDWOOD_STA_JOIN_DONE, error);
			if (error == 0) {
				redwood_apple80211_event(REDWOOD_STA_LINK, 1);
			}
			/* a join that did not come through (a wrong passphrase) leaves things as they were: the standing network again */
			lck_mtx_lock(&sta_lock);
			if (error != 0 && fallback.ssid_length != 0 && !asked_join && !asked_leave && !asked_power) {
				standing = asked_join_what = fallback;
				asked_join = true;
			}
			bzero(&fallback, sizeof(fallback));
			lck_mtx_unlock(&sta_lock);
		} else if (do_scan) {
			error = ops->scan(&scan);
			lck_mtx_lock(&sta_lock);
			heard_count = 0;
			lck_mtx_unlock(&sta_lock);
			ops->heard(heard_one, NULL);
			redwood_apple80211_event(REDWOOD_STA_SCAN_DONE, error);
		}

		lck_mtx_lock(&sta_lock);
		sta_calls = false;
		lck_mtx_unlock(&sta_lock);
		thread_wakeup((event_t)&sta_calls);
	}
}

/* ---- the station side ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

void
redwood_sta_attach(const struct redwood_sta_ops *ops)
{
	thread_t thread;

	if (ops == NULL) {
		lck_mtx_lock(&sta_lock);
		sta_ops = NULL;
		asked_power = asked_scan = asked_join = asked_leave = false;
		while (sta_calls || sta_reads != 0) {
			lck_mtx_sleep(&sta_lock, LCK_SLEEP_DEFAULT, (event_t)&sta_calls, THREAD_UNINT);
		}
		heard_count = channel_count = 0;
		lck_mtx_unlock(&sta_lock);
		return;
	}
	if (heard == NULL) {
		heard = kalloc_data(HEARD_MOST * sizeof(*heard), Z_WAITOK | Z_ZERO);
	}
	if (heard == NULL) {
		redwood_wifi_tell("wifi: no memory for what a scan hears: nobody can ask the radio for a network\n");
		return;
	}
	if (!sta_thread_made) {
		if (kernel_thread_start(sta_runs, NULL, &thread) != KERN_SUCCESS) {
			redwood_wifi_tell("wifi: no thread for the station: nobody can ask the radio for a network\n");
			return;
		}
		thread_set_thread_name(thread, "wifi-station");
		thread_deallocate(thread);
		sta_thread_made = true;
	}
	channel_count = ops->channels(channels, CHANNELS_MOST);
	lck_mtx_lock(&sta_lock);
	sta_ops = ops;
	sta_on = true;
	lck_mtx_unlock(&sta_lock);
	thread_wakeup((event_t)&sta_ops);
	redwood_apple80211_event(REDWOOD_STA_POWER, 1);
}

void
redwood_sta_lost(int error)
{
	redwood_apple80211_event(REDWOOD_STA_LINK, error != 0 ? error : ECONNRESET);
}

/* ---- who wants a network ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

bool
redwood_sta_present(void)
{
	return sta_ops != NULL;
}

bool
redwood_sta_powered(void)
{
	return sta_ops != NULL && sta_on;
}

bool
redwood_sta_busy(void)
{
	bool busy;

	lck_mtx_lock(&sta_lock);
	busy = sta_ops != NULL && (sta_calls || asked_power || asked_leave || asked_join || asked_scan);
	lck_mtx_unlock(&sta_lock);
	return busy;
}

int
redwood_sta_ask_power(bool on)
{
	lck_mtx_lock(&sta_lock);
	if (sta_ops == NULL) {
		lck_mtx_unlock(&sta_lock);
		return ENXIO;
	}
	sta_on = on;
	asked_power = true;
	asked_power_on = on;
	if (!on) {
		asked_scan = asked_join = asked_leave = false;
	}
	lck_mtx_unlock(&sta_lock);
	thread_wakeup((event_t)&sta_ops);
	return 0;
}

int
redwood_sta_ask_scan(const struct redwood_sta_scan *what)
{
	lck_mtx_lock(&sta_lock);
	if (sta_ops == NULL || !sta_on) {
		lck_mtx_unlock(&sta_lock);
		return sta_ops == NULL ? ENXIO : ENETDOWN;
	}
	asked_scan_what = *what;
	asked_scan = true;
	lck_mtx_unlock(&sta_lock);
	thread_wakeup((event_t)&sta_ops);
	return 0;
}

int
redwood_sta_ask_join_standing(const struct redwood_sta_join *what)
{
	int error = redwood_sta_ask_join(what);

	lck_mtx_lock(&sta_lock);
	if (error == 0) {
		standing = *what;
	}
	lck_mtx_unlock(&sta_lock);
	return error;
}

int
redwood_sta_ask_join(const struct redwood_sta_join *what)
{
	lck_mtx_lock(&sta_lock);
	if (sta_ops == NULL || !sta_on) {
		lck_mtx_unlock(&sta_lock);
		return sta_ops == NULL ? ENXIO : ENETDOWN;
	}
	if (standing.ssid_length != 0) {
		fallback = standing;
	}
	bzero(&standing, sizeof(standing));     /* (whoever asks for a network now has the say) */
	asked_join_what = *what;
	asked_join = true;
	asked_leave = false;
	lck_mtx_unlock(&sta_lock);
	thread_wakeup((event_t)&sta_ops);
	return 0;
}

int
redwood_sta_ask_leave(void)
{
	lck_mtx_lock(&sta_lock);
	if (sta_ops == NULL) {
		lck_mtx_unlock(&sta_lock);
		return ENXIO;
	}
	asked_leave = true;
	asked_join = false;
	bzero(&asked_join_what, sizeof(asked_join_what));
	bzero(&fallback, sizeof(fallback));
	lck_mtx_unlock(&sta_lock);
	thread_wakeup((event_t)&sta_ops);
	return 0;
}

bool
redwood_sta_heard(unsigned index, struct redwood_sta_bss *bss)
{
	bool there;

	lck_mtx_lock(&sta_lock);
	if ((there = index < heard_count)) {
		*bss = heard[index];
	}
	lck_mtx_unlock(&sta_lock);
	return there;
}

void
redwood_sta_state(struct redwood_sta_state *state)
{
	const struct redwood_sta_ops *ops;

	bzero(state, sizeof(*state));
	lck_mtx_lock(&sta_lock);
	if ((ops = sta_ops) != NULL) {
		sta_reads++;
	}
	lck_mtx_unlock(&sta_lock);
	if (ops != NULL) {
		ops->state(state);
		lck_mtx_lock(&sta_lock);
		sta_reads--;
		lck_mtx_unlock(&sta_lock);
		thread_wakeup((event_t)&sta_calls);
	}
}

unsigned
redwood_sta_channels(struct redwood_sta_channel *out, unsigned most)
{
	unsigned count;

	lck_mtx_lock(&sta_lock);
	count = channel_count < most ? channel_count : most;
	memcpy(out, channels, count * sizeof(*out));
	lck_mtx_unlock(&sta_lock);
	return count;
}

bool
redwood_sta_address(uint8_t *address)
{
	const struct redwood_sta_ops *ops = sta_ops;

	if (ops != NULL) {
		memcpy(address, ops->address, 6);
	}
	return ops != NULL;
}
```

`xnu/files/bsd/dev/redwood_torch.c`:

```c
/*
 * The flashlight of the POCO X5 Pro (redwood): the flash LED module of the PM8350C (SPMI slave 2,
 * registers 0xee00; "qcom,pm8350c-flash-led", four channels), the rear flash LED on its channel 0.
 * Every address and number below belongs to this phone, from Android's own device tree, Xiaomi's
 * driver for it (drivers/leds/leds-qti-flash.c of the phone's kernel, MiCode redwood-s-oss) and
 * what Android does when its own flashlight is switched on (its LED class devices read, nothing
 * written by us):
 *
 *   Android's torch    led:torch_0 at 125 mA through led:switch_0 (channel 0 alone), current
 *                      resolution 12.5 mA ("qcom,ires-ua" 12500): IRESOLUTION bit 0 clear, ITARGET
 *                      code round(125 / 12.5) - 1 = 9; the module enabled (0x46 = 0x80), then the
 *                      channel (0x4e bit 0). Off in the reverse order, ITARGET back to 0. The
 *                      torch has no safety timer (its bit is kept clear, as the driver keeps it)
 *   at Android's probe channel 0's strobe is the software's (0x4a: bits 6:4 and 2 clear) and its
 *                      safety timer off (0x3e bit 7 clear)
 *
 * Writing to a PMIC is not like writing anywhere else: the PMICs make the phone's supplies. So
 * every write goes through one function that takes only this module's registers above (the
 * peripheral the arbiter's channel is checked to be, the registers by a list), every write is
 * read back, and any surprise ends all writing for the run. Transfers through the arbiter are made
 * one at a time with the buttons' driver (redwood_spmi_lock()): two at once, and it drops one.
 *
 * What iOS's flashlight is on this machine: the loader says the camera has a flash (with torch=N,
 * /product/camera "flash": MobileGestalt's camera-flash, Control Center's flashlight button), and
 * libredwood-media.dylib in mediaserverd hands FigFlashlight, which finds no camera here, a device
 * of ours whose torch level is written to /dev/redwood-torch (userland/src/inject_media.c).
 *
 * Nothing here is done unless a boot-arg asks for it:
 *
 *   torch=1    a look, reading only: the arbiter's channel for the module and who may write
 *              through it, the module's type, its registers, the PMIC's temperature alarm
 *   torch=2    ... and the light on once at Android's torch current for torch_secs (default 2),
 *              then off, every write read back
 *   torch=3    ... no light at the start; the light for iOS until the run ends: /dev/redwood-torch
 *              takes a level of 0 to 1000 (a 32-bit number; thousandths of Android's current, 0
 *              off) and the module is set to it -- never above Android's 125 mA; a read gives
 *              what is lit now
 *
 * Limits, whatever asks: Android's current at most; the light on for torch_max_s at a time at most
 * (default 30, never more than 120), after which it stays off until it is asked for anew (0, then
 * more); while it is on, ten times a second, the module's fault and over-temperature flags, the
 * PMIC's temperature alarm and the battery's temperature (at most 45 C; from the audio DSP's battery
 * manager with adsp=1, or the firmware's with battery=1; with neither the other two guard): any of
 * them, a read that fails or a write that does not read back, and the light goes off and stays off
 * for the rest of the run. At the run's end (and on a panic's way out) it goes off.
 *
 * Register layouts: Linux drivers/spmi/spmi-pmic-arb.c (arbiter version 5: a system's write
 * channel for a peripheral is 0x10000 bytes of "chnls" per channel), Xiaomi's leds-qti-flash.c,
 * drivers/thermal/qcom/qcom-spmi-temp-alarm.c.
 */
#include <kern/clock.h>
#include <kern/thread.h>
#include <libkern/libkern.h>
#include <mach/mach_types.h>
#include <machine/machine_routines.h>
#include <miscfs/devfs/devfs.h>
#include <pexpert/pexpert.h>
#include <sys/conf.h>
#include <sys/redwood_audio.h>
#include <sys/redwood_input.h>
#include <sys/systm.h>
#include <sys/uio.h>

extern vm_offset_t ml_io_map(vm_offset_t phys_addr, vm_size_t size);
extern kern_return_t thread_terminate(thread_t thread);
extern void loader_log_putc(char c);

static uint32_t level;
static bool broken, leaving;

static int say(const char *format, ...) __printflike(1, 2);

/* every line to the loader's log as well (and to the console when that may be written) */
static int
say(const char *format, ...)
{
	char line[300];
	va_list list;
	int length;

	va_start(list, format);
	length = vsnprintf(line, sizeof(line), format, list);
	va_end(list);
	for (const char *c = line; *c != 0; c++) {
		loader_log_putc(*c);
	}
	if (!leaving && ml_get_interrupts_enabled()) {
		printf("%s", line);
	}
	return length;
}

/*
 * The events that matter (lit, off, cut, trouble) are also kept, and said again at the run's end:
 * the log of a long run keeps its beginning and its end, and these happen in between.
 */
#define NOTES                   24
static char notes[NOTES][200];
static unsigned noted;

static void note(const char *format, ...) __printflike(1, 2);

static void
note(const char *format, ...)
{
	char *slot = notes[noted++ % NOTES];
	uint64_t ns;
	va_list list;
	int n;

	absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(mach_absolute_time(), &ns);
	n = snprintf(slot, sizeof(notes[0]), "%llu.%03llu s: ", ns / NSEC_PER_SEC, ns / NSEC_PER_MSEC % 1000);
	va_start(list, format);
	vsnprintf(slot + n, sizeof(notes[0]) - (size_t)n, format, list);
	va_end(list);
	say("torch: %s\n", slot);
}

static inline uint32_t
rd(vm_offset_t address)
{
	return *(volatile uint32_t *)address;
}

static inline void
wr(vm_offset_t address, uint32_t value)
{
	*(volatile uint32_t *)address = value;
}

static void
spin_us(uint32_t us)
{
	uint64_t until;

	nanoseconds_to_absolutetime((uint64_t)us * NSEC_PER_USEC, &until);
	until += mach_absolute_time();
	while (mach_absolute_time() < until) {
	}
}

static void
wait_ms(uint32_t ms)
{
	if (leaving) {
		spin_us(ms * 1000);
	} else {
		delay_for_interval(ms, NSEC_PER_MSEC);
	}
}

/* ---- the PMIC arbiter (version 5) ---------------------------------------------------------------- */

#define ARB_CORE_PHYS           0x0c440000UL    /* the version, and which peripheral each channel is */
#define ARB_CORE_SIZE           0x1100UL
#define ARB_CNFG_PHYS           0x0c40a000UL    /* which system may write through each channel */
#define ARB_CNFG_SIZE           0x1000UL
#define ARB_OBSERVER_PHYS       0x0e600000UL    /* reads: 0x80 per channel for our system (the first) */
#define ARB_OBSERVER_SIZE       0x10000UL
#define ARB_CHNLS_PHYS          0x0c600000UL    /* writes: 0x10000 per channel */
#define ARB_SYSTEM              0               /* who we are to the arbiter: the device tree's "qcom,ee" */

#define ARB_VERSION             0x000
#define ARB_VERSION_5           0x50000000u
#define ARB_VERSION_7           0x70000000u
#define ARB_FEATURES            0x004
#define ARB_CHANNEL(n)          (0x900 + 4 * (n))       /* [19:8] slave and peripheral */
#define ARB_OWNER(n)            (0x700 + 4 * (n))       /* [2:0] the system that may write through channel n */
#define ARB_MAX_CHANNELS        512

#define CHANNEL_COMMAND         0x00
#define CHANNEL_STATUS          0x08
#define CHANNEL_WDATA0          0x10
#define OBSERVER_DATA0          0x18
#define OBSERVER_DATA1          0x1c
#define STATUS_DONE             0x1
#define STATUS_FAILURE          0x2
#define STATUS_DENIED           0x4
#define STATUS_DROPPED          0x8
#define COMMAND_WRITE           (0u << 27)      /* "extended register write long"; [11:4] register, [2:0] bytes - 1 */
#define COMMAND_READ            (1u << 27)      /* "extended register read long" */
#define TRANSFER_TIMEOUT_US     2000
#define DROPPED                 "the transfer was dropped"

struct peripheral {
	const char *    name;
	uint16_t        id;             /* slave << 8 | peripheral */
	uint16_t        channel;
	bool            found, writable;
	vm_offset_t     write;          /* its write channel, mapped (only the flash module's) */
};
static struct peripheral flash = { .name = "the PM8350C's flash LED module", .id = 0x2ee };
static struct peripheral alarm = { .name = "the PM8350C's temperature alarm", .id = 0x20a };

static vm_offset_t arb_core, arb_cnfg, arb_observer;
static uint8_t alarm_subtype;

/* (the arbiter one transfer at a time with the buttons' driver; at the run's end the others are stopped, perhaps holding it) */
static void
lock(void)
{
	if (!leaving) {
		redwood_spmi_lock();
	}
}

static void
unlock(void)
{
	if (!leaving) {
		redwood_spmi_unlock();
	}
}

static const char *
wait_done(vm_offset_t channel)
{
	uint64_t start = mach_absolute_time(), interval;
	uint32_t status;

	nanoseconds_to_absolutetime(TRANSFER_TIMEOUT_US * (uint64_t)NSEC_PER_USEC, &interval);
	do {
		status = rd(channel + CHANNEL_STATUS);
	} while (!(status & STATUS_DONE) && mach_absolute_time() - start < interval);
	return !(status & STATUS_DONE) ? "no answer from the arbiter" : (status & STATUS_DENIED) ? "the arbiter refuses" :
	       (status & STATUS_FAILURE) ? "the transfer failed" : (status & STATUS_DROPPED) ? DROPPED : NULL;
}

/*
 * `count' (1 to 8) registers from `reg' on; NULL, or what went wrong. A transfer the arbiter drops
 * now and then (the buttons' driver sees one in a thousand or so, from whatever else is on the bus)
 * is asked for again, twice at most.
 */
static const char *spmi_read_once(const struct peripheral *p, uint8_t reg, uint8_t *bytes, uint32_t count);

static const char *
spmi_read(const struct peripheral *p, uint8_t reg, uint8_t *bytes, uint32_t count)
{
	const char *problem = NULL;

	for (int tries = 0; tries < 3; tries++) {
		if ((problem = spmi_read_once(p, reg, bytes, count)) == NULL || strcmp(problem, DROPPED) != 0) {
			break;
		}
	}
	return problem;
}

static const char *
spmi_read_once(const struct peripheral *p, uint8_t reg, uint8_t *bytes, uint32_t count)
{
	vm_offset_t channel = arb_observer + 0x10000UL * ARB_SYSTEM + 0x80UL * p->channel;
	const char *problem;
	uint32_t data[2];

	if (!p->found) {
		return "no channel";
	}
	lock();
	wr(channel + CHANNEL_COMMAND, COMMAND_READ | (uint32_t)reg << 4 | (count - 1));
	problem = wait_done(channel);
	data[0] = rd(channel + OBSERVER_DATA0);
	data[1] = count > 4 ? rd(channel + OBSERVER_DATA1) : 0;
	unlock();
	if (problem != NULL) {
		return problem;
	}
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
		bytes[i] = (uint8_t)(data[i / 4] >> (8 * (i % 4)));
	}
	return NULL;
}

/* ---- the flash LED module -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

#define FLASH_REVISION1         0x00
#define FLASH_TYPE              0x04            /* 0x18: a flash LED module */
#define FLASH_SUBTYPE           0x05            /* 0x07: four channels */
#define FLASH_STATUS1           0x06            /* a channel open or shorted */
#define FLASH_STATUS2           0x07
#define  STATUS2_OTST1          0x20            /* over-temperature, the first and the second threshold */
#define  STATUS2_OTST2          0x10
#define  STATUS2_VPH_LOW        0x01            /* the supply drooped */
#define FLASH_INT_RT_STS        0x10
#define  RT_STS_FAULT           0x01            /* open, short, or its supply not ready */
#define FLASH_SAFETY_TIMER0     0x3e            /* [7] on */
#define FLASH_ITARGET0          0x42            /* [6:0]: (code + 1) x the resolution */
#define FLASH_MODULE_EN         0x46            /* [7] */
#define FLASH_IRESOLUTION       0x49            /* a bit per channel: 0 12.5 mA, 1 5 mA */
#define FLASH_STROBE_CTRL0      0x4a            /* [6:4] hardware strobe's kind, [2] hardware strobe */
#define FLASH_EN_LED_CTRL       0x4e            /* a bit per channel */
#define FLASH_OTST2_CFG1        0x78
#define FLASH_OTST1_CFG1        0x7a

#define ALARM_SUBTYPE           0x05            /* 0x08: the first generation, 0x09 the second */
#define ALARM_STATUS            0x08            /* the over-temperature stage: [1:0] (first generation) or [6:4] */

#define ANDROID_TORCH_MA        125             /* led:torch_0 while Android's flashlight is on */
#define IRES_UA                 12500           /* its resolution ("qcom,ires-ua") */
#define ANDROID_ITARGET         9               /* round(125000 / 12500) - 1: the most ever written */
#define HOTTEST_BATTERY_C       45

static const uint8_t writable_regs[] = {
	FLASH_SAFETY_TIMER0, FLASH_ITARGET0, FLASH_MODULE_EN, FLASH_IRESOLUTION, FLASH_STROBE_CTRL0, FLASH_EN_LED_CTRL,
};

static void
give_up(const char *why)
{
	if (!broken) {
		broken = true;
		note("%s: no more writing to the flash module for the rest of the run", why);
	}
}

/*
 * One register of the flash module (and of the six above only) written and read back: false, and
 * no more writing, if it cannot be or does not read back.
 */
static bool
put(uint8_t reg, uint8_t value)
{
	const char *problem;
	uint8_t back = 0xff;
	bool allowed = false;

	for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof(writable_regs); i++) {
		allowed |= writable_regs[i] == reg;
	}
	if (broken || !allowed || !flash.writable || flash.write == 0 || flash.id != 0x2ee) {
		give_up(allowed ? "a write that may not be made" : "a register that is not to be written");
		return false;
	}
	/* (the channel is still the module's: its entry in the arbiter's table is looked at again) */
	if (((rd(arb_core + ARB_CHANNEL(flash.channel)) >> 8) & 0xfff) != flash.id) {
		give_up("the arbiter's channel is no longer the flash module's");
		return false;
	}
	for (int tries = 0; tries < 3; tries++) {
		lock();
		wr(flash.write + CHANNEL_WDATA0, value);
		wr(flash.write + CHANNEL_COMMAND, COMMAND_WRITE | (uint32_t)reg << 4);
		problem = wait_done(flash.write);
		unlock();
		if (problem == NULL || strcmp(problem, DROPPED) != 0) {
			break;          /* (a dropped write has not been made: asked for again, then read back) */
		}
	}
	if (problem != NULL || (problem = spmi_read(&flash, reg, &back, 1)) != NULL) {
		say("torch: %#04x <- %#04x: %s\n", reg, value, problem);
		give_up("a write that failed");
		return false;
	}
	if (back != value) {
		say("torch: %#04x <- %#04x, but it reads %#04x\n", reg, value, back);
		give_up("a register that did not read back as written");
		return false;
	}
	return true;
}

static bool
get(const struct peripheral *p, uint8_t reg, uint8_t *value)
{
	const char *problem = spmi_read(p, reg, value, 1);

	if (problem != NULL) {
		say("torch: reading %#04x of %s: %s\n", reg, p->name, problem);
		return false;
	}
	return true;
}

/* only the bits of `mask' changed, as the driver's masked writes do */
static bool
put_bits(uint8_t reg, uint8_t mask, uint8_t value)
{
	uint8_t now;

	if (!get(&flash, reg, &now)) {
		give_up("a read that failed");
		return false;
	}
	return (now & mask) == (value & mask) || put(reg, (uint8_t)((now & ~mask) | (value & mask)));
}

static void
find_channel(struct peripheral *p, uint32_t channels)
{
	for (uint32_t n = 0; n < channels; n++) {
		uint32_t map = rd(arb_core + ARB_CHANNEL(n)), owner;

		if (map == 0 || ((map >> 8) & 0xfff) != p->id) {
			continue;
		}
		owner = rd(arb_cnfg + ARB_OWNER(n)) & 7;
		say("torch: channel %u is %s (%#x); written by system %u%s\n", n, p->name, map, owner,
		    owner == ARB_SYSTEM ? ", which is us" : "");
		if (!p->found || owner == ARB_SYSTEM) {
			p->found = true;
			p->channel = (uint16_t)n;
			p->writable = owner == ARB_SYSTEM;
		}
	}
	if (!p->found) {
		say("torch: no channel of the arbiter is %s\n", p->name);
	}
}

static void
show_registers(void)
{
	uint8_t r[8];
	char line[200];

	for (unsigned base = 0; base < 0x100; base += 0x20) {
		int n = snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "torch: %#04x:", base);

		for (unsigned i = 0; i < 0x20; i += 8) {
			if (spmi_read(&flash, (uint8_t)(base + i), r, 8) != NULL) {
				n += snprintf(line + n, sizeof(line) - (size_t)n, " (unreadable)");
				continue;
			}
			for (unsigned j = 0; j < 8; j++) {
				n += snprintf(line + n, sizeof(line) - (size_t)n, " %02x", r[j]);
			}
		}
		say("%s\n", line);
	}
}

/* What would make the light go off now, or NULL. */
static const char *
trouble(void)
{
	static char why[180];
	uint8_t rt = 0, status1 = 0, status2 = 0, alarm_status = 0, stage;

	if (!get(&flash, FLASH_INT_RT_STS, &rt) || !get(&flash, FLASH_STATUS1, &status1) ||
	    !get(&flash, FLASH_STATUS2, &status2) || (alarm.found && !get(&alarm, ALARM_STATUS, &alarm_status))) {
		return "a read of the flags that failed";
	}
	stage = alarm_subtype == 0x08 ? alarm_status & 0x03 : (alarm_status >> 4) & 0x07;
	if ((rt & RT_STS_FAULT) || status1 != 0 || (status2 & (STATUS2_OTST1 | STATUS2_OTST2 | STATUS2_VPH_LOW)) || stage != 0) {
		uint8_t more[8] = { 0 }, latched[2] = { 0 };

		(void)spmi_read(&flash, 0x06, more, 8);
		(void)spmi_read(&flash, 0x18, latched, 2);
		snprintf(why, sizeof(why), "the module says fault %#x, channels %#x, temperature and supply %#x (0x06-0x0d: %02x %02x %02x "
		    "%02x %02x %02x %02x %02x, latched %#x); the PMIC's temperature stage %u", rt, status1, status2, more[0], more[1],
		    more[2], more[3], more[4], more[5], more[6], more[7], latched[0], stage);
		return why;
	}
	if (redwood_battery_temperature() >= HOTTEST_BATTERY_C) {
		snprintf(why, sizeof(why), "the battery is at %d C", redwood_battery_temperature());
		return why;
	}
	return NULL;
}

static bool configured, lit;

/* Android's probe, once: channel 0 strobed by software, its safety timer off. */
static bool
configure(void)
{
	if (!configured && put_bits(FLASH_STROBE_CTRL0, 0x74, 0x00) && put_bits(FLASH_SAFETY_TIMER0, 0x80, 0x00)) {
		configured = true;
	}
	return configured;
}

/* The light at `permille' of Android's current: its writes in its order. */
static bool
light(uint32_t permille)
{
	uint32_t ua = ANDROID_TORCH_MA * 1000 * permille / 1000, code;
	const char *why;

	if (ua < IRES_UA) {
		ua = IRES_UA;           /* (the driver's least: one step) */
	}
	code = (ua + IRES_UA / 2) / IRES_UA - 1;
	if (code > ANDROID_ITARGET) {
		code = ANDROID_ITARGET;
	}
	if (!lit && (why = trouble()) != NULL) {
		note("not lit: %s", why);
		give_up("trouble before the light");
		return false;
	}
	if (!configure() || !put_bits(FLASH_IRESOLUTION, 0x01, 0x00) || !put_bits(FLASH_ITARGET0, 0x7f, (uint8_t)code)) {
		return false;
	}
	if (!lit && (!put(FLASH_MODULE_EN, 0x80) || !put_bits(FLASH_EN_LED_CTRL, 0x01, 0x01))) {
		return false;
	}
	lit = true;
	return true;
}

/* Off, in Android's order: the channel, the module, the target current, the timer's bit. */
static bool
dark(void)
{
	bool ok = put_bits(FLASH_EN_LED_CTRL, 0x01, 0x00) && put(FLASH_MODULE_EN, 0x00) && put_bits(FLASH_ITARGET0, 0x7f, 0x00) &&
	    put_bits(FLASH_SAFETY_TIMER0, 0x80, 0x00);

	lit = !ok && lit;
	return ok;
}

/* ---- torch=3: the light for iOS --------------------------------------------------------------------- */

static volatile uint32_t wanted;                /* the level asked for last, 0 to 1000 */
static volatile uint32_t asked;                 /* how many times one was */
static uint32_t max_secs = 30;

static int
torch_write(__unused dev_t dev, struct uio *uio, __unused int ioflag)
{
	uint32_t value;
	int error;

	while (uio_resid(uio) >= (user_ssize_t)sizeof(value)) {
		if ((error = uiomove((caddr_t)&value, sizeof(value), uio)) != 0) {
			return error;
		}
		wanted = value > 1000 ? 1000 : value;
		asked++;
	}
	return 0;
}

/* what is lit now: the level, 0 if nothing */
static uint32_t shown;

static int
torch_read(__unused dev_t dev, struct uio *uio, __unused int ioflag)
{
	uint32_t value = shown;

	return uiomove((caddr_t)&value, (int)MIN(sizeof(value), (size_t)uio_resid(uio)), uio);
}

static int
torch_open(__unused dev_t dev, __unused int flags, __unused int type, __unused struct proc *p)
{
	return 0;
}

static const struct cdevsw torch_cdevsw = {
	.d_open = torch_open, .d_close = torch_open, .d_read = torch_read, .d_write = torch_write,
	.d_ioctl = eno_ioctl, .d_stop = eno_stop, .d_reset = eno_reset, .d_select = eno_select,
	.d_mmap = eno_mmap, .d_strategy = eno_strat, .d_type = 0
};

static uint64_t
now_ms(void)
{
	uint64_t ns;

	absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(mach_absolute_time(), &ns);
	return ns / NSEC_PER_MSEC;
}

static void
serve(void)
{
	uint32_t applied = 0, times = 0, cut = 0;
	uint64_t since = 0, last_look = 0;
	bool waiting_for_off = false;           /* cut at the limit: dark until iOS asks for 0 */
	int major = cdevsw_add(-1, &torch_cdevsw);

	if (major < 0 || devfs_make_node(makedev(major, 0), DEVFS_CHAR, UID_ROOT, GID_WHEEL, 0666, "redwood-torch") == NULL) {
		say("torch: /dev/redwood-torch cannot be made\n");
		return;
	}
	say("torch: THE LIGHT IS IOS'S (/dev/redwood-torch) from here on, until the run ends: at most Android's %u mA, at most %u s "
	    "at a time\n", ANDROID_TORCH_MA, max_secs);
	while (!broken) {
		uint32_t want = wanted;
		uint64_t now = now_ms();

		if (want == 0) {
			waiting_for_off = false;
		}
		if (waiting_for_off) {
			want = 0;
		}
		if (want != applied) {
			if (want == 0 ? dark() : light(want)) {
				if (applied == 0) {
					since = now;
					times++;
				}
				if (want == 0) {
					note("off (iOS asked for 0)");
				} else {
					note("ON (iOS asked for %u of 1000; the battery %d C)", wanted, redwood_battery_temperature());
				}
				applied = want;
				shown = want;
			} else {
				break;
			}
		}
		if (applied != 0 && now - since >= max_secs * 1000ull) {
			cut++;
			note("on for %u s, the limit: off until iOS asks again", max_secs);
			waiting_for_off = true;
			if (!dark()) {
				break;
			}
			applied = 0;
			shown = 0;
			continue;
		}
		if (applied != 0 && now - last_look >= 100) {
			const char *why;

			last_look = now;
			if ((why = trouble()) != NULL) {
				note("OFF: %s", why);
				(void)dark();
				give_up("trouble while lit");
				break;
			}
		}
		wait_ms(20);
	}
	if (lit) {
		(void)dark();
	}
	shown = 0;
	say("torch: the light is given up on (%u times lit, %u cut at %u s)\n", times, cut, max_secs);
}

/* ---- the start ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

static void
torch_thread(__unused void *parameter, __unused wait_result_t result)
{
	uint32_t version, channels;
	uint8_t id[2] = { 0, 0 }, revision = 0, alarm_status = 0;

	say("torch: level %u: %s\n", level, level == 1 ? "a look, reading only" : level == 2 ? "the light on once" :
	    "the light for iOS");
	arb_core = ml_io_map(ARB_CORE_PHYS, ARB_CORE_SIZE);
	arb_cnfg = ml_io_map(ARB_CNFG_PHYS, ARB_CNFG_SIZE);
	arb_observer = ml_io_map(ARB_OBSERVER_PHYS, ARB_OBSERVER_SIZE);
	version = rd(arb_core + ARB_VERSION);
	channels = rd(arb_core + ARB_FEATURES) & 0x7ff;
	if (version < ARB_VERSION_5 || version >= ARB_VERSION_7) {
		say("torch: PMIC arbiter version %#x, not 5: nothing done\n", version);
		goto out;
	}
	if (channels == 0 || channels > ARB_MAX_CHANNELS) {
		channels = ARB_MAX_CHANNELS;
	}
	find_channel(&flash, channels);
	find_channel(&alarm, channels);
	if (!flash.found || spmi_read(&flash, FLASH_TYPE, id, 2) != NULL || spmi_read(&flash, FLASH_REVISION1, &revision, 1) != NULL) {
		say("torch: the flash module cannot be read\n");
		goto out;
	}
	say("torch: the module says type %#x, subtype %#x, revision %#x%s\n", id[0], id[1], revision,
	    id[0] == 0x18 && id[1] == 0x07 ? ": a flash LED module of four channels, as Android's driver expects" : ": NOT WHAT WAS EXPECTED");
	show_registers();
	if (alarm.found && get(&alarm, ALARM_SUBTYPE, &alarm_subtype) && get(&alarm, ALARM_STATUS, &alarm_status)) {
		uint8_t stage = alarm_subtype == 0x08 ? alarm_status & 0x03 : (alarm_status >> 4) & 0x07;

		say("torch: the PMIC's temperature alarm (subtype %#x) says %#x: stage %u%s\n", alarm_subtype, alarm_status, stage,
		    stage == 0 ? " (all is well)" : "");
	} else {
		alarm.found = false;
	}
	if (id[0] != 0x18 || id[1] != 0x07 || level < 2) {
		goto out;
	}
	if (!flash.writable) {
		say("torch: the channel is not ours to write through: nothing written\n");
		goto out;
	}
	flash.write = ml_io_map(ARB_CHNLS_PHYS + 0x10000UL * flash.channel, 0x1000);
	PE_parse_boot_argn("torch_max_s", &max_secs, sizeof(max_secs));
	max_secs = max_secs < 1 ? 1 : max_secs > 120 ? 120 : max_secs;
	if (level == 2) {
		uint32_t secs = 2;
		uint64_t until;
		const char *why = NULL;

		PE_parse_boot_argn("torch_secs", &secs, sizeof(secs));
		secs = secs < 1 ? 1 : secs > max_secs ? max_secs : secs;
		say("torch: the light ON at Android's %u mA (ITARGET %u, 12.5 mA steps) for %u s\n", ANDROID_TORCH_MA, ANDROID_ITARGET,
		    secs);
		if (light(1000)) {
			uint8_t rt = 0, s1 = 0, s2 = 0;

			wait_ms(50);
			(void)get(&flash, FLASH_INT_RT_STS, &rt);
			(void)get(&flash, FLASH_STATUS1, &s1);
			(void)get(&flash, FLASH_STATUS2, &s2);
			note("lit at Android's %u mA; 50 ms on: interrupt status %#x (%s), channels %#x, temperature and supply %#x",
			    ANDROID_TORCH_MA, rt, (rt & 0x10) ? "ramped up" : "NOT ramped up", s1, s2);
			show_registers();
			for (until = now_ms() + secs * 1000ull; now_ms() < until && (why = trouble()) == NULL;) {
				wait_ms(100);
			}
			if (why != NULL) {
				note("OFF early: %s", why);
			}
			if (dark()) {
				note("off again after %u s", secs);
			}
			show_registers();
		}
	} else {
		serve();
	}
out:
	say("torch: done\n");
	thread_terminate(current_thread());
}

void
redwood_torch_init(void)
{
	thread_t thread;

	if (!PE_parse_boot_argn("torch", &level, sizeof(level)) || level == 0) {
		return;
	}
	level = level > 3 ? 3 : level;
	if (kernel_thread_start(torch_thread, NULL, &thread) == KERN_SUCCESS) {
		thread_deallocate(thread);
	}
}

/* At the run's end and on a panic's way out: the light off, if it was ever lit. */
void
redwood_torch_quiesce(void)
{
	uint8_t module = 0xff, channels = 0xff, target = 0xff;

	if (level < 2 || flash.write == 0) {
		return;
	}
	leaving = true;
	if (lit) {
		broken = false;         /* (one last time, whatever went before) */
		say("torch: at the run's end: the light %s\n", dark() ? "switched off" : "COULD NOT BE SWITCHED OFF");
	}
	say("torch: what happened in this run (%u events):\n", noted);
	for (unsigned i = noted > NOTES ? noted - NOTES : 0; i < noted; i++) {
		say("torch:   %s\n", notes[i % NOTES]);
	}
	(void)spmi_read(&flash, FLASH_MODULE_EN, &module, 1);
	(void)spmi_read(&flash, FLASH_EN_LED_CTRL, &channels, 1);
	(void)spmi_read(&flash, FLASH_ITARGET0, &target, 1);
	say("torch: at the run's end the module reads: enable %#04x, channels %#04x, target %#04x%s\n", module, channels, target,
	    module == 0 && (channels & 0x01) == 0 && target == 0 ? " (dark)" : " (NOT DARK)");
}

```

`xnu/files/bsd/dev/redwood_ufs.c`:

```c
/*
 * The phone's storage: one block device and one character device for every GPT partition of its
 * UFS (/dev/ufs_NAME and /dev/rufs_NAME, NAME as the partition table has it). Read only, but for
 * the one place the data of iOS lives (ufs_write=1, below).
 *
 * There is no UFS driver here, and none is needed. UEFI never exits on this port: Qualcomm's own
 * UFS driver (UFSDxe) has brought up the controller, its PHY, its clocks and power, and stays
 * resident, and xnuloader keeps serving the kernel from core 0 while the kernel runs on another
 * core (it already does for the battery). So with ufs=2 on its command line the loader publishes a
 * page (ufs_shared_pa=) with the table of partitions, a request and an answer, and a buffer; this
 * driver writes a request -- which partition, which blocks -- and core 0 reads them with that
```
