```c
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/* Mount operations                                                         */

/* mount(2) with no arguments: an empty filesystem appears. */
static int
ramfs_mount(mount_t mp, __unused vnode_t devvp, __unused user_addr_t data, __unused vfs_context_t ctx)
{
	struct ramfs_mount *rm;
	struct vfsstatfs *sp;

	if (vfs_isupdate(mp)) {
		return 0;
	}
	rm = kalloc_type(struct ramfs_mount, Z_WAITOK | Z_ZERO | Z_NOFAIL);
	lck_mtx_init(&rm->rm_lock, &ramfs_lck_grp, LCK_ATTR_NULL);
	rm->rm_mp = mp;
	rm->rm_next_ino = RAMFS_ROOT_INO + 1;
	/* a runaway writer must not be able to take the whole machine: a quarter of memory at most */
	rm->rm_max_pages = (max_mem / 4) / PAGE_SIZE;

	rm->rm_hash = kalloc_type(struct ramfs_node *, RAMFS_HASH_SIZE, Z_WAITOK | Z_ZERO | Z_NOFAIL);
	rm->rm_root = ramfs_node_alloc(rm, VDIR, NULL);
	rm->rm_root->rn_ino = RAMFS_ROOT_INO;
	ramfs_hash_insert(rm, rm->rm_root);
	rm->rm_root->rn_nlink = 2;
	rm->rm_root->rn_parent = rm->rm_root;
	rm->rm_nodes = 1;

	vfs_setfsprivate(mp, rm);
	vfs_setlocklocal(mp);
	/* ACLs and owner UUIDs: VFS keeps them in an extended attribute of the file */
	vfs_setextendedsecurity(mp);
	vfs_getnewfsid(mp);

	sp = vfs_statfs(mp);
	sp->f_bsize = PAGE_SIZE;
	sp->f_iosize = PAGE_SIZE;
	sp->f_blocks = rm->rm_max_pages;
	sp->f_bfree = sp->f_bavail = rm->rm_max_pages;
	sp->f_bused = 0;
	/* there is no table of nodes to run out of; report as many as there could be pages */
	sp->f_files = rm->rm_max_pages;
	sp->f_ffree = rm->rm_max_pages - 1;
	strlcpy(sp->f_mntfromname, "ramfs", sizeof(sp->f_mntfromname));
	return 0;
}

/* Free a directory's subtree; every vnode is gone, so nothing else can be looking. */
static void
ramfs_free_tree(struct ramfs_node *dir)
{
	struct ramfs_dirent *de;

	while ((de = TAILQ_FIRST(&dir->rn_entries)) != NULL) {
		struct ramfs_node *node = de->rd_node;

		TAILQ_REMOVE(&dir->rn_entries, de, rd_link);
		ramfs_dirent_free(de);
		if (node->rn_type == VDIR) {
			ramfs_free_tree(node);
			ramfs_node_free(node);
		} else if (--node->rn_nlink == 0) {
			ramfs_node_free(node);
		}
	}
}

static int
ramfs_unmount(mount_t mp, int mntflags, __unused vfs_context_t ctx)
{
	struct ramfs_mount *rm = RAMFS_MP(mp);
	int error = vflush(mp, NULLVP, (mntflags & MNT_FORCE) ? FORCECLOSE : 0);

	if (error) {
		return error;
	}
	lck_mtx_lock(&rm->rm_lock);
	ramfs_free_tree(rm->rm_root);
	ramfs_node_free(rm->rm_root);
	lck_mtx_unlock(&rm->rm_lock);

	vfs_setfsprivate(mp, NULL);
	lck_mtx_destroy(&rm->rm_lock, &ramfs_lck_grp);
	kfree_type(struct ramfs_node *, RAMFS_HASH_SIZE, rm->rm_hash);
	kfree_type(struct ramfs_mount, rm);
	return 0;
}

static int
ramfs_root(mount_t mp, vnode_t *vpp, __unused vfs_context_t ctx)
{
	struct ramfs_mount *rm = RAMFS_MP(mp);
	int error;

	do {
		lck_mtx_lock(&rm->rm_lock);
		error = ramfs_vget_locked(rm, rm->rm_root, NULLVP, NULL, vpp);
	} while (error == EAGAIN);
	return error;
}

/* A node by its number (fsgetpath, and whoever else asks by file ID): see ramfs_hash_insert(). */
static int
ramfs_vfs_vget(mount_t mp, ino64_t ino, vnode_t *vpp, __unused vfs_context_t ctx)
{
	struct ramfs_mount *rm = RAMFS_MP(mp);
	int error;

	do {
		struct ramfs_node *node;

		lck_mtx_lock(&rm->rm_lock);
		for (node = rm->rm_hash[ino & (RAMFS_HASH_SIZE - 1)]; node != NULL && node->rn_ino != ino;
		    node = node->rn_hnext) {
		}
		if (node == NULL || node->rn_nlink == 0) {
			lck_mtx_unlock(&rm->rm_lock);
			return ENOENT;
		}
		error = ramfs_vget_locked(rm, node, NULLVP, NULL, vpp);
	} while (error == EAGAIN);
	return error;
}

static int
ramfs_vfs_getattr(mount_t mp, struct vfs_attr *fsap, __unused vfs_context_t ctx)
{
	struct ramfs_mount *rm = RAMFS_MP(mp);
	uint64_t used, nodes;

	lck_mtx_lock(&rm->rm_lock);
	used = rm->rm_pages;
	nodes = rm->rm_nodes;
	lck_mtx_unlock(&rm->rm_lock);

	VFSATTR_RETURN(fsap, f_objcount, nodes);
	VFSATTR_RETURN(fsap, f_bsize, PAGE_SIZE);
	VFSATTR_RETURN(fsap, f_iosize, PAGE_SIZE);
	VFSATTR_RETURN(fsap, f_blocks, rm->rm_max_pages);
	VFSATTR_RETURN(fsap, f_bfree, rm->rm_max_pages - MIN(used, rm->rm_max_pages));
	VFSATTR_RETURN(fsap, f_bavail, rm->rm_max_pages - MIN(used, rm->rm_max_pages));
	VFSATTR_RETURN(fsap, f_bused, used);
	VFSATTR_RETURN(fsap, f_files, rm->rm_max_pages);
	VFSATTR_RETURN(fsap, f_ffree, rm->rm_max_pages - MIN(nodes, rm->rm_max_pages));

	if (VFSATTR_IS_ACTIVE(fsap, f_capabilities)) {
		vol_capabilities_attr_t *cap = &fsap->f_capabilities;

		bzero(cap, sizeof(*cap));
		cap->capabilities[VOL_CAPABILITIES_FORMAT] =
		    VOL_CAP_FMT_SYMBOLICLINKS |
		    VOL_CAP_FMT_HARDLINKS |
		    VOL_CAP_FMT_SPARSE_FILES |
		    VOL_CAP_FMT_CASE_SENSITIVE |
		    VOL_CAP_FMT_CASE_PRESERVING |
		    VOL_CAP_FMT_FAST_STATFS |
		    VOL_CAP_FMT_2TB_FILESIZE |
		    /*
		     * A file keeps its number for as long as it exists (the life of the mount, a boot), a node is
		     * found by it (vfs_vget) and a path made from it (fsgetpath): LaunchServices keeps an
		     * application by number, and takes none from a volume that does not say so -- everything a
		     * package installed under the prefix was "Unable to register", with nothing tried on its files.
		     */
		    VOL_CAP_FMT_PERSISTENTOBJECTIDS |
		    VOL_CAP_FMT_PATH_FROM_ID;
		cap->capabilities[VOL_CAPABILITIES_INTERFACES] =
		    VOL_CAP_INT_ADVLOCK |
		    VOL_CAP_INT_FLOCK |
		    VOL_CAP_INT_EXTENDED_SECURITY |
		    VOL_CAP_INT_EXTENDED_ATTR;
		cap->valid[VOL_CAPABILITIES_FORMAT] =
		    VOL_CAP_FMT_PERSISTENTOBJECTIDS |
		    VOL_CAP_FMT_SYMBOLICLINKS |
		    VOL_CAP_FMT_HARDLINKS |
		    VOL_CAP_FMT_JOURNAL |
		    VOL_CAP_FMT_JOURNAL_ACTIVE |
		    VOL_CAP_FMT_NO_ROOT_TIMES |
		    VOL_CAP_FMT_SPARSE_FILES |
		    VOL_CAP_FMT_ZERO_RUNS |
		    VOL_CAP_FMT_CASE_SENSITIVE |
		    VOL_CAP_FMT_CASE_PRESERVING |
		    VOL_CAP_FMT_FAST_STATFS |
		    VOL_CAP_FMT_2TB_FILESIZE |
		    VOL_CAP_FMT_OPENDENYMODES |
		    VOL_CAP_FMT_HIDDEN_FILES |
		    VOL_CAP_FMT_PATH_FROM_ID;
		cap->valid[VOL_CAPABILITIES_INTERFACES] =
		    VOL_CAP_INT_SEARCHFS |
		    VOL_CAP_INT_ATTRLIST |
		    VOL_CAP_INT_NFSEXPORT |
		    VOL_CAP_INT_READDIRATTR |
		    VOL_CAP_INT_EXCHANGEDATA |
		    VOL_CAP_INT_COPYFILE |
		    VOL_CAP_INT_ALLOCATE |
		    VOL_CAP_INT_VOL_RENAME |
		    VOL_CAP_INT_ADVLOCK |
		    VOL_CAP_INT_FLOCK |
		    VOL_CAP_INT_EXTENDED_SECURITY |
		    VOL_CAP_INT_USERACCESS |
		    VOL_CAP_INT_MANLOCK |
		    VOL_CAP_INT_EXTENDED_ATTR |
		    VOL_CAP_INT_NAMEDSTREAMS;
		VFSATTR_SET_SUPPORTED(fsap, f_capabilities);
	}
	/*
	 * The rest of what getattrlist(2) may be asked about a volume. Unless the caller also asks
	 * which attributes came back, one that the filesystem leaves out fails the whole call with
	 * EINVAL, and callers take that badly: CacheDelete then hands assetsd a nil volume, which
	 * ends in an uncaught exception.
	 */
	VFSATTR_RETURN(fsap, f_filecount, nodes);
	VFSATTR_RETURN(fsap, f_dircount, 0);
	VFSATTR_RETURN(fsap, f_maxobjcount, rm->rm_max_pages);
	VFSATTR_RETURN(fsap, f_owner, 0);
	VFSATTR_RETURN(fsap, f_fssubtype, 0);
	VFSATTR_RETURN(fsap, f_signature, 0x4244);              /* 'BD', what the VFS layer defaults to */
	VFSATTR_RETURN(fsap, f_carbon_fsid, 0);
	VFSATTR_RETURN(fsap, f_quota, 0);
	VFSATTR_RETURN(fsap, f_reserved, 0);
	if (VFSATTR_IS_ACTIVE(fsap, f_fsid)) {
		fsap->f_fsid = vfs_statfs(mp)->f_fsid;
		VFSATTR_SET_SUPPORTED(fsap, f_fsid);
	}
	if (VFSATTR_IS_ACTIVE(fsap, f_create_time) || VFSATTR_IS_ACTIVE(fsap, f_modify_time) ||
	    VFSATTR_IS_ACTIVE(fsap, f_access_time) || VFSATTR_IS_ACTIVE(fsap, f_backup_time)) {
		struct timeval boot;
		struct timespec since = { .tv_sec = 0, .tv_nsec = 0 };

		/* nothing here is older than this boot */
		boottime_timeval(&boot);
		since.tv_sec = boot.tv_sec;
		VFSATTR_RETURN(fsap, f_create_time, since);
		VFSATTR_RETURN(fsap, f_modify_time, since);
		VFSATTR_RETURN(fsap, f_access_time, since);
		since.tv_sec = 0;
		VFSATTR_RETURN(fsap, f_backup_time, since);
	}
	if (VFSATTR_IS_ACTIVE(fsap, f_uuid)) {
		/* the same at every boot as long as the mounts are made in the same order: programs key caches by it */
		static const uuid_t base = { 'r', 'e', 'd', 'w', 'o', 'o', 0x50, 'd', 0x80, 'R', 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0 };
		fsid_t fsid = vfs_statfs(mp)->f_fsid;

		memcpy(fsap->f_uuid, base, sizeof(uuid_t));
		memcpy(&fsap->f_uuid[10], &fsid.val[0], 4);
		fsap->f_uuid[14] = (uint8_t)fsid.val[1];
		VFSATTR_SET_SUPPORTED(fsap, f_uuid);
	}
	if (VFSATTR_IS_ACTIVE(fsap, f_attributes)) {
		vol_attributes_attr_t *attr = &fsap->f_attributes;

		attr->validattr.commonattr = ATTR_CMN_VALIDMASK;
		attr->validattr.volattr = ATTR_VOL_VALIDMASK;
		attr->validattr.dirattr = ATTR_DIR_VALIDMASK;
		attr->validattr.fileattr = ATTR_FILE_VALIDMASK;
		attr->validattr.forkattr = 0;
		attr->nativeattr = attr->validattr;
		VFSATTR_SET_SUPPORTED(fsap, f_attributes);
	}
	if (VFSATTR_IS_ACTIVE(fsap, f_vol_name)) {
		strlcpy(fsap->f_vol_name, "ramfs", MAXPATHLEN);
		VFSATTR_SET_SUPPORTED(fsap, f_vol_name);
	}
	return 0;
}

ramfs_sync(__unused mount_t mp, __unused int waitfor, __unused vfs_context_t ctx)

	return 0;
}

static int
ramfs_init(__unused struct vfsconf *vfsc)

}
```

`xnu/files/bsd/pthread/pthread_kext_static.c`:

```c
/*
 * Starts the pthread kernel extension when it is linked statically into the
 * kernel image.
 *
 * com.apple.kec.pthread (open source, libpthread/kern) normally arrives as a
 * prelinked kext whose start routine registers its function table with
 * pthread_shims.c. This configuration has no kext loading at all, so the kext
 * is built as libpthread_kext.a, linked in, and started from here before
 * bsd_init() needs it.
 */
#include <mach/kmod.h>
#include <kern/startup.h>
#include <kern/debug.h>

extern kern_return_t pthread_start(kmod_info_t *ki, void *d);

__startup_func
static void
pthread_kext_static_start(void)
{
	kern_return_t kr = pthread_start(NULL, NULL);
	if (kr != KERN_SUCCESS) {
		panic("static pthread kext failed to start: %d", kr);
	}
}
STARTUP(EARLY_BOOT, STARTUP_RANK_LAST, pthread_kext_static_start);
```

`xnu/files/bsd/sys/redwood_audio.h`:

```h
/*
 * /dev/redwood-audio: the sound iOS plays, on its way to whatever can make it heard.
 *
 * iOS expects its output devices from Apple's audio drivers through IOAudio2; neither exists
 * here. Instead the audio server (mediaserverd) is given a plug-in of ours that presents one
 * stereo output device, and the plug-in writes what the server has mixed for that device
 * here. In the kernel the samples go to a sink -- a driver for something that plays them --
 * and, if asked for, into a recording that outlives the kernel (see dev/redwood_audio.c).
 *
 *   write(): whole frames in the format below. Never blocks: the writer is the audio server's
 *            real-time thread, which paces itself (48000 frames a second while anything
 *            plays, nothing at all otherwise). What the sink cannot take is dropped.
 */
#ifndef _SYS_REDWOOD_AUDIO_H_
#define _SYS_REDWOOD_AUDIO_H_

#include <stdint.h>

#define REDWOOD_AUDIO_DEVICE    "/dev/redwood-audio"

/* The one format: 16-bit signed little-endian samples, left then right. */
#define REDWOOD_AUDIO_RATE      48000
#define REDWOOD_AUDIO_CHANNELS  2
#define REDWOOD_AUDIO_FRAME     4       /* bytes */

/*
 * ioctl(REDWOOD_AUDIO_SET_VOLUME): the speakers' volume, as iOS sets it on the plug-in's volume
 * control -- how many eighths of a dB under the loudest they may play, and whether they are
 * muted (iOS's volume at 0). The loudest is the kernel's to say (on the phone: Android's own
 * level less sound_below, redwood_sound.c); the plug-in only says how far under it.
 */
#include <sys/ioccom.h>

struct redwood_audio_volume {
	uint32_t below;                 /* eighths of a dB */
	uint32_t muted;
};
#define REDWOOD_AUDIO_SET_VOLUME _IOW('r', 1, struct redwood_audio_volume)

#ifdef KERNEL
#include <stdbool.h>

/*
 * For drivers. A sink is offered frames as they are written and says how many it took (the
 * rest are lost); it is called from the writer's thread and must not wait.
 */
typedef uint32_t (*redwood_audio_sink_t)(const int16_t *frames, uint32_t count);

void redwood_audio_set_sink(const char *name, redwood_audio_sink_t sink);
/* The volume iOS has set last (REDWOOD_AUDIO_SET_VOLUME): false if it has set none; *generation counts the settings. */
bool redwood_audio_volume(uint32_t *below, bool *muted, uint32_t *generation);
void redwood_audio_init(void);
void redwood_virtio_sound_init(void);   /* boot-arg virtio_sound=1: QEMU's virtio sound device */
void redwood_speaker_init(void);        /* boot-arg speaker_probe=N: a look at the phone's speaker amplifiers */
void redwood_haptic_init(void);         /* boot-arg haptic=N: the phone's vibration motor (bsd/dev/redwood_haptic.c) */
void redwood_haptic_quiesce(void);      /* its chip back into reset: at the run's end and on a panic's way out */
void redwood_haptic_pretend(uint32_t peak); /* a test's stand-in for iOS's waveform: as if a write of this loudness came */
void redwood_torch_init(void);          /* boot-arg torch=N: the phone's flashlight (bsd/dev/redwood_torch.c) */
void redwood_torch_quiesce(void);       /* the light off: at the run's end and on a panic's way out */
void redwood_camera_init(void);         /* boot-arg cam=N: the phone's cameras (bsd/dev/redwood_camera.c) */
void redwood_camera_quiesce(void);      /* whatever of them was switched on, off: at the run's end and on a panic's way out */

/*
 * The phone's speakers (bsd/dev/redwood_speaker.c): its two Awinic amplifiers, set up as
 * Android's driver sets them up, from Android's own configuration file (see there).
 */
bool redwood_speaker_prepare(const uint8_t *acf, uint64_t size);       /* found, reset, configured: powered down, muted */
bool redwood_speaker_start(void);       /* powered up and unmuted at the lowest volume: only while the I2S clock runs */
bool redwood_speaker_volume(uint32_t below, uint32_t step_ms); /* below Android's level, in eighths of a dB; 6 dB a step */
bool redwood_speaker_healthy(void);     /* no fault reported; on one, both are powered down at once */
void redwood_speaker_stop(void);        /* faded out, muted, powered down, in Android's order */
void redwood_speaker_quiesce(void);     /* powered down at once, without sleeping: on a panic's way out */
/* the amplifiers' own temperature and battery voltage read (every second while they play): the reduction they call for */
uint32_t redwood_speaker_monitor(bool tell);

/*
 * The speakers' guard (bsd/dev/redwood_guard.c): what the samples go through in the feeder on their
 * way to the amplifiers, for want of the DSP's speaker protection. Levels in eighths of a dB.
 */
#define REDWOOD_GUARD_SILENT    0xffffffffu     /* the amplifiers are off: nothing reaches the speakers */
struct redwood_guard_report {
	uint32_t blocks, rms_blocks, fast_blocks, slow_blocks;  /* blocks done, and in how many each average held the level down */
	uint32_t limited_frames;        /* frames in which the peak limiter turned the level down */
	uint32_t peak_in, peak_out;     /* the largest sample that came in and that went out */
	uint32_t least_peak_gain;       /* the peak limiter's least gain, in 1/65536 */
	uint64_t least_gain, gain;      /* the power guard's (with the monitor's) least gain and the latest, Q30 */
	uint64_t rms, fast, slow;       /* the averages now, the louder speaker's: Q30 of a full-scale square wave at Android's level */
};
#define REDWOOD_GUARD_MAX_GAIN  (12 * 8)        /* the most gain before the guard: 12 dB */
void redwood_guard_configure(bool hpf, uint32_t gain);         /* the high-pass filter; `gain' before everything */
void redwood_guard_attenuation(uint32_t below);                 /* the amplifiers' level under Android's (or REDWOOD_GUARD_SILENT):
                                                                 * what the limits are reckoned from */
void redwood_guard_monitor(uint32_t below);                     /* a reduction asked for by redwood_speaker_monitor() */
void redwood_guard_process(int16_t *frames, uint32_t count);    /* stereo frames, in place */
void redwood_guard_take_report(struct redwood_guard_report *report);   /* what happened since the last call */
int redwood_guard_decibels(uint64_t ratio);                     /* 10 log10 of a Q30 ratio, in tenths of a dB */
/* boot-arg rec_sound_fed=1: the recording (rec_sound=N) has what the guard let through instead of what iOS wrote */
bool redwood_audio_recording_fed(void);
void redwood_audio_record_fed(const int16_t *frames, uint32_t count);

/*
 * The audio DSP's services, for the sound's path (bsd/dev/redwood_adsp.c, bsd/dev/redwood_sound.c).
 * redwood_adsp_apr() sends one APR packet to a service of the DSP (AFE 4, ASM 7, ADM 8) with the
 * given port and token (0: one of its own) and, with wait_ms, waits for the packet that carries
 * that token back. What is not waited for goes to the handler of events, if there is one and it
 * takes it (returns true). The handler is called on the link's thread and must not wait.
 */
struct redwood_apr_answer {
	uint32_t opcode, token, length;         /* length: of the payload, in bytes */
	uint32_t words[64];
};
typedef bool (*redwood_apr_events_t)(uint8_t service, uint16_t port, uint32_t opcode, uint32_t token, const uint32_t *payload,
    uint32_t length);

bool redwood_adsp_apr(uint8_t service, uint16_t port, uint32_t token, uint32_t opcode, const void *payload, uint32_t length,
    uint32_t wait_ms, struct redwood_apr_answer *answer);
void redwood_adsp_apr_events(redwood_apr_events_t handler);
const uint8_t *redwood_adsp_fw_file(const char *name, uint64_t *size);        /* /fw/name, read whole; give back with: */
void redwood_adsp_fw_free(const uint8_t *data, uint64_t size);

void redwood_sound_dsp_up(void);        /* the DSP's audio services are up (adsp=1): boot-arg sound=N begins */
void redwood_sound_dsp_down(void);      /* before the DSP is shut down at the run's end: everything of the sound's stopped */
void redwood_sound_quiesce(void);       /* on a panic's way out: the amplifiers off, without sleeping */
/* the microphones' part of the memory the DSP sees (redwood_sound.c): false if it cannot be had; given back with _put() */
bool redwood_audio_dsp_memory(uintptr_t *memory, uint64_t *dsp_address, uint32_t *bytes);
void redwood_audio_dsp_memory_put(void);
/* a second handler of the DSP's events (the microphones'), asked when the first does not take one */
void redwood_adsp_apr_events_second(redwood_apr_events_t handler);
/* boot-arg rec_sound_mic=1: the recording (rec_sound=N) has what the microphone hears (given with redwood_audio_record_fed()) */
bool redwood_audio_recording_mic(void);
void redwood_mic_dsp_up(void);          /* the DSP's audio services are up (adsp=1): boot-arg mic=N begins */
void redwood_mic_dsp_down(void);        /* before the DSP is shut down at the run's end: what the microphones' path asked for given back */
#endif

#endif /* _SYS_REDWOOD_AUDIO_H_ */
```

`xnu/files/bsd/sys/redwood_camera.h`:

```h
/*
 * /dev/redwood-camera: the phone's wide camera for iOS (boot-arg cam=5; bsd/dev/redwood_camera.c).
 *
 *   open()   the first one powers the sensor up and starts its frames (the sensor's mode: boot-arg
 *            cam_mode, else the module file's 4000x3000 one); the last close puts everything down
 *            again, and so does a second without a read.
 *   read()   waits (at most a second) for the newest frame not read yet: a struct
 *            redwood_camera_frame, then as many of the frame's bytes as the buffer has room for.
 *            A buffer of the header's size learns the frame's size and nothing else is copied.
 *            EIO when the camera has had a fault: it stays off for the rest of the run.
 *   write()  commands: a struct redwood_camera_command, then what it says follows.
 */
#ifndef _SYS_REDWOOD_CAMERA_H_
#define _SYS_REDWOOD_CAMERA_H_

#include <stdint.h>

#define REDWOOD_CAMERA_DEVICE           "/dev/redwood-camera"
#define REDWOOD_CAMERA_MAGIC            "RWFRAME1"

struct redwood_camera_frame {
	char            magic[8];       /* REDWOOD_CAMERA_MAGIC */
	uint32_t        header_bytes;   /* this structure's size: the frame's bytes follow */
	uint32_t        width, height;  /* pixels */
	uint32_t        stride;         /* bytes from one line to the next */
	uint32_t        format;         /* 1: MIPI RAW10, four pixels in five bytes */
	uint32_t        bayer;          /* the order of a 2x2 cell: 0 RGGB, 1 GRBG, 2 GBRG, 3 BGGR */
	uint32_t        black;          /* the black level, in 10-bit steps */
	uint64_t        sequence;       /* the frame's number since the sensor started, from 1 */
	uint64_t        time;           /* when the frame was done, in mach_absolute_time()'s units */
	uint32_t        exposure_lines; /* the exposure it was taken with, in lines ... */
	uint32_t        line_ns;        /* ... of this many nanoseconds */
	uint32_t        gain;           /* the sensor's analog gain register ... */
	uint32_t        gain_unity;     /* ... which is this for 1x */
	uint32_t        gain_max;       /* the most it may be given */
	uint32_t        frame_lines;    /* the frame's length in lines (frames a second: 1e9 / (frame_lines * line_ns)) */
	uint32_t        frame_lines_min; /* the mode's own length: the shortest frame */
	uint32_t        frame_lines_max; /* the longest frame it may be given */
	uint32_t        margin;         /* exposure_lines is at most frame_lines - margin */
	uint32_t        sensor;         /* which: 0 the macro, 1 the wide, 2 the front, 3 the ultra-wide camera */
	uint32_t        focus;          /* the lens's position as last set, 0 (the furthest) to 1023: REDWOOD_CAMERA_NO_FOCUS where it
	                                 * has no motor (or it does not answer) */
	uint32_t        reserved[5];
};

#define REDWOOD_CAMERA_NO_FOCUS 0xffffffffu

enum {
	REDWOOD_CAMERA_EXPOSURE = 1,    /* a: lines, b: gain, c: frame lines (0: the shortest that holds the exposure) */
	REDWOOD_CAMERA_KEEP = 2,        /* a picture for the host: a width, b height, c stride, d format (1 the frame's RAW10, 2 NV12,
	                                 * 3 BGRA); bytes follow */
	REDWOOD_CAMERA_SENSOR = 3,      /* another sensor: a which (as in the frames' header), b its mode (~0: the usual one);
	                                 * the frames stop, everything goes down, and the next read starts the other one */
	REDWOOD_CAMERA_FOCUS = 4,       /* the lens to a: 0 (the furthest) to 1023, from the next frame or so */
};

struct redwood_camera_command {
	uint32_t        command;
	uint32_t        bytes;          /* of what follows this structure */
	uint32_t        a, b, c, d;
};

#endif /* _SYS_REDWOOD_CAMERA_H_ */

```

```h
/*
 * /dev/redwood-touch: touch samples on their way from whoever produces them to the
 * program that turns them into HID events for the window server.
 *
 * iOS expects touches from Apple's multitouch driver through IOHIDFamily; neither exists
 * here. Instead a producer -- a kernel driver for a real touch controller or for an emulated
 * pointer, or a user program replaying a script -- posts samples, and code of ours running
 * inside backboardd reads them and synthesizes the events. Both sides use the same record.
 *
 *   write(): one or more records (time is ignored; the kernel stamps them)
 *   read():  blocks until there is at least one record, returns as many whole ones as fit
 */
#ifndef _SYS_REDWOOD_INPUT_H_
#define _SYS_REDWOOD_INPUT_H_

#include <stdint.h>

#define REDWOOD_TOUCH_DEVICE    "/dev/redwood-touch"

#define REDWOOD_TOUCH_DOWN      1       /* a finger has landed */
#define REDWOOD_TOUCH_MOVE      2
#define REDWOOD_TOUCH_UP        3       /* it has lifted (x, y: where it was last) */
#define REDWOOD_BUTTON_DOWN     4       /* a hardware button; `finger` says which (REDWOOD_BUTTON_*), x and y are 0 */
#define REDWOOD_BUTTON_UP       5

#define REDWOOD_BUTTON_LOCK     1       /* the side button */
#define REDWOOD_BUTTON_VOLUME_UP 2
#define REDWOOD_BUTTON_VOLUME_DOWN 3
#define REDWOOD_BUTTON_HOME     4

struct redwood_touch {
	uint64_t time;                  /* mach_absolute_time() when the sample was posted */
	uint32_t type;                  /* REDWOOD_TOUCH_* or REDWOOD_BUTTON_DOWN/UP */
	uint32_t finger;                /* which finger, from 0 (or which button) */
	uint32_t x, y;                  /* position on the display, 0 = left/top edge, 65535 = right/bottom edge */
};

 * handed to bsd/dev/redwood_battery.c, which keeps it for the sysctls kern.redwood.battery_* and
```

`xnu/files/bsd/sys/redwood_lx.h`:

```h
/*
 * The whole of what the Wi-Fi driver's object asks of the kernel it is linked into. That object
 * (tools/mk-ath11k.sh in the repository: Linux's ath11k on FreeBSD's LinuxKPI headers and our
 * wifi/lx) is compiled as FreeBSD kernel code, bsd/dev/redwood_lx.c on this side as XNU's;
 * neither sees the other's headers, so nothing but C's own types crosses (and the station
 * boundary's, redwood_sta.h, which is written for both). Everything the
 * driver's side knows of locks, timers, work queues and buffers is built in wifi/lx/src on the
 * few calls here.
 *
 * Threads: the driver's code runs on threads made by lx_os_thread() and on the kernel's own
 * threads that call into it; never in an interrupt.
 */
#ifndef _SYS_REDWOOD_LX_H_
#define _SYS_REDWOOD_LX_H_

#include "redwood_sta.h"

/* ---- memory ---- */
void	*lx_os_alloc(unsigned long size);			/* zeroed; NULL when there is none */
void	 lx_os_free(void *memory, unsigned long size);
/*
 * Memory the radio itself reads and writes: whole pages, zeroed, which the radio knows from
 * *address on (the machine says where: the radio sees memory through an SMMU). What either
 * side writes the other sees at once: the processor's cache is not in between, which makes
 * reading it slow. NULL when there is none; never given back.
 */
void	*lx_os_radio_memory(unsigned long size, unsigned long long *address);
void	*lx_os_map_registers(unsigned long long physical, unsigned long size);	/* never unmapped */

/* ---- saying things ---- */
void	 lx_os_print(const char *text);				/* for whoever looks for a fault: may be kept back */
void	 lx_os_tell(const char *text);				/* for whoever runs the machine: always said */
void	 lx_os_panic(const char *text) __attribute__((noreturn));

/* ---- time, threads, sleeping ---- */
unsigned long long lx_os_nanoseconds(void);			/* since some moment; never goes back */
void	*lx_os_thread_self(void);				/* a value that tells the kernel's threads apart */
/* a thread that runs function(argument) and ends when that returns: 0, or an errno */
int	 lx_os_thread(const char *name, void (*function)(void *), void *argument);
/*
 * One lock, and sleeping under it as with a condition variable: lx_os_sleep() is called with the
 * lock held, gives it up while asleep and has it again when it returns -- 0 when woken by
 * lx_os_wakeup() on the same address, 1 when the time (nanoseconds; 0: no limit) ran out.
 * The lock is held for a few instructions at a time and never across a call out of the layer.
 */
void	 lx_os_lock(void);
void	 lx_os_unlock(void);
int	 lx_os_sleep(const void *address, unsigned long long nanoseconds);
void	 lx_os_wakeup(const void *address);			/* everyone asleep on it */

/* ---- the rest of the machine ---- */
void	 lx_os_random(void *buffer, unsigned long size);	/* bytes nobody can guess */
/* a number given to the kernel when it was started ("wifi_lx=2"); 0 if it was not */
unsigned lx_os_option(const char *name);
/* a file the driver asks for by the name Linux has for it, in place: 0, or an errno (ENOENT) */
int	 lx_os_firmware(const char *name, const void **data, unsigned long *size);
/* the processor that runs the radio's firmware: started, and up when this returns; 0 or an errno */
int	 lx_os_rproc_boot(void);
/* the radio's own address (six bytes), if the machine has one for it: 1, or 0 and nothing written */
int	 lx_os_radio_address(unsigned char *address);
/*
 * The network the radio is to join, if the machine was given one: its name and its passphrase,
 * into buffers whose sizes come in and whose contents' lengths go out. 1, or 0.
 */
int	 lx_os_network(unsigned char *name, unsigned *name_length, unsigned char *passphrase, unsigned *passphrase_length);

/* ---- frames: the radio as what carries the machine's network interface ---- */
void	 lx_os_net_attach(const unsigned char *address);	/* there is a radio, and this is its address */
void	 lx_os_net_link(int up);				/* frames can pass now (a network is joined) / no longer */
void	 lx_os_net_input(const unsigned char *frame, unsigned long length);	/* an Ethernet frame has arrived */

/*
 * ---- the radio's interrupts (wifi_irq=1). The radio raises one by writing a number to an address
 * (an "MSI": the GIC's register that raises the SPI of that number); vector v of its 32 is data + v.
 * The driver's work for one is done in thread context, on the kernel's thread for them: the
 * function given for a vector is called there after it has fired, with the vector masked until
 * lx_os_irq_enable(). Nothing of the driver runs in an interrupt.
 */
int	 lx_os_irq_msi(unsigned long long *address, unsigned *data);	/* where and what: 1, or 0 (no interrupts) */
int	 lx_os_irq_attach(unsigned vector, void (*function)(void *), void *argument);	/* masked to begin with; 0 or an errno */
void	 lx_os_irq_enable(unsigned vector);
void	 lx_os_irq_disable(unsigned vector);			/* returns when its function is not running */
void	 lx_os_irq_detach_all(void);				/* returns when no function is running */
unsigned long long lx_os_irq_count(unsigned vector);		/* how many have arrived */

/* ---- the station: scanning and joining, for whoever asks the kernel (redwood_sta.h) ---- */
void	 lx_os_station(const struct redwood_sta_ops *ops);	/* here it is, to be asked; NULL: no longer (returns when no call is under way) */
void	 lx_os_station_lost(int error);				/* the network joined is gone by itself */

/*
 * ---- the names the object shows the kernel. lx_start(): bring the driver up on the radio and
 * do what the kernel's options ask (scan; join a network). 0, or an errno. Returns when that is
 * over or has failed; with a network joined the driver stays up, lx_transmit() sends an
 * Ethernet frame through it (0, or an errno; called by one thread, the kernel's own for that),
 * and lx_stop() leaves the network and takes the driver down in order (and does nothing if it
 * is not up).
 */
int	 lx_start(void);
void	 lx_stop(void);
int	 lx_transmit(const unsigned char *frame, unsigned long length);
/* before lx_start(), if the kernel wants it early: take the memory the radio will be shown. 0, or an errno. */
int	 lx_prepare(void);

#endif
```

`xnu/files/bsd/sys/redwood_net.h`:

```h
/*
 * en0, and what stands behind it.
 *
 * The network interface iOS uses here is made in bsd/dev/redwood_net.c with the kernel's own
 * interface KPI: Ethernet as far as the rest of the kernel and user space can tell. What carries
 * the frames is a "link", a driver of its own that knows nothing about interfaces: QEMU's virtio
 * network device today (bsd/dev/redwood_virtio_net.c), the phone's radio or frames carried over
 * the boot loader's USB channel tomorrow. This is all the two know of each other.
 *
 * A link driver
 *   - fills in a struct redwood_net_link and calls redwood_net_attach() once, when it is ready
 *     to carry frames (for a radio: when its firmware is up, not when it has joined a network);
 *   - hands every frame that arrives to redwood_net_input(): from its own thread, or from
 *     the poll function the interface's thread calls for it. Not from interrupt context;
 *   - says with redwood_net_link_state() when frames can pass and when they no longer can
 *     (the cable, or for a radio: associated and the keys set). configd starts DHCP on that.
 * A frame is what goes over an Ethernet cable without the checksum at its end: destination,
 * source, type, payload; at most REDWOOD_NET_FRAME_MAX bytes. A radio whose frames are 802.11
 * converts in its driver (or has its firmware do it: "Ethernet decap/encap").
 */
#ifndef _SYS_REDWOOD_NET_H_
#define _SYS_REDWOOD_NET_H_

#ifdef KERNEL
#include <sys/kpi_mbuf.h>

#define REDWOOD_NET_FRAME_MAX   1514

struct redwood_net_link {
	const char *    name;           /* for the log */
	uint8_t         address[6];     /* the interface's Ethernet address */
	bool            wireless;       /* the interface is told to be Wi-Fi (its "subfamily"), which is how the
	                                 * network stack and configd tell a radio from a cable */
	bool            up;             /* frames can pass from the start (else: wait for redwood_net_link_state()) */
	/*
	 * Send one frame: a chain of mbufs, `length` bytes in all, the Ethernet header first. The
	 * packet stays the caller's: copy it (mbuf_copydata()). Returns false if it had to be dropped.
	 * Called by one thread at a time, never from interrupt context.
	 */
	bool            (*transmit)(mbuf_t packet, size_t length);
	/*
	 * Optional. Look whether frames have arrived and call redwood_net_input() for each; returns
	 * how many there were. The interface's thread calls it every 2 ms while frames are coming and
	 * every 10 ms when none has for a while. A link that has a thread or an interrupt of its own
	 * leaves it NULL.
	 */
	unsigned        (*poll)(void);
};

/* Make en0 on top of that link (the structure must stay). One link, once: false if there is one already. */
bool redwood_net_attach(const struct redwood_net_link *link);
/* A frame has arrived. Copied; the buffer is the caller's again on return. */
void redwood_net_input(const uint8_t *frame, size_t length);
/* Frames can pass now / can no longer pass. */
void redwood_net_link_state(bool up);

void redwood_net_init(void);            /* the links there are: each looks for its hardware (or its boot-arg) */
/* an Apple80211 request (SIOCGA80211, SIOCSA80211) for the interface of a radio: redwood_apple80211.c */
errno_t redwood_apple80211_ioctl(u_long command, void *data);
void redwood_virtio_net_init(void);     /* boot-arg virtio_net=1: QEMU's virtio network device */
#endif /* KERNEL */

#endif /* _SYS_REDWOOD_NET_H_ */

```

`xnu/files/bsd/sys/redwood_qmi.h`:

```h
/*
 * QMI, the message protocol the firmware of Qualcomm's processors speaks (the Wi-Fi DSP's
 * "WLFW" service among them): the helpers a client needs, under the names and with the meaning
 * of Linux's <linux/soc/qcom/qmi.h>, so that a driver written for Linux -- ath11k's qmi.c --
 * compiles against this header unchanged. The implementation (bsd/dev/redwood_qmi.c) is ours,
 * written from what the interface and the wire format are publicly described to be; nothing of
 * Linux's implementation is in it.
 *
 * What is here: messages described by tables of struct qmi_elem_info and coded to and from C
 * structures by them; a handle that owns a port of the IPC router (sys/redwood_qrtr.h), looks a
 * service up and tells its user when the service appears and goes; requests as transactions
 * (init, send, wait or cancel) whose reply is decoded into the caller's structure; indications
 * handed to handlers. What is not: serving (no qmi_add_server, no replies of our own).
 *
 * Only <stdint.h> types are used, so that the header does not care what the driver's own
 * compatibility headers call a byte or a mutex.
 *
 * Who calls what from where: new_server, del_server and the indication handlers are called
 * from the router's delivery thread, with no lock of the helpers held; they may send. A reply
 * wakes the thread waiting in qmi_txn_wait().
 */
#ifndef _SYS_REDWOOD_QMI_H_
#define _SYS_REDWOOD_QMI_H_

#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>

/* ---- messages -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

/* The first seven bytes of every message, little-endian. */
#define QMI_REQUEST             0
#define QMI_RESPONSE            2
#define QMI_INDICATION          4
#define QMI_HEADER_SIZE         7       /* type (1), transaction (2), message id (2), length of the rest (2) */

/* The kind of an element of a message's description. */
enum qmi_elem_type {
	QMI_EOTI,                       /* the end of the table */
	QMI_OPT_FLAG,                   /* a byte of the C structure, not of the message: whether the element after it is there */
	QMI_DATA_LEN,                   /* the number of entries in the array after it: a uint32_t in C; elem_size 1
	                                 * or 2 is its size in the message */
	QMI_UNSIGNED_1_BYTE,
	QMI_UNSIGNED_2_BYTE,
	QMI_UNSIGNED_4_BYTE,
	QMI_UNSIGNED_8_BYTE,
	QMI_SIGNED_2_BYTE_ENUM,
	QMI_SIGNED_4_BYTE_ENUM,
	QMI_STRUCT,                     /* described by ei_array */
	QMI_STRING,                     /* in C: characters and a zero in elem_len bytes */
};

enum qmi_array_type {
	NO_ARRAY,
	STATIC_ARRAY,                   /* always elem_len entries */
	VAR_LEN_ARRAY,                  /* as many as the QMI_DATA_LEN element before it says, at most elem_len */
};

struct qmi_elem_info {
	enum qmi_elem_type      data_type;
	uint32_t                elem_len;       /* entries (for a string: bytes in C, the zero included) */
	uint32_t                elem_size;      /* bytes of one entry in C; of a basic type, on the wire as well */
	enum qmi_array_type     array_type;
	uint8_t                 tlv_type;       /* at the top level: the type of the TLV the element is in */
	uint32_t                offset;         /* where it is in the C structure */
	const struct qmi_elem_info *ei_array;   /* QMI_STRUCT: its elements */
};

#define QMI_COMMON_TLV_TYPE     0

/* The TLV of type 2 that every reply starts with. */
struct qmi_response_type_v01 {
	uint16_t result;
	uint16_t error;
};
extern const struct qmi_elem_info qmi_response_type_v01_ei[];

#define QMI_RESULT_SUCCESS_V01          0
#define QMI_RESULT_FAILURE_V01          1

#define QMI_ERR_NONE_V01                0
#define QMI_ERR_MALFORMED_MSG_V01       1
#define QMI_ERR_NO_MEMORY_V01           2
#define QMI_ERR_INTERNAL_V01            3
#define QMI_ERR_CLIENT_IDS_EXHAUSTED_V01 5
#define QMI_ERR_INVALID_ID_V01          41
#define QMI_ERR_ENCODING_V01            58
#define QMI_ERR_DISABLED_V01            69
#define QMI_ERR_INCOMPATIBLE_STATE_V01  90
#define QMI_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED_V01       94

/*
 * The coding by itself (the helpers below use it; tests call it directly). Both return the
 * number of bytes of the message, header included, or a negative errno.
 *   encode: `structure` by `ei` into `buffer` of `size` bytes, behind a header of that type,
 *           message id and transaction;
 *   decode: the message of `length` bytes at `buffer` by `ei` into `structure` (which the caller
 *           has zeroed: what the message does not have is left as it is).
 */
int redwood_qmi_encode(uint8_t type, uint16_t message, uint16_t transaction, const struct qmi_elem_info *ei, const void *structure,
    void *buffer, size_t size);
int redwood_qmi_decode(const void *buffer, size_t length, const struct qmi_elem_info *ei, void *structure);

/* ---- the router's addresses -------------------------------------------------------------------- */

#ifndef AF_QIPCRTR
#define AF_QIPCRTR              42
#endif
struct sockaddr_qrtr {
	uint16_t sq_family;
	uint32_t sq_node;
	uint32_t sq_port;
};

/* ---- a handle, services, transactions ------------------------------------------------------------ */

struct qmi_handle;
struct qmi_txn;
struct socket;                          /* (only ever a pointer here: what a handle's `sock` is called in Linux) */

/* A server of a service that was looked up. */
struct qmi_service {
	unsigned int service, version, instance;
	unsigned int node, port;
	void *priv;                     /* the user's */
	struct qmi_service *next;       /* the helpers' */
};

struct qmi_ops {
	/* a server has appeared; a negative answer and it is forgotten again */
	int (*new_server)(struct qmi_handle *qmi, struct qmi_service *service);
	/* ... and has gone */
	void (*del_server)(struct qmi_handle *qmi, struct qmi_service *service);
	/* (the rest of Linux's structure, for sources that fill it in; never called here) */
	void (*net_reset)(struct qmi_handle *qmi);
	void (*msg_handler)(struct qmi_handle *qmi, struct sockaddr_qrtr *sq, const void *data, size_t length);
	void (*bye)(struct qmi_handle *qmi, unsigned int node);
	void (*del_client)(struct qmi_handle *qmi, unsigned int node, unsigned int port);
};

/* What to do with a message that is no reply to a transaction; the list ends with an entry without fn. */
struct qmi_msg_handler {
	unsigned int type;              /* QMI_INDICATION (or QMI_REQUEST, QMI_RESPONSE) */
	unsigned int msg_id;
	const struct qmi_elem_info *ei;
	size_t decoded_size;            /* of the C structure, which is made, filled in and freed around fn */
	void (*fn)(struct qmi_handle *qmi, struct sockaddr_qrtr *sq, struct qmi_txn *txn, const void *decoded);
};

struct qmi_handle {
	struct socket *sock;            /* what kernel_connect() is given; not NULL while the handle is in use */
};

struct qmi_txn {
	struct qmi_handle *qmi;
	uint16_t id;
	int result;                     /* of decoding the reply */
	const struct qmi_elem_info *ei; /* the reply's description, and ... */
	void *dest;                     /* ... the structure it goes into */
	struct qmi_txn *next;           /* the helpers' */
	bool done, waiting;
};

/*
 * `largest`: the biggest message that will be taken (bigger ones are dropped). 0, or a negative
 * errno: -ENXIO where there is no router (redwood_qmi_set_transport() has not been called).
 */
int qmi_handle_init(struct qmi_handle *qmi, size_t largest, const struct qmi_ops *ops, const struct qmi_msg_handler *handlers);
void qmi_handle_release(struct qmi_handle *qmi);
/* Ask for a service: ops->new_server is called for every server of it there is and will be. */
int qmi_add_lookup(struct qmi_handle *qmi, unsigned int service, unsigned int version, unsigned int instance);

/* A transaction: its number (not negative), or a negative errno. The reply will be decoded by `ei` into `structure`. */
int qmi_txn_init(struct qmi_handle *qmi, struct qmi_txn *txn, const struct qmi_elem_info *ei, void *structure);
/*
 * Send the request of that transaction to `sq`, or with sq NULL to the server the handle was
 * connected to. `largest`: the most the encoded message may take, header not counted.
 */
int qmi_send_request(struct qmi_handle *qmi, struct sockaddr_qrtr *sq, struct qmi_txn *txn, int msg_id, size_t largest,
    const struct qmi_elem_info *ei, const void *structure);
/* Give a transaction up that will not be waited for. */
void qmi_txn_cancel(struct qmi_txn *txn);
/*
 * Wait for the reply: what decoding it gave (not negative: the bytes decoded), -ETIMEDOUT, or
 * the error of a reply that could not be decoded. The transaction is over either way.
 */
int redwood_qmi_txn_wait_ms(struct qmi_txn *txn, uint64_t milliseconds);

/*
 * Linux's qmi_txn_wait() takes the time in "jiffies", of which the caller's Linux has HZ a second.
 * HZ is looked up where qmi_txn_wait() is used, so it is the caller's whatever it is (a number,
 * a variable); a caller without one defines REDWOOD_QMI_JIFFIES_TO_MS(j) itself before this.
 */
#ifndef REDWOOD_QMI_JIFFIES_TO_MS
#define REDWOOD_QMI_JIFFIES_TO_MS(j)    ((uint64_t)(j) * 1000 / HZ)
#endif
#define qmi_txn_wait(txn, timeout)      redwood_qmi_txn_wait_ms((txn), REDWOOD_QMI_JIFFIES_TO_MS(timeout))

/*
 * The server that requests without an address go to. In Linux this is a connect() on the
 * handle's socket, which is how ath11k does it; here that call is this one.
 */
int redwood_qmi_connect(struct socket *sock, uint32_t node, uint32_t port);
#ifndef REDWOOD_QMI_NO_KERNEL_CONNECT
static inline int
kernel_connect(struct socket *sock, void *address, __attribute__((unused)) int length, __attribute__((unused)) int flags)
{
	const struct sockaddr_qrtr *sq = address;       /* (a pointer of whatever type the caller's Linux has for it) */

	return redwood_qmi_connect(sock, sq->sq_node, sq->sq_port);
}
#endif

#endif /* _SYS_REDWOOD_QMI_H_ */

```

`xnu/files/bsd/sys/redwood_qrtr.h`:

```h
/*
 * QRTR as the QMI helpers (sys/redwood_qmi.h) need it: datagrams to and from a port of a node of
 * Qualcomm's IPC router, and the question "where is that service".
 *
 * On the phone the router's other nodes are the processors beside ours (the Wi-Fi DSP is one), and
 * the datagrams travel over GLINK; whoever implements that hands these four calls to the QMI
 * helpers with redwood_qmi_set_transport(). On a development machine a test puts a fake in the
 * same place. Nothing here knows what is inside a datagram.
 */
#ifndef _SYS_REDWOOD_QRTR_H_
#define _SYS_REDWOOD_QRTR_H_

#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>

struct redwood_qrtr_port;

/*
 * A datagram for the port has arrived from (node, port). The data is the caller's again on return.
 */
typedef void (*redwood_qrtr_receive_t)(void *context, uint32_t node, uint32_t port, const void *data, size_t length);
/*
 * A server of a service that was asked for with lookup() has appeared at (node, port), or the one
 * that was there has gone. Called once for each that exists when the question is asked, too.
 */
typedef void (*redwood_qrtr_server_t)(void *context, bool arrived, uint32_t service, uint32_t version, uint32_t instance,
    uint32_t node, uint32_t port);

/*
 * Both callbacks come from one thread at a time, never from interrupt context, and may sleep
 * (the QMI helpers take a mutex in them and call their user's handlers from them). `context` is
 * what open() was given.
 */
struct redwood_qrtr_ops {
	/* A port of our own node; NULL if there is none to be had. */
	struct redwood_qrtr_port *(*open)(redwood_qrtr_receive_t receive, redwood_qrtr_server_t server, void *context);
	/* One datagram to (node, port); 0, or an errno. May sleep. Up to 8192 bytes. */
	int (*send)(struct redwood_qrtr_port *port, uint32_t node, uint32_t to_port, const void *data, size_t length);
	/* Tell this port's `server` callback about the servers of that service, now and from now on; 0, or an errno. */
	int (*lookup)(struct redwood_qrtr_port *port, uint32_t service, uint32_t version, uint32_t instance);
	/* No callback comes after this has returned. */
	void (*close)(struct redwood_qrtr_port *port);
};

/* The transport there is; NULL takes it away (handles made before keep the one they were made with). */
void redwood_qmi_set_transport(const struct redwood_qrtr_ops *ops);

#endif /* _SYS_REDWOOD_QRTR_H_ */

```

`xnu/files/bsd/sys/redwood_sta.h`:

```h
/*
 * Darwin-on-redwood: the station boundary.
 *
 * On one side whatever does the scanning and the joining with a radio: the station logic over
 * ath11k on the phone (wifi/lx in the repository). On the other whoever wants a network: the
 * Apple80211 requests of iOS's Wi-Fi side, answered in bsd/dev/redwood_apple80211.c, and the
 * kernel's own join of the network it was given in a file (bsd/dev/redwood_wifi.c). Frames do
 * not pass here, and neither does "the link is up": those go through bsd/sys/redwood_net.h,
 * which the station side calls itself.
 *
 * Between the two stands bsd/dev/redwood_sta.c: one thread, on which every call into the station
 * side is made, one at a time, and what the last scan heard, kept for whoever asks.
 *
 * Nothing but C's own types here: the station side is not compiled as XNU's code.
 */
#ifndef _SYS_REDWOOD_STA_H_
#define _SYS_REDWOOD_STA_H_

#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdint.h>

#define REDWOOD_STA_ELEMENTS_MOST       1024

/* One access point, as a scan heard it. */
struct redwood_sta_bss {
	uint8_t bssid[6];
	uint8_t ssid[32], ssid_length;
	uint16_t frequency;                     /* MHz */
	int16_t rssi;                           /* dBm */
	uint16_t beacon_interval;               /* in units of 1024 microseconds */
	uint16_t capability;                    /* the beacon's capability field */
	uint32_t age_ms;                        /* how long ago it was last heard */
	uint16_t elements_length;               /* the beacon's information elements as received: who asks */
	uint8_t elements[REDWOOD_STA_ELEMENTS_MOST];    /* reads the network's protection out of them itself */
};

/* What to scan for. All zero: every channel, the radio's own way. */
struct redwood_sta_scan {
	uint8_t ssid[32], ssid_length;          /* ask for this network by name (a hidden one answers only then) */
	uint16_t frequencies[64], frequency_count;      /* only these channels */
	bool passive;                           /* only listen */
	uint16_t dwell_ms;                      /* on each channel; 0: the radio's own */
};

enum { REDWOOD_STA_OPEN, REDWOOD_STA_WPA2_PSK };

struct redwood_sta_join {
	uint8_t ssid[32], ssid_length;
	uint8_t bssid[6];                       /* all zero: the access point of that name heard best */
	int security;
	uint8_t pmk[32];                        /* WPA2 with a passphrase: the key made of the passphrase and the name ... */
	uint8_t passphrase[64], passphrase_length;      /* ... or, if this is not empty, the passphrase itself */
};

enum redwood_sta_phase { REDWOOD_STA_OFF, REDWOOD_STA_IDLE, REDWOOD_STA_SCANNING, REDWOOD_STA_JOINING, REDWOOD_STA_JOINED };

struct redwood_sta_state {
	enum redwood_sta_phase phase;
	struct redwood_sta_bss bss;             /* the network joined or being joined */
	int last_error;                         /* why the last join failed or the network was lost (an errno); 0: it was not */
};

#define REDWOOD_STA_CHANNEL_PASSIVE     1u      /* the radio may only listen there */
#define REDWOOD_STA_CHANNEL_RADAR       2u      /* ... and has to look out for radar */

struct redwood_sta_channel {
	uint16_t frequency;                     /* MHz */
	uint16_t flags;
};

/*
 * What the station side supplies. All but state() are called on one thread, one at a time, and
 * may take as long as the thing takes: scan() returns when the scan is over, join() when frames
 * can pass or it is known why not. Each gives 0 or an errno.
 */
struct redwood_sta_ops {
	int (*power)(bool on);                  /* off: leave the network, stop the radio; on: start it */
	int (*scan)(const struct redwood_sta_scan *what);
	void (*heard)(void (*each)(const struct redwood_sta_bss *bss, void *context), void *context);   /* by the last scan */
	int (*join)(const struct redwood_sta_join *what);
	int (*leave)(void);
	void (*state)(struct redwood_sta_state *state);         /* on any thread; does not sleep */
	unsigned (*channels)(struct redwood_sta_channel *channels, unsigned most);      /* what the radio may tune to */
	uint8_t address[6];
};

/* What happens, said to whoever listens (the Apple80211 side). */
enum redwood_sta_event {
	REDWOOD_STA_POWER,                      /* status: 1 on, 0 off */
	REDWOOD_STA_SCAN_DONE,                  /* status: 0, or the scan's errno */
	REDWOOD_STA_JOIN_DONE,                  /* status: 0, or the join's errno */
	REDWOOD_STA_LINK,                       /* status: 1 a network is joined, 0 it has been left when asked,
	                                         * an errno: it was lost (the access point showed us the door) */
};

#ifdef KERNEL
/* ---- the station side ---- */
void     redwood_sta_attach(const struct redwood_sta_ops *ops);         /* NULL: it is going away (waits for a call under way) */
void     redwood_sta_lost(int error);                                   /* the network joined is gone by itself */

/* ---- who wants a network: each asks and returns; the outcome is an event. 0, or an errno ---- */
bool     redwood_sta_present(void);
int      redwood_sta_ask_power(bool on);
int      redwood_sta_ask_scan(const struct redwood_sta_scan *what);
int      redwood_sta_ask_join(const struct redwood_sta_join *what);
/* ... and joined again whenever the radio is turned on, until some other network is asked for */
int      redwood_sta_ask_join_standing(const struct redwood_sta_join *what);
int      redwood_sta_ask_leave(void);
bool     redwood_sta_busy(void);                                        /* something asked for is not over yet */
bool     redwood_sta_powered(void);
/* the `index`th access point the last scan heard: true, or false when there are not that many */
bool     redwood_sta_heard(unsigned index, struct redwood_sta_bss *bss);
void     redwood_sta_state(struct redwood_sta_state *state);
unsigned redwood_sta_channels(struct redwood_sta_channel *channels, unsigned most);
bool     redwood_sta_address(uint8_t *address);

/* ---- the listener: bsd/dev/redwood_apple80211.c ---- */
void     redwood_apple80211_event(enum redwood_sta_event event, int status);
void     redwood_apple80211_summary(void);                              /* what was asked in this run, to the log */
#endif

#endif
```

`xnu/files/iokit/Kernel/GenericARMPE.cpp`:

```cpp
/*
 * GenericARMPE: a minimal platform expert for non-Apple ARMv8 boards.
 *
 * On Apple hardware the platform expert comes from a closed kext
 * (AppleARMPlatform). Without one, IOKit falls through to IOPanicPlatform
 * ("Unable to find driver for this platform"). This class is the least that
 * lets IOKit start on a board described by a loader-built device tree:
 * it publishes the device-tree nodes as nubs and names the machine.
 */
extern "C" {
#include <pexpert/pexpert.h>
#include <pexpert/arm64/board_config.h>
#include <kern/cpu_number.h>
}
#include <machine/machine_routines.h>
#include <IOKit/IOPlatformExpert.h>
#include <IOKit/IODeviceTreeSupport.h>
#include <IOKit/IOLib.h>
#include <IOKit/IOCPU.h>
#include <kern/clock.h>
#include <kern/thread_call.h>

#include "MiniDrivers.h"

extern "C" {
kern_return_t processor_start(processor_t processor);
kern_return_t processor_exit(processor_t processor);
extern uint32_t processor_avail_count;

/* osfmk/arm64/psci_smp.c and gic_v3_irq.c */
void psci_smp_init(void);
kern_return_t psci_smp_start_cpu(int cpu);
void psci_smp_cpu_running(void);
void psci_smp_cpu_off(void) __dead2;
void gic_v3_irq_signal(uint32_t phys_id);
}

/*
 * GenericARMCPU: registers a device-tree CPU node with the kernel. The closed
 * AppleARMCPU driver does this on Apple hardware; without it the kernel waits
 * forever for the CPU count (ml_wait_max_cpus) and never calls
 * cpu_machine_init() on the boot processor.
 *
 * The other processors are started through the firmware (PSCI CPU_ON, see
 * osfmk/arm64/psci_smp.c) and signalled with interrupts of the GIC
 * (osfmk/arm64/gic_v3_irq.c). How many there are is the device tree's and the
 * boot-arg cpus=N's to say (ml_parse_cpu_topology()); with one, nothing of
 * that is used.
 */
class GenericARMCPU : public IOCPU
{
	OSDeclareDefaultStructors(GenericARMCPU);

	uint32_t physID;        /* the device tree's "reg": the low affinity fields of the core's MPIDR */

public:
	virtual bool start(IOService * provider) APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE;
	virtual void initCPU(bool boot) APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE;
	virtual void quiesceCPU(void) APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE;
	virtual kern_return_t startCPU(vm_offset_t start_paddr, vm_offset_t arg_paddr) APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE;
	virtual void haltCPU(void) APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE;
	virtual void signalCPU(IOCPU * target) APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE;
	virtual const OSSymbol * getCPUName(void) APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE;

	static int cpuNumberOfNub(IOService * nub);
	void run(void);
};

OSDefineMetaClassAndStructors(GenericARMCPU, IOCPU);

/* The kernel's number for the processor of a /cpus node, -1 if it is not to be used (boot-arg cpus=N). */
int
GenericARMCPU::cpuNumberOfNub(IOService * nub)
{
	OSData * reg = OSDynamicCast(OSData, nub->getProperty("reg"));

	if (nub->getProperty("state") == NULL || reg == NULL || reg->getLength() < sizeof(uint32_t)) {
		return -1;
	}
	return ml_get_cpu_number(*(const uint32_t *)reg->getBytesNoCopy());
}

/* Registers the processor; run() starts it. */
bool
GenericARMCPU::start(IOService * provider)
{
	ml_processor_info_t info;
	perfmon_interrupt_handler_func pmi_handler = NULL;
	int cpu = cpuNumberOfNub(provider);

	if (cpu < 0 || !IOCPU::start(provider)) {
		return false;
	}
	const ml_topology_cpu_t * topology = &ml_get_topology_info()->cpus[cpu];

	physID = topology->phys_id;
	setCPUNumber((UInt32)cpu);

	bzero(&info, sizeof(info));
	info.cpu_id = (cpu_id_t)this;
	info.log_id = getCPUNumber();
	info.phys_id = physID;
	info.cluster_id = topology->cluster_id;
	info.cluster_type = topology->cluster_type;
	if (ml_processor_register(&info, &machProcessor, &ipi_handler, &pmi_handler) != KERN_SUCCESS) {
		IOLog("GenericARMCPU: ml_processor_register failed\n");
		return false;
	}

	setCPUState(kIOCPUStateUninitalized);
	registerService();
	IOLog("GenericARMCPU: cpu %u (phys id 0x%x) registered\n", (unsigned)getCPUNumber(), physID);
	return true;
}

/*
 * The boot processor: runs cpu_machine_init() -> initCPU(true) on it, right here.
 * Any other: cpu_start() -> startCPU(), and the new core comes to initCPU() by itself.
 */
void
GenericARMCPU::run(void)
{
	processor_start(machProcessor);
}

/* On the processor itself, with its interrupts off, when it joins (or rejoins) the scheduler. */
void
GenericARMCPU::initCPU(bool boot)
{
	/* The interrupt controller and timer were set up in arm_init / arm_init_cpu (pe_init_fiq). */
	setCPUState(kIOCPUStateRunning);
	if (ml_get_cpu_count() > 1) {
		psci_smp_cpu_running();
		/*
		 * A processor takes no signals until it has handled an interrupt for one
		 * (cpu_signal_handler() lifts SIGPdisabled), and until then it does not go to
		 * sleep when idle either: send it its first.
		 */
		gic_v3_irq_signal(physID);
	}
}

/* On the processor itself, at the end of processor_exit(): it is to stop for good. */
void
GenericARMCPU::quiesceCPU(void)
{
	if (getCPUNumber() != (UInt32)master_cpu) {
		setCPUState(kIOCPUStateStopped);
		psci_smp_cpu_off();
	}
}

kern_return_t
GenericARMCPU::startCPU(vm_offset_t start_paddr, vm_offset_t arg_paddr)
{
	return psci_smp_start_cpu((int)getCPUNumber());
}

void
GenericARMCPU::haltCPU(void)
{
	if (getCPUNumber() != (UInt32)master_cpu) {
		processor_exit(machProcessor);
	}
}

void
GenericARMCPU::signalCPU(IOCPU * target)
{
	gic_v3_irq_signal(((GenericARMCPU *)target)->physID);
}

const OSSymbol *
GenericARMCPU::getCPUName(void)
{
	char name[32];
	snprintf(name, sizeof(name), "Primary%u", (unsigned)getCPUNumber());
	return OSSymbol::withCString(name);
}

class GenericARMPE : public IODTPlatformExpert
{
	OSDeclareDefaultStructors(GenericARMPE);

public:
	virtual IOService * probe(IOService * provider, SInt32 * score) APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE;
	virtual bool start(IOService * provider) APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE;
	virtual const char * deleteList(void) APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE;
	virtual const char * excludeList(void) APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE;
	virtual bool getMachineName(char * name, int maxLength) APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE;
	virtual long getGMTTimeOfDay(void) APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE;
	virtual void setGMTTimeOfDay(long secs) APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE;
};

#define super IODTPlatformExpert

OSDefineMetaClassAndStructors(GenericARMPE, IODTPlatformExpert);

IOService *
GenericARMPE::probe(IOService * provider, SInt32 * score)
{
	/*
	 * IODTPlatformExpert::probe() wants an IONameMatch against the root
	 * node; this expert is the only one built in, so it takes any board.
	 */
	if (!IOPlatformExpert::probe(provider, score)) {
		return NULL;
	}
	return this;
}

bool
GenericARMPE::start(IOService * provider)
{
	if (!super::start(provider)) {
		return false;
	}
	IOLog("GenericARMPE: platform \"%s\"\n", provider->getName());

	/*
	 * super::start() published the /cpus children as nubs. Attach a CPU driver to each
	 * one the kernel has a number for, register them all -- that settles the CPU count --
	 * and then start them, the boot processor (number master_cpu) first.
	 */
	static GenericARMCPU * cpus[MAX_CPUS];        /* (static: the slower cores may be started later, see below) */
	unsigned int count = 0;
	OSIterator * iter = getChildIterator(gIOServicePlane);
	if (iter != NULL) {
		OSObject * obj;
		while ((obj = iter->getNextObject()) != NULL) {
			IOService * nub = OSDynamicCast(IOService, obj);
			int number = nub ? GenericARMCPU::cpuNumberOfNub(nub) : -1;

			if (number < 0 || number >= MAX_CPUS || cpus[number] != NULL) {
				continue;
			}
			GenericARMCPU * cpu = new GenericARMCPU;
			if (cpu != NULL && cpu->init() && cpu->attach(nub)) {
				if (cpu->start(nub)) {
					cpus[number] = cpu;     /* kept: the kernel has its address as the cpu's id */
					count++;
					continue;
				}
				cpu->detach(nub);
			}
			if (cpu != NULL) {
				cpu->release();
			}
		}
		iter->release();
	}
	if (cpus[master_cpu] != NULL) {
		/* Unblocks everything that waits for the CPU count to be known. */
		ml_set_max_cpus(count);
		if (count > 1) {
			psci_smp_init();
		}
		/*
		 * The slower cores (an L2 access penalty, the loader's "small-core") are started 28 seconds
		 * later (boot-arg small_cores_after=S; 0: at once). With all seven from the start the lock
		 * screen came 1.5 s later than with the four big ones alone (26.5-27.0 s after the kernel
		 * began instead of 25.3-25.5: start-up's other work shares memory and cache with
		 * SpringBoard's), while that work as a whole was done earlier (34 s instead of 38). With
		 * the slower cores joining once the lock screen is there: 25.3 s and 36 s.
		 */
		uint32_t later = 28;
		static thread_call_t later_call;

		PE_parse_boot_argn("small_cores_after", &later, sizeof(later));
		cpus[master_cpu]->run();
		for (unsigned int number = 0; number < MAX_CPUS; number++) {
			if (cpus[number] != NULL && number != (unsigned int)master_cpu) {
				if (later != 0 && ml_get_topology_info()->cpus[number].l2_access_penalty != 0) {
					continue;
				}
				cpus[number]->run();
			}
		}
		if (later != 0) {
			uint64_t deadline;

			later_call = thread_call_allocate([](thread_call_param_t, thread_call_param_t) {
				for (unsigned int number = 0; number < MAX_CPUS; number++) {
					if (cpus[number] != NULL && ml_get_topology_info()->cpus[number].l2_access_penalty != 0) {
						cpus[number]->run();
					}
				}
				IOLog("GenericARMPE: the slower cores started too: %u processors running\n", processor_avail_count);
			}, NULL);
			clock_interval_to_deadline(later, NSEC_PER_SEC, &deadline);
			thread_call_enter_delayed(later_call, deadline);
		}
		if (count > 1) {
			IOLog("GenericARMPE: %u of %u processors are running\n", processor_avail_count, count);
		}
	}

	/* BSD looks the platform expert up by class (IOSecureBSDRoot). */
	registerService();

	/* Stand-ins for the closed graphics drivers that the iOS window server talks to. */
	MiniIOSurfaceStart(this);
	MiniIOMobileFramebufferStart(this);
	MiniAppleKeyStoreStart();
	MiniIONetworkStackStart();
	return true;
}

/*
 * The time of day. There is no driver for a real-time clock here; whoever started the kernel
 * says what time it was then -- the boot-arg epoch= (seconds since 1970, put there by the
 * host scripts) or, failing that, the property boot-epoch of /chosen (the loader, from the
 * firmware's clock) -- and the kernel's own timer counts from there. Without either the
 * calendar starts in 1970, as before.
 */
static long gBootEpoch;         /* the calendar time at which the system timer read zero */
static bool gBootEpochKnown;

static void
findBootEpoch(void)
{
	uint64_t epoch = 0;

	if (gBootEpochKnown) {
		return;
	}
	gBootEpochKnown = true;
	if (!PE_parse_boot_argn("epoch", &epoch, sizeof(epoch)) || epoch == 0) {
		IORegistryEntry * chosen = IORegistryEntry::fromPath("/chosen", gIODTPlane);
		OSData * data = chosen ? OSDynamicCast(OSData, chosen->getProperty("boot-epoch")) : NULL;

		if (data != NULL && data->getLength() == sizeof(epoch)) {
			memcpy(&epoch, data->getBytesNoCopy(), sizeof(epoch));
		}
		OSSafeReleaseNULL(chosen);
	}
	if (epoch != 0) {
		clock_sec_t secs;
		clock_usec_t usecs;

		clock_get_system_microtime(&secs, &usecs);
		gBootEpoch = (long) epoch - (long) secs;
	}
}

long
GenericARMPE::getGMTTimeOfDay(void)
{
	clock_sec_t secs;
	clock_usec_t usecs;

	findBootEpoch();
	if (gBootEpoch == 0) {
		return 0;
	}
	clock_get_system_microtime(&secs, &usecs);
	return gBootEpoch + (long) secs;
}

void
GenericARMPE::setGMTTimeOfDay(long secs)
{
	clock_sec_t uptime;
	clock_usec_t usecs;

	clock_get_system_microtime(&uptime, &usecs);
	gBootEpoch = secs - (long) uptime;
	gBootEpochKnown = true;
}

/* Device-tree nodes to drop entirely. */
const char *
GenericARMPE::deleteList(void)
{
	return "('packages', 'psuedo-usb', 'psuedo-hid', 'multiboot', 'rtas')";
}

/* Top-level nodes that describe boot state rather than devices: no nubs for these. */
const char *
GenericARMPE::excludeList(void)
{
	return "('chosen', 'memory', 'options', 'aliases', 'defaults', 'pram', 'cpus')";
}

/*
 * hw.machine. On Apple's devices it is the product type ("iPhone10,3"), from the device tree's
 * "model", and iOS decides from it what kind of device it is on: with anything it does not know
 * MobileGestalt settles for an iPod touch.
 */
bool
GenericARMPE::getMachineName(char * name, int maxLength)
{
	uint32_t real = 1;

	/*
	 * hw.machine is the model the loader put into the device tree, "iPhone10,3". It has to
	 * begin with "iPhone": CoreFoundation picks the device-specific variants of resources
	 * (Something~iphone.plist, Key~iphone in an Info.plist) by this string, and for a name it
	 * does not know it picks none at all -- Control Center, for one, then lays its modules out
	 * without their sizes. (boot-arg machine_name=0: the plain "arm64" this used to be.)
	 */
	PE_parse_boot_argn("machine_name", &real, sizeof(real));
	if (!real || !IODTPlatformExpert::getMachineName(name, maxLength) || name[0] == 0) {
		strlcpy(name, "arm64", maxLength);
	}
	return true;
}
```

`xnu/files/iokit/Kernel/MiniAppleKeyStore.cpp`:

```cpp
/*
 * MiniAppleKeyStore: a stand-in for Apple's AppleKeyStore (the kernel side of the keybag,
 * which on real hardware talks to the Secure Enclave), as seen by MobileKeyBag.framework
 * and libaks.
 *
 * It describes one fixed situation: a device that has no passcode -- never locked, unlocked
 * since boot. No keys exist here. The keychain (securityd) gives every item a key of its own and
 * has it wrapped by the key of the item's protection class (kAKSWrapKey) before it stores it, and
 * unwrapped (kAKSUnwrapKey) to read the item: that is answered, so that the keychain works -- but
 * with nothing secret to wrap with, the "wrapping" is a reversible transformation and protects
 * nothing (and the keychain lives in /private/var, in memory, and is gone at the next start).
 * Requests that would need real keys or bags otherwise (creating or loading bags, keys kept in the
 * key store) are refused, logged once.
 *
 * The protocol was worked out from the user-space side of iOS 16.5: selectors, and the
 * DER-encoded answers ("SET of SEQUENCE { UTF8String key, INTEGER value }").
 */

#include <IOKit/IOLib.h>
#include <IOKit/IOKitKeys.h>
#include <IOKit/IOService.h>
#include <IOKit/IOUserClient.h>
#include <IOKit/IOMemoryDescriptor.h>
#include <sys/systm.h>
#include <sys/proc.h>

#include "MiniDrivers.h"

enum {
	kAKSOpenCheck           = 0x00,
	kAKSGetLockState        = 0x07,         /* in: handle; out: state flags */
	kAKSLockDevice          = 0x08,
	kAKSUnlockDevice        = 0x09,
	kAKSWrapKey             = 0x0a,         /* in: handle, class; a key; out: the class, the key wrapped */
	kAKSUnwrapKey           = 0x0b,         /* in: handle, class; a wrapped key; out: the key */
	kAKSUnlockBag           = 0x0c,
	kAKSGetSystem           = 0x0e,         /* out: the handle of the system keybag */
	kAKSGetDeviceState      = 0x11,         /* in: handle; out: DER */
	kAKSGetBagUUID          = 0x17,         /* out: 16 bytes */
	kAKSAssertHold          = 0x1a,
	kAKSAssertDrop          = 0x1b,
	kAKSGetConfiguration    = 0x1f,         /* in: handle; out: DER (a big buffer, so out of line) */
	kAKSLockDeviceNow       = 0x20,
	kAKSGetExtendedState    = 0x23,         /* as kAKSGetDeviceState */
	kAKSGeneration          = 0x28,
	kAKSAssertPromote       = 0x64,
	kAKSAssertConsume       = 0x65,
	kAKSNotifyStateSet      = 0x66,         /* "the first-unlock notification has been posted" */
	kAKSNotifyStateIsSet    = 0x67,
	kAKSPrewarm             = 0x73,
};

/* state flags: bit 1 no passcode, bit 2 unlocked since boot */
#define kAKSStateFlags          0x6
/* lock state: 0 unlocked, 1 locked, 2 locking, 3 disabled (no passcode) */
#define kAKSLockStateDisabled   3

static uint64_t gAKSLogged[4];          /* selectors already reported */
static bool     gAKSNotifyState;

/* Append SEQUENCE { UTF8String key, INTEGER value } for a value below 128; returns the new length. */
static size_t
derPut(uint8_t * buf, size_t length, const char * key, uint8_t value)
{
	size_t keyLength = strlen(key);

	buf[length++] = 0x30;
	buf[length++] = (uint8_t) (keyLength + 5);
	buf[length++] = 0x0c;
	buf[length++] = (uint8_t) keyLength;
	memcpy(buf + length, key, keyLength);
	length += keyLength;
	buf[length++] = 0x02;
	buf[length++] = 0x01;
	buf[length++] = value;
	return length;
}

/* The answer to "device state": every field zero, except the two that say "no passcode, unlocked". */
static size_t
deviceState(uint8_t * buf)
{
	size_t length = 2;

	length = derPut(buf, length, "sb", 0);          /* backoff */
	length = derPut(buf, length, "sr", 0);
	length = derPut(buf, length, "ss", kAKSStateFlags);
	length = derPut(buf, length, "sas", 0);         /* assertion set */
	length = derPut(buf, length, "sfa", 0);         /* failed attempts */
	length = derPut(buf, length, "sgs", 0);         /* generation state */
	length = derPut(buf, length, "sls", kAKSLockStateDisabled);
	length = derPut(buf, length, "sgpe", 0);        /* grace period enabled */
	length = derPut(buf, length, "srcd", 0);        /* recovery countdown */
	buf[0] = 0x31;
	buf[1] = (uint8_t) (length - 2);
	return length;
}

static size_t
configuration(uint8_t * buf)
{
	size_t length = 2;

	length = derPut(buf, length, "bd", 0);          /* backoff delay */
	length = derPut(buf, length, "gp", 0);          /* grace period */
	length = derPut(buf, length, "mua", 10);        /* maximum unlock attempts */
	buf[0] = 0x31;
	buf[1] = (uint8_t) (length - 2);
	return length;
}

/* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * */

public:

	return kIOReturnSuccess;
}

/* keybagd asks to be told about keys to back up and bags to save; there never are any. */
IOReturn
AppleKeyStoreUserClient::registerNotificationPort(mach_port_t port, UInt32 type, io_user_reference_t refCon)
{
	releaseNotificationPort(port);
	return kIOReturnSuccess;
}

/*
 * kAKSWrapKey and kAKSUnwrapKey. A wrapped key is 8 bytes longer than the key, as with AES key
 * wrap (RFC 3394), which is what callers size their buffers for: a mark, the class, and the key
 * mixed with a fixed pattern. Not encryption: there is no secret here to encrypt with.
 */
static const uint8_t kWrapMark[4] = { 'H', 'K', 'w', 'r' };

static void
wrapMix(uint8_t * bytes, size_t length)
{
	for (size_t i = 0; i < length; i++) {
		bytes[i] ^= (uint8_t)(0x5a + 37 * i);
	}
}

/* A structure answer; a big buffer on the other side arrives as a memory descriptor. */
IOReturn
AppleKeyStoreUserClient::answer(IOExternalMethodArguments * args, const uint8_t * bytes, size_t length)
{
	if (args->structureOutputDescriptor != NULL) {
		IOMemoryDescriptor * out = args->structureOutputDescriptor;
		IOReturn ret;

		if (out->getLength() < length) {
			return kIOReturnNoSpace;
		}
		ret = out->prepare();
		if (ret == kIOReturnSuccess) {
			out->writeBytes(0, bytes, length);
			out->complete();
			args->structureOutputDescriptorSize = (uint32_t) length;
		}
		return ret;
	}
	if (args->structureOutput == NULL || args->structureOutputSize < length) {
		return kIOReturnNoSpace;
	}
	memcpy(args->structureOutput, bytes, length);
	args->structureOutputSize = (uint32_t) length;
	return kIOReturnSuccess;
}

IOReturn
AppleKeyStoreUserClient::externalMethod(uint32_t selector, IOExternalMethodArguments * args,
    IOExternalMethodDispatch * dispatch, OSObject * target, void * reference)
{
	static const uint8_t bagUUID[16] = { 0x72, 0x65, 0x64, 0x77, 0x6f, 0x6f, 0x64, 0x00, 0x6b, 0x65, 0x79, 0x62, 0x61, 0x67, 0x00, 0x01 };
	uint8_t der[128];
	uint64_t * out = args->scalarOutput;

	switch (selector) {
	case kAKSOpenCheck:
	case kAKSLockDevice:
	case kAKSLockDeviceNow:
	case kAKSUnlockDevice:
	case kAKSUnlockBag:
	case kAKSAssertHold:
	case kAKSAssertDrop:
	case kAKSAssertPromote:
	case kAKSAssertConsume:
	case kAKSPrewarm:
		return kIOReturnSuccess;

	case kAKSGetLockState:
		if (args->scalarOutputCount < 1) {
			return kIOReturnBadArgument;
		}
		out[0] = kAKSStateFlags;
		args->scalarOutputCount = 1;
		return kIOReturnSuccess;

	case kAKSGetSystem:
	case kAKSGeneration:
		if (args->scalarOutputCount >= 1) {
			out[0] = 0;
			args->scalarOutputCount = 1;
		}
		return kIOReturnSuccess;

	case kAKSGetDeviceState:
	case kAKSGetExtendedState:
		return answer(args, der, deviceState(der));

	case kAKSGetConfiguration:
		return answer(args, der, configuration(der));

	case kAKSGetBagUUID:
		return answer(args, bagUUID, sizeof(bagUUID));

	case kAKSNotifyStateSet:
		gAKSNotifyState = true;
		return kIOReturnSuccess;

	case kAKSWrapKey: {
		uint8_t wrapped[8 + 64];
		size_t length = args->structureInputSize;

		if (args->structureInput == NULL || length == 0 || length > 64 || args->scalarInputCount < 2) {
			return kIOReturnBadArgument;
		}
		memcpy(wrapped, kWrapMark, sizeof(kWrapMark));
		wrapped[4] = (uint8_t)args->scalarInput[1];
		wrapped[5] = wrapped[6] = wrapped[7] = 0;
		memcpy(wrapped + 8, args->structureInput, length);
		wrapMix(wrapped + 8, length);
		if (args->scalarOutputCount >= 1) {
			out[0] = args->scalarInput[1];
			args->scalarOutputCount = 1;
		}
		return answer(args, wrapped, 8 + length);
	}

	case kAKSUnwrapKey: {
		uint8_t key[64];
		const uint8_t * wrapped = (const uint8_t *)args->structureInput;
		size_t length = args->structureInputSize;

		if (wrapped == NULL || length <= 8 || length > 8 + sizeof(key) || memcmp(wrapped, kWrapMark, sizeof(kWrapMark)) != 0) {
			return kIOReturnBadArgument;
		}
		memcpy(key, wrapped + 8, length - 8);
		wrapMix(key, length - 8);
		return answer(args, key, length - 8);
	}

	case kAKSNotifyStateIsSet:
		if (args->scalarOutputCount < 1) {
			return kIOReturnBadArgument;
		}
		out[0] = gAKSNotifyState;
		args->scalarOutputCount = 1;
		return kIOReturnSuccess;

	default:
		break;
	}

	if (selector < 256 && !(gAKSLogged[selector / 64] & (1ULL << (selector % 64)))) {
		char procname[32] = "?";

		gAKSLogged[selector / 64] |= 1ULL << (selector % 64);
		proc_selfname(procname, sizeof(procname));
		IOLog("MiniAppleKeyStore: %s[%d] selector 0x%x not implemented (scalars %u in, %u out; structure %u in, %u out)\n",
		    procname, proc_selfpid(), selector, args->scalarInputCount, args->scalarOutputCount, args->structureInputSize,
		    args->structureOutputSize);
	}
	return kIOReturnUnsupported;
}

/* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * */

void
MiniAppleKeyStoreStart(void)
{
	/* user space looks for it by class, and by the path IOService:/IOResources/AppleKeyStore */
	IOService * resources = IOService::getResourceService();
	AppleKeyStore * store = OSTypeAlloc(AppleKeyStore);

	if (resources == NULL || store == NULL || !store->init() || !store->attach(resources)) {
		OSSafeReleaseNULL(store);
		IOLog("MiniAppleKeyStore: cannot create the service\n");
		return;
	}
	if (!store->start(resources)) {
		store->detach(resources);
	}
	store->release();
}
```
